IT WOULD BE MORE IMPORTANT TO RECORD THE UNDERGRADUATE DEGREE OF ORIGIN, THAT IS, THE PREVIOUS PATH, AS WELL AS THE MOTIVATIONS THAT INDUCE ENROLLMENT IN LM 85.
BASED ON THE PRELIMINARY ASSESSMENTS THIS PRESIDENCY PERSONALLY FOLLOW, IT CAN BE SAID, IN BROAD TERMS, THAT THE MAJORITY OF UNDERGRADUATE ORIGIN COMES FROM A HUMANISTIC PEDAGOGICAL, LITERARY STUDY PATH. INTERESTING ARE THE UNDERGRADUATE GRADUATES OR MULTIPLE DEGREE HOLDERS FROM SCIENTIFIC DISCIPLINES OR HEALTH/SOCIAL PATHS WHO CHOOSE TO ENROLL IN PEDAGOGICAL SCIENCES, ALTHOUGH IN SMALL NUMBERS.
Regarding the Almalaurea survey (Box B 7), 62 Master's graduates were consulted; the number of graduates was 62 in the biennial Master's, of which 43 were interviewed, with a response rate of approximately 70%, the vast majority being women, with only 3% men, an average age at graduation of 33 years, and an average grade of 103.
The average study duration was slightly over two years. Regarding post-graduation training, almost 40% of biennial Master's graduates opted for post-graduation training as a form of voluntary collaboration in 2% of cases, but mainly because they attended a first-level master, which is the highest figure at 18.6%.
Regarding employment status, 72% of graduates are employed, 23% are currently seeking work, and 16.3% have post-graduation work experience; the employment rate for 76% concerns women, and the unemployment rate is 13%.
Regarding entry into the labor market, 31 are employed in the Master's, representing 58.1% of cases, and 22.6% have started a new job after graduation. Regarding the time to enter the labor market, the average number of months is 1.8 months for the first job, two months for the first job. In summary, we have about 2 months for the first job and about 4 months for entering the labor market. Regarding the characteristics of current work for Master's graduates, 54.8% work in intellectual, scientific professions requiring high specialization, and 32.3% in technical professions. These are the two sectors most engaged by people. Regarding the type of work activity, most, 51.6%, have an open-ended contract, while non-standard contracts account for 41.9%. Smart Working is widespread in about one-third of cases, and part-time work is about 30% of cases, with an average of 27 weekly working hours. The characteristic of the company where they work: almost 42% of Master's graduates work in the private sector, 38.7% in the public sector; interestingly, about 20% of graduates are engaged in the non-profit sector. Most graduates work in Southern Italy, clearly linked to the student base served by the D'Annunzio university, while about 10% work in the North. Regarding salary, the average monthly net salary is slightly over €1100.
Regarding those who continue the job started before graduation, they report an improvement in their work due to the degree in one-third of cases, with some 16% reporting improvement. From an economic perspective, as well as regarding their work position, over two-thirds report having improved their professional skills thanks to the degree. It is interesting to note that over half of graduates use the skills acquired through the degree to a high extent (51.6%), while a small third declare to use them to a lesser extent. However, this is relative to whether the professional training acquired at university is appropriate; over 70% consider it very appropriate, while about 20% consider it poorly appropriate. Regarding the effectiveness of the degree, over 60% of Master's graduates in Pedagogical Sciences declare their degree to be very effective in their work, 20% consider it fairly effective, and 20% consider it ineffective. Regarding satisfaction with the work performed on a scale from 1 to 10, over 80% of Master's graduates in Pedagogical Sciences declare satisfaction, with a collective score of 8.2 points.
Satisfaction with the completed degree course and employment status of graduates (Almalaurea data/base UNICH data as of April 2021)
Regarding satisfaction of Pedagogical Sciences graduates with the completed degree course, first, we quantify the number of graduates and degree holders in Pedagogical Sciences in 2020, which amounts to 63 people. Of these, over half, 34 people, were interviewed.
The interviewed graduates were those enrolled from 2017, of which 27 were interviewed.
Regarding attendance, it concerned more than 75% of courses. This behavior was implemented by over 40% of enrolled students, compared to almost 43% nationally. A small 30% attended between half and three-quarters of courses, in a higher percentage than the national average. In contrast, at the Gabriele d'Annunzio university in Chieti, the presence of those attending less than half of the courses is residual, while over 25% attend at least a quarter of the courses, which is likely due to work reasons.
Regarding the judgment graduates give of the study load of courses, particularly whether the workload is appropriate for the duration of the course, the course is decidedly praised by over half of graduates, with almost 56%, as over 40% appreciate it. There are no students who consider the study load too burdensome relative to the course duration.
This means that the teaching staff of the course is able to evaluate the workload to be assigned to their students in a more than appropriate manner and with great balance.
Graduates and degree holders of Pedagogical Sciences at the Chieti-Pescara university consider the organization of exams, that is, the scheduling of sessions, times, related information, and booking procedures, to be satisfactory for more than half of the exams, according to six out of ten graduates. In general, the vast majority of graduates and degree holders recall a good organization regarding exams, more or less in line with the national average.
Regarding relationships with professors, graduates and degree holders are more than satisfied, with over 95%; this is a slightly higher figure than the national average.
Also from a logistical perspective, graduates and degree holders have a good memory of the degree course, judging the classrooms appropriate for 75% of respondents, although this figure is lower than the national average. However, this aspect is confirmed by the fact that over one-fifth of respondents find classrooms rarely appropriate, a higher figure than nationally.
Regarding computer workstations, less than two-thirds have used them, and the majority find the number inadequate. Although the use of computer workstations at the Gabriele D'Annunzio university, Pedagogical Sciences degree course, is in line with the national trend, dissatisfaction with the availability of such equipment is much higher in Chieti than elsewhere in the country.
Regarding the evaluation of equipment for other teaching activities, such as laboratories and practical activities, two-thirds of graduates and degree holders have used them, but only one-third found them appropriate; 39% found them often appropriate, and over one-fifth found them often inappropriate.
Regarding the evaluation of the library service, including borrowing, consultation, and opening hours, despite the fact that last year, due to the Covid-19 pandemic, access procedures were strictly controlled and regulated, over 80% of current graduates and degree holders have used and found it substantially in line with their desires and needs, expressing a positive judgment.
Regarding the question of whether they would enroll in university again, over 34 would enroll in the same degree course, and slightly over 10% would enroll in the same degree course at another university, showing the deep affection of Pedagogical Sciences graduates for the Gabriele D'Annunzio University in Chieti-Pescara.
Regarding employment status of graduates in Pedagogical Sciences, 25 graduates from 2019, 16 from 2017, and 26 from 2015 were interviewed to understand their employment situation and their career progression one, three, and five years after obtaining the degree. Additionally, data on graduates who were not employed at the time of graduation are reported.
Regarding the employment rate, graduates of the Pedagogical Sciences degree course at the Chieti-Pescara university work one year after obtaining the degree at 40%, 4 out of 10 graduates found employment one year after graduation; at 75% after five years, almost 58% have a job. Compared to the national average, the Chieti-Pescara figure is lower one year after the degree; it is higher three years after obtaining the degree and lower five years after. Those who do not work after graduation and are not seeking work because they are engaged in another university course or doing an internship are less than 4% after five years; the data is not available for graduates one year and three years after.
Regarding the time to enter the labor market, on average, after five years from graduation, the Pedagogical Sciences degree requires 13.6 months, more than double the national average (6.6 months).
Finally, those who use the skills acquired through the degree one year after obtaining the degree, half of graduates and degree holders in Pedagogical Sciences at the D'Annunzio University in Chieti-Pescara are in this condition one year and three years after graduation, and almost all, 93.3%, five years after obtaining the degree. Regarding comparison with graduates at other universities, the data one year and three years after is lower in Chieti than for Pedagogical Sciences graduates at other Italian universities; but it is higher than the national average five years after obtaining the degree.
Regarding salary, monthly net after one year, graduates and degree holders in Pedagogical Sciences at the Chieti-Pescara university earn €900, a figure lower than the average for graduates and degree holders in Pedagogical Sciences at other Italian universities. The same applies three years after obtaining the degree, but five years after obtaining the degree, graduates and degree holders in Pedagogical Sciences at the Chieti-Pescara university earn more than their colleagues at other Italian universities.
Regarding satisfaction with the work performed, graduates and degree holders in Pedagogical Sciences at the D'Annunzio University in Chieti-Pescara register a figure that is slightly higher than their colleagues at other Italian universities.
Regarding the survey of graduated students, compared to the national average class, 77 graduates were recorded in 2019, with less than half responding to the interview.
Regarding the COURSE EVALUATION, regarding attendance, UDA graduates attended much more than the national average: for example, more than 75% of courses were attended by 64.3% of UDA students, compared to only 42.1% of their colleagues at other Italian universities. UDA graduates are very satisfied with the chosen degree course. This orientation is shared with their national colleagues, although in this and subsequent responses, UDA graduates show greater enthusiasm, meaning that 'definitely yes' responses are higher than nationally, although summing 'definitely yes' and 'more yes than no' levels equalize.
UDA graduates consider the study load of courses appropriate for the duration of the degree course in the same measure as elsewhere in Italy (approximately 90%). UDA graduates in LM 85, like their national colleagues, are satisfied with the teaching organization, particularly exams, as well as with relationships with professors.
Regarding infrastructure and logistics, the evaluation concurs in a slight criticism; the message they send is that there is room for improvement in classrooms and computer equipment. In the latter case, UDA graduates in LM 85 show a more critical evaluation than the national average. A similar reasoning is applied regarding the evaluation of equipment for other teaching activities, such as laboratories or practical activities. Regarding library services, UDA evaluations are substantially aligned with national averages.
Regarding the last question 'would you enroll in university again', UDA graduates would re-enroll in the same course at the university at a lower rate than other national colleagues; UDA graduates in LM 85 would choose another course at the same university three times more often than the national average.
The 2019 year confirmed the trend of the previous year. According to the AlmaLaurea survey, the analysis of graduate opinions generally shows a high level of satisfaction among students who attended the course. In particular, 55% of respondents rated the study load of courses relative to the duration of the course as 'definitely appropriate'; for most exams, students declared satisfaction with the organization; respondents were satisfied with relationships with professors and the degree course overall (40% 'definitely satisfied'), considering classrooms 'often appropriate' (50%), the library service offered 'reasonably positive' (45%), concluding with a positive figure regarding the possibility of re-enrolling in the same course (55.0% compared to 75% the previous year). Data reveals some criticisms regarding teaching activity equipment and computer workstations, which should be made more appropriate for 50% of respondents and more numerous (55% of respondents).
Important is the data regarding post-graduation employment and the ability to express acquired competencies in the workplace. From this perspective, a gratifying relationship emerges between the degree obtained and the type of work and salary in the subsequent period. Data is positive (one year: 44.3%; three years: 68.5%; five years: 72.3%).
In the Report on the survey of student opinions for the academic year 2017-2018, approved by the Evaluation Committee at the meeting on April 29, 2019, regarding the survey of graduate opinions (Table 14, p. 33), out of 62 graduates, 25 questionnaires were completed, representing 40%. This figure requires appropriate interventions to bring this percentage closer to that of other Master's degree courses at the university, through measures to be evaluated collegially, for example, completing the questionnaire at the time of administrative procedures required to take the graduation exam.
Regarding overall graduate satisfaction in LM 85 (Table 15, p. 36), it is noteworthy that over 90% declare overall satisfaction with the degree course, and about half of graduates would re-enroll in the same course. The experience of graduates with professors of the degree course has been widely satisfactory (Table 16, p. 38).

Learning Skills
Graduates must demonstrate the ability to identify necessary areas for in-depth study, organize the modalities for researching sources and appropriate support tools. They must be able to use their knowledge and skills as a work and orientation tool in situations, as well as sources for possible theoretical-practical connections.
The course also aims to develop in students the ability to learn in updating processes in professional contexts and in personal research to enhance knowledge for practical purposes.
Expected learning skills results will be periodically verified through traditional verification methods within individual courses and training internship activities.

The Course will rely on the specific competencies of representatives of university structures (Student Secretariat, Evaluation Committee, Quality Office, etc.) or department (Department Secretariat) for organizational and administrative issues.

Program of work and deadlines for implementing initiatives As a management habit of the Course, in addition to regular monthly meetings of the Course Council, periodic meetings of the Parity Committee and the Review Group are scheduled, activities and meetings aimed at verifying the possible presence of criticalities, based on new national laws, statutes, and regulations.
For the current academic year, corrective and improvement measures have been prepared regarding the teaching delivered to students, so that the offered content is increasingly characterized by alignment with the educational objectives of the course and the training needs of the professional figures the course aims to form.
This is especially necessary in light of the national relevance acquired by the issue of defining normative figures for socio-pedagogical educators and pedagogists (known as 'Iori Law', effective January 1, 2018, with Law No. 205, paragraphs 594-601 - G.U. No. 302 of December 29, 2017).
This is complemented by the development and strengthening of the Course's quality monitoring system. On one hand, periodic meetings of discussion with students (during the last semester, meetings of discussion and dialogue between experts, professors, and students were held regarding: 12/12/2018: Study Plans, Access to Teaching, International Mobility; 19/02/2019: Teaching and Evaluation in University; 20/03/2019: Self-Evaluation of the Degree Course), on the other hand, tools for monitoring the quality of the educational offer have been developed. Among these, the Internship Experience Questionnaire (attached link) not only allows evaluation of the quality of the internship experience of students, but also the coherence between educational objectives, transmitted content, and competencies developed by the Course and the needs for developing expertise in educational fields. Reflection on collected data annually allows the Course to reflect on the effectiveness of its educational action.
Annual Review in Progress The Course is currently revising its regulations, adapting the course to new developments related to TFA support. Other documents deemed useful to justify the activation of the Course are under revision.
Brief Course Description The Master's degree in Pedagogical Sciences trains professionals in pedagogy, education, and training. At the end of the study path, they will have acquired a deep knowledge of both pedagogical theories and the application areas of such knowledge. Master's graduates will be able to propose pedagogical consultations regarding complex problems, as well as manage and coordinate services and organizations in educational and training contexts. Preparation will therefore be aimed at developing competencies related to planning, evaluating educational and training services and interventions, identifying and interpreting problems within educational and training processes, and developing methodological competencies necessary for managing organizational contexts. Competencies in pedagogical elaboration and training organization will allow them to hold high-level technical-decisional roles in both public and private sectors.
To this end, teaching activities allow for in-depth study of specific cases, even with direct pedagogical intervention 'in situ'.
The Master's degree in 'Pedagogical Sciences', in line with levels 6 and 7 of the European Qualifications Framework for Lifelong Learning and in line with what is provided by Law 205, paragraphs 594-601 (G.U. No. 302 of December 29, 2017), effective January 1, 2018, is aimed at training professional figures able to position themselves in the labor market as operators of planning, monitoring, evaluation, and management of integrated training processes, initiatives, and cooperation programs promoted and developed by the European Union.
External Effectiveness Regarding external effectiveness, data is available on the Alma Laurea website.
Regarding employment status, we have graduates from 2021 (one year after graduation), graduates from 2019 (three years after graduation), and graduates from 2017 (five years after graduation). These are the data and the population analyzed in 2022. One year after graduation, 14 were interviewed, with an average age of 29 years, all women, with an average grade of 107.6. Over one-third participated in or are engaged in post-graduation training. 64.3% are employed. Most, 55%, work in intellectual, scientific professions requiring high specialization; 44% are employed on an open-ended contract, 22% on a fixed-term contract; 33% have other contractual forms; 11% work in Smart Working; 44% work part-time, with an average of 24 weekly working hours. 44% work in the public sector, 22% in the private sector, and one-third in the non-profit sector. Most work in services. Therefore, they are concentrated in services and predominantly work in the South, over three-quarters, and in the Northeast, 22%.
Regarding the use of skills acquired through the degree, over half, 55%, consider them highly utilized, while 44% consider them utilized to a lesser extent. The appropriateness of professional training acquired at university is considered very appropriate by 77.8%, while 22% consider it poorly appropriate. For the most part, 44% work in jobs requiring a degree (clearly teachers), while 11% perform work not requiring a degree, but the degree is considered necessary even if not required, and useful for 44% of people. Regarding the effectiveness of the degree, satisfaction with current work. Two-thirds express that the degree is very effective in performing the job and finding satisfaction with the current work, which is considered fairly effective. 33% are satisfied with the work performed on a scale from one to ten, with a collective score of 8.2 points.
Regarding satisfaction with the completed degree course and employment status of graduates based on Almalaurea data, referring to graduates in 2021, we have 44 graduates, 35 interviewed, who attended regularly and thus graduated on-time (73% of graduates). They consider the study load of courses appropriate for the duration of the degree course: 'definitely yes' and 'more yes than no' over 90% of cases. They consider exam organization (sessions, times, information, booking) satisfactory for more than half of exams, with 46% of graduates being satisfied with relationships with professors in general. 'Definitely yes' over 40%, 'more yes than no' 50%.
Therefore, overall, over 90% of graduates are satisfied with relationships with professors, slightly lower than the national average. They are overall satisfied with the degree course: 'definitely yes' almost 54% of graduates, compared to 52.3% nationally. Regarding infrastructure, the figure is lower than the national average: 44% found classrooms often appropriate, compared to 50% nationally. Computer workstations also show a lower adequacy rate at D'Annunzio university compared to the national average. Finally, they would re-enroll in university in the same course or almost 85% of graduates, compared to almost 82% nationally. Regarding their employment status, they are employed one year after graduation at 47%, three years at 60.4%, five years at 65%. The figure is lower than the national average regarding the time to enter the labor market: they entered the labor market two and a half months after graduation; at the national level, after five years from graduation, over six months were needed.
The fact that graduates use in a high degree the skills acquired through the degree is relatively in line, only slightly lower than the national average. Regarding satisfaction with the work performed, graduates of our degree course express themselves more positively than their national colleagues. Regarding employment status, one-third of UDA LM 85 graduates work one year after graduation; after three and five years, about two-thirds of graduates work. The percentage is higher nationally.
Generally, statistical data shows that there has been further improvement in the employment rate of graduates in the labor market, higher than the previous academic year data and undoubtedly higher than the national average (one year: 33.3%; three years: 70.6%; five years: 83.3%) and the possibility of 'using to a high degree the skills acquired through the degree' (one year: 57.1%; three years: 58.3%; five years: 25%).
From the Almalaurea 2019 website, it emerges that the employability of Master's graduates (https://www.almalaurea.it/sites/almalaurea.it/files/docs/universita/occupazione/occupazione17/almalaurea_occupazione_rapporto2019_05_laureati_magistrali_biennali.pdf) in at least half of cases, particularly in Pedagogical Sciences, referring to 2018, is linked to employment prior to obtaining the degree. In general, the Pedagogical Sciences degree belongs to the group of disciplines with greater difficulties in the labor market.
These data are further confirmed by the OECD (http://www.oecd.org/education/education-at-a-glance) in September 2019, which notes that compared to STEM disciplines with an employment rate between 85% and 90% of graduates, the employment rate for those with tertiary education in artistic and humanistic disciplines, social sciences, and information sectors is relatively low (77%).
Finally, it is worth noting that although Pedagogical Sciences graduates are predominantly women, men are more advantaged in terms of employment upon entering the labor market (AlmaLaurea, §5.5.2).

Specific Educational Objectives and Description of the Educational Path The Master's degree in Pedagogical Sciences aims to train professionals in the fields of education and training, with a deep general knowledge of pedagogical problems and theories, and specific knowledge of the application areas of such knowledge. Master's graduates will be able to propose pedagogical consultations regarding complex problems, manage and coordinate services and organizations in educational and training contexts. Therefore, the preparation provided by the degree course will be aimed at acquiring competencies related to planning and evaluating educational and training services and interventions, identifying and interpreting problems within educational and training processes, as well as competencies related to methodologies and tools for managing organizational contexts.
Additionally, teaching activities aim to allow students to deepen specific case studies, even with direct involvement aimed at a greater understanding of the characteristics of pedagogical intervention 'in situ'.
The Master's degree in 'Pedagogical Sciences' is also aimed at training professional figures able to position themselves in the labor market as operators of planning, monitoring, and management of integrated training processes, community initiatives, and cooperation programs for the development of Communities in Europe.
Competencies in pedagogical elaboration and training organization will allow them to hold high-level technical-decisional roles in both public and private sectors.
To achieve the educational objectives, the Master's degree course provides teaching laboratories, training internships, and project work.

Due to pandemic-related interaction difficulties, it is noted that due to the pandemic situation, in-person curricular activities have been suspended, which are mostly in schools. An alternative model of internship has been chosen, with our graduates actively engaged in research projects and training internship projects to compensate for this lack. This orientation has been shared nationally by other pedagogical courses. The course has followed, over the last four academic years, the work of consolidating and improving relations with organizations and local structures, seeking to increase quantitatively the number of agreements and qualitatively the connection between university and local entities. In particular, through curricular internships, students have experienced the educational effects of the synergy between university training and first contact with the professional world. This has been contributed to by the organization and management of indirect internships, following emerging training strategies in socio-psychopedagogical fields, by the Internship Coordinator, who has followed the phases of orientation and tutoring for students in identifying the content of the training project, the methodological phases for its realization during direct internship, and the appropriate choice of structure among the agreed ones and other potential ones for establishing agreements. The involved structures have appreciated, alongside the positive synergy, the progressive simplification of the forms published on the department and university websites.
Numerous structures have been welcoming with which the curricular internship project has been structured. With all, the exchange has been constant, especially to identify strengths and potential criticalities. This work has been marked by a fruitful educational circularity that has also involved the pedagogical courses provided in the course and seminars with national experts engaged in research groups of the Pedagogical Society.
The students' final reports after direct internship have reserved space for the opinions of supervisors who followed individual students in the welcoming structures, especially nurseries, comprehensive schools, kindergarten, secondary school, and the Chieti and Pescara State Archives. During the academic year 2017/2018, the degree course welcomed 4 Spanish students from the University of León who completed their curricular internship at Pescara 4 Comprehensive School. Very positive opinions were constantly recorded thanks to the exchange with structure managers and school directors. For the academic year 2018/2019, such evaluations will be carried out through the administration of a questionnaire for evaluating the student's path by the welcoming structures and self-evaluation of the supervisor-tutor of the structures.
To strengthen this policy of cohesion with the territory and local productive realities, the Degree Course has prepared a new version of the questionnaire for both students and companies hosting them, to better monitor this important part of the educational activity. The questionnaire is downloadable from the degree course website, which, at the time of writing, is also preparing it in anticipation of implementing the e-learning promoted by our University. Summary of the Regional Coordination Committee's Opinion Professor Gaetano Bonetta, Dean of the Faculty of Educational Sciences, presents the Degree Course. The Degree Course in Pedagogical Sciences aims to train professionals in the fields of education and training with a deep general knowledge of pedagogical problems and theories, and specific knowledge of the application areas of such knowledge. The Committee examined the objectives and purposes of the Course, focusing on related professional opportunities. Graduates in Pedagogical Sciences can carry out educational research and consultancy activities in the programming and management of training interventions within educational institutions and within projects and educational services provided and/or funded by public, private, and third-sector entities. In the public sector, within programming and management activities of integrated training, also as directors of educational and training sectors. In the private sector, they can perform functions as independent professionals or managers operating at accredited training agencies, companies, or private entities, also for the creation of development partnerships and financed design. Following a thorough examination, the Committee expresses a positive opinion.

It would be much more interesting and therefore useful to evaluate the first-level degree path to understand whether a Pedagogical Sciences Master's is the result of a linear path, I would say a pedagogical vocation, rather than a choice that tends to enrich a curriculum oriented towards other subjects.

Analyzing the cohort progression from the first to the second year, the student body continuing studies has earned approximately half of the CFU.
The analysis is performed based on available data and related to enrolled students (cohort) in the first year of the Course.
The 2017 year confirmed the positive trend of enrollments. In particular, 178 students were enrolled.
The user base is gradually shifting outside the region. Since 2010, there has been a progressive shift of the center of gravity outside Abruzzo, towards Southern Italy. A more in-depth and dynamic analysis shows the lack of a redistributive spatial effect on the user base. Gini concentration indices measure high values in all three periods, between 0.77 and 0.88, confirming a successful development policy not accompanied, however, by equivalent consolidation actions. Enrolled students continue to arrive predominantly from high school or magistral training, as in the tradition of the degree class under examination. From the results achieved by students, in 2017, a more qualified preparation was recorded both at entry and exit.
Regarding more recent data, regarding the cohort trend, although data is partial at the time of writing as the academic year 2018/2019 is not yet completed, the following emerges:
The cohort year considered is 2017. In the enrollment year 2017, 71 people were enrolled, and in 2018, 47 people. There were 17 explicit withdrawals and 7 non-renewals of enrollment.
Regarding student performance, the average number of exams passed per student in 2017 was 3.96, and 4.83 in 2018. Regarding the percentage of CFU acquired out of the theoretical total, it was 53.1% in 2017 and 57.8% in 2018.

Characteristics of the Final Exam The final exam consists of elaborating (also using computer tools) a research paper or an intervention project aimed at the educational and/or training field, referring to topics covered in the course, accompanied by a detailed and updated bibliography.
The final exam also requires the presentation and discussion of the elaboration in a public session before a committee of professors.
Final Exam Procedure The final exam consists of elaborating (also using computer tools) a research paper or an intervention project aimed at the educational and/or training field, referring to topics covered in the course, accompanied by a detailed and updated bibliography.
The final exam also requires the presentation and discussion of the elaboration in a public session before a committee of professors.
The grading takes into account:
a) the student's academic record (average of passed exams; whether the student is on-track or off-track);
b) the manner of conducting the exam;
c) the originality of the chosen topic; the accuracy in selecting sources, and whether these are in line with international debate and to what percentage they refer to literature in foreign languages;
d) whether during the discussion the candidate provided convincing and exhaustive answers.
Regarding the grading, up to five points are awarded; where special conditions arise, for example, an extremely positive judgment by the Committee on the work, which is appreciated as of particular quality, or if it is possible to reach a grade of 110/110, the Committee may award six points.
This practice is customary within the Degree Course and has been passed down since it was established during the time of the Faculty of Educational Sciences.
THE RULES REGARDING THE FINAL EXAM ARE THOSE PROVIDED BY REGULATIONS. REGARDING THE COMPOSITION OF THE COMMITTEES, ALL RELATORS AND SOMETIMES CORRELATORS ARE CALLED TO THE SESSION. THE ISSUE OF OTHER LANGUAGES HAS NEVER BEEN RAISED.

Department DEPARTMENT OF LEGAL AND SOCIAL SCIENCES Website http://giurinn.unich.it  Admission requirements Required knowledge for admission To be admitted to the Master's Degree in Legal Sciences for Internationalization and Innovation of Business (Giurinn), one must hold a three-year university degree or a three-year diploma in the following degree classes, or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent.
All candidates who have obtained a three-year degree or a single-cycle Master's degree in the following degree classes may be admitted: L-14 Legal Services Sciences and LMG/01 - Jurisprudence, under DM 270/04 and DM 509/99. Additionally, candidates with degrees in the following classes may be admitted: L-18 Economics and Business Management Sciences; L-33 Economic Sciences; L-16 Administration Sciences; L-36 Political Sciences and International Relations; L-39 Social Services Sciences; L-40 Sociology, under DM 270/04 and DM 509/99.
For candidates with degrees in other classes, admission to the course is conditional upon acquiring at least 48 university credits in specific SSD (basic, characterizing, related, or elective) across the following three groupings:
1) At least 24 CFU in the fields: IUS/01, IUS/02, IUS/03, IUS/04, IUS/05, IUS/06, IUS/07, IUS/08, IUS/09, IUS/10, IUS/12, IUS/13, IUS/14, IUS/15, IUS/16, IUS/17, IUS/20, IUS/21. At least 12 CFU must be obtained in IUS/01 Private Law and IUS/08 or IUS/09 Constitutional or Public Law.
2) At least 12 CFU in the fields SECS-P and SECS-S: SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/03, SECS-P/04, SECS-P/05, SECS-P/06, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/09, SECS-P/10, SECS-P/11, SECS-P/13, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/03, SECS-S/05.
3) At least 12 CFU in the fields: INF/01, ING-INF/05, ING-IND/35, SPS/04, SPS/07, SPS/09, SPS/12, M-STO/02, M-GGR/01, M-PSI/05, M-PSI/06, L-LIN.
Subject to the above, enrollment is conditional upon verification of personal preparation and/or passing an admission test, and possession of English language competence at least at B2 level. A tolerance of up to 10% is permitted for individual disciplinary groupings or the overall set.
Admission requirements are considered fulfilled upon obtaining a three-year degree in class L-14 or a single-cycle Master's degree in class L-MG/01 with a final grade exceeding 90/110.
In other cases, the fulfillment of curricular requirements will be verified, according to procedures outlined in the Course Didactic Regulations and based on the candidate's documentation, by a Commission appointed by the Course Council. The Commission will assess the student's personal preparation through an oral interview and/or an admission test. The Commission will inform students of required readings to improve foundational knowledge and publish a schedule for interviews on the official Course and Department websites. Following the interview, if the Commission deems the student's knowledge and skills sufficient, it will issue a positive admission recommendation. In such cases, the student may enroll in the Course. In case of negative outcome, the Commission will provide justification for non-admission, conditioning enrollment on recovery of missing credits through passing relevant exams or, for language deficiencies, obtaining an appropriate certification.

Admission Procedures To be admitted to the Master's Degree in Legal Sciences for Internationalization and Business Innovation (Giurinn), one must hold a three-year university degree or a three-year diploma in the following degree classes, or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent.
All candidates who have obtained a three-year degree or a single-cycle Master's degree in the following degree classes may be admitted: L-14 Legal Services Sciences and LMG/01 Jurisprudence, under DM 270/04 and DM 509/99. Additionally, candidates with degrees in the following classes may be admitted: L-18 Economics and Business Management Sciences; L-33 Economic Sciences; L-16 Administration Sciences; L-36 Political Sciences and International Relations; L-39 Social Services Sciences; L-40 Sociology, under DM 270/04 and DM 509/99.
For graduates in degree classes other than those listed above, admission to the course is conditional upon acquiring at least 48 university credits (CFU) in specific SSD (basic, characterizing, related, or elective) across the following three groupings:
1) At least 24 CFU in the sectors: IUS/01, IUS/02, IUS/03, IUS/04, IUS/05, IUS/06, IUS/07, IUS/08, IUS/09, IUS/10, IUS/12, IUS/13, IUS/14, IUS/15, IUS/16, IUS/17, IUS/20, IUS/21. At least 12 CFU must be obtained in IUS/01 Private Law and IUS/08 or IUS/09 Constitutional or Public Law.
2) At least 12 CFU in the sectors SECS-P and SECS-S: SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/03, SECS-P/04, SECS-P/05, SECS-P/06, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/09, SECS-P/10, SECS-P/11, SECS-P/13, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/03, SECS-S/05.
3) At least 12 CFU in the sectors: INF/01, ING-INF/05, ING-IND/35, SPS/04, SPS/07, SPS/09, SPS/12, M-STO/02, M-GGR/01, M-PSI/05, M-PSI/06, L-LIN.
Subject to the above, admission is conditional upon verification of personal preparation and/or passing an admission test, and possessing an English language proficiency level of at least B2. A tolerance of up to 10% is permitted for individual disciplinary groupings or the overall set.
Admission requirements are considered fulfilled upon obtaining a three-year degree in class L-14 or a single-cycle Master's degree in class L-MG/01 with a final grade exceeding 90/110.
In other cases, the fulfillment of curricular requirements will be verified by a committee appointed by the Course Council, according to the procedures outlined in the Course's Didactic Regulations and based on the candidate's documentation. The committee will assess the student's personal preparation through an oral interview and/or an admission test. The committee will inform students of required readings to improve foundational knowledge and publish a schedule for interviews on the Course and Department of Legal and Social Sciences website. Following the interview, if the committee deems the student's knowledge and skills sufficient, a positive admission recommendation will be issued. In such cases, the student may enroll in the Course. In case of negative outcome, the committee will provide justification for non-admission, subjecting enrollment to the recovery of missing credits through passing relevant exams or, for language deficiencies, obtaining an appropriate certification.

Program, texts and objectives Note regarding the sectors and credits selected for characteristic activities The introduction of courses belonging to different disciplinary fields among the characteristic activities responds to the specific training objectives of the study path, which, on the one hand, require adequate preparation in general disciplines concerning the regulatory context of the internal market in the European Union, the regulation of competition and state aid studied from an economic or legal perspective in the first year of the course; on the other hand, in the second year of the course, allow students to deepen their knowledge and skills in professional fields related to contracts and public services, or to transnational dispute resolution procedures for civil and commercial matters, both highly specialized subjects aimed at completing the training of the business lawyer operating in an international/transnational context.

CURRICULUM: Communication Skills
SECTION: Communication Skills
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/1803

Communication Skills (communication skills)
The master's graduate in Legal Sciences for Internationalization and Business Innovation acquires in the study program the ability to present technical concepts in oral and written form; to communicate and transmit information, value judgments, and proposals; to draft documents, opinions, and projects by reprocessing and classifying information; to critically use arguments; and to strategically use digital technologies.
The programming and organization of teaching activities include seminars, also in English or other foreign language, discussion of cases and reports, drafting of projects and opinions on specific issues, and presence of business and institutional testimonies. The verification of acquisition of communication skills, in synthetic or analytical form, is entrusted to oral or written exercises provided by each course, culminating in the final exam, which constitutes the verification moment for the achieved abilities in this area.
In particular, interactive teaching methods, as well as interaction with business testimonies aim to promote the acquisition and expression of communication skills in students. Through the organization of work groups and presentation of cases, students are encouraged to present their ideas to peers and/or external interlocutors, to argue their positions, and to clearly and concisely present their viewpoint on analyzed issues.
Special attention will be given to computer-supported communication and communication in English through seminars and professional workshops where students can learn new communication methods and techniques. Specific courses are dedicated to communication strategies through digital technologies.

CURRICULUM:
SECTION: JUDGMENT AUTONOMY
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/1803

Judgment autonomy (making judgements)
The Master's graduate in Legal Sciences for Internationalization and Business Innovation, thanks to possessing critical and analytical knowledge and skills on major private and public law categories not only in the national context but also with reference to the European and international legal space, as well as multidisciplinary methodological knowledge and skills, develops the ability to address complex situations and formulate innovative strategies, with strong attention to the transnational dimension and the ability to handle legal issues related to the use of digital technologies.
The Master's training path traverses traditional disciplinary knowledge and strongly encourages the student's judgment autonomy, leading them to construct their own study path by exercising choices among different courses, acquiring distinct methodological skills, and utilizing the skills acquired during internship and placement periods for the preparation of the thesis, which may have an original and innovative character, fully applying the acquired critical knowledge and skills.
The novelty of the study course and the proposed teaching programs (this is not the traditional teaching programs of legal study courses, as comprehensive and appropriate textbooks are often missing or not available on the Italian publishing market) obliges the student to draw from various sources, compare them, acquire different perspectives and methodological approaches, even on foreign texts and documents. The plurality of sources and the need to interpret and correctly frame them within the multilevel legal system, distinguishing between binding and non-binding instruments, strongly stimulates judgment autonomy and analytical ability, contributing to forming a legal expert aware of the various possible solutions to complex issues.
The verification of the acquisition of autonomous judgment ability is tested through the evaluation of individual contribution to in-depth seminar activities, case discussions, legal clinics preparation, internship and placement activities, as well as the elaboration of the thesis.

International Mobility Section Within the framework of the Alliance Ingenium among 10 European universities including UdA, the Giurinn Study Course has signed a double degree agreement with the University of Rouen Normandie (URN). Starting from the 2024-25 academic year, this agreement will allow Giurinn students enrolled in the international pathway to spend one semester abroad at URN, attend courses specified in the agreed study plan for 30 CFU, and obtain a double Master's degree in Juridical Sciences and a Master 2 in Droit international. Similarly, URN students enrolled in the Master 2 in Droit international will spend one semester in Italy attending five courses of the Giurinn Study Course for a total of 30 CFU. The international pathway requires attending courses taught in English at both universities, passing the relevant exams, and the possibility to complete the final exam under the supervision of a host university co-advisor, also in English. The coordinator for the double degree pathway, together with Prof. Fausta Guarriello, President of Giurinn, is Prof. Filippo Lorenzon, who will support incoming and outgoing students from URN and UdA (see attached resolution by the CdS Council of February 28, 2024, approved by the Department Council on February 29, 2024, and by the SEAGS School Board on March 6, 2024).

For the double degree agreement, a series of Giurinn courses will be taught in English for incoming students from the University of Rouen: seven courses, from which foreign students may choose five, totaling 30 CFU.

Within the Alliance Ingenium, Professors Paola Puoti and Fausta Guarriello conducted an Erasmus mission during the week of January 21-26, 2024, each delivering 10 hours of teaching to Master 2 students at the University of Rouen.

The Department of Juridical and Social Sciences has also renewed agreements with foreign universities for international student mobility. Within existing relations, the Giurinn Study Course appointed Professor Ilaria Ottaviano (email: ilaria.ottaviano@unich.it), Professor of European Union Law, as the Erasmus coordinator for Giurinn (email: ilaria.ottaviano@unich.it). In coordination with Professor Alessandro Serpe (email: alessandro.serpe@unich.it), the Department's legal section representative, she carries out the following activities:
- Evaluation of the conditions for extending agreements with foreign institutions and mobility agreements for students and teachers, both incoming and outgoing;
- Orientation and information for students in class and/or via online appointment;
- Organization of information and orientation meetings with students before the application deadline for Erasmus programs. At these meetings, students are informed about partner institutions and the scholarships provided by the CdS to supplement the University scholarship for the first four students in the ranking.

Other initiatives Attached is the updated list as of March 2024 of Erasmus agreements for students of the Bachelor's and Master's Degree Course SEGI and GIURINN Student opinions The students' opinion was collected through a questionnaire administered before each exam; the collection was carried out until July 31, 2023.
The average of the responses to the 121 processed questionnaires further improves the already excellent result achieved by Giurinn last year, increasing from 3.70 to 3.80, placing it first among social area degrees, whose average is 3.49. Particularly appreciated at the aggregated level is the effectiveness of teaching, which achieves an excellent average of 3.85, followed by the aggregated data on logistical-organizational aspects with 3.82. All 12 out of 26 listed training activities achieved a result above 3.50, so this year 100% of the listed activities places the CdS at level A of student appreciation (with evaluations between 3.50 and 4). The overall improvement in the average is due to a significant improvement in the evaluations of individual courses and a higher level of responses to the questionnaire questions.
Students' opinions have remained very positive, both regarding the interest of the teaching subjects and regarding the adequacy of the required knowledge upon entry, judged adequate by 100% of the surveyed attending students. All teachers are considered very available to provide clarifications, and the learning process is positively evaluated regarding the teaching materials provided and the integrated and supportive activities organized by the degree course and arranged by individual teachers. Particularly appreciated are seminars, simulated processes, and the discussion of papers and theses prepared individually or in small groups as positive examples of interactive teaching.
The percentage of fully positive or more positive than negative responses is quite high even among non-attending students, perhaps also due to the availability of recorded lectures for students with work commitments. Teachers have followed the suggestion made by students in CPDS to provide teaching materials in advance of lectures to involve students more in the classroom discussion of the topics. From students' opinions, the experimental nature of the CdS and the teaching subjects is reinforced, requiring teachers to make an effort to systematize and synthesize sources of various origins, with strong attention to the practical-applicative dimension of the treated institutions, also through the organization of professionalizing seminars with companies/entities.
Students' opinions will be discussed by the CdS GAQ before the next September Council.
The CdS has not established a specific procedure for handling complaints, which are currently directed to the president and teacher-tutors. The CdS website promotes the complaint management procedure provided at the University level, reporting the address: https://www.unich.it/parla-con-noi Graduate opinions From the survey of graduates' opinions (7 for the Giurinn CdS) published by PQA, the average score achieved (3.34) is higher than the University average and the averages of social area courses, respectively recorded at 3.23 and 3.22. Data for previous years are not available, due to the recent establishment of the Giurinn CdS in the academic year 2019-20.
For question 2, "Is the study load of the courses in the reference period acceptable?", the average response was 3.86 (compared to a more modest 3.29 for the University), as for D3 on the overall organization (schedule, exams, intermediate and final) of the courses in the reference period, the average was 3.42 (compared to the University average of 3.14); for D4 on the schedule of the courses in the reference period being designed to allow adequate attendance and individual study, the response was 3.43 against the University average of 3.20; for D6 on overall satisfaction with the courses, with an average of 3.71, compared to a University average of 3.33; for overall satisfaction with the CdS, with an average of 3.71 against a University average of 3.31. Therefore, the overall evaluation of the CdS is very positive, but elements of dissatisfaction compared to the University average are noted regarding administrative services managed by secretariats, with a score of 2.57 against a University average of 2.99; and particularly the support provided by the University for internship or trainee activities, evaluated with an average of 2.83 against a University average of 3.15, as well as the evaluation regarding internship or trainee activities, which stands at 3.33 for the CdS while being evaluated at 3.48 for the University. These are issues related to administrative support for the CdS, which will need to be reported and discussed with student secretariats and the School's administrative secretariat to improve the service provided to students, especially at the exit phase from the CdS. Another criticality to highlight is the low number of students who have completed a study period abroad, not recorded by PQA perhaps because it is a very small number (3 graduates, as far as is known).
From Almalaurea data on the Master's degree class SC-GIUR, recorded only since 2021 and 2022, with very few graduates one year after obtaining the Master's degree (respectively 34 and 107), it emerges that graduates are predominantly Women (79.4%) against only 20.6% Men, the average age of graduation is 26.7 years, 86% of students obtain the degree during the course, and the average degree grade is very high, reaching 109.7/110.
These data are confirmed by Giurinn graduates of our University, respectively 2 in 2021 with a grade of 110 and honors and 1 with a grade of 105-110; for 2022 all 5 graduates, of whom 4 during the course and 1 FC, achieved the maximum score of 110 and honors.
In all 14 Universities that have activated the SC-GIUR class, the origin of new students is 88% from the Bachelor's degree course in Legal Services; 78.4% regularly attend lectures; 54.6% have completed a curricular internship; 10.3% have completed study periods abroad; and 71.4% continue their post-graduation training.
One year after graduation, the employment rate of graduates of the class is 90.5%, confirming the strongly professionalizing nature of the CdS. The average monthly net salary is 1362 Euros. Due to the recent establishment and activation of the Master's degree class, employment data for 5 years after obtaining the degree are not available, nor other relevant information.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding (applying knowledge and understanding)
Traditional frontal teaching methods are supplemented or replaced with interactive dialogue forms between teacher and students to stimulate reactions, discussions, and positions. The encouragement to research and analyze relevant documents on the topics treated, to discuss complex cases, to adopt different viewpoints, to draft reports and opinions, and to present them publicly contributes to fostering the adequate expression of acquired knowledge, the ability to connect different disciplinary fields, coherent argumentation of one's theses, preparing the student for their future professional activity.
The study course is characterized by the interdisciplinary nature of the acquired knowledge, tending to form the figure of a legal expert open to the international and comparative dimension of legal studies, with particular regard to the regulation of business and the market and the understanding of the new challenges brought by technological innovation to traditional ways of producing and exchanging goods and services. Participation in the design of the Study Course by a Steering Committee composed of qualified stakeholders interested in the training of this new figure of business legal expert, completely absent in traditional legal studies, will contribute to identifying forms and methods that favor the ability to apply acquired knowledge in real contexts, also through the practice of qualifying internships in companies and organizations. The analysis of practical cases is an integral part of the teaching method of the Study Course, carried out through specific seminar activities, legal clinics with the aid of external experts and stakeholders, and company testimonials. The verification of expected learning outcomes occurs through a formal evaluation of the individual involvement in the preparation and discussion of the analyzed cases.
Learning skills (learning skills)
The Master's graduate in Legal Sciences for Internationalization and Innovation of Business gradually realizes learning in each of the skills and abilities – learning to know, to do, to communicate, to form an idea of reality – in close adherence to the themes and methodologies of legal, business, economic, and social sciences disciplines provided for in the curriculum and specified in the training objectives. Through teaching activities, the graduate acquires not only notions and information, but conceptual schemes through which they are able to frame new knowledge, transfer it from one field to another, increase the capacity for self-learning or learning to learn.
The learning ability is stimulated by active research for information and documents, analysis of case studies, drafting of opinions and contractual clauses, resolution of complex legal problems by identifying applicable norms for the specific case, commenting on judgments, preparing planned interventions in seminars with experts and company witnesses, reading and analyzing company financial statements, and responding to questions aimed at verifying learning abilities.
Through professionalizing seminars and laboratories, as well as through the completion of internship periods in companies and organizations, the student has the opportunity to develop an autonomous ability to apply acquired knowledge in real situations, enhancing their learning ability. The acquisition of such abilities is verified through an analytical judgment entrusted to the company tutor in case of internship and stage, or through the teacher's evaluation regarding the degree of participation and involvement in seminar, laboratory, and legal clinic activities.
Knowledge and understanding (knowledge and understanding)
Graduates of the new Master's degree class SC-GIUR must combine in-depth knowledge in the legal field with a good mastery of economic-management and socio-institutional disciplines. They must be able to acquire advanced knowledge on international and European regulations of a general or sectoral nature, to use at least one foreign language proficiently, and to read and understand texts and documents written in English, to analyze and understand complex organizational realities in the international and transnational dimension. Specialized knowledge in the legal area must positively integrate with the understanding of economic and socio-institutional factors, as well as with a suitable mastery of business management tools and techniques, so as to be able to verify in practice the application of regulatory tools of hard law or soft law at national or international level applied to business. To the aptitude for acquiring knowledge in the international and comparative dimension, is added the ability to analyze and deepen legal issues posed by technological innovation, such as data collection and use, protection of intellectual property, personal data protection. In addition to the adoption of qualified textbooks, the student's understanding ability is stimulated by the presentation of cases, practical exercises, reasoned reading of acts and documents, role-playing games, testimonies from interlocutors focusing attention on the practical-applicative dimension of different institutions, and the argumentative presentation of theses. The verification of the degree of acquisition of an advanced level of knowledge in each course occurs in intermediate tests and exercises and in the final exam, where the student demonstrates mastery of the topics covered by answering questions on key aspects of the subject.

CdS design The new Master's Degree Course aims to address the traditional lack of an advanced legal path different from the single-cycle Master's Degree in Jurisprudence, not present at the University, offering the Bachelor's graduate of Class L-14 the opportunity to continue their studies at the same University where they obtained their Bachelor's degree. The GIUR.INN Master's Degree Course, activated by the Department of Legal and Social Sciences, aims to train a legal expert in internationalization and innovation of business who combines in-depth knowledge of the main legal issues concerning business, in its national and transnational dimension, with solid interdisciplinary competencies in economic-management areas and social and communication processes. It is a figure capable of performing general counsel functions within companies and organizations, with the ability to analyze broadly the processes of internationalization and innovation related to the use of digital technologies, interacting with all internal sectors of the company and with external consultants to prevent and resolve complex legal problems and ensure decision-making processes compliant with sectoral, national, and international regulations.
The Master's Degree Course in Legal Sciences for Internationalization and Innovation of Business is characterized by training objectives referable to the figure of the legal expert in internationalization and innovation of businesses, possessing high interdisciplinary competencies applicable in internal company services, or as an external consultant specialized in internationalization and/or innovation projects, or as a highly qualified paralegal collaborator of international law firms dealing with innovation and internationalization of business.
Description of related and complementary activities Related and complementary activities concern a modular teaching on scientific-disciplinary areas of economic and business nature not included among the characteristic sectors of the degree class, enriching the interdisciplinary knowledge and competencies acquired by the student, allowing them to reach the professional training objectives of the degree course for an international business legal expert. The specific implementation of such activities, strongly integrated with company testimonials, practical problem-solving, and guided discussions, allows the student to verify their acquired knowledge with the real problems of production and distribution sectors both at the territorial and global level. These activities provide the student with adequate knowledge to investigate specific issues of production companies, logistics, and supply chain management, introducing them to issues related to the analysis of supply and demand, production costs, and digital and technological innovation of processes, to sector concentration and structural dynamics, to supply chain and business logistics. Legal experts in business require specific skills in digital technologies; company management systems constitute the tool for processing, analyzing, and controlling certain merchandise characteristics (e.g., origin and customs classification) basic for applying customs regulations. The ability to interact with IT is therefore of fundamental importance. At the end of such training activities, the student will acquire knowledge and skills that enable them to connect economic/business and technological aspects of production, logistics, and cross-border business, and to understand the main technical-operational issues concerning production companies, logistics, and cross-border business, such as commercial development, strategic and operational planning. The student can also use the acquired knowledge and skills to understand and solve the main business and economic issues that distinguish consultancy activities for companies engaged in market globalization, internationalization, and relocation of production activities.
Brief description of the course The Master's Degree Course in Legal Sciences for Internationalization and Innovation of Businesses and Public Administrations (GIUR.INN), established within the Master's Degree Class of Legal Sciences LM SC-GIUR, as per DM 77/2018, constitutes the natural continuation and completion of the Bachelor's Degree Course in Legal Services (L-14).
The GIUR.INN Master's Degree Course, activated by the Department of Legal and Social Sciences, aims to train a legal expert with solid knowledge on issues concerning the internationalization and innovation of businesses and public administrations, who combines in-depth knowledge of the main legal issues concerning business and public administration in the national and transnational context with solid interdisciplinary competencies in economic-management areas. It is a figure capable of performing general counsel functions within companies, organizations, and public administrations, with the ability to analyze broadly the processes of internationalization and innovation related to the use of digital technologies, interacting with all internal sectors and with external consultants to prevent and resolve complex legal problems and ensure decision-making processes compliant with sectoral, national, European, and international regulations.
Starting from the academic year 2024-25, the CdS provides an 'international path' activated together with the Université de Rouen Normandie (URN) Faculté de Droit, aimed at enabling students enrolled in this path to obtain a double degree in Legal Sciences and Master 2 in Droit International, conditioned on the outcome of a semester of study abroad at URN and the positive achievement of the profit exams required by the study plan for 30 CFU out of the 120 required by the Master's degree.
External effectiveness The Almalaurea 2022 data report an employment rate of Master's graduates of the SC_GIUR class of 90.5% with an average monthly net salary of 1362 EURO. The data, although referring to a relatively small cohort, as graduates of the Master's degree class represent a still small number (a little over a hundred, in the 14 university sites where the class has been activated, of which 8 in Uda between 2021 and 2022 calendar year), is very significant as it demonstrates the usefulness of the differentiation from the single-cycle Master's Degree in Jurisprudence and its direct professionalizing vocation, which finds positive confirmation in the employment data one year after obtaining the degree. The gender composition data of graduates also finds confirmation in Giurinn data, with a majority of Women compared to Men, as well as regarding the degree grade, which is very high among our graduates: 7 out of 8 graduated with the maximum grade (110 and honors), only 1 with a grade between 105 and 110.
As far as direct contact with our graduates is concerned, almost all have found work shortly after obtaining their degree.
Specific training objectives of the course and description of the training path The Master's Degree Course in Legal Sciences for Internationalization and Innovation of Business is characterized by training objectives referable to the figure of the legal expert in internationalization and innovation of businesses, possessing high interdisciplinary competencies applicable in internal company services, or as an external consultant specialized in internationalization and/or innovation projects, or as a highly qualified paralegal collaborator of international law firms dealing with innovation and internationalization of business.
The training path aims to provide advanced legal knowledge to understand global investment market dynamics and business development strategies through the use of new technologies through an interdisciplinary path whose training activities are traceable to the following four learning areas, identified based on criteria of scientific-disciplinary homogeneity:
- Legal Area
- Business Area
- Economic Area
- Social Sciences Area Within the first two learning areas, the training path provides mandatory and optional courses; in the other two areas, it provides optional courses or included in the student's choice of courses consistent with the training path. The path gradually introduces courses and seminar activities in English to acquire the international specialist technical language; professionalizing seminars, stages, and training internships at companies, national and international organizations, and professional studios; as well as case design, research, or analysis activities that stimulate the ability to operate in complex situations using interdisciplinary tools.
At the end of studies, the Master's graduate in Legal Sciences for Internationalization and Innovation of Business:
- is able to assist the company in negotiating international investment contracts and in relocation and personnel management and industrial relations practices;
- is able to carry out administrative procedures related to international trade, import-export, including customs deposit and VAT tax deposit;
- is able to draft and interpret international contracts and manage their execution, resolve commercial disputes through international arbitration and ADR forms, interpret and apply internal and European regulations in company law and competition;
- is able to interpret and resolve legal issues related to the information society, particularly e-commerce, privacy protection, and data bank management;
- is able to register trademarks and patents and use innovation forms related to the functioning of business networks and technological clusters and manage digital marketing;
- is able to present, implement, and account for international and European funding projects in the fields of new technologies, environment, and sustainable development, transport, and infrastructure;
- is capable of negotiating and implementing transnational collective agreements and models of corporate social responsibility in global supply chains;
- is able to manage private and public tender procedures, national and international, and verify the adequacy of adopted organizational models with particular regard to transparency, anti-corruption, and the emergence of criminal liability;
- possesses communication skills that allow interaction with different company sectors and to interact with external professionals, commercial partners, and national and international institutions.
Opinions of companies and organizations with stage/internship agreements or extra-curricular internships The data collected by the SEAGS School shows a number of CdS students who have carried out curricular or extra-curricular internship activities equal to 13, doubling compared to last year (6). All students have completed the 8 CFU required by the study course in companies/professional studios for at least 200 hours of activity: in 4 cases, the internship was extended up to 296 hours, in one case to 241 hours, in two other cases to a number of hours slightly above 200. In some cases, the host companies were contacted directly by the teacher to whom the student turned to request the thesis (in at least 3 cases), while in other cases it involves companies that have a convention with the SEAGS School. It should be noted that not always companies dealing with issues related to internationalization and innovation were found, therefore in line with the specific training of the course: some requests to carry out activities related to internationalization and innovation of businesses were not satisfied due to the difficulty of identifying companies actually interested in this specific profile in the Abruzzo region. This criticality will need to be discussed in the Steering Committee with stakeholders, whose presence will be increased. The availability to offer internship and training opportunities must focus on companies/entities that have a real interest in issues concerning internationalization and innovation, to give students real opportunities to apply knowledge/skills acquired in the CdS.
From the evaluations made by the 13 host companies/professional studios, belonging to the private sector (only in one case a public company) and engaged in the area of trade, transport, logistics, or carrying out consultancy, training, and administrative activities, the university preparation of the interns was considered adequate for business/professional needs, with full achievement of the set goals, and in one case with a job offer to the intern. The competencies acquired during the internship mainly concerned technical, IT, and management skills. All host entities expressed a high degree of appreciation for the activities carried out by students, reliability, ability to work in groups, problem solving, and no criticalities were reported.
It should also be noted that teachers of the CdS organize professionalizing seminars, guided company visits, and company testimonials, for which CFU letter f) are recognized, as provided for in the training path.
Some Giurinn students participated in 2022 in the Innovation Hackaton organized by Confindustria where, in small groups with students from other Universities and other courses, they tackled - with excellent results - complex business issues concerning internationalization, foreign investments, and innovation.
All contact activities with the business world and professions are informed to students, particularly in the second year, through the thorough orientation activities carried out by individual teachers and tutors, as well as through the CdS and School website and information disseminated on social media. In particular, many participated in the Impresa in Accademia meetings and Career Day, where they had the opportunity to meet company managers, improve their curriculum presentation methods, and obtain information on job opportunities.
The collection and processing of opinions from companies and entities receiving students in internships is carried out by the SEAGS School through the administration of a structured questionnaire (PDF attached), as well as through a discussion to be held at the CdS Steering Committee meeting, where representatives of interested parties are present.
