Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding (applying knowledge and understanding)
The interdisciplinary strategy programmed and the subsequent credit distribution, practical internships, and experimental thesis contribute to forming master's graduates capable of addressing and solving innovative problems.
Practical internships at partner facilities and experimental theses will be planned, organized, and evaluated based on acquiring necessary training for understanding practical problems within recent dynamics in the sector, and in line with professional opportunities of the class:
- Evaluation of quality characteristics and evolving dynamics related to technological and biotechnological processes in food;
- Evaluation of bioavailability and biomolecular mechanisms, in vivo and in vitro, of nutrients, dietary supplements, and nutraceuticals;
- Collaboration in investigations related to food habits and consumption patterns and morbidity factors;
- Evaluation of nutritional status and body composition in relation to nutrient, dietary supplement, novel food, and nutraceutical use, in adults and pediatric age, as well as in sports activities;
- Evaluation of pharmacological properties of nutrients, dietary supplements, novel foods, and nutraceuticals used in prevention and therapy of various diseases, in adults and pediatric age;
- Consultancy in the agri-food system, including certification procedures for production processes and products (international safety standards);
- Participation in training, education, and dissemination activities on food quality, safety, and wholesomeness.
Acquisition of the described competencies will be verified through:
- Reports on laboratory and classroom exercises;
- Ability to analyze, present, and discuss scientific literature data;
- Written theoretical exams (open questions and multiple-choice) and oral exams (ability to address and solve problems through discussion).
Finally, the following will be verified:
- Activities and methods related to thesis preparation and writing;
- Discussion of scientific results presented to the Course Commission.
Learning Skills (learning skills)
Master's graduates in Nutrition and Health must possess learning abilities based on the educational path undertaken and continuous updating through consultation of scientific literature, especially through sector databases.
Learning is guaranteed by the availability of reference texts and materials in Italian and foreign languages for various curricular disciplines. Further in-depth learning will be provided through seminars with renowned professors and professionals from the sector.
To improve learning abilities, specialized visits, internships, and ad hoc meetings will be organized at facilities, laboratories, public and private structures in the sector, especially in the reference territory. These opportunities are planned based on concrete knowledge of Mediterranean productions of interest to the territory and related nutritional and health issues.
Master's graduates in Nutrition and Health must demonstrate such learning abilities through evaluations of disciplines taught (with written and oral exams, reports) and through the final exam.
University Communication to CUN The requested modification to the Educational Ordinance concerns access to the SAS course for students from Bachelor's programs (or equivalent foreign degrees) not on direct access, provided they hold 60 CFU (currently distributed among: FIS/07, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/02; CHIM/01, CHIM/03, CHIM/06; AGR/13; INF/01; MED/42, MED/49; IUS/01, BIO/09, BIO/13, BIO/10, BIO/14, BIO/16, BIO/19),
to which the following sectors are added:
AGR/15, CHIM/10, CHIM/09, MED/07, and MED/44.
Additionally, the activation of SSD among the specific characterizing educational activities for class LM61 is requested, such as: BIO/11 in biomedical disciplines and M-PSI/01 and MED/13 in human nutrition disciplines.
Knowledge and Understanding (knowledge and understanding)
The Study Course is structured based on interdisciplinary integrated courses.
The didactic programming aims at an integrated approach to issues related to food quality and safety, human nutrition and clinical nutrition, and the role of functional foods, novel foods, and nutraceuticals as per European Regulation.
It also aims to ensure acquisition of new analytical techniques and evaluation methods for processes and products, with particular reference to nutritional safety and quality of food and in the field of disease prevention.
Students must be able to correlate content from different reference areas, acquiring innovative interdisciplinary knowledge on topics:
- Food quality (nutritional, hygienic-sanitary, sensory) and production processes in the agri-food system;
- Topics covered during nutrition-focused courses;
- Topics specific to biomedical disciplines.
These abilities are acquired through frontal lectures and classroom/laboratory exercises, and through internships. Verification methods include classic oral interviews, possibly preceded by written reports, and/or unknown laboratory tests, as well as reports and/or internship reports.
University Organizational Structure and Responsibilities The organizational structure and responsibilities at the university level are available in full at the link:
https://pqa.unich.it/pqa/struttura-organizzativa-e-responsabilita-livello-di-ateneo
Organization and Responsibilities of Quality Assurance at the Course Level Quality assurance for the Course is organized in a Quality Assurance Group (GAQ) composed of:
Prof. Luca FEDERICI, Head Prof. Ester VITACOLONNA, Member Dr. Chiara CUCCURULLO, Member
The Head of Quality Assurance for the Course:
- Coordinates the group's activities and supervises the implementation of Quality Assurance within the Course;
- Periodically updates the Course Council on Quality Assurance activities and results;
- Maintains relations with the University Quality Assurance Body, the Evaluation Committee, and the Parity Committee of professors and students, supported by the student representative Dr. Simone Pillitteri.
The GAQ, in addition, is required to:
- Supervise the implementation of Quality Assurance within the Course;
- Monitor indicators for continuous process control and improvement;
- Plan and control the efficiency of contextual services.
The GAQ also conducts monitoring and self-assessment of the educational path to identify strengths and weaknesses of the Course. These activities are directed at planning corrective and preventive actions for criticalities and implementing improvement plans to propose to the Course Council.
The liaison figure with the Department as the Departmental Quality Assurance Representative (ReAQD) is Prof. Gabriella Mincione.
Planning of Work and Implementation Deadlines The Course is framed within the School of Medicine and the DTIMO Department, to which most course professors belong.
Therefore, course responsibility is managed in a way and at times appropriate, considering student needs and intervening promptly for student needs, with the parity delegate and all professors maintaining daily and constructive dialogue with students.
The Course follows a constant update of programs related to different courses and a careful monitoring of laboratory and internship training activities. Specifically for internships, a mutual satisfaction questionnaire from student to company and company to student is being implemented for adequate internship monitoring.
The Course has certainly planned to expand the enrollment of international students, setting the goal of recruiting a few units in the 2024-2025 cohort.
Additionally, the Course has planned to establish agreements with foreign institutions and companies for student internships abroad. The goal is to have at least one for the next academic year.
The Course has also planned to increase agreements with foreign universities and promote the possibility of taking courses and exams abroad.
Brief Description of Related and Complementary Activities Related and complementary activities are developed in modular courses that deepen nutrition and food topics in relation to the specific educational goals of the course, allowing completion of educational and cultural differences of students in relation to acquired competencies.
The proposed training activities aim to develop the following transversal competencies:
- Basic chemical and biochemical foundations of nutrition sciences (structure, function, nutritional value of macronutrients, vitamins, and minerals) together with digestion and nutrient absorption mechanisms and main metabolic pathways for energy extraction from nutrients.
- In-depth analysis of chemical-physical and microbiological food analysis for risk assessment (chemical and biological contaminants) (BIO 14) and in-depth knowledge of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of substances in food and/or health products (e.g., supplements, functional foods, nutraceuticals), used also in prevention and therapy of diseases, in adults and pediatric age.
- Knowledge of typical food resources with strong territorial connotation and the nutritional and health value of plants characterizing the Mediterranean diet.
- Competencies related to nutrition and physical-sports activity.
- Knowledge of the development, anatomy of the oral cavity, and its functioning (mastication and swallowing) with basic concepts of dental hygiene and nutrition related to oral health.
- Competencies on the basic mechanisms of immune-mediated toxic and allergic reactions caused by food, symptoms, associated pathologies, and main diagnostic tools available.
Brief Course Description The premises leading to the establishment of the Master's Degree in Nutrition and Health at G. D'Annunzio University of Chieti-Pescara, with its cultural and professional aspects, stem from increasingly evident and shared scientific findings establishing significant correlations between food quality, health, and well-being. Understanding these interrelationships first requires innovative, multidisciplinary approaches that allow research and teaching 'along the chain' from agricultural production and transformation sectors, often controlling environmental variables, to the food product with evaluation of multiple nutritional and medical implications.
This strategic approach, fundamentally aimed at sharing both research and teaching a multidisciplinary and multisectoral programming, was the basis for evaluating resources and interest both within the University and outside in the reference geographical area. Regarding the first point, having identified the organizing committee for useful synergies between teachers from different Departments, in some cases historically proven and positive between closely related scientific areas (technological and pharmaceutical, nutrition, health), it was possible to recognize significant potential for the initiative of a Master's Course with such content, which naturally complements the training of Dietetics graduates, whose need is to complete their three-year path with specialized training. In line with the educational offer but outside, in the area where D'Annunzio is located, it is noted that no Bachelor's program in Class LM 61 is active in regions bordering the central Adriatic coast – Marche, Emilia Romagna, Veneto, Friuli – practically north of Abruzzo Region; this circumstance allows anticipating attractiveness for three-year graduates with competencies in different bio-technological areas, as indicated in the entry requirements. Ultimately, the goal is to form a marked specialization in nutrition and disease prevention sectors, especially in particular areas such as pediatric, sports, and geriatric.
Regarding the socio-economic and social context in the Abruzzo Region and neighboring regions (mainly Molise, Marche, and Northern Puglia), agri-food chains represent an important and driving productive sector, widespread throughout the territory, and consultation revealed strong interest in such professional figures, with new professional opportunities in production and control, commercialization, and catering, for a health-oriented characterization of traditional Mediterranean foods, alongside specific competencies applicable in Institutions and/or Local Public Bodies.
External Effectiveness The number of graduates was 25 (16% male and 84% female), of whom 17 were interviewed. Of these, 7 work full-time and 2 part-time.
However, it must be specified that at graduation, there were 9 students, all of whom responded to the interview, already working, of whom 7 full-time and 2 part-time. Thus, new workers after graduation might be only 2.
Nevertheless, regarding employment data, there are few indications since the first graduates of the 2018-2019 cohort are few and not all responded to the interview, so real data for time to enter the labor market at one year and three years should be monitored in future years.
It is recalled that employed individuals (considered employed all those who declare to carry out any activity, even training or irregular, provided it is paid) who use the competencies acquired with the degree are 33.3% at one year with a monthly net salary of €1,042 in the first year. Job satisfaction is approximately 7 (on a scale from 1 to 10).
Specific Educational Objectives and Course Description Graduates of the Master's Degree in Nutrition and Health must acquire a solid scientific foundation on food and nutrition. In particular, graduates must be able to evaluate: the properties of nutrients and xenobiotics in food and any modifications during technological processes (primary, transformation, and commercialization phases), also for interventions to maintain health conditions and prevent related diseases; the biochemical and physiological mechanisms of digestion and absorption and metabolic processes of nutrients.
The Study Course must provide:
- Knowledge of chemical and structural characteristics: a) of food, with particular reference to intrinsic quality (nutritional, hygienic-sanitary, chemical-physical, and sensory); b) of dietary products, supplements, and functional foods, approved and used for their health benefits;
- Knowledge of correlations between diet and pathogenesis of digestive, endocrine-metabolic, and neurodegenerative diseases;
- Methodological foundations of research in the field of applied food science;
- Knowledge of the pharmacological activity of nutrients, dietary supplements, and nutraceuticals in prevention and therapy of diseases, in adults and pediatric age;
- Knowledge of the pharmacological activity of nutrients, dietary supplements, and nutraceuticals used in sports;
- Knowledge of potentially toxic substances in food, including additives, pesticides, and environmental and veterinary drug residues;
- Basic knowledge of general plant biology and horticulture in the diet.
Specific Course Objectives provide:
- Tools for correct evaluation of body composition and nutritional status, also in relation to food products considering different geographical and socioeconomic variables;
- Necessary knowledge to define energy intake and nutritional qualities of individual foods and their basic composition, and factors regulating bioavailability of macronutrients and micronutrients, in adults and pediatric age;
- Knowledge of the role of nutrients, dietary supplements, and nutraceuticals in physical activity and sports;
- Knowledge of techniques for monitoring food consumption and nutritional surveillance protocols for individuals or populations in specific physiological conditions (pregnancy, lactation, childhood, aging, etc.) or with specific lifestyles;
- Adequate scientific and technological competencies for formulation, evaluation, and control of new functional foods (novel food, functional food);
- In-depth knowledge of food safety issues, in terms of hygienic-sanitary characteristics of food;
- Knowledge of national and EU food and health legislation regarding commercialization and control of food, from production to consumption, ingredients, additives, and dietary supplements;
- Knowledge of correlations between nutrients, dietary supplements, and nutraceuticals with disease pathogenesis, in adults and pediatric age, with particular reference to modulation of genetic/proteomic profile and cellular metabolism;
- Knowledge of the pharmacological properties of nutrients, dietary supplements, and nutraceuticals used in prevention and therapy of diseases, in adults and pediatric age;
- Knowledge of the possible role of natural and industrial pollutants in food in disease pathogenesis, in adults and pediatric age;
- Knowledge of the role probiotic microorganisms play in regulating intestinal homeostasis and basal metabolism for maintaining health status;
- Knowledge of main factors controlling microbial development in food and classical and molecular methodologies for microbiological analysis;
- Knowledge of main relationships between diet and digestive tract pathologies, with particular reference to etiopathogenetic mechanisms and interaction between eating habits and intestinal microbiota composition, in adults and pediatric age.
- Basic knowledge and competencies related to clinical psychology, clinical psychological assessment, and reactions to illness specifically related to eating and nutrition disorders.
- Knowledge of endocrine pathophysiology with particular attention to endocrine-metabolic pathologies.
Graduates will also be able to use English, in written and oral form.
Students will address, through a series of integrated courses with an interdisciplinary approach, knowledge in the disciplines characterizing most three-year degrees.
In this way, consolidation of previous preparation will be ensured, providing specific content characterizing this master's degree class.
Topics regarding nutrition biochemistry will be addressed with particular attention to technological aspects related to components, residues, and additives in food, and metabolic aspects in both physiological and pathological conditions.
Additionally, students must learn the principles of human nutrition physiology useful for interpreting different eating behaviors, in adults and pediatric age; they must also learn basic knowledge on absorption, bioavailability, and biomolecular mechanisms of nutrients, dietary supplements, and nutraceuticals, used as drugs in prevention and therapy of various pathological conditions.
Finally, students must know and detect microbial alterations in preserved and industrially produced food, risks related to allergens and additives, hygienic-organizational characteristics of community nutrition and catering.
Internship activities, in line with the Ministerial declaration, will be integrated with the performance of internships at public and private companies regarding functional foods, dietary supplements, novel foods, and foods considered useful for disease prevention.
The educational path includes theoretical activities that form the basis of acquiring fundamental knowledge in the complex relationships between food quality and health and disease prevention. The path includes the study of food in terms of technologies and objective quality (chemical-physical, nutritional, hygienic-sanitary, and sensory), nutrition, and health status.
The educational activity integrates the planned courses in a multidisciplinary strategy, with different teaching forms and methods: frontal lectures, laboratory exercises, seminars, visits to food sector facilities (production and control) and health facilities for data collection and analysis (consumption, nutritional, epidemiological).
Learning outcomes verification is carried out through written and oral exams, discussion of essays, and reports to verify expected learning outcomes in line with European study title descriptors.
The educational path of the Master's Degree in Nutrition and Health includes 54-79 CFU as characterizing educational activities, divided into 15-24 CFU in Biomedical Disciplines; 24-30 CFU in Human Nutrition Disciplines; 15-25 CFU in Food Characterization and Agri-Food System Management Disciplines. The educational path also includes related and complementary activities for 12-24 CFU, further deepening advanced knowledge of specific food and nutrition topics. Student choice activities for 8 CFU complete knowledge and competencies in socio-economic and psychological areas. 15 CFU are allocated for the thesis, experimental in nature, either at the University research laboratories or at Research Institutes or Public/Private Companies cooperating in the food and human nutrition sector.
The first-year educational path is characterized by acquiring basic knowledge in Biomedical Disciplines, with particular reference to general biology, biochemistry, physiology, and microbiology; in Human Nutrition Disciplines and those characterizing food, aspects related to hygiene, food education, dietetics, and food technology and composition will be addressed. The educational offer will be completed with part of the student choice activities and internship.
The second-year educational path is characterized by acquiring knowledge in Human Nutrition Disciplines aimed at deepening the role of nutrition and food products in preventing and treating major diseases, cardiovascular, metabolic, and gastroenterological, in both adult and pediatric age and in sports, as well as the pharmacological properties of nutrients and dietary supplements.
The educational offer is completed with the English language course, part of the student choice activities, and internship activities.
Graduate and Company Opinions on Internships and Internship Agreements The number of internships carried out by enrolled students from the 2018-2019 academic year to 2022-2023 is reported. In the 2018-2019 academic year, 41 internships were completed out of 46 possible (85%), in 2019-2020 35 out of 48 (73%), and in 2020-2021 only 22 out of 57 (39%). This decreasing trend should be monitored, possibly still an effect of the pandemic, in which case we should recover in the coming years, or it might conceal a structural deficiency requiring correction. However, the latter hypothesis is less likely as we have signed a significant number of agreements with local and even non-regional companies, so we are confident that the availability of internship facilities is ample.
Regarding the types of agreements, we have hotels, laboratories, nutraceutical companies, ASL, care homes, other universities, nutritionists/dietitians, agri-food companies, and University laboratories. From the 2018-2019 academic year to the current year, the number of agreements has increased, adding 38, 39, 22, and 6 in the last academic year. Most agreements concern both University laboratories and nutritionist laboratories, which provide approximately 40-50% of available positions.
We recall that starting from the COVID-19 emergency, a channel on the Microsoft Teams platform dedicated to internship initiatives was created in addition to existing agreements, and students who began in this way could either complete remotely or switch to in-person, depending on the host company's availability.
Students complete a report or questionnaire detailing the activities carried out and self-assess the quality of the experience.
First and second-year internships are possible at the following University laboratories available to host students:
- Functional Assessment Laboratory (Prof. Pietrangelo) - at UDA
- Microbiology Laboratory (Prof. Cellini) - at UDA
- Clinical Nutrition Laboratory (Prof. Vitacolonna) - at O.C. SS. Annunziata
- Biochemistry Laboratory (Prof. Pieragostino) - at UDA
- Body Composition and Sports Medicine Nutrition Support Laboratory (Prof. Ripari/Tripodi) - at UDA
- ex CIAPI
We recall that student training internships are provided at companies, hospitals, and local and national food companies to acquire complementary credits, as well as attendance for thesis preparation. In recent years, the availability of sector companies, regional and non-regional, has increased with numerous new agreements for experimental thesis work.
Students complete a report or questionnaire detailing the activities carried out and self-assess the quality of the experience. Companies provide feedback on the student's performance.
Summary of Regional Coordination Committee Opinion In the meeting on January 9, 2018, via teleconference, the Regional Coordination Committee of Abruzzo Universities convened. During the meeting, the President informed the members that G. d'Annunzio University of Chieti-Pescara had requested the Regional Committee to express the mandatory opinion required for activating new Study Courses. Specifically, the request relates to establishing the new Master's Degree in Nutrition and Health (LM/61).
All members unanimously agreed to approve the establishment of the Master's Degree in Nutrition and Health (LM/61).
Consultation with Representative Organizations - at National and International Levels - of Goods and Services Production, Professions (Course Establishment)
Consultation with representative organizations at the local level for production, services, and professions was initiated during 2017 by the Organizing Committee. Specifically, the following were consulted:
- Leading agri-food companies: (De Cecco SpA, Pizzoli SpA, Pastificio Cocco, Rustichella d'Abruzzo, Citra Vini, Oleificio Capo, Oleificio La Casolana, SoGeDa, Tenuta Secolo IX, SOL & PHARMA);
- Professional organizations and associations (Confindustria Chieti-Pescara, Coldiretti Regional, Celiac and Diabetic Associations, CIA - Italian Confederation of Agriculture);
- Public Institutions (Regional Health Department, Regional Agriculture Department, Regional Public Works, Urban Planning, and Special Territorial Projects Department, ASL Chieti and Pescara, IQRF - Food Quality and Fraud Repression Inspectorate of the Ministry of Agricultural Policies, INAIL, Carabinieri Command for Forest, Environmental, and Agri-Food Protection, Pescara Province, ARTA Abruzzo - Regional Environmental Protection Agency, Secondary School Institutes, AGIRE Pole - AGroIndustry Research Ecosustainability, manager of the Abruzzo Agri-Food Innovation Pole, IT.QSA - Consortium for Research, Innovation, Technology, Quality, and Safety of Food, College of Agricultural Engineers and Graduates in Agriculture, Abruzzo Foundation for Life Sciences, UNASA – National Union of Academies of Agricultural Sciences).
Organizations were consulted primarily via teleconference (Skype meetings, emails), and at the end of the meetings, questionnaires containing questions about the professional figures the course aims to train and the knowledge and competencies it proposes to impart to students were administered (Attachment 1 to the project document).
From an initial analysis of the responses received, all interviewed subjects believe the name clearly communicates the course's purpose and that the professional figures it aims to train respond to the needs of the sector or productive area represented by the interviewed subject. Regarding the expected learning outcomes in different learning areas, subjects express full alignment with the project, particularly regarding the area of food characterization and agri-food system management.
Suggestions emerging from the consultations were considered during the planning phase, specifically:
- The need to deepen the characterization of Mediterranean productions of regional interest from a health perspective, both to translate empirical knowledge of typical and sustainable productions into technical-scientific terms and to increase the qualified employment potential of small and medium enterprises in the reference area (expressed by Regional Departments, Secondary Schools, and some companies, as well as INAIL);
- The need to offer significant knowledge of production and transformation of agri-food products with a mixed training approach, also in synergy with local realities (such as Biocampus, Innovative School, funded by MIUR and other universities in the territory) (indicated by UNASA, POLO AGIRE, Regional Department for Special Projects);
- Emphasis on internationalization (highlighted by UNASA, SOL & PHARMA);
- Proposed content: knowledge of new certification schemes and standards related to food safety and microbiology issues (suggested by Pizzoli, Rustichella d'Abruzzo).
The high approval of the initiative suggested the formation of a Steering Committee with members including not only internal university representatives but also delegates from the production world, public institutions, and consumers.
Finally, the following documents and sector studies were consulted to support the Course planning:
- 'Global Burden of Disease Study 2010' (WHO);
- 'European Food and Nutrition Action Plan 2015-2020';
- FAO- CIHEAM 2017 'Development of voluntary guidelines for the sustainability of the Mediterranean diet in the Mediterranean region';
- Documents and studies at: www.efsa.europa.eu/it - www.salute.gov.it - www.politicheagricole.it - www.crea.gov.it
In the context of adapting the course to new requests from interested parties, regularly consulted, the educational offer was proposed for revision through a revision of the educational ordinance.
Representatives were consulted who reported student requests to streamline enrollment requirements from Bachelor's programs other than those listed for direct access, subject to holding at least 60 CFU.
The three-year course L29, Eco-Sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology (TESTA), at UdA, was identified as a stakeholder based on a request from the course president, following the collection of opinions from graduates of that course, who are very interested in the master's opportunity offered by Nutrition and Health (SAS). In fact, TESTA students face difficulties accessing SAS with 60 CFU, despite having a three-year training whose master's outcome aligns well with SAS course goals.
Consultations with local representative organizations, conducted during the post-pandemic period, also in relation to internships carried out by first and second-year students at local companies, motivated the reformulation of the educational offer to respond primarily to the needs of the local productive force. In fact, agri-food companies and professional activities related to dietetics and nutrition are those most frequently chosen by our students for internships, and thus those that regularly present their needs in terms of expected professional competencies and knowledge.
On October 2, 2023, at 5:30 PM, in mixed mode (online and in-person), consultations were held with the following organizations/professional orders and the business world (stakeholders):
• SALPA - Abruzzo Food Products Processing Society
• Abruzzo Food Technologists Association
• Abruzzo Lazio Biologists Association
• Coldiretti Abruzzo
• Tenute Talamonti
• Biogroup S.p.A. Benefit Company
• Steering Committee Member
• Three-Year Course in Eco-Sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology (T.E.S.T.A.)
For the SAS Course, the following were present:
• SAS Course President
• SAS Course Vice President
• Teaching Coordinator
• Internship Coordinator
• Student representatives from the first and second year
The SAS Course President clarified to the parties that the purpose of the meeting is to evaluate the current educational offer, receive requests from stakeholders that have been presented in the short and long term, with the aim of updating the educational offer in response to their needs and those of students.
Briefly, below is an excerpt of the contributions from the representatives who attended the consultation, fully described in the attached minutes.
The Vice President of OTA Abruzzo emphasized the importance of the Course and its educational path, including internships, characterized by competencies and knowledge highly interesting to the business world.
Talamonti and SALPA companies suggest implementing competencies in food legislation, marketing, and corporate communication in European and extra-CEE contexts, hygiene knowledge, mandatory certifications, voluntary certifications, and valorization of production waste in a sustainability and circular economy perspective.
Biogroup Company considers it important to implement knowledge related to medicinal plants, extracts derived from them, and metabolic interactions, highlighting the complexity of plant extract pharmacology.
The President of the Lazio Abruzzo Biologists Association considers it important to adjust the educational offer towards topics and themes of great impact for industrial realities such as legislation, food certifications, and marketing.
From Coldiretti Abruzzo, a reformulation of the educational offer, including internships, is necessary to reduce the gap with the constantly growing and renewing productive sector.
Student representatives agree with what was reported by companies, stressing the importance of continuous updating of training to meet the needs of the productive sector.
The SAS Course President informed that requests were also received via email from Pastificio Cocco, INAIL, and a member of the SAS Course Steering Committee, who agree with the requests expressed during the consultation.
Therefore, based on the consultation results, the proposed ordinance modifications include:
- Insertion of new disciplines among the SSD required for non-direct access, contributing to achieving the educational objectives of the SAS course regarding knowledge of production and formulation processes in the context of food integration, prebiotic and probiotic formulations, deepening of topics related to safety and health, sustainability, food waste, and quality evaluation of food.
- Activation of SSD among the specific characterizing educational activities for class LM61, such as: BIO/11, M-PSI/01, and MED/13.
Consultation with Representative Organizations - at National and International Levels - of Goods and Services Production, Professions (Subsequent Consultations)
During 2019, the Course, in addition to expanding the list of consultations by adding numerous private sector companies and public institutions, formalized the establishment of a Steering Committee composed of:
- Course Coordinator
- Managing Director of the Abruzzo Agri-Food Innovation Pole
- Regional Coordinator of the Biologists Association
- President of the National Union of Academies Applied to Agricultural Development, Food Safety, and Environmental Protection.
During 2020, despite pandemic-related limitations, the course continued the consultation process with organizations at the local level, production, services, and professions, providing the following suggestions:
- Implementation of the Course with new disciplines (e.g., production techniques, food technology, healthy nutrition, elements of food resource policy) (22%)
- In-depth on food safety, microbiological aspects, and prevention (22%)
- Attention to communication, international trade, and network approach (e-commerce) (17%)
- Valorization of local productions (17%)
- Integration with other degree courses and particular attention to internationalization of the new course with the establishment of courses in English (11%)
- In-depth with laboratory and/or training internship activities (11%)
The Steering Committee met twice from the start of the 2021-2022 academic year.

The participation of the two members, Mr. Donatantonio De Falcis, former ARSA Director, and Mr. Filareto Antonio, former President of the Abruzzo Biologists Association, was confirmed.

Entry, Path, and Exit Data Entry 2022-2023
Entry Data The enrolled students were 39, of which 10 pure, for a total of 94, of which 80 in course, 14 out of course, and 80 regular.
Enrolled students decreased compared to the previous year, which had 53 (12 pure, for a total of 132, of which 104 in course, 28 out of course, and 103 regular).
Cohort Trend
54 enrolled in 2021, decreased to 39 in 2022. None left or transferred out or reactivated. There were 7 suspensions and 8 non-renewed enrollments.
The average number of exams passed per student was 5.15 in 2021 and 3.28 in 2022.
The percentage of acquired CFU out of required CFU was 56.3% in 2021 and 44.3% in 2022.
Exit Data Of the 44 who graduated, 31 were in course, 10 were one year out of course, and 3 with two years out of course.
Grade range 110 and honors: 17, of which 12 in course and 4 with one year out of course.
110: 4, of which 1 in course, 2 with over one year out of course, and 1 with two years out of course.
105-110: 19, of which 15 with over one year out of course.
105: 4, of which 3 in course and 1 with one year out of course.
------
Entry 2021-2022
53 students were enrolled, of which 12 pure. Total students: 132.
Of these, 104 are in course and 103 regular, 28 out of course.
Exit data indicate that the 25 graduates achieved a grade of 110 and honors in 13, 110 in 4, between 105-110 in 2, and 105 in 6. Of the total, 21 were in course, 3 were one year out of course, and only 1 over two years out of course. Of the graduates with 110 and honors, the majority (11) were in course, and only 2 were one year out of course.
Data on cohort trend as of August 23, 2022, indicate that in the 20-21 academic year, 67 students enrolled, of which 13 withdrew and 4 did not renew enrollment, leaving a cohort of 50 students. Each of these on average passed 5.01 exams in 2020 and 4.04 in 2021, acquiring 54.9% CFU in 2020 and 52.8% CFU in 2021. Note that the 2021 values are partial as the 21-22 academic year is not yet concluded.
Entry 2020-2021
66 regular students were enrolled, of which 19 pure, for a total of 130.
Of these, 112 are in course and regular, 18 out of course.
Regarding geographical origin, students come from:
- The same municipality as the University: 8, of which 3 pure (similar to the previous year);
- Other municipalities in the Province: 22, of which 2 pure (similar to the previous year);
- Other Provinces in the Region: 13, of which 3 pure (similar to the previous year);
- Other Regions: 23, of which 11 pure (increased compared to the previous year).
Statistical data show that enrolled students by diploma type are distributed as follows:
- From High Schools: 46, of which 12 pure;
- From Technical Institutes: 5, of which 4 pure;
- From Professional Institutes: 6, of which 1 pure;
- From Magistrali: 6, of which 1 pure;
- From other types: 4, of which 1 pure.
Regarding diploma grades:
- Students with grade 100 and honors: 1 (0 pure);
- Students with grade 100: 8, of which 2 pure;
- Students with grade between 80-99: 32, of which 7 pure;
- Students with grade up to 80: 25, of which 10 pure;
- Grade not defined: 1 (0 pure).
----------------------
Regarding the analysis of the study path for the 2019-2020 academic year, particularly the transition from the first to the second year of the Course, the following data are noted:
- Percentage of continuation in the same course to the second year: 72%;
- Percentage of continuation in the same course to the second year with more than 40 CFU: 38.24%;
- Percentage of inactive cohort members (CFU <= 20% of required CFU): 29.41%;
- Percentage of cohort members with 0 CFU acquired: 22.06%;
- Percentage of CFU acquired / CFU to be taken: 50.00%.
It should be noted that non-attending students account for 43.3%.
This analysis highlights a good result, with a high percentage of students passing to the second year (72%), not reaching 100% probably because a significant portion of non-attending students are working students who can dedicate less time to study than attending students.
Exit Data: Of the 15 graduates, 8 received 110 and honors, 2 received 110, 4 received a grade between 105-110, and 1 graduated with 105, all in course.
The cohort trend for the 2019 year (enrollment year 2019 and 2020) saw 53 enrolled in 2019 and 45 in 2020. Among the 2019 enrollees, 4 out of 53 students withdrew and did not renew enrollment.
The average number of exams passed per student among 2019 enrollees was 5.53 with 58.3% of CFU acquired out of required CFU.
The average number of exams passed per student among 2020 enrollees was 1.82 with 26.8% of CFU acquired out of required CFU.
Final Exam Characteristics The final exam consists of a public discussion in front of a committee of professors of an original experimental research activity report.
The graduation exam takes place in the sessions indicated by the Course's Didactic Regulation.
The composition of the Graduation Committee complies with Article 6 of DPR 2/1/2001.
Final Exam Execution Method To be admitted to the final exam, which entails acquiring 15 CFU, the student must:
- Acquire all educational credits related to passing exams, including 8 CFU of autonomous choice and CFU related to other educational activities.
The final exam consists of discussing a written report structured according to the lines of a scientific publication, written by the student under the supervision of the thesis advisor, in front of a Committee. The candidate presents and discusses their thesis, highlighting the state of the art of the topic addressed, the purpose of the work, the procedures used, the results obtained, and the conclusions drawn. The thesis can be written in English and the final exam can be conducted in the same language. The final grade is expressed in hundredths.
For the final exam, students may take exams or carry out research activities for thesis preparation at foreign universities within the 'LLP Erasmus', 'LLP Erasmus Student Placement', or other specific agreements outside the EU program framework.
Participation in Erasmus programs entitles the student to an additional point.
The composition and appointment of the Committee is carried out in accordance with the University Regulation. The periods for holding graduation sessions are decided and scheduled by the Course Council.

CURRICULUM: INTERCLASS
SECTION: PROGRAM, TEXTS AND OBJECTIVES
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/1883

Program, texts and objectives Motivations for the establishment of the interclass course. The Course of Study in Social Research, Security Policies and Crime aims to contribute to the formation of a specialized cultural and professional profile, characterized by a solid knowledge of sociology, criminology, political science, statistical analysis, along with specific historical-philosophical, anthropological, and legal knowledge, capable of operating in the fields of social analysis, with particular reference to the issues of security and crime arising in the complex scenarios of contemporary society. Indeed, such complexity requires cultural and professional figures capable of intervening within the social, political, and administrative world (carrying out analyses and planning of policies and interventions for social security and for the prevention and counteraction of crime) and within the justice system, with the complex aims of establishing the facts, collecting evidence, and reconstructing the criminal scenario. To form this type of professional figure, solid knowledge of social sciences is required, and therefore sociological, political, criminological, legal, political, statistical, and historical-philosophical. These profiles find optimal conditions for realization in this interclass (which, once activated, will lead to the simultaneous deactivation of the Course of Study LM-88 currently offered by the University), which brings together the development potential of the socio-criminological, juridico-political, statistical, and historical-philosophical fields of the LM-88 and LM-62 degree classes. During the planning phase of the interclass Course of Study, the training potential was considered in relation to the presence of similar or analogous courses at universities in the region or neighboring regions. From examining this context, it emerged that, regarding LM-88, the closest university is the University of Salento (Lecce campus), where a Master's program in Sociology and Social Research (LM-88) is active, which includes, among others, a curriculum focused on the themes of social deviance and crime. Regarding LM-62, courses are present both at universities in the same region (University of Teramo with International Political Sciences) and in neighboring regions (University of Molise with Political Sciences and European Institutions; University of Macerata with European Policies and Euro-Mediterranean Relations), which are characterized by training profiles oriented towards international institutional dimensions or the in-depth study of theoretical political sciences. The Interclass Course LM-88 – LM-62 the subject of this proposal would be unique in the landscape of the training offer provided both locally and nationally, as it would combine—within the perspective of specific training—sociological-criminological studies with political studies, thus contributing to the formation of more structured professional figures that respond to the demands of the labor market. Indeed, the Master's degree obtained in this interclass course will allow for a successful entry into the labor market within public or private entities. Additionally, it will permit access to public competitions of the public administration (local authorities, regions, ministries), as well as managerial positions in the State Police and the Penitentiary Administration Department, as well as in numerous other state sectors dependent on the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of the Interior. The degree title will allow one to undertake the path to acquire the expert and senior criminologist profile (in accordance with the UNI-11783:2020 Standard 'Unregulated Professional Activities – Criminologist – Knowledge, Skills, and Competencies Requirements'). Regarding the employment outcomes of the two Master's degree classes that constitute the interclass in question, the LM-88 Master's program already active at this university for the 2019 academic year, in reference to the employment status of its graduates (source Almalaurea), has recorded a decrease compared to previous years, both one year after the degree (36.4%) and three years (55.6%). This trend is further highlighted when compared to the same Master's program active at the 'Sapienza' University of Rome (51.4% - 64.1%), the University of Salento (62.5% - 62.5%), the University of Perugia (83.3% and 76.9%, although with very low absolute values), and the national average of the class (57.3% - 66.7%). In light of these data (also highlighted by the Evaluation Committee in the recent AVA Report 2020), the need emerges to structurally enhance further employment opportunities by combining LM-88 with LM-62. The data of this latter class show more encouraging employment outcomes, both one year and three years after obtaining the degree. The national average one year after obtaining the degree is around 56.6%, while three years it is at 75.2%; considering neighboring universities where this degree class is active, at the University of Teramo the figure is 66.7% one year and 71.0% three years; at the University of Molise it is 50.0% one year and 33.3% three years; at the University of Macerata it is 56.3% one year and 77.8% three years. In light of these findings and the proposal for the development and expansion of the previously mentioned cultural and professional profiles, the interclass tool allows for the possibility of offering the specificity of a Course of Study in the sociological-political area with a criminological focus, also in reference to the preparation of security policies. The proposal for the establishment of the LM-88 – LM-62 Interclass was formulated in a first consultation of the Steering Committee of the current LM-88 Course of Study offered by the d'Annunzio University: during the meeting, the Dean of the Course, Prof. Michele Cascavilla, informed the committee members of a decrease in the employment performance of graduates, emphasizing the need for a profound revision of the training offer or the establishment of an Interclass. The stakeholders, in full agreement with the Dean, noted that while the training offer is considered valid from a content perspective, it does not correspond to satisfactory employment effectiveness, particularly penalized by the inability to compete for top positions in the police forces and other public competitions. This is a critical issue that the Course of Study has already raised in the past, but without success, with the competent ministries (MIUR – Ministry of the Interior). This criticality has contributed to accelerating the proposal process for the LM-88 – LM-62 interclass degree course. Following the initiation of the design proposal, the 'G. D'Annunzio' Chieti Pescara University convened—via teleconference—the permanent consultation table with representatives of the productive system and professional sectors on November 26, 2020. The Consultation Committee expressed a favorable opinion regarding the training framework, referring, among others, to the newly established Interclass Master's Course LM-62 & LM-88. Following the university consultation, an additional discussion was held with the representative organizations on November 27, 2020, through the establishment and subsequent convening of a new Steering Committee for the Interclass, composed of members of the LM-88 committee, integrated with representatives of additional social groups interested in the outgoing cultural-professional profiles. The consultation on the proposal for activating the Interclass and the educational framework was conducted in relation to the needs and training demands emerging from the represented contexts. In expressing their favorable opinion regarding the training framework related to the interclass Course of Study in Social Research, Security Policies, and Crime, the Steering Committee also shared the full correspondence between the outlined training objectives and the employment and professional outcomes considered in the degree course project, as well as their potential contribution to meeting the broad need to address gaps identified in the exercise of organizational-institutional activities, in the context of promoting emerging needs in the fields of social security and the planning/provision of preventive countermeasures against the most widespread and alarming phenomena of deviance and crime. The Committee also expressed unanimous appreciation for the proposal, particularly for the opportunity offered to future graduates by the interclass to compete in additional public competitive initiatives offered even within the security sector. Note regarding the sectors and credits selected for the characteristic activities. In order to implement, as provided by the proposal approved by the Regional Coordination Committee of Abruzzo Universities on December 4, 2020, a «reference cultural and professional profile» that «aligns with the profiles provided by the three-year degree in Sociology and Criminology (L-40) already present at the university», among the selectable characteristic SSDs (based on the Master's classes decrees LM62 and LM88) in the curriculum, the following SSDs (SPS/07, SPS/08, SPS/11, SPS/12, IUS/01, M-STO/04, M-FIL/06, SECS-S/05) have been inserted, first and foremost, which are particularly consistent with the interclass Course of Study (i.e., with at least one of the cultural areas identified by its title: 1. Social Research 2. Security Policies 3. Study of Crime) and present in the planned and delivered teaching of the last academic years of the active LM88 Course of Study (born on the basis of the «continuity with the profiles provided by the three-year degree in Sociology and Criminology (L-40) already present at the university» referred to in the cited resolution, and for which the university proposes simultaneous deactivation, to be implemented at the time of establishing the interclass LM66 – LM88). In this way, the university can immediately demonstrate its ability to meet the quantitative and qualitative teaching requirements necessary for the establishment of the interclass LM62 – LM88 (being able to list among the 2021 reference teachers of the interclass the reference teachers indicated in 2020 to meet the requirements of the currently active LM88 Course of Study at the university). Additionally, thanks to this insertion, it will be possible to allow graduates of the aforementioned LM88 Course of Study from previous years before 2021 to enroll in the interclass Course of Study LM62 – LM88, obtaining recognition of a sufficient number of CFU. In addition to the SSDs mentioned above, to clearly define the profile of the new interclass Course of Study (respecting the CUN indication that the interclass course is «a single course that meets the requirements of two classes, and not of two parallel courses (one for each class) inserted in the same container»), a limited number of additional SSDs have been indicated in the curriculum, particularly consistent with the new interclass Course of Study LM62 – LM88 (i.e., with at least one of the cultural areas identified by its title: 1. Social Research 2. Security Policies 3. Study of Crime), belonging to the political, sociological, legal, and anthropological fields.

Communication Skills (communication skills)
In light of the training path provided, graduates with expertise in political and social sciences will be able to establish appropriate relational and communication forms in work contexts. The course teachings place particular emphasis on the communicative dimension, allowing the acquisition of theoretical competencies on themes concerning the reference fields. Moreover, through laboratory exercises aimed at experimenting with models and techniques to improve the quality and effectiveness of one's communication, graduates will be able to acquire in particular the following skills:
- identify the most appropriate tools and channels for communication, depending on the content to be transmitted and the work contexts in which they will find themselves;
- clearly and understandably present concepts related to their professional area of competence, once adequately assimilated, even to non-specialists;
- understand the different modes and nuances of communication in interpersonal relationships;
- interact correctly in communication relationships within work groups.
The expected learning outcomes in terms of communication skills can be assessed through traditional verification methods (oral and/or written exams) and through dedicated laboratories; moreover, through discussions with professionals operating in the areas of competence, during which students will be able to compare the theoretical information acquired.

Judgment Autonomy (making judgements)
The solid theoretical and methodological training will enable the graduate to identify the sources, premises, and consequences of theories and practices with which they will come into contact; moreover, it will allow them to reconstruct the context of complex and problematic situations. In this way, the graduate will be able to develop their own understanding of the situations they will be engaged in, formulating autonomous judgments even in contexts of heightened complexity and incomplete information. The acquisition of increasing judgment autonomy will be periodically assessed during written and/or oral examinations, during which the student will be able to demonstrate having personally assimilated and critically understood the content of the exam; moreover, through discussions between teachers, students, and representatives of professional realities.

Incoming Orientation Within the framework of incoming orientation activities, the Study Course promotes stable - in agreement with the University Orientation - meetings and interactions with graduates of first-level courses from regional and extra-regional origins, aimed at illustrating the training paths offered and the professional opportunities related to them.
Organized by the teachers affiliated with the Study Course and under the coordination of the Orientation Delegate, Prof. Thea Rossi, these meetings take place throughout the academic year and include presentations of the training paths activated within the active Disciplinary Areas at this University. Students are informed about the didactic contents of each course.
All orientation initiatives involve active participation - besides the Orientation Delegate - of student-tutors of the Study Course. Moreover, following the University's guidelines, the Study Course has prepared, building on previous experiences, a dedicated orientation page (from which orientation events and their modalities can be inferred) and two social media pages (Facebook and Instagram). Orientational and ongoing tutoring The orientation and ongoing tutoring is carried out through didactic accompaniment, listening and guidance activities, managed and promoted by specific tutor teachers coordinated by the orientation delegate. With the support of teaching tutors recruited among deserving students following an annual selective call. The Study Course provides access for interested students to appropriate orientation and ongoing tutoring paths activated within the Study Course, with the aim of improving mutual information and knowledge flows, towards a more adequate satisfaction of the training and professional needs required by the users of the educational offer. For this purpose, each year some teachers affiliated with the Study Course are identified and appointed with orientation functions at entry and ongoing, and facilitation in resolving emerging issues within the context of internship and traineeship activities. The teachers are Thea Rossi (Area Coordinator), Andrea Antonilli, Piergiorgio Della Pelle, Vanessa Russo, Raffaella De Girolamo (Academic office coordinator of the CDS). The CDS monitors the tutoring activity through the administration of a specific evaluation form (see attached PDF) completed by enrolled students to assess the effectiveness of the service provided.
Regarding the results emerging from the administration of the paper forms, due to Covid it is currently not possible to access them.
Additionally, the Academic office provides information on courses regarding the conduct of lessons, schedules, locations, student contacts, supported by the tutoring service.
The tutoring office operates according to predetermined hours publicized on the University website and at the Academic office location. The GAQ will monitor data related to the academic careers of enrolled students, reporting trends and consequent issues to the CDS.
Furthermore, to enhance ongoing orientation, 'd'Annunzio' University organizes - in collaboration with Companies and other partners - career orientation workshops. Through these meetings, the University aims to contribute to improving the employability levels of students enrolled in various Study Courses. Companies, organizations and institutions are thus offered the opportunity to present their working reality and recruitment policies, as well as illustrate career opportunities for new graduates. Prior to the meetings, organizations can collect applications and curricula of participating graduates through the innovative automated systems for promoting and managing the University 'd'Annunzio' Career Services.
Within the workshops, orientation workshops for CV preparation and managing job interviews, European citizenship, starting a business, using social networks for job search and personal branding are also proposed. The intention is to strengthen the cross-cultural level of university students, enabling them to expand their empowerment toolset.

Assistance for Training Periods The Study Course promotes student mobility and the performance of training activities outside the institution to better complete the educational path in line with the increasingly pressing need to expand knowledge at an international level.
To this end, an information and orientation service is available to students at the Academic Secretariat in collaboration with the tutoring service.
At the Academic Secretariat of the Study Course, a service is active to assist in identifying training offers and the operational execution of internship and/or placement experiences at companies and public and private institutions with which agreements have been established.
The Academic Secretariat also allows students to identify the organization where they wish to complete their internship. After making the choice and completing the internship, the student must submit documentation proving the activity, and the hosting organization must evaluate the student's performance. The evaluation forms for students are kept at the Academic Secretariat and available to the GAQ for monitoring the effectiveness of internships (for further details, see the attachment and Table C3).
Between June 2022 and December 2023, the number of interns was approximately 120 (data available at the Academic Secretariat).
Students have the possibility to complete the internships required by the Study Course at the organizations and entities listed in the attached document. Students may also identify non-conventioned organizations and propose them to the University.
Furthermore, the Course Council has established a dedicated Commission to better coordinate and monitor the implementation of internships and placements. The professor responsible for coordinating internships is Prof. Antonello Canzano, together with the Academic Secretariat and student-tutors assigned to assist interns.
Following the GAQ's indication and in compliance with the Triennial Cycle Review guidelines, the Course Council appointed a support commission composed of the professors: Cristiana Valentini, Andrea Antonilli, Carmelita Della Penna, Alfredo Agustoni, and Piergiorgio Della Pelle, and the student Giulia Pestarino, tasked with monitoring internship and professional training activities, submitting their evaluations to the Course Council.

International Mobility Office In addition to the international mobility opportunities provided by the Erasmus program (see the dedicated University link), the Degree Program aims to offer enrolled students the possibility to benefit from study opportunities abroad derived from specific conventional agreements (currently in place for active Degree Programs in the social sciences area) - aimed at promoting student mobility. Career support The Course of Study provides stable access for students to in-course and post-graduation internship experiences, which are characterized by being attributable to differentiated typological categories based on legal nature and territorial affiliation: these internship pathways take place at public and private structures connected to the Course of Study through institutional agreements formalized in convention. To these career support opportunities, particularly for the first occupational entry - which the Course of Study aims to increase through the stable organization of dedicated forums - must be integrated the opportunities reported by the Job Placement service active at the University. The Course of Study has activated an Outgoing Orientation service that periodically organizes workshops on behavioral skills necessary for entering the job market and meetings with professions aimed at introducing graduates to the various professional figures they can aspire to with the acquired competencies. The schedule will be available on the Course of Study website. Additionally, during the academic year, representatives of the cooperating entities are invited to deliver thematic seminars or professionalizing workshops at the Course of Study. During the 2021-2022 academic year, the customary 'Meetings with Professions' with local and national representatives of the world of work were resumed. In this context, a Course of Study career day was held in July 2022, with the participation of entities and companies that presented the main job opportunities to students, followed by interview simulations and the collection of applications. The same initiative is scheduled for May 21, 2024. Furthermore, to increase the employment and employability of its students, the 'd'Annunzio' University has activated a genuine placement structure. Indeed, in accordance with Law 30/03, commonly known as the Biagi Law, Italian universities can now carry out labor intermediation activities, complementing public employment centers and private operators in providing new services for employment (Start Program). Among the various services available to recent graduates are:
• BASIC AND SPECIALIZED CONSULTING FOR STUDENTS, BUSINESSES AND GRADUATES: the front-office activities managed by the Placement include providing information on numerous services dedicated to graduates and businesses, as well as on specific topics relevant to different target groups (contract types, labor market regulations, production and business systems, CV preparation, employment prospects). Individual meetings with graduates are also held to identify and analyze their competencies for developing a professional project. Meetings with company representatives are organized to analyze professional needs. The University's Placement promotes seminars, calls, career days, internships, and job offers through SMS and/or dedicated mailing lists for businesses and students/graduates of the Departments, as well as via popular social networks.
• SERVICES FOR BUSINESSES AND GRADUATES - LABOR INTERMEDIATION: therefore, to increase the employment and employability of its students, based on the guidelines in Law 30/03, the 'd'Annunzio' University has activated a genuine placement structure. The University is thus able to offer, to those seeking young resources to be integrated into their structure - whether through employment contracts or training and orientation internships - not only a direct connection with the sought professional figure, but also support services aimed at facilitating the identification of professionals matching the specific needs expressed. The service is managed with the help of the online platform JOB (http://job.unich.it), designed to meet the specific intermediation needs of d'Annunzio. In compliance with the recent regulations in this area (Law 183/2010 - so-called Labor Package and Law 111/2011), the University has also enhanced its technical and instrumental resources for labor intermediation with the CURRICULA application. Available on the University website, CURRICULA provides free access to the CVs of approximately 80,000 students and graduates from the last six years who have authorized the publication of their data. At the same time, companies, entities, organizations, and private employers can consult the database and, through the interconnection between CURRICULA and JOB (currently being integrated into the national Clic lavoro system), request the support of Placement Operators to conduct detailed searches for specific professional profiles and/or publish job/stage offers free of charge, also dedicated to students seeking to support themselves financially during their studies.
• ORIENTATION FOR STARTING A BUSINESS AND MICROCREDIT: within the Standard Setting procedure, the University has made available, for the benefit of Students, Graduates, and Research Doctors, the Business Start-up Orientation service. To this end, it has initiated a dialogue with local and national stakeholders to identify collaboration dynamics. The Placement, with this new service, aims to provide initial orientation to those interested in an entrepreneurial career and, based on the outcomes of the initial orientation meetings, to refer them to other services available in the territory that may be useful to the student/graduate. More details
• Microcredit Desk. To facilitate the identification of initial financial resources by young entrepreneurs, the University Placement Service provides Microcredit Orientation. The 'd'Annunzio' University has joined the 'Micro-Work' project, which aims to build a permanent microcredit network based on public-private collaboration, with the purpose of contributing to strengthening microcredit as an active labor policy tool.

GRADUATE OPINIONS The form is not fillable due to lack of data, since the interdepartmental course was established in the 2021/22 academic year.
Applying Knowledge and Understanding (applying knowledge and understanding)
Graduates will be able to apply the knowledge acquired through in-depth study of social and political contexts, socio-relational characteristics of groups and individuals, and decision-making activities for programming political and normative interventions. Additionally, through possession of specific conceptual tools, they will be able to address and resolve social issues related to deviant, criminal phenomena, and insecurity processes.
Specifically, the acquired knowledge will enable:
- Designing and programming interventions within public policy contexts in social settings;
- Analyzing, using social research methodologies and techniques, situations at risk of deviance and crime to implement preventive and/or countermeasures in relation to criminal phenomena trends;
- Mastering the acquired conceptual tools to structure solutions for complex social and political problems.
Didactic tools used to achieve these objectives include frontal lectures, as well as frontal and laboratory activities. Assessment methods involve oral or written exams.
Learning Skills (learning skills)
After assimilating curricular training activities through the most up-to-date didactic methodologies, graduates will develop autonomous abilities to:
- Learn for continuous updating of their knowledge;
- Use digital consultation tools such as databases;
- Employ all necessary knowledge, information, conceptual schemes, and languages useful for forming autonomous judgment capabilities.
Additionally, they must be able to expand their knowledge, even autonomously, through reading scientific texts and publications. Learning skills results will be periodically evaluated within individual courses through traditional assessment methods (oral interviews, exercises, written tests), as well as within various laboratory and internship activities.
University Communications to CUN In order to implement, as provided by the proposal approved by the Regional University Coordination Committee on December 4, 2020, a "reference cultural and professional profile" that "continues the profiles previously established by the three-year degree in Sociology and Criminology (L-40) already offered at the university," among the selectable SSDs (based on the Master's Class Decrees LM62 and LM88) in the curriculum, the following SSDs (SPS/07, SPS/08, SPS/11, SPS/12, IUS/01, M-STO/04, M-FIL/06, IUS/04, M-FIL/02, SECS-S/05) were inserted first, particularly consistent with the interdepartmental course (i.e., with at least one of the cultural areas identified by the title: 1. Social Research 2. Security Policies 3. Study of Crime) and present in the didactic programming and delivery of the last academic years of the active LM88 course (established based on the "continuity with the profiles previously established by the three-year degree in Sociology and Criminology (L-40) already offered at the university," as referenced in the resolution, and for which the university proposes simultaneous deactivation, to be implemented upon establishment of the interdepartmental LM66–LM88 course). Thus, the university can immediately demonstrate its ability to meet the quantitative and qualitative teaching requirements necessary for establishing the interdepartmental LM62–LM88 course (by indicating the 2021 reference teachers for the interdepartmental course as the reference teachers indicated in 2020 to meet the requirements of the currently active LM88 course). Furthermore, due to this insertion, the university will allow graduates of the previously active LM88 course (before 2021) to enroll in the interdepartmental LM62–LM88 course, obtaining recognition of a sufficient number of CFU.
Knowledge and Understanding (knowledge and understanding)
Graduates will achieve in-depth knowledge in the fields of social and political research, security policies, and qualitative/quantitative research methodologies within complex societies in contexts of deviance and crime. Additionally, they will acquire analytical, comprehension, and interpretation capabilities of political phenomena, also considering legal-political knowledge. Such knowledge is achieved through frontal lectures, seminar activities, laboratory activities, and internships. Assessment methods refer to oral and written exams during exam sessions and a graduation exam.
Organization and Responsibility of AQ at Course Level
- The Course Director, in accordance with Article 56 of the University Statute, will be elected by the Council from among the permanent professors and will serve a three-year term. They are responsible for the functioning of the degree course and convene and preside over regular and extraordinary Council meetings.
- The Review Group (GdR) is a committee of the Course whose main activity consists of analyzing the results of the training processes, with the aim of identifying critical points and possible improvement actions. The GdR is responsible for the Annual Monitoring Sheet (SMA) based on Anvur indicators analysis, and for periodically drafting the Cyclic Review Report. The GdR operates as the committee for the Course Council, to which it submits its main acts for approval.
Specifically, the GdR is responsible for monitoring and evaluating: the attractiveness and dropouts of the Course; regularity of academic careers and time to graduation; external effectiveness of the Course in terms of graduate employability and/or continuation in university education; level of internationalization of the Course.
- The Parity Commission operates within the School and is composed of a representation of professors and enrolled students. The Commission carries out continuous monitoring of the educational offer and teaching quality, as well as the service activities provided by professors to students, and identifies indicators for evaluating the results of these activities.
Following the monitoring activities, the Commission prepares an annual report containing evaluations and proposals to the Quality Assessment Unit regarding the improvement of quality and effectiveness of teaching structures, also in relation to learning outcomes, occupational and personal/professional development prospects, and economic and productive system needs. The Parity Commission annually prepares the Annual Report.
The Annual Report evaluates whether:
1. the Course project maintains due attention to the functions and skills required by occupational and personal/professional development prospects, identified considering the needs of the economic and productive system;
2. the expected learning outcomes are effective in relation to the reference functions and skills (coherence between planned teaching activities and specific educational objectives);
3. the teaching activities of professors, knowledge transmission methods, materials, didactic aids, laboratories, classrooms, equipment, and student services provided by professors and researchers are effective in achieving the desired learning outcomes;
4. examination methods correctly assess results in relation to expected learning outcomes;
5. the Annual Review leads to effective corrective and improvement actions by the Course in subsequent years;
6. student satisfaction questionnaires are effectively managed, analyzed, and used to improve teaching;
7. up-to-date, impartial, objective, quantitative, and qualitative information on each offered Course is made publicly available through regular and accessible publication of the public parts of the SUA-CdS.
- The Teaching Council of the Social Research, Security Policies, and Crime Degree Course is composed of professors responsible for courses and student representatives elected according to the procedures established by the University General Regulation (pursuant to Article 56 of the Statute). The Teaching Council functions to program all attributions assigned to it by current national regulations and the University Teaching Regulation. Specifically, the Teaching Council of the Course performs the following tasks:

3. Plans all teaching activities necessary to achieve the Course's educational objectives and monitors their regular execution;
