Course Design
The Social Research, Security Policies, and Crime Master's Course aims to contribute to the formation of a specialized cultural and professional profile characterized by solid sociological, criminological, political, and statistical analytical knowledge, combined with specific historical-philosophical, anthropological, and legal knowledge, capable of operating in social analysis sectors, particularly concerning security and crime issues in the complex scenarios of contemporary society. This complexity requires cultural and professional figures able to intervene within the social, political, and administrative world (conducting analyses and designing security policies and crime prevention and countermeasures) and within the justice system, with the aim of establishing facts, collecting evidence, and reconstructing criminal scenarios. To form such professionals, solid knowledge of social sciences, including sociological, political, criminological, legal, statistical, and historical-philosophical disciplines, is required.
The reference cultural and professional profile aligns with the profiles previously established by the three-year degree in Sociology and Criminology (L-40) already offered at the university, while also complementing the profiles established by first-level degrees in political sciences. These profiles find optimal conditions for realization in this interdepartmental course, which synergizes the developmental potential of socio-criminological fields of the LM-88 degree class with the political fields contemplated by the LM-62 degree class.
Indeed, the Master's Degree obtained in this interdepartmental course enables successful entry into the job market as specialists in public and private entities, allowing access to public administration competitions (local authorities, regions, ministries), as well as leadership roles in the Police Force and the Penitentiary Administration Department, as well as in numerous other state sectors dependent on the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of the Interior. Graduates may also work as experts and consultants in designing public and social policies, performing high-responsibility functions in public administration or private company organizational and management contexts, particularly regarding decision-making models related to public policy management and third-sector entities. The degree also enables pursuing the profile of expert and senior criminologist (pursuant to UNI-11783:2020 'Unregulated Professional Activities – Criminologist – Knowledge, Skills, and Competencies Requirements').
The degree also allows acquiring solid knowledge and a sufficient number of CFU in sociological and historical-philosophical disciplines, enabling graduates to pursue the path for teaching qualifications in Philosophy and Humanities (A18), with some necessary integrations (1).
Regarding the employment outcomes of the two Master's degree classes forming the interdepartmental course, the existing LM-88 course at this university for the 2019 academic year, in terms of graduate employment status (source Almalaurea), showed a decline compared to previous years, both one year (36.4%) and three years (55.6%) after graduation. This trend is further evident when compared to the same LM-88 course at Sapienza University of Rome (51.4% - 64.1%), Salento University (62.5% - 62.5%), Perugia University (83.3% and 76.9%, despite low absolute values), and the national average for the class (57.3% - 66.7%). Given these data (also highlighted by the Assessment Unit in the recent 2020 AVA Report), there is a need to structurally expand further employment opportunities by complementing LM-88 with LM-62. Data for the latter class show more encouraging employment outcomes, both one and three years after graduation. The national one-year employment rate is approximately 56.6%, while the three-year rate is 75.2%. Considering nearby universities offering this degree class, Teramo University reports 66.7% at one year and 71.0% at three years; Molise University reports 50.0% at one year and 33.3% at three years; Macerata University reports 56.3% at one year and 77.8% at three years.
Based on these findings and the proposed development and expansion of the reference cultural and professional profiles, the interdepartmental course enables offering the specificity of a socio-political course with a criminological focus, also in relation to the design of security policies.
Brief Course Description
The Social Research, Security Policies, and Crime Master's Course aims to contribute to the formation of a specialized cultural and professional profile characterized by solid sociological, criminological, political, and statistical analytical knowledge, combined with specific historical-philosophical, anthropological, and legal knowledge, capable of operating in social analysis sectors, particularly concerning security and crime issues in the complex scenarios of contemporary society. This complexity requires cultural and professional figures able to intervene within the social, political, and administrative world (conducting analyses and designing security policies and crime prevention and countermeasures) and within the justice system, with the aim of establishing facts, collecting evidence, and reconstructing criminal scenarios. The reference cultural and professional profile aligns with the profiles previously established by the three-year degree in Sociology and Criminology (L-40) already offered at the university, while also complementing the profiles established by first-level degrees in political sciences. Prof. Cascavilla thanked participants and recalled the Steering Committee's function.
This is an organ provided for by the University Regulation, composed of professors from the Courses, student representatives, and representatives of public and private entities that have established collaboration with the Courses, representing structures where graduates can perform internships and post-graduation activities.
To reduce the gap between university training and the labor market, the Steering Committee was established by University Regulation to allow students to apply the skills and competencies acquired during their university path within the professional world, reducing the gap between theoretical training (university) and the concreteness of the working world. According to the Regulation, the Steering Committee must meet at least once a year to be informed about the Course programming and to formulate useful proposals for the following academic year.
The Committee includes various entities representing public and private organizations. The Chair read the list of members composing the current Steering Committee.

Entry, Path, and Exit Data
Regarding the enrollment flow recorded in 2022/2023, there is a growing number of enrollments totaling 163, compared to 131 in the previous year. Regarding the type of high school diploma, for the 2022/23 academic year, 41.1% hold a high school diploma (46.6% in the previous year), 31.2% hold a magistral diploma (26% in 21/22), 14.1% hold a technical diploma (22.6% in 21/22), and 4.3% hold a professional diploma (a significant decrease from the previous year: 14%).
The diploma was obtained with a grade 'up to 80' by 62.6% and with a 'between 80 and 99' by 33.7%. 70.5% of enrolled students come from regions outside Abruzzo, while 6.4% come from another municipality in the province.
32.14% graduate with a grade up to 105/110, and 32.14% graduate with a grade between 105 and 110. 34.5% graduate with a grade of 110 cum laude.

Final Project Characteristics
Written thesis of at least 200,000 characters. It may consist of a comprehensive critical literature review or a field-based project or analytical research in one of the disciplines covered in the chosen path and characteristic of the selected study direction.
Coherence around the topic that gives the title to the thesis, a well-structured and logical organization of the subject, and a sufficiently broad and relevant bibliography are required.
Final Project Execution Method
The final project is carried out through in-depth discussions of the theses proposed by individual candidates, with the simultaneous presence of a designated supervisor, within specific public sessions managed by appointed teaching committees and coordinated by professors affiliated with the Course.
Considering the academic background of individual candidates, the quality of the thesis work, and the adequacy of its discussion (in Italian or, following a Course Council resolution, in another language), the Committee awards a score ranging from zero to eight additional points on top of the base score derived from the weighted average of the grades obtained during the curricular exams, with the possibility of awarding the cum laude distinction if the Committee unanimously agrees.
Additionally, one extra point will be awarded if the graduate has spent a period of study abroad or participated in one of the Erasmus exchange programs.
The written thesis, written in Italian (or, following a Course Council resolution, in another language), must be at least 200,000 characters. It may consist of a comprehensive critical literature review or a field-based project or analytical research in one of the disciplines covered in the chosen path and characteristic of the selected study direction.
Coherence around the topic that gives the title to the thesis, a well-structured and logical organization of the subject, and a sufficiently broad and relevant bibliography are required.

Technical Report Summary by the Assessment Unit - SUA Sheet
Clearly and convincingly, the motivations for activating the interdepartmental Course based on an analysis of training demand and departmental and University strategies are outlined. The new interdepartmental Master's Course would replace the currently active LM-88 Course, potentially expanding its employment opportunities and presenting itself as more attractive to graduates of the L-40 Sociology and Criminology Course.
The Course design was carried out with adequate timing and attention. The cultural and professional profiles of the figure the Course aims to form are clearly defined. Direct consultation with interested parties is adequate at the local level, though not fully at the national level.
Functions and skills are described with sufficient precision and consistency with professional profiles. For the disciplinary competencies of the Assessment Unit members, the path appears sufficiently consistent with the formed professional profiles. The verification methods for personal preparation for admission to the Master's Course require improvement.
The structural resources and teaching staff allocation appears generally adequate.
Course monitoring is consistent with the University's AQ system.

Admission Requirements Required Knowledge for Admission To be admitted to the Master's degree course in Psychology of Well-being and Performance, one must hold a three-year university degree or a university diploma of three-year duration, or another foreign degree recognized as suitable.
Admission to the course is conditional upon possessing:
For Italian students: a degree in class L-24 PSYCHOLOGICAL SCIENCES AND TECHNIQUES (ex. Ministerial Decree 270/04), or a degree in class 34 PSYCHOLOGICAL SCIENCES AND TECHNIQUES (ex. Ministerial Decree 509/99), or holding a degree and having acquired at least 60 CFU in the field of psychology.
For students from foreign universities: solid foundational preparation in all areas of psychology: the psychophysiological processes underlying behavior, general psychology, social psychology, developmental psychology, clinical psychology, human relationship dynamics, psychological research methodologies, statistical, psychometric methods, and computer procedures for data processing.
b. knowledge of English not below B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference.
The verification of personal preparation is mandatory, and only students possessing the required academic qualifications may enroll. The adequacy of personal preparation is verified by a committee composed of the course instructors.
For the purpose of enrolling in the Master's degree course in Psychology, those who have obtained a degree in Psychological Sciences and Techniques - class L-24 under the previous academic framework and have not completed the professional training activities corresponding to the 10 CFU specified in paragraph 5 (Interministerial Decree No. 654 of July 5, 2022), may request recognition of activities completed and certified during the three-year degree course, specifically regarding:
a) activities, carried out individually or in small groups, aimed at learning methods, tools, and procedures related to the practical contexts of psychology;
b) practical experiences, laboratories, simulations, role-playing, project writing, carried out individually or in small groups, concerning tools, methods, and procedures aimed at developing the knowledge necessary to operate in contexts where psychologists are involved.
In the absence, total or partial, of recognition of the aforementioned CFU (Interministerial Decree No. 654 of July 5, 2022, Article 2, Paragraph 6), three-year graduates acquire the missing internship CFU in addition to the 120 CFU of the Master's degree.

Admission Requirements To be admitted to the Master's Degree in Psychology of Well-being and Performance, one must hold a three-year university degree or a three-year university diploma, or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent. The course has open access. The number of incoming students will be determined annually by the Master's Degree Course Council, taking into account available educational resources. If applications exceed the planned number, a selection based on qualifications will be conducted, and a ranking will be established according to specific criteria outlined in the Admission Notice. Additionally, candidates must possess specific academic requirements and adequate preparation, and be positioned favorably in the merit ranking.

Admission to the course of study is conditional upon possessing:
a. For Italian students only: a degree in class L-24 PSYCHOLOGICAL SCIENCES AND TECHNIQUES (ex D.M. 270/04), or a degree in class 34 PSYCHOLOGICAL SCIENCES AND TECHNIQUES (ex D.M. 509/99), or a degree with at least 60 CFU in psychological fields, both curricular and extracurricular.
For students from foreign universities, a solid foundational preparation in all areas of psychology is required: psychophysiological processes underlying behavior, general psychology, social psychology, developmental psychology, clinical psychology, human relationship dynamics, psychological research methodologies, statistical and psychometric methods, and computer procedures for data processing.
b. For both Italian and foreign students: English language proficiency at least at B2 level. If the access degree was obtained after completing a study program taught in English, this requirement is considered satisfied.

Verification of personal preparation is mandatory and only students meeting the academic requirements may participate. The adequacy of personal preparation is verified through analysis of the academic curriculum and an obligatory interview with the Course of Study faculty.

Communication Skills (communication skills)
The master's graduate is able to:
- To present in written and oral form, effectively and with language appropriate for different interlocutors, one's conclusions regarding studies and analyses, clearly explaining one's reasoning.
- To communicate effectively and unambiguously to experts and non-experts one's conclusions, both regarding the evaluation of behavior and to the specific intervention proposals that individual situations require.
Written and oral communication skills are particularly developed during laboratory activities and presentations carried out individually and in groups in the classroom, in which students are encouraged to participate publicly, to improve their ability to present a project.
The verification of such skills occurs in the form of end-of-year seminars during which students must present orally and through computer presentations the results of their learning in an area among those proposed during the year.

TYPE: Master's Degree
CURRICULUM: Judgment Autonomy
SECTION: Judgment Autonomy
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/2305

Judgment Autonomy (making judgements)
The master's graduate is able to: - Develop complex analyses based on incomplete information and formulate autonomous reflections on specific topics of in-depth study. - Formulate independent judgments regarding evaluations of cognitive-emotional, behavioral, and professional functioning. - Communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions to non-specialist interlocutors. - Draft reports and relations. These objectives are developed through the production of experimental designs on various proposed topics, demonstrating the student's ability to place empirical evaluation tests within a theoretical framework: state of the art, experimental hypotheses, materials and methods used, data analysis methods, discussion of obtained results; the ability to design an intervention aimed at articulating the acquired knowledge to modify behaviors in an adaptive sense. The acquisition of judgment autonomy is verified through the evaluation of the student's study plan courses and the assessment of the degree of autonomy and ability to work individually during the activity assigned in preparation for the final exam.

Entry Orientation The Master's Degree Course in Psychology of Well-being and Performance offers its students an integrated orientation service, including specific actions for entry, in-course, and exit orientation, with the aim of facilitating the transition to third-level training paths and supporting professional integration.
The orientation service is provided in collaboration with the University's Orientation Division and includes public presentations of the educational offer, monitoring of student skills, and information on internal and external educational offerings.
The Course also organizes an annual orientation meeting for graduates of the Bachelor's Degree in Psychological Sciences and Techniques, in collaboration with other Psychology Courses, to present the Master's Degree Course and its main characteristics.

The educational offer is also presented during the Night of Researchers and the orientation fairs at which the university participates.

Ongoing Orientation and Tutoring The coordination and dialogue with the University's Central Orientation Division is realized through periodic meetings, through the figure of the orientation coordinator, in order to monitor university dropout rates and be able to intervene promptly to contain and prevent the same.

Regarding ongoing orientation, students have access to a tutoring service, characterized by both disciplinary and methodological support, to address individual exams and the preparation of the thesis, with the aim of reducing the dropout rate among graduating students; this service is provided by all faculty members of the Course (subject tutors), typically during office hours, and is aimed at assisting students in resolving their issues (e.g., suggesting a correct study method).
Additionally, each student will be assigned a tutor, a faculty member of the Course, who will guide them throughout their studies. Student Vittoria Marchesani will be the tutor representative for the Course students.
The evaluation of the effectiveness of the service provided for ongoing orientation is carried out through periodic consultation with the student representatives of the Course, tasked with collecting opinions, issues, and suggestions. This activity is coordinated by Professor Chiara Berti, the tutor representative for the Course. These meetings will take place in hybrid mode to ensure maximum participation.

CURRICULUM: Student opinions
SECTION: Student opinions
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/2305

Student opinions The Master's Degree in 'Psychology of Well-being and Performance' is a novelty in the academic landscape, having been established just one year ago. Despite its recent introduction, the course has demonstrated a positive impact on student satisfaction. This report aims to analyze data regarding student satisfaction, comparing it with the average of courses in the social sciences area and the university-wide average.
1. Overall Satisfaction:
The overall satisfaction of students for the 'Psychology of Well-being and Performance' course was rated with an average score of 3.59. This value is above the average of courses in the social sciences area and also exceeds the university-wide average. This data suggests that students are generally highly satisfied with the quality of education and experiences offered by the course.
2. Logistical-Organizational Aspects and Teaching Efficiency:
Students have positively evaluated both the logistical-organizational aspects and the teaching efficiency of the course. Specifically:
Logistical-organizational aspects received a score of 3.60, placing the course above the social sciences area average and the university average.
Teaching efficiency received a score of 3.68, also surpassing the reference averages.
These data indicate that the course is well-organized from a logistical perspective and that teaching is perceived as effective and of high quality.
Conclusions:
The Master's Degree in 'Psychology of Well-being and Performance', despite having been established only twelve months ago, has already demonstrated its ability to meet and exceed student expectations. The results achieved in terms of overall satisfaction and specific evaluations on logistical-organizational aspects and teaching efficiency are particularly encouraging, especially when compared to the averages of the social sciences area and the university.
These data are a promising sign for the course's future. However, it is essential to continue monitoring student satisfaction and making further improvements based on feedback to ensure the course maintains its high quality standard over time.

Applying Knowledge and Understanding (applying knowledge and understanding)
Applying Knowledge and Understanding (applying knowledge and understanding) :
(Quadro A4.b.1 SUA)
The master's graduate is able to: - refer to specific explanatory theories within general psychology to understand and intervene in individual and group work situations in order to promote well-being and performance; - design action-research interventions to respond to needs expressed by clients; - use individual and group observation and evaluation tools for the purpose of designing interventions and proposals; - conduct evaluations on the effectiveness of proposed interventions; - draft, implement, and monitor person- and community-oriented projects; - use knowledge in the context of oral and written communication to provide appropriate feedback; - design and implement intervention and training activities for various types of interlocutors. The achievement of the above-mentioned applying knowledge and understanding skills occurs through critical reflection on texts proposed for individual study within classroom activities, presentation of cases by instructors, and research solicited from students, drawn from the scientific-practical experience of instructors and students, practical exercises, and guided construction of individual and/or small group research/intervention projects. Assessments are carried out through written reports, through which students demonstrate their mastery of tools, methodologies, and critical autonomy.
Learning Skills (learning skills)
The master's graduate is able to:
- Define a plan for continuous professional development, guided by the awareness that psychological approaches are evidence-based and therefore subject to continuous updating.
- Define a research and development plan for one's professional career having received psychological training in innovative fields.
- Undertake higher-level studies (master's, specialization schools, and doctoral programs) and apply acquired experiences in professional contexts.
The master's graduate develops the necessary learning skills not only to achieve good results in current studies but also to plan continuous professional development, ensure professional quality, and potentially undertake further studies and continuous updating activities independently.
These skills are verified through participation in practical training activities, through the presentation of content in written and oral form that demonstrate students' reflective abilities and therefore learning capabilities.
Knowledge and Understanding (knowledge and understanding)
The master's graduate: - knows the main explanatory theories within the field of well-being and performance psychology; - knows the main research methods and data analysis techniques within well-being and performance psychology; - understands the relationships between research methods, investigation techniques, and data analysis within psychological disciplines; - understands the importance of correctly using observation and evaluation tools in psychology. The aforementioned knowledge and understanding skills are acquired through attending lectures, practical exercises, seminars, guided personal study, and the use of periodically monitored thematic forums. The verification of learning outcomes is carried out through oral and/or written exams, prepared in agreement between instructors, and oral presentations during intermediate phases of courses. Brief Description of Related and Integrative Activities Related and integrative activities aim to provide knowledge in the field of motor activity sciences. Among the educational objectives of the CdS is the training of professional figures capable of operating in sports contexts to promote individual well-being and improve performance. Related and integrative activities in the field of motor activity sciences contribute to achieving this objective by providing knowledge and skills for designing, implementing, promoting, and evaluating interventions for athletes and coaches.
Additionally, related and integrative activities aim to provide knowledge in the field of biology, with particular reference to the functional organization of living systems. One of the approaches used to promote well-being, the main educational objective of the CdS, is the ability to use innovative paradigms, such as biofeedback. Biological teaching contributes to providing solid knowledge to achieve this objective.
Finally, related and integrative activities aim to provide knowledge and skills to promote well-being and optimize performance using new technologies. In particular, the current pandemic has imposed a radical change in teaching delivery methods (e.g., distance learning). Therefore, related and integrative activities aim to provide theoretical and practical knowledge regarding teaching, techniques, and educational technologies in both school contexts and broader training environments.
For related and integrative activities, a minimum of 18 credits is required.
Brief Course Description The CdS in Psychology of Well-being and Performance (Psychology of Well-being and Performance), with an international character, aims to train professional figures capable of designing, implementing, promoting, and evaluating psychological interventions for the development of personal, social, communication, organizational, and management skills aimed at promoting individual and group well-being in the contexts of work organizations, schools, institutions, and sports.
Among the strategic objectives of the Italian government (e.g., PNR 2021-2027) and the European community (e.g., Horizon Europe) is the promotion of well-being and the valorization of the individual in their reference contexts. To contribute to achieving this objective, it is necessary to train professional figures capable not only of addressing illness and psychological distress but especially of promoting behaviors that improve the quality of life of individuals. To date, such professional figures are virtually absent in Italy.
The educational offer integrates competencies and knowledge in psychological and neuroscientific fields, with particular attention to well-being and performance sciences, to train professionals capable of operating in individual, sports, school, and business contexts.
The first-year educational activities aim to provide solid theoretical and methodological knowledge through a teaching approach that integrates lectures and practical activities, promoting individual well-being in individual, social, and sports contexts.
In the second year, educational activities aim to provide solid theoretical and methodological knowledge, again through an integrated teaching approach, promoting well-being and optimizing performance in individual and work contexts.
Upon completion of the program, the graduate, after passing the practical evaluation test and registering with the psychologists' register, will be able to practice freely, find employment in public and private national and international entities focused on promoting well-being and performance of individuals and groups throughout life, with particular reference to schools, sports associations, healthcare organizations, and the workplace.
To be admitted to the Master's program in Psychology of Well-being and Performance, one must hold a three-year university degree or equivalent foreign degree recognized as suitable.
Admission to the Master's program is subject to passing an assessment of personal preparation, carried out according to the procedures defined in the Course's Didactic Regulations.
External Effectiveness New course, data not available Reasons for establishing multiple courses in the class At the university, two existing Master's programs in class LM-51 are already active, titled Psychology and Clinical Psychology and Health. Both programs are not international and are delivered in Italian. The project to establish a new LM-51 responds to the intent of offering a different educational path in terms of content and form compared to existing ones. The proposed LM-51 will be international, delivered entirely in English. Additionally, the existing LM-51 programs focus on understanding psychological processes—cognitive, emotional, and social—that characterize mental functioning in situations of psychological distress and suffering. In contrast, the proposed LM-51 will focus, with an international reference framework, on promoting well-being and optimizing performance in business, school, and institutional contexts. Therefore, due to their different purposes, the study programs refer to very different theoretical and methodological premises.
Regarding the regional and neighboring regional landscape, two international LM-51 courses are currently active, delivered in English, both at the "La Sapienza" University of Rome. The aforementioned courses aim to train clinical psychologists and sexologists (LM-51 – Clinical Psychosexology) and psychologists specializing in clinical neuropsychology, cognitive psychology, and applied research methodology in cognitive neuroscience (LM-51 – Cognitive Neuroscience). Therefore, there are no CdS with international character and similar educational objectives.
The course in Psychology of Well-being and Performance aims to provide specialized training in the fields of positive psychology, well-being, and human performance.
The cultural and professional profile characterizing the Psychology of Well-being and Performance study path and distinguishing it from all other courses in the same class active in Italian universities is, on one hand, openness to the international landscape, and on the other, professional ability to improve individual well-being and optimize performance in various psychological contexts.
The final educational objective is to assist the graduate in acquiring knowledge and professional skills to develop a deep understanding of the concepts of well-being and performance, leveraging internal individual resources. In relation to these strategic and disciplinary premises, the Master's program in Psychology of Well-being and Performance aims to train psychologists specialized in promoting health, well-being, and optimizing performance in work, school, and institutional contexts.
Specific Educational Objectives of the Course and Description of the Study Path The CdS in Psychology of Well-being and Performance (Psychology of Well-being and Performance), with an international character, aims to train professional figures capable of designing, implementing, promoting, and evaluating psychological interventions for the development of personal, social, communication, organizational, and management skills aimed at promoting individual and group well-being in the contexts of work organizations, schools, institutions, and sports. The CdS in Psychology of Well-being and Performance is in line with the cultural and technical-scientific evolution of the European community. The nature of the CdS is derived from its name: Psychology of Well-being and Performance. The expression has good self-explanatory capacity, as its general meaning is immediately evident from the terms that compose it: a design oriented towards training psychologists specialized in well-being and performance. The cultural, scientific, and professional aspects characterizing the CdS in Psychology of Well-being and Performance are not overlapping with other active Master's programs in psychology in Italy, especially due to its international vocation. The CdS in Psychology of Well-being and Performance is characterized by an international and interdisciplinary path oriented towards, on one hand, the formation of a cultural profile sensitive to positive psychology and well-being, and on the other, a professional profile capable of optimizing individual performance. Specifically, the study path in Psychology of Well-being and Performance promotes cultural, scientific, and professional profiles consistently united by conceptual, methodological, and applied synergies between different psychological fields, such as cognitive and general, developmental, community, and work, and finally dynamic-clinical. Based on these synergies and intersections, the CdS in Psychology of Well-being and Performance aims to value a professional figure of a Master's graduate in well-being and performance psychology. In particular, the educational activities of the CdS are related to the following learning areas: area of general and physiological psychology, area of developmental and educational psychology, area of social and work psychology, area of dynamic and clinical psychology. The educational activities of the general and physiological psychology area are included in SSD M-PSI/01, M-PSI/02, and M-PSI/03. These educational activities are particularly dedicated to the study of cognitive empowerment, promotion of creativity, optimization of sports performance, and related psychobiological aspects of well-being. The educational activities of the developmental and educational psychology area are included in SSD M-PSI/04. These educational activities are particularly dedicated to the study of the role of emotions in well-being throughout life. The educational activities of the social and work psychology area are included in SSD M-PSI/05 and M-PSI/06. These educational activities are particularly dedicated to the study of evaluating and promoting positive and prosocial behaviors in groups and organizations. The educational activities of the dynamic and clinical psychology area are included in SSD M-PSI/07 and M-PSI/08. These educational activities are particularly dedicated to the study of clinical psychology, health, and positive psychology with the possibility of targeted interventions to promote well-being in family, work, and institutional contexts. Given the enabling nature of the CdS, ample space, consistently with current regulations, will be dedicated to the practical evaluation internship.

Consultation with Representative Organizations - at National and International Levels - of Goods and Services Production, and Professions (Course Establishment)
The proposal stems from a joint study conducted with consultation of interested parties. In September, October, and November 2021, questionnaires were sent to representative organizations of goods and services production and professions, both national and international, to ensure the definition of an educational path enabling professional opportunities closely related to the regional, national, and international productive reality. The questionnaire responses were subsequently analyzed by the working group composed of the proposing department's instructors. All reflections emerging from the questionnaires were considered, analyzing and discussing the main occupational potentialities of graduates (attached minutes). As highlighted by social partners, professional activity must be directed and exercised i) in public and/or private structures in the field of well-being promotion; ii) in sports, competitive, and non-competitive contexts, assuming support, technical, managerial, and promotional roles for the graduate's core activities; iii) in companies, assuming active roles as well-being and performance psychologists.
Consultation with Representative Organizations - at National and International Levels - of Goods and Services Production, and Professions (Subsequent Consultations)
The educational project also benefited from stakeholder contributions. The meeting was held in mixed mode on December 21, 2022, in the university's multimedia room. The meeting included internal and external parties interested in changes dictated by Law 163/2021, which requires Bachelor's (L-24) and Master's (LM-51) programs to effectively combine the quality of education with the time constraints, including 30 CFU of internship in the educational path, making constant dialogue between universities and the territory more necessary than ever. To discuss the challenges posed by the law on qualifying degrees to L-24 and LM-51 programs, the following participated in order: the Rector's Delegate for Teaching; the coordinator of the CdS in Psychological Sciences and Techniques; the President of the Deontological Commission and Permanent Observatory of the Code of Ethics (CNOP); the President of the Abruzzo Region Psychologists' Order; the President of the National Association of Public Administrators and High Professionalities (ANP); the President of "La Rete per Lavorare"; the President of the Abruzzo and Molise Chapter of the Italian Association for Personnel Management (AIDP); the Student Secretariat Manager for Psychology and Social Sciences; the Director of "Debate Italia"; student representatives of the CdS; the President of FEPSAC (European Federation of Sport Psychology). From the overall interventions, it became clear that there is broad appreciation for the international nature of the course and its vocation to promote well-being. A critical aspect, emphasized by multiple parties, is the need to characterize all courses with practical activities to prepare students for the TPV. Another meeting was held on Monday, January 16, 2023, with students currently enrolled in the CdS in Psychology of Well-being and Performance. In this case, students clearly expressed the need to make courses less theoretical and more applied. Based on this indication, the President will invite all instructors to include practical activities within the courses.
The next consultation is scheduled for autumn 2024
Entry, Course, and Exit Data The 'Psychology of Well-being and Performance' study program has demonstrated the ability to attract a significant number of students, despite being a new educational path. Currently, the program has 15 enrolled students.
The geographical origin of students is quite varied, demonstrating the course's appeal at local, regional, national, and international levels. Specifically:
- 2 students come from the same municipality where the university is located.
- 3 students are from other municipalities within the same province.
- 1 student comes from another province within the same region.
- 7 students reside in other regions of Italy.
- Finally, 2 students reside abroad.
These data suggest that the course has appeal at both local and national and international levels.
The enrollment grades of enrolled students vary:
- 4 students achieved a grade between 80 and 99.
- 8 students obtained a score up to 80.
- For 3 students, the enrollment grade is not defined.
Regarding students' educational background:
- Most students (8) come from high schools.
- 1 student attended technical institutes.
- 3 students come from magistral institutes.
- The other 3 students have unspecified educational backgrounds.
The 'Psychology of Well-being and Performance' study program has shown to be attractive to a wide range of students from diverse educational and geographical backgrounds. The diversity in geographical origin and school background of students could contribute to a rich and stimulating learning environment. It will be interesting to monitor how this student composition influences the overall course experience in the coming years.
Final Exam Characteristics The final exam consists of the development of an original thesis on topics related to the Master's program courses, under the guidance of a supervisor.
As per DI 654/2022, to access the final exam, one must have passed the Practical-Valuation Test (PPV), following the achievement of a satisfactory evaluation (30 CFU of professional training activities) for the practical-evaluation internship (TPV) throughout the entire educational path (Bachelor's and/or Master's).
Final Exam Execution Method The final exam consists of the development of an original thesis on topics related to the Master's program courses, under the guidance of a supervisor. The student may choose between two different thesis formats:
- Empirical type, which involves literature review as well as planning, implementation, administration, and analysis of experimental data collected by the student.
- Compilation type, consisting of an original critical reading on scientifically relevant disciplinary topics.
The graduation exam will, as legally required, be public and conducted according to a predetermined program, with each candidate having an average of 15 minutes, divided into a first part dedicated to the thesis presentation and a second part for discussion. Candidates are encouraged to use audiovisual aids for presentations.
The Commission, whose composition is established by the University's Didactic Regulations, evaluates each candidate considering the overall academic performance, thesis content, and final exam execution; the evaluation is expressed in hundredths. The score assigned to the thesis and its presentation ranges from a minimum of 0 to a maximum of 8 points, according to the following scale:
- 0-1: sufficient
- 2-3: fair
- 4-5: good
- 6-7: excellent
- 8: outstanding
The criteria for evaluating the score to be assigned to the thesis include:
1. Ordered and coherent organization of topics treated in the thesis;
2. Mastery of specialized language and discipline-specific terminology;
3. Originality of the thesis topic;
4. Level of depth of the topic treated;
5. Accuracy of bibliographic research;
6. Relevance assigned to the most recent literature on the thesis topic;
7. Completeness of the treatment of the thesis topic;
8. Expressive and presentation ability of the thesis.
The exam is considered passed with a minimum grade of 66/110. In case of a maximum grade (110/110), the Commission may award honors by unanimous decision.

Admission Procedures The course has local programmed access. The number of incoming students will be defined annually based on the proposal of the Master's Degree Course Council, taking into account available educational resources. If applications exceed the programmed number, a selection based on qualifications will be conducted, and a ranking list will be established according to specific criteria indicated in the Admission Notice.
Additionally, candidates must possess specific academic requirements and adequate preparation, and be positioned favorably in the merit ranking.
The required academic qualifications for admission are as follows:
a. Possession of a Bachelor's Degree or equivalent title (Italian or foreign) documenting a study curriculum consisting of at least 95 CFU, distributed within psychological disciplines (with the following minimum criteria: at least 18 CFU in disciplines M-PSI/01, 02, 03; at least 6 CFU in discipline M-PSI/04; at least 9 CFU in disciplines M-PSI/05, 06; at least 12 CFU in disciplines M-PSI/07, 08).
b. Knowledge of English at an appropriate level: passing a university-level English exam equivalent to B1 level or a B1 certificate issued by an MUR-accredited certification body, not older than three years.
Pursuant to Article 2, paragraphs 6 and 7, of DM 654/2022, for enrollment in the Master's Degree course, those who have obtained a Bachelor's Degree in Psychological Sciences and Techniques - class L-24 under the previous regulations and have not completed the professional training activities corresponding to 10 CFU of TPV may request recognition of activities completed and certified during the Bachelor's Degree course, according to the procedures defined in the Didactic Regulations.
In case of total or partial non-recognition of CFU, Bachelor's Degree graduates must acquire the missing internship CFU in addition to the 120 CFU of the Master's Degree.
Verification of personal preparation is mandatory and can only be accessed by students possessing the required academic qualifications.
The adequacy of personal preparation is verified through analysis of the study curriculum, using the weighted average of all exams in the student's study plan and exams taken in the Scientific Disciplinary Areas M-PSI/07 and/or M-PSI/08.

Autonomy of judgment (making judgements)
The course provides both conceptual and operational tools to acquire the ability to select and apply, with a critical and conscious approach, appropriate methods and techniques, as well as to interpret data in the various fields of clinical psychology, health, and well-being to enable independent analysis and judgment. Through participation in TPV, exercises, and interactive teaching activities (applied work projects, individual and group), both on the different theoretical and practical positions regarding the specific topics covered and on the main ethical and professional guidelines for psychologists, the development of the ability to adopt and adapt one's own intervention model and apply it fully autonomously with contextual sensitivity will be fostered. These competencies will be assessed at various stages of the training path: during the course through exercises and progress exams, and at the final stage of the course through the practical evaluation test (PPV) and the final exam.

Entry Orientation The Master's Degree Course in Clinical and Health Psychology offers to its students, both currently enrolled and potentially interested in enrollment, an integrated orientation service, which provides targeted actions for entry orientation, in-course orientation, and exit orientation, understood as placement (internal transition, towards a third-level training path) and as job placement, genuine out-placement towards the profession.
In detail, the service involves coordination with the University's Central Orientation Division and with the services activated within it, with periodic public presentations of the educational offer, to which students graduating from the Bachelor's Degree in Psychological Sciences and Techniques are invited, in the context of vertical university orientation, corresponding to the 3+2 cycles.
Constant monitoring of competencies expressed by students is carried out, to support them towards suitable Master's Degree paths, with periodic information actions on the internal educational offer but also on that of the entire national territory.
The Course of Study, in collaboration with the Master's Degree Course of Study in Psychology, organizes on an annual basis an orientation meeting for graduating/graduated students from the Bachelor's Degree in Psychological Sciences and Techniques, with the aim of presenting the Course of Study, in all its main characteristics, from the educational offer, to employment opportunities, to the presentation of the entry selection process. These meetings, with a highly participatory format, aim to answer questions from incoming students and allow them to make a conscious and mature choice of the Master's Course of Study.
Orientation activities are also carried out, on request, at secondary schools in the territory.
Finally, the educational offer is presented at the annual Night of Researchers event and during the orientation fairs to which the university is invited to participate.
Entry orientation is coordinated by an orientation coordinator, Prof. Michela Cortini, appointed by the Chair of the Course of Study.
In-course orientation is carried out by all professors of the Course of Study during office hours and aims to support students in organizing their studies and resolving any difficulties. Additionally, tutor professors are available for students to request an individual tutoring service, agreeing on the method of implementation.
All orientation activities (entry, in-course, and exit) take into account the monitoring of academic careers and employment prospects carried out periodically by the Chair of the Course of Study and the AQ group.

Graduate Opinions From the analysis of the 2022 graduate profile (source AlmaLaurea), it emerges that 86.4% of graduates regularly attended at least half of the courses. The majority of 2022 graduates consider the study load adequate (89.2%), declare satisfaction with the relationship with professors (97.2%), and express overall satisfaction with the degree course (96%). 85.2% of graduates considered the exam organization satisfactory. Infrastructure evaluation shows the following: classrooms adequate to the course needs (84.4%), equipment for laboratory activities and practical experiences adequate to the purpose (77.7% of 46% of graduates who stated they used them), adequate computer workstations (60.7% of 31.8% of graduates who stated they used them). For 94.8% of graduates (of the 55% who used them), the services offered by libraries are evaluated positively. Periodically, within the framework of the Study Course Council, the results of the graduate opinion survey are adequately analyzed and discussed.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding (applying knowledge and understanding)
The course provides the ability to critically apply acquired knowledge and techniques to carry out interventions, at individual and group levels, in different clinical psychological settings, in relation to situations of psychological distress, crisis, and maladjustment. Specifically, graduates must be able to: - conduct clinical interviews and psychological diagnostic evaluations; identify the most appropriate tools in relation to the context and clientele; plan and carry out clinical, preventive, and rehabilitation interventions, also in collaboration with professionals from other disciplines; design and carry out monitoring and evaluation activities for interventions. The tools used to develop and foster the ability to apply knowledge and understanding are the TPV, guided practical exercises, and interactive teaching activities. The acquisition of these abilities will be verified through: - a practical evaluation test (PPV) of professional skills acquired with the TPV for the purpose of professional qualification, which precedes the thesis discussion; - passing exams; - evaluation of laboratory teaching activities.

Learning Skills (learning skills)
Graduates at the end of the study path will acquire good individual study skills, self-assessment and self-reflection abilities, and awareness of their level of skills and knowledge. These competencies will enable adequate realization of their professional practice, facilitating the choice of further professional training paths aimed at promoting a high-value continuous education. The teaching tools to achieve these goals will be: supervised activities during the TPV, individual and interactive study activities, interim assessments, and supervision in thesis writing. The acquisition of these abilities will be verified through the PPV, the results of passing exams, monitoring of laboratory and interactive teaching activities, as well as the evaluation of the final thesis.

Knowledge and Understanding (knowledge and understanding)
Graduates must acquire knowledge and understanding related to theoretical and methodological content in clinical and dynamic psychology, which will facilitate the identification of relevant themes in the sector and their connection to disciplines present in the curriculum. Graduates must demonstrate the acquisition of: - advanced knowledge of theoretical models and methodologies of the sciences of human behavior, with particular reference to dysfunctional psychological processes, individual and interpersonal, and their cognitive, emotional, and behavioral correlates; - knowledge and skills for planning and carrying out diagnostic evaluations and clinical, preventive, and rehabilitation interventions for individuals and groups, in different life stages, in various public and private contexts. The acquisition of knowledge and understanding occurs through participation in frontal lectures and in-depth seminars, supplemented by individual and interactive study activities, and the writing of the supervised final thesis. The aim is to reach a deep understanding that will allow the generalization and transfer of theories and techniques in the various contexts of clinical and health psychology intervention. The achievement of these educational goals will be evaluated through passing exams for each course, approval of laboratory activities, and thesis evaluation.

The bodies and organizations involved in the AQ process of the degree course, with reference to their composition, skills, and assigned responsibilities, are described below:

The Coordinator of the AQ Group is responsible for: - coordinating activities; - maintaining direct relationships with the Departmental AQ Referee, the University Quality Office, the Evaluation Committee, and the Parity Commission of Teachers-Students; - periodically updating the Course Director on the progress of the degree course's AQ.

Members of the AQ Group are responsible for: - supervising the implementation of AQ within the degree course; - monitoring indicators for continuous process control and improvement; - promoting a quality culture within the degree course; - planning and controlling the efficiency of contextual services.

The AQ Group also carries out monitoring and self-evaluation activities of the educational path to identify strengths and weaknesses to be reported within the degree course. These activities are aimed at designing corrective and preventive actions for identified issues and implementing improvement plans to be proposed to the Course Director and the Course Council.

Course Council: Discusses and approves activities carried out by the AQ Group; collaborates in the proper functioning of the degree course's AQ.

Brief Description of Related and Complementary Activities
Related and complementary activities, present in the study path of the degree course in Clinical and Health Psychology, are aimed at acquiring knowledge that contributes to defining the interdisciplinary nature of clinical psychology, which, in the study of the mind and behavior, is characterized by proximity to other scientific and professional fields.

These activities contribute to the educational goal of an adequate framework: a) of knowledge of theoretical models of the sciences of human behavior, aimed at understanding and explaining dysfunctional mental processes, individual and interpersonal, and their reorganization, with particular attention to the most relevant psychopathogenetic models, including psychobiological ones; b) of knowledge of the main clinical pictures associated with different life stages in neuro- and psychopathological, psychosomatic disorders, and mental disorders associated with medical conditions, in an integrated multidimensional (bio-psychosocial) perspective.

Course Description
The Master's Degree in Clinical and Health Psychology (LM-51) aims to provide specialized knowledge of theoretical and methodological content of intervention and research in the clinical and dynamic psychological field, with the intent of training professional figures who will operate in various areas of psychological health.

It aims to provide adequate training to continue study and research activities independently or with a high level of responsibility in identifying goals and learning strategies, thus laying the foundation for access to a third-level specialist training (schools of specialization in Clinical Psychology, Health Psychology, Psychological Assessment and Counseling, Neuropsychology, and Life Cycle Psychology, which also qualify for psychotherapy practice; research doctorate after passing a competitive exam; master's and advanced courses). Additionally, it constitutes a distinctive educational path that prioritizes subsequent specialization in psychotherapy through recognized schools (Law n. 56/89).

Graduates in Clinical and Health Psychology can register with the A professional register of Psychologists and will be able to operate independently in professional practice using clinical approaches, methods, and techniques.

The Master's program in Clinical and Health Psychology adheres to the guidelines proposed by Europsy regarding the curriculum suggestions for the second level (corresponding to the Master's degree), concerning the preparation of students for independent professional practice as psychologists, where the clinical and health area constitutes a specific professional area, differentiated from others (school or education; work and organizations). Europsy also suggests that the knowledge and specialized skills to be acquired, as well as internship activities and basic research skills, come from specific educational curricula. It is noted that the evaluation to activate a specific and different Master's degree in the clinical-health field is supported by the increasing number of Psychology students directed towards occupational dimensions in both clinical-cure and health and well-being.

External Effectiveness
Based on the employment data published by AlmaLaurea for 2022, the employment rate one year after graduation is 36.4%. This percentage should be considered in light of the fact that the degree course in Clinical and Health Psychology (like all Psychology degree courses), before Law n. 163/2021 (Provisions on university qualifications), included a one-year training internship after graduation followed by a professional qualification exam.

Three years after graduation, the employment rate rises to 62.6%, and five years to 73%. Additionally, five years after graduation, job satisfaction is at a good level (average score of 8.2 on a scale from 1 to 10).

Reasons for Establishing Multiple Courses in the Class
Psychology has always been characterized, since its origins, as a varied and articulated set of multiple 'psychologies', based on very different theoretical constructs and methodological practices. This eclectic nature of psychology has, over time, manifested in different psychological professional roles, each characterized by its own operational specificity requiring a specific and distinct training.

Considering the above differentiation, distinctive of psychology and its related professional roles, it is proposed to activate two different Master's degree courses belonging to the same class, named respectively Psychology and Clinical and Health Psychology, to offer two specific educational and professional training paths. The Psychology degree course is directed towards understanding psychological processes—cognitive, emotional, and social—that characterize mental functioning at both individual and group levels, while the Clinical and Health Psychology degree course is more directed towards intervention in situations of psychological distress and suffering. Based on these distinct purposes, the curricula of the two courses refer to different theoretical and methodological premises, more formative and general in the first case and more applied and experiential in the second.

In accordance with DM 270, it is considered that offering two distinct courses more effectively responds to the specialist nature of the Master's degree, allowing the training of different professional roles that will have an easier access to the job market, while also providing a more targeted preparatory foundation for the third level of training, consisting of specialized schools, master's, and doctoral courses. In particular, the specific degree course prepares for entry into specialized schools in Clinical Psychology and Health Psychology. Additionally, it constitutes a distinctive educational path that prioritizes subsequent specialization in psychotherapy through schools recognized by the Ministry (Law n. 56/89).

Furthermore, the proposal arises from the consideration regarding the reorganization project for the three-year degree course in Psychological Sciences, which aims to provide basic training, eliminating specific curricula and not considering professional training objectives.

Finally, it is emphasized that the project of two differentiated and autonomous Master's paths adheres to the guidelines proposed by Europsy regarding the curriculum suggestions for the second level (corresponding to the Master's degree), concerning the preparation of students for independent professional practice as psychologists, where the clinical and health area is differentiated and distinct from others (education and work). Europsy suggests that the knowledge and specialized skills to be acquired, as well as internship activities and basic research skills, come from specific educational curricula.

It is also noted that the evaluation to activate a specific and different Master's degree is supported by organizational issues arising from the high number of enrolled students, which would cause difficulties in a single course with multiple specializations, both didactic (e.g., duplication of courses) and formative.

Specific Educational Objectives and Description of the Educational Path
The Master's Degree in Clinical and Health Psychology aims to provide specialized knowledge of theoretical and methodological content of intervention and research in the clinical and dynamic psychological field, with the intent of training professional figures who will operate in various areas of psychological health. The educational path aims to provide both advanced knowledge and skills; regarding knowledge, it aims to foster the development of: - advanced knowledge of basic theoretical models and methodologies of the sciences of human behavior, aimed at exploring, explaining, interpreting, and reorganizing dysfunctional mental processes, individual and interpersonal (with particular attention to the most relevant psychopathological-clinical phenomena) and their behavioral and psychobiological correlates; - basic knowledge of the history of clinical psychology, psychopathology, and psychotherapy; - knowledge of forms of distress in different life stages, as well as adaptive reactions (coping in psychological crisis); - knowledge of main psychological practices in the field of clinical psychology, with particular reference to counseling, diagnosis, therapy, and treatment of organizational psychology, individual and group, in its problematic aspects as well as its interpersonal, social, and psychosomatic outcomes; - knowledge of main psychological practices in forensic psychology, with particular reference to technical consultation and expert opinion in civil and criminal matters; - basic knowledge of behavioral and psychological complications of internal and metabolic diseases and organ pathologies throughout the life cycle (with particular reference to their psychological impact on family and social contexts); - knowledge of theoretical models and methodologies of research in neuroscience, with particular reference to molecular and functional mechanisms of physiological (aging) and pathological (dementia) cognitive decline, as well as neurodegenerative diseases; - basic knowledge of neuropsychopharmacology principles; - knowledge of genetic and biological foundations necessary for acquiring specific psychological assistance tools in pathologies with a prevalence of such components (genetic, constitutional, and temperamental); - knowledge of different models of the psychologist/client/patient relationship and related issues of alliance in its different forms (work, diagnostic, and specifically therapeutic); - knowledge of verbal and non-verbal communication processes; - knowledge of ethical dimensions and deontological issues, shared and supported by the professional community; - knowledge of main research methodologies in the field of evaluation, treatment, and care of mental states and dysfunctional and pathological systems.

The advanced skills to be acquired are: - recognize and regulate cognitive and emotional processes associated with different forms of distress in interaction with: clients/patients; - detect, using appropriate tools, alterations in personality characteristics, cognitive functioning, emotional and affective attitudes, and interpersonal relationships; - develop appropriate awareness of the emotional and motivational implications underlying the choice of the psychological profession, valuing them in clinical relationships; - communicate effectively with clients/patients in different phases of interventions, referring to institutional, sociocultural, and gender dimensions; - evaluate and identify different forms of preventive, therapeutic, and rehabilitative treatment; - develop skills related to educational, preventive, rehabilitative, and therapeutic interventions in the helping relationship, in different forms of distress and disability throughout the life cycle.

These educational objectives will be achieved through characteristic educational activities related to Clinical and Dynamic Psychology, General and Physiological Psychology, Work and Organizational Psychology, and related and complementary activities aimed at completing the professional profile through the in-depth of advanced themes in line with market needs.

The educational path, structured over two years, includes the following types of educational activities: classroom lectures, practical evaluation internship (TPV), individual or small group study, seminars led by professionals working in services, study stays at other European universities (within the Erasmus program) or extra-European (within bilateral agreements between the University d'Annunzio and foreign partners) to foster the development of solid skills for professional practice.

Within the professional training activities, 20 university credit points (CFU) are acquired through the completion of the TPV, internal to the degree course. The TPV consists of contextualized and supervised practical activities, involving direct observation and execution of activities aimed at situated learning and the development of fundamental procedural and relational skills for professional practice. These skills refer to typical and reserved acts of the psychologist profession, also as per Article 1 of Law 18 February 1989, n. 56, and include the use of knowledge and intervention tools for prevention, diagnosis, rehabilitation, support in psychological contexts for individuals, groups, social organizations, and communities, as well as research, experimentation, and teaching activities.

The TPV activities of the degree course relate to the specific specialist area of clinical and health psychology. In particular, the TPV is aimed at developing psychodiagnostic skills, elaboration of diagnostic reports and feedback to clients, clinical interview and observation practices, implementation of rehabilitation interventions, promotion of health, and prevention of risk behaviors, realization of psychological intervention projects, evaluation of intervention processes and outcomes, and communication with clients and colleagues. The TPV is passed by obtaining a final suitability judgment.

Within the path, there is also the enhancement of English language skills (level B2) with particular reference to the specific terminology of psychological disciplines, through a specific course and guided reading of international articles. Finally, the preparation of the thesis, of empirical or critical analysis of theoretical models, provides the opportunity to demonstrate the level of learning achieved on a specific topic.

Opinions of Entities and Companies with Internship Agreements
Regarding the post-graduation internship required by the previous regulations, there are 791 agreements with 791 companies (updated as of September 2023), both public and private, distributed throughout the national territory, allowing students a wider choice.

The constant contact between the degree course and internship structures is guaranteed by the presence of a dedicated Secretariat Service (also through the activation of a dedicated email address) and a Teaching Coordinator for internships. This figure is responsible for collecting reports from companies and interns and reporting them to the Parity Commission for Internships (Ordine degli Psicologi - University 'G. d'Annunzio') and the Course Council, with the general objective of ensuring the quality of the internship.

Since 2021, an online monitoring and evaluation system has been implemented to assess interns' opinions on the educational activities. The questionnaire consists of a general first part, requesting the academic year of graduation, sociodemographic information (gender, age, and region of residence), and satisfaction regarding organizational/administrative aspects related to the internship experience, concerning the "Internships" section of the University's website and the Internship Offices.

Regarding the internship experience, information is requested on the time period, host organization, areas of activity (e.g., clinical and community psychology; developmental psychology, etc.), mode of activity execution (remote work, in-person, hybrid), and satisfaction regarding integration with the work group or availability of work spaces and tools. Additional questions are included regarding the characteristics of the activities performed (e.g., clarity, required effort, variety of activities), the link between university studies and the development of practical skills gained through the internship (e.g., improvement of study methods, acquisition of more operational preparation, understanding of professional work methods), and skills acquired during the internship (e.g., problem-solving, decision-making, communication, teamwork).

A final section focuses on analyzing how the internship experience has been useful for students to clarify aspects related to post-graduation training and future career choices.

From the analysis of responses provided by interns who participated in the survey from May 2021 to August 2023 (see attached file), overall satisfaction with the activities performed during the internship and the availability of mentors is evident. The data will be discussed in the Course Council and then in the Parity Commission for Internships.

Regarding the evaluation of opinions from entities and companies about hosted interns, the Parity Commission for Internships (Ordine degli Psicologi - University 'G. d'Annunzio') is currently studying the design of a similar online monitoring and evaluation system, also in relation to the new provisions introduced by the activation of the new qualifying path under Law n. 163/2021 – "Provisions on university qualifications" – which requires the internship to be carried out during the degree course.

Summary of the Regional Coordination Committee's Opinion
The Committee, having examined the proposal for the establishment of the aforementioned educational initiative and considering that it aims to train professional figures who will operate in various areas of psychological health, and that graduates in clinical and health psychology can register with the professional register of psychologists and operate in various institutional, public, and private contexts, unanimously approves it.

The President, in presenting the course, notes that graduates in Clinical and Health Psychology can register with the professional register of psychologists and operate independently in professional practice.

Consultation as per Article 11, paragraph 4 of DM n. 270 of October 22, 2004, is carried out. Following a thorough examination, the consultation is positive.

In the last academic year, in preparation to restart consultation with representative organizations of goods and service production and professions, the following documentation was consulted:

- APA document: Guidelines and Principles for Accreditation of Programs in Professional Psychology;

- Guidelines provided by the Academic Psychology Conference (CPA) and the European Federation of Psychological Associations (EFPA);

- EuroPsy-T document and the subsequent reference framework of the European Diploma in Psychology (EuroPsy);

- White paper on psychological professions prepared by the Organizational and Consumer Culture Laboratory of the Catholic University of Milan for the National Council of Psychologists;

- Market survey on professional psychology in Italy. New Needs, New Areas, New Roles, ENPAP.

From the analysis of some of these documents, important suggestions emerged regarding the reorientation and expansion of the psychologist profession, which seems possible only through a change in approach to the market and the profession itself. The report suggests that to build the psychologist profession in new areas, it will be necessary to overcome certain limiting conditions that hinder, according to research, growth potential, such as: a passive and non-proactive role interpretation, difficulty working in teams with other specialists, and low responsiveness to emerging social dynamics.

The scenario described in the ENPAP market survey report is encouraging for the future of psychologists, as, thanks to the credibility built in recent years, these figures have the authority to respond to the demand for support in addressing the precarity induced by the current crisis and to actively enter the open demand areas, including psychological well-being. In this area, "the psychologist should tend to become a facilitator for achieving a specific, desired concrete goal, related to: quality of life, acquisition of rules and techniques to face daily challenges, the union between theory and practice to free oneself from behaviors, thoughts, and actions that hinder emotional balance; and also tend to become a tutor for targeted, flexible, and continuous listening and support in: personal growth and psycho-physical health; acquisition of methods and practices in an exploratory perspective; synergy with other disciplines or approaches (mental and physical) to achieve greater self-awareness and harmonization of relationships in different areas" (see pages 42 and following of the Market Survey on Professional Psychology in Italy. New Needs, New Areas, New Roles, ENPAP).

In line with these suggestions and with the intent to make the degree course more consistent with new socio-cultural and professional needs, the Course Director, in collaboration with the AQ group, proposed to make organizational changes, also establishing an Advisory Committee composed of members of the Course Council and recognized interested parties.
