Ability to apply knowledge and understanding (applying knowledge and understanding)
The Master's graduate in Health Professions of Rehabilitation Sciences will be able to:
- use at least one European Union language besides Italian, with reference also to disciplinary lexicons (CI English);
- identify environmental risk factors, evaluate their effects on health, and plan protective and primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention interventions in work environments (CI Prevention and diagnosis of congenital disabilities I and II; CI Community Medicine);
- examine patients by selecting innovative rehabilitation intervention strategies and administering valid and reliable tests, scales for evaluation related to age and disability/impairment (CI Prevention and diagnosis of congenital disabilities I and II; CI Therapy of congenital and acquired disabilities I and II);
- design and implement, in collaboration with other professionals, educational and support interventions for the individual and the community for self-management and control of risk factors and health issues (CI Community Medicine; CI Therapy of congenital and acquired disabilities I and II);
- conduct systematic bibliographic research and literature reviews, also through databases and their periodic updates, in order to produce scientific articles and disability registers (CI Methodology of teaching and research in rehabilitation; laboratories and elective activities);
- collaborate on quantitative and qualitative research projects and verify the application of research results for continuous improvement of rehabilitation activities (CI Methodology of teaching and research in rehabilitation; laboratories and elective activities);
- coordinate simple and complex organizations using tools and measures for planning, human resource management, and accounting in business economics (CI Programming, organization and control of health companies; internship);
- apply knowledge to analyze work processes in health organizations, personnel management strategies, and professional accreditation systems in order to promote the integration of rehabilitation teams in services for achieving safe, effective, efficient, relevant, culturally sensitive, appropriately documented, and competent personnel (CI Programming, organization and control of health companies; internship);
- apply knowledge on interpersonal relationships in the work environment to harmonize the contribution of different professionalities engaged in rehabilitation (CI Programming, organization and control of health companies; internship);
- monitor and critically evaluate the evolution of rehabilitation needs and plan therapeutic interventions in the rehabilitation field of the belonging class (CI Diagnostic-therapeutic pathways of sensory abilities; CI Diagnostic-therapeutic pathways of psycho-neuromotricity; internship);
- collaborate with the care team to implement and develop protocols and guidelines (CI Diagnostic-therapeutic pathways of sensory abilities; CI Diagnostic-therapeutic pathways of psycho-neuromotricity; internship; laboratories and elective activities);
- apply leadership and management theories to develop collaborative alliances between different health professions in their work context (internship; stage; laboratories and elective activities);
- apply pedagogical knowledge and theories of experiential learning to carry out teaching, tutoring, and training design activities (internship; stage; laboratories and elective activities);
- apply structured patient and disability/impairment evaluation systems in rehabilitation practice (internship; stage; laboratories and elective activities);
- apply theoretical, operational, and research models to the specific rehabilitation field (internship; stage; laboratories and elective activities);
- apply evidence-based practice methodology to evaluate the effectiveness of rehabilitation treatments (internship; stage; laboratories and elective activities);
- participate in and observe management, conduct, and programming processes of a three-year and Master's degree course, master's degree level I and II (internship; stage; laboratories and elective activities);
- participate in the design and management of teaching activities within continuous training for rehabilitation professionals (internship; stage; laboratories and elective activities);
- synthesize functional diagnosis data and analyze them to issue clinical rehabilitation judgments regarding patient management (internship; stage; laboratories and elective activities);
- use effectiveness and efficiency indicators considering potential ethical, legal, and deontological implications that may arise in rehabilitation practice (internship; stage; laboratories and elective activities);
- assume responsibility for the quality of their professional practice (internship; stage; laboratories and elective activities);
- critically evaluate published studies related to clinical rehabilitation intervention, organizational process management, human resource management, training, and research, and demonstrate the ability to apply them to professional choices (internship; stage; laboratories and elective activities);
- prepare a CV, face a selection interview, and manage employment contracts (laboratories and elective activities).
The teaching tools aimed at achieving the above abilities include lectures, small group case discussions with presentations in plenary sessions, seminars, laboratories, elective activities, guided and individual study.
These abilities will be assessed through written and/or oral certification exams, practical tests, and reports.
Learning skills (learning skills)
Master's graduates in Health Professions of Rehabilitation Sciences will be able to:
- evaluate their performance based on professional practice standards and organizational criteria, continuously identifying their educational needs in relation to the nature and complexity of problems to be addressed and the design and operational strategies to be managed, in order to realize their professional improvement plan;
- independently adopt effective strategies to continue learning throughout their professional life, both formally and informally, through further training paths;
- attend further higher education training paths oriented towards the profession, research, health management, and educational methodology;
- use complete information systems, software, and databases to collect, organize, and catalog information, identify a problem, conduct a literature review on the topic, critically analyze the problem and current knowledge, develop a strategy to apply research in practice, and facilitate the dissemination of research results.
Learning abilities will be acquired during the two-year path through lectures, stage, seminars with in-depth projects, and individual study activities as part of the research methodology and evidence-based rehabilitation methodology, and activities carried out in preparation for the thesis.
Verification of these abilities occurs through the formulation of the research problem, data collection based on the analyzed context, evaluation of the collected evidence, integration between collection and the formulated problem/question, and evaluation of the entire process by querying databases and critically analyzing international scientific publications.
University communication to CUN It is noted that the English translation of the term Scienze della Riabilitazione delle Professioni Sanitarie, or Health Professions of Rehabilitation Sciences, is not perfectly consistent with the Italian definition. It is proposed to modify the translation to Rehabilitation Sciences of Health Professions.
It is also noted that the ISTAT code that the system allowed us to insert does not perfectly match the professional profile of the present activation project.
Knowledge and understanding (knowledge and understanding)
The Master's graduate in Health Professions of Rehabilitation Sciences:
- knows at least one European Union language besides Italian, with reference also to disciplinary lexicons (CI Additional linguistic knowledge etc.);
- knows and understands the principles and methods of general and applied hygiene, risk factors for work-related injuries and diseases (chemical, physical, biological, and psychosocial agents), and principles and methods of primary health care (CI Community Medicine);
- knows and understands the causes and environmental and genetic factors predisposing to congenital disabilities (CI Prevention and diagnosis of congenital disabilities I and II);
- knows and understands the principles, methods, and therapeutic strategies (acupuncture, osteopathy, hippotherapy, etc.) to be used for rehabilitation and prevention of congenital and acquired disabilities (CI Therapy of congenital and acquired disabilities I and II);
- knows and interprets epidemiological and experimental statistics data to analyze complex phenomena and problems in health and in the specific rehabilitation professional profile (CI Methodology of teaching and research in rehabilitation);
- knows and deepens didactic and tutorial methodologies to implement different teaching strategies motivated by educational theories and evidence-based practices (CI Methodology of teaching and research in rehabilitation);
- knows the training needs of rehabilitation professions (CI Methodology of teaching and research in rehabilitation);
- knows and understands the organization of health systems, including European ones, planning and funding modalities, as well as the organization of rehabilitation services (CI Programming, organization and control of health companies);
- knows and interprets the principles of health, administrative, and labor law to understand their application in managing health services, work processes, and professional relationships (CI Programming, organization and control of health companies);
- knows the diagnostic maneuvers and therapeutic procedures regarding sensory disabilities (CI Diagnostic-therapeutic pathways of sensory abilities);
- knows the diagnostic maneuvers and therapeutic procedures of virtual medicine, robotics, and tele-rehabilitation regarding psycho-neuromotricity (CI Diagnostic-therapeutic pathways of psycho-neuromotricity).
The above knowledge and understanding abilities will be acquired through attendance at lectures, laboratories, seminars, elective activities, and guided and autonomous personal study. Verification of learning outcomes will primarily occur through oral and/or written exams, in-course or final, and written elaborations with in-depth research on acquired knowledge.
Organization and responsibility of AQ at the Course of Study Level The bodies and organizations involved in the CdS AQ process are as follows:
1. Joint Teaching-Student Committee: carries out monitoring activities on the educational offer and the quality of teaching and services provided to students by teachers and teaching structures.
2. Departmental Teaching AQ Representative (ReAQD-D): supports and monitors AQ processes related to the Department and the Courses of Study attached to it.
3. CdS Council: discusses and approves the review report; collaborates in the smooth operation of CdS AQ.
4. CdS Chairperson: coordinates the CdS AQ system and oversees compliance with obligations set by regulations, with the collaboration of the Joint Committee and the review group, in line with what is indicated by the University's central bodies on AQ.
5. AQ/Review Group of CdS: prepares the review report, analyzing the current situation of the CdS, highlighting strengths and improvement opportunities, and proposing corresponding objectives, indicators, and targets/values.
Brief description of related and complementary activities The related and complementary activities activated and/or to be activated are aimed at acquiring knowledge, skills, and abilities functionally related to the cultural and professional profile identified by the Master's Degree Course. Among the educational objectives of the CdS is the training of professional figures capable of designing primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention interventions. The related and complementary activities activated or to be activated contribute to achieving this objective by providing knowledge related to the causes and incidence of congenital disabilities and the currently available neonatal screening tests in Italy and/or abroad.
Another area that may be included as a related and complementary activity will be related to the psychopedagogical and training area and will allow the implementation of new forms of learning and didactic experimentation.
Brief course description The Master's Degree Course in Health Professions of Rehabilitation Sciences of the Gabriele d'Annunzio University of Chieti-Pescara belongs to the School of Medicine and Health Sciences and is a two-year, limited-enrollment course that responds to the need to offer innovative and up-to-date cultural and professional training to graduates of three-year Rehabilitation Health Professions (class L/SNT2) (podiatrist, physiotherapist, speech therapist, neuro- and psycho-motor therapist for children, orthoptist–ophthalmology assistant, psychiatric and psychosocial rehabilitation educator, occupational therapist, professional educator) focused on rehabilitation prevention aspects, technological innovation, and alignment with European standards for rehabilitation professionals.
The Master's graduate will therefore be able to: i) monitor and critically evaluate the evolution of rehabilitation needs and plan therapeutic interventions in the rehabilitation field of the belonging class; ii) identify environmental risk factors, evaluate their effects on health, and plan protective interventions in work environments; iii) conduct systematic bibliographic research and collaborate on research projects; iv) participate in the design and management of teaching activities within continuous training for rehabilitation professionals; v) coordinate simple and complex organizations using tools and measures for planning and human resource management in business economics.
To acquire these competencies, the Master's Degree Course in Health Professions of Rehabilitation Sciences provides: i) a limited-enrollment, English-language entrance test (required level: QCER B2); ii) common training for all students on topics related to the characterizing scientific sectors, such as Medical and Applied Technical Sciences, Robotics, Telemedicine and tele-rehabilitation, and in sectors of Medicine related to medical and biomedical disciplines such as Embryology, Medical Genetics, Child Neuropsychiatry, Electronic and Computer Bioengineering; iii) specific training more focused on professionalization divided into 4 training areas: 1) professional area; 2) health management area for public, private, and accredited private sectors; 3) research area; 4) teaching and training area. These specific training areas will be the subject of laboratory activities, elective activities, and professional internships, providing Master's graduates with competencies in particularly sought-after labor market sectors or particularly advanced for rehabilitation technologies (robotics, mirror therapy, etc.) or for managerial strategies (innovation management), didactic (Problem-Based Learning, flipped classroom, etc.), or research (functional magnetic resonance, neonatal screening, etc.).
Internship activities will be carried out within public or private health structures, teaching structures, rehabilitation and prevention centers, departments, and research laboratories belonging to the G. d'Annunzio University.
Employment opportunities The Master's graduate in Health Professions of Rehabilitation Sciences finds placement in the National and Regional Health System (SS.SS.), following a competition, in private accredited structures and contracted with the S.S.N. (Clinics, structures and centers for rehabilitation, Residential Health Care Facilities, thermal resorts and wellness centers, medical and/or multi-specialty outpatient clinics), IRCCS, university and extra-university research centers where managerial, applied research, and training competencies are required.
Access to positions in public structures (S.S.N., Universities, etc.) is subject to passing a competitive examination.
The possession of the Master's Degree is a legally and contractually required prerequisite for roles in the S.S.N. (L. 43/2006) for managerial and teaching positions and to hold the role of Director of Professional Teaching for three-year and/or Master's Degree Courses in the specific area.
Post-graduation training The Master's Degree allows access to Doctoral Programs, following a competitive examination, at University Institutions. Among the numerous active Doctoral Programs at the G. d'Annunzio University of Chieti-Pescara, the Doctoral Program in Kinesiology can be mentioned, also due to the numerous international mobility agreements.
Level of internationalization The Master's Degree Course in Health Professions of Rehabilitation Sciences will be the first LM/SNT2 course in Italy taught in English, and since the Master's degree title is recognized throughout Europe (EU Directive 2005/36), currently subject to a recognition procedure, Master's graduates will be able to access professional roles reserved for European Master's graduates such as Director of Rehabilitation (DOR), Executive Leader, Research Scientist, Usability Specialist. The internationalization of the CdS will be guaranteed by the presence in the Steering Committee of the University Erasmus Delegate and an international partner belonging to the INGENIUM network, by the international relations of the reference teachers, and by the numerous Erasmus agreements and conventions concluded by the DMSI, DSMOB, and, in general, by the University with foreign Institutions.
The attachment contains data on the high levels of employability at the national level as evidenced by the SMA indicators.
Specific educational objectives of the course and description of the training path The Master's Degree Course is structured over 2 years and 4 semesters and provides a total of 120 CFU between delivered teaching (DE), interactive teaching (DI) (group presentations, discussion tables, and role-playing), and self-learning activities. The Course includes 9 mandatory integrated courses (CI) and 6 single-discipline courses, including 1 English language course, 2 student-selected teaching courses, 2 professional internship courses, laboratories, and the final exam. As provided for by Article 10, paragraph 5, letters a), c), d), e), of Ministerial Decree 22 October 2004, n. 270, the training activities have the following CFU: 6 for student choice; 9 for the final exam and English language; 5 for other activities such as computer science, laboratories, etc.; 30 for the training internship and stage. Attendance is mandatory at 70% for CIs and single-discipline courses and at 100% for professional internships and Laboratories.
The Master's graduate in Health Professions of Rehabilitation Sciences is a professional figure with broad, multidisciplinary, and integrated competencies, able to seamlessly integrate into the world of work and high-specialization professions in the health sector. The identified training areas will allow the Master's graduate to successfully integrate into the prevention of primary disabilities, neurosciences and psycho-neuromotricity, public and private health management, research, teaching, and community medicine.
The functions performed in each of these areas include:
1. design of primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention interventions
2. design of neuropsychomotor rehabilitation interventions using advanced technologies
3. design and coordination of public and private health management activities and community hospitals
4. design of teaching and training activities.
Graduates will possess the necessary knowledge to carry out the above professional activities in hospital and non-hospital settings (Community Hospitals and Rehabilitation Departments) public, private, and private accredited, in specialist outpatient clinics, in care homes or elderly care facilities, in public health services, fitness and mental health centers, maternal and child departments, occupational medicine.
Additionally, the solid technical-scientific preparation will allow the Master's graduate to update their knowledge and contribute to teaching and research activities in the public and private sectors.
The specific educational objectives are firmly anchored to those of class LM/SNT2:
- Know and be able to use at least one European Union language besides Italian, with reference also to disciplinary lexicons.
- Identify environmental risk factors, evaluate their effects on health, and plan protective interventions in work environments.
- Conduct systematic bibliographic research and literature reviews, also through databases and their periodic updates, in order to produce scientific articles and disability registers.
- Collaborate on quantitative and qualitative research projects and verify the application of research results for continuous improvement of rehabilitation activities.
- Coordinate simple and complex organizations using tools and measures for planning, human resource management, and accounting in business economics.
- Monitor and critically evaluate the evolution of rehabilitation needs and plan therapeutic interventions in the rehabilitation field of the belonging class.
- Collaborate with the care team to implement and develop protocols and guidelines.
- Participate in and observe management, conduct, and programming processes of a three-year and Master's degree course, master's degree level I and II.
- Participate in the design and management of teaching activities within continuous training for rehabilitation professionals.
- Design and implement, in collaboration with other professionals, educational and support interventions for the individual and the community for self-management and control of risk factors and health issues.
The high interdisciplinarity will be guaranteed by the variety of topics covered in both Laboratories, widely present, and Elective Activities, in order to ensure the attractiveness of the Course for the different professions belonging to class SNT2 but especially the acquisition of specific competencies and achievement of specific educational objectives.
From an organizational perspective, most lectures will be delivered ex cathedra, with frequent references to practical case studies, while Laboratories and Elective Activities will also experiment with innovative small-group teaching methods with the aim of promoting the active role of the student in the learning process in a socio-constructivist perspective where the teacher acts as a mediator to stimulate students to express themselves and collaborate, together building knowledge (role-playing, Problem-Based Learning, etc.).
The guided internship and stage activities at public specialized health services in Italy or abroad, linked by specific conventions, will complement the classroom teaching. Laboratory and internship activities will be carried out under the supervision and guidance of professional tutors, specifically designated and assigned to each student, coordinated by a teacher belonging to the highest training level for the specific profile.
Finally, extracurricular congresses and seminars will be integrated with the courses, carried out by rehabilitation professionals external to the teaching body, both at the level of public bodies (hospitals, health companies) and private bodies (conventioned rehabilitation structures and centers), who will address specific themes of interest for the different professions enrolled in the Master's Degree Course.
At the end of the study path, the Master's graduate will have acquired interdisciplinary and specific knowledge related to rehabilitation and attributable to their field of reference.
They will also have acquired some general abilities and competencies related to English language, common to all training areas, and especially to the offer and teaching methodology, including:
a) multiple professionalizing laboratories, also in small groups of students;
b) extracurricular congresses and seminars organized by societies and associations in the rehabilitation field as well as by external teachers not belonging to the University or coming from foreign or local, national, and/or international productive realities;
c) in-course and/or partial tests to facilitate students and allow teachers to verify students' preparation in real time.
The Course will develop the following general abilities in students:
i) ability to identify, formulate, and solve medium-complexity problems related to the chosen specific training;
ii) ability to retrieve, consult, and interpret scientific data published in major technical journals and national and international regulations;
iii) ability to update on methods, techniques, and tools in the field of the chosen training area;
iv) critical sense, autonomy of judgment, and independence of action;
v) ability to interact with health personnel and multidisciplinary teams to evaluate their technical, instrumental, and organizational needs and to propose the use of techniques, processes, and materials most suitable for their professional activity;
vi) ability to carry out teaching and training activities and collaborate on research, development, and experimentation activities in the public and private sector within their professional field, including the ability to undertake higher-level studies (such as Doctoral Programs).
Written and oral communication abilities will be developed and assessed during exam tests and even more during the internship-stage and preparatory training activities for the final elaboration.
In particular, the first year is aimed at providing the models and conceptual and methodological principles of two areas of competence of the Master's graduate:
- Management area: occupational medicine and business economics
- Professional area: prevention and diagnosis of congenital disabilities.
An internship and seminar experience in accredited services chosen by the student is planned to build a relevant improvement process in rehabilitation practice within the specific professional profile.
The second year is aimed at learning and applying the methodologies and knowledge of the Master's graduate, with specific reference to future work contexts:
- Research area: analysis of qualitative and quantitative research studies and training in deducing implications for rehabilitation practice, statistics, and epidemiology applied to the health, clinical, and social context of disability and the specific tasks of the belonging class. Research methodology for evidence-based health practice.
- Professional area: in-depth of the most relevant clinical and technological advances in the field of neurosciences and rehabilitation.
- Management area: in-depth of leadership and management strategies for rehabilitation services, human resource management, design of organizational integration tools, and quality performance evaluation.
- Training area: in-depth on design and management of basic and advanced training systems, teaching methods, management of training groups to activate specific training events for rehabilitation professions.
An internship experience in accredited services chosen by the student (Directors of Health Professions, Training Services, Research Centers, Quality Offices) is planned.
The training network of the CdS will include public (ASL) and private health structures and internal University structures that, with the tutors provided, will ensure the full success of the training project for the entire student cohort assigned to the site over the two years of the Course.

Parallel to the consultation of the IP, an analysis of the training demand was carried out by consulting regional, national, and international documents.
In particular, the following were consulted:
1. the annual reports of Prof. Angelo Mastrillo (2021/22 and 2022/23), from which an increase in the need for rehabilitation professionals and a D/P ratio of 2.4 is evident, considering all national Master's Degree Courses in Rehabilitation Sciences in the 2022/23 academic year (https://www.assocarenews.it/wp/wpcontent/uploads/2022/11/Report-Mastrillo-2022-23.pdf);
2. the Alma Laurea report of 2021 regarding Master's graduates of class SNT2 one year after graduation;
3. the Unioncamere – ANPAL report, Excelsior Information System, with Medium-Term Occupational Needs Forecast in Italy (quinquennium 2018-22);
4. the National Prevention Plan (PNP) 2020-25 (https://www.salute.gov.it/portale/news/p3_2_1_1_1.jsp?menu=notizie&id=50299);
5. the network for the prevention of congenital malformations (https://www.ccm-network.it/progetto.jsp?id=node/1988&idP=740);
6. Cochrane Rehabilitation, the global reference institution for the dissemination and production of scientific evidence in rehabilitation (https://rehabilitation.cochrane.org);
7. the Rehabilitation 2030 Initiative launched by WHO in February 2017 to facilitate and improve rehabilitation worldwide (https://www.who.int/initiatives/rehabilitation-2030);
8. the scientific work: Cieza A, Causev K, Kamenov K, Wulf Hanson S, Chatterji S, Vos T. Global estimates of the need for rehabilitation based on the Global Burden of Disease study 2019: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2019. The Lancet 2020, 396, 2006-2017.
All consulted documents showed an increased need for rehabilitation professionals and rehabilitation research both nationally and internationally.
Given that the increased need for rehabilitation is mainly the result of population growth and aging, in the Abruzzo Region, there is also a need for rehabilitation professionals due to the progressive aging of the population, despite the annual entry of trained professionals into the labor market by Abruzzo universities. According to data in the PRP 2020-25, in 2021, Abruzzo residents aged 65 or older were 316,000, representing 24.7% of the regional population.
The 93,000 over 80 represent 7.3% of the Abruzzo population.
Figures destined to increase in the coming years, considering that a large part of the residents are between 45 and 60 years old.

Characteristics of the final exam According to Article 5 of the Interministerial Decree of January 8, 2009, the final exam consists of writing an elaboration on the in-depth study of managerial, training, professional, and applied research topics. As provided for by Ministerial Decree 270/2004, the graduation exam is based on the dissertation of the thesis prepared by the student in an original manner under the guidance of a supervisor. The thesis can be experimental or theoretical-applied, and for its preparation, a co-supervisor teacher may be provided.
To be admitted to take the final exam, the student must have regularly attended, for the total hours required, the individual integrated courses, laboratories, and elective activities, passed all the required profit exams, and completed all the required training internships with a positive evaluation, certified.
Mode of conducting the final exam
1. The mode of conducting the final exam is regulated by Article 21 of the University Teaching Regulations. The exam consists of preparing, under the guidance of a supervisor, a thesis of experimental or theoretical-applied nature regarding the in-depth study of managerial, training, professional, and applied research topics and its dissertation. The presentation and discussion of the elaboration occur in English before a specific Commission.
2. The Graduation Commission is composed of a number of members ranging from 7 to 11. The Commission is appointed by a Rectoral Decree.
3. The evaluation of the thesis represents a comprehensive assessment of the ability to apply what has been learned in the various courses. The final exam requires the integration of acquired knowledge and the ability to bring new developments.
4. The final exam grade is expressed in hundredths (110) and derives from the sum of the base score, obtained from the arithmetic mean of the profit exams reported in hundredths, the score attributed to the thesis, and the score attributed to the entire study path. In particular, the evaluation of the thesis and the study path contribute to a score from 0 to 8 points as follows:
- quality of the dissertation from 0 to 3 points;
- content and methodology used from 0 to 3 points.
- participation in mobility paths 1 point
- ongoing degree 1 point The honor is awarded unanimously by the Commissioners to candidates who have achieved a total score of 113 and have had a path characterized by the presence of one or more honors.

Access Requirements Required knowledge for access To access the Course, it is necessary to hold a Three-year Degree in Letters (class L-10), or an equivalent title (Italian or foreign), or to hold a Degree obtained in another class with a minimum of 60 CFU acquired among the following SSD: L-FIL-LET/02, L-FIL-LET/04, L-FIL-LET/05, L-FIL-LET/06, L-FIL-LET/07, L-FIL-LET/08, L-FIL-LET/09, L-FIL-LET/10, L-FIL-LET/11, L-FIL-LET/12, L-FIL-LET/13, L-FIL-LET/14, L-LIN/01, L-LIN/02 L-ANT/02, L-ANT/03, M-STO/01, M-STO/02, M-STO/03, M-STO/04, M-STO/05, M-STO/08, M-STO/09. Admission to the Master's degree course is subject to passing an assessment of the suitability of personal preparation, which will be carried out according to the procedures defined in the admission procedures section. Additionally, adequate linguistic competences in a European Community language (level B1) will be verified.
Admission Procedures Admission to the Study Programme occurs following a mandatory assessment of the student's curriculum by the Pre-admission Committee. The Committee verifies the possession of curricular requirements, in particular the possession of 60 CFU acquired in the necessary SSD: L-FIL-LET/02, L-FIL-LET/04, L-FIL-LET/05, L-FIL-LET/06, L-FIL-LET/07, L-FIL-LET/08, L-FIL-LET/09, L-FIL-LET/10, L-FIL-LET/11, L-FIL-LET/12, L-FIL-LET/13, L-FIL-LET/14, L-LIN/01, L-LIN/02 L-ANT/02, L-ANT/03, M-STO/01, M-STO/02, M-STO/03, M-STO/04, M-STO/05, M-STO/08, M-STO/09. The Committee communicates the result of the assessment to the candidate, and in case of negative outcome, the procedures for acquiring the missing CFU. Regarding the verification of knowledge and competences in a European Community language, it may be considered fulfilled by passing a language proficiency test at B1 level in the previous training path.

Program, texts and objectives Motivations for the establishment of the interdisciplinary course Beyond the common level of in-depth study of themes and the use of advanced research methodologies within the same disciplinary fields (philological, literary, linguistic and - not insignificant - historical), the reason for establishing a degree course belonging to both classes LM 14 and LM 15 is solidly grounded in the common heuristic heritage, a legacy of a centuries-old tradition of studies, knowledge and methodological applications, offering valuable opportunities for enrichment and comparison in the educational path, also in a comparative direction.
Note regarding credits for other activities Laboratories in language will be organized for students who need to reach the required language level (B2).
Communication skills
Graduates must be able to communicate clearly and unambiguously the results of their studies, as well as the knowledge underlying them, to both specialist and non-specialist audiences. Communication skills are furthermore connected to the mastery of at least one European Union foreign language, in both written and oral form, with reference also to disciplinary lexicons. The development of communication skills is supported by laboratory activities and proceeds through the presentation and verification of written and oral works produced by the student, as well as through in-course assessments established within each teaching unit. Communication skills will also be continuously assessed at various levels of the learning evaluation tests to which students will be subjected.

Critical Judgment (making judgments)
Graduates, developing the research techniques learned in the previous study path, must demonstrate the ability to collect, interpret and manage complex cultural data within broad cultural frameworks, with mature critical thinking attentive to scientific, social and ethical implications. To foster the acquisition of critical judgment, interdisciplinary connections between teaching activities are planned through the organization of seminars and conferences on common topics. Additionally, the seminar organization of some teaching activities involves assigning topics for in-depth study on which students will report during the course of lectures.
Critical judgment will be constantly verified at different levels of the learning assessment tests to which students will be subjected.

The 'G. d'Annunzio' University of Chieti-Pescara has a centralized structure 'Orientation & Placement' (Orientation, Tutoring, Placement, Right to Study and Disability) that, in synergy with the Rector's Delegates, designs, organizes and manages incoming orientation activities in close collaboration with the Departments.
In particular, incoming orientation provides high school students with information useful for understanding the University's educational offerings. By activating interaction between the university world and Regional and non-Regional High Schools, the University offers targeted services, including orientation videoconferences carried out within the 'School-University on Net' project, guided visits of Schools to the Departments in the Chieti and Pescara Campuses, meetings of faculty with students directly at various school locations, as well as providing information and clarifications via email upon request. Incoming orientation activities are also conducted through the preparation and distribution of printed informational material and the availability of numerous online services, ranging from pre-enrollment and matriculation to administrative procedures and exam booking.
Regarding specific incoming orientation activities for the Course of Study in Literature, Linguistics and Literary Traditions, they take place at the beginning of the academic year with meetings for new students aimed at guiding them in choosing their study plan and most suitable educational path. Assigning a tutor at the time of enrollment ensures the student constant guidance and a reference point throughout their academic journey.

A total of 135 students registered for pre-enrollment, of which 114 regularized their enrollment (by May 11, 2020), showing a significant increase compared to the previous academic year. Starting from 2020, orientation activities will be targeted through the organization of meetings for incoming and outgoing students, in agreement with the University Placement Service.

Orientation and ongoing tutoring Each tutor, assigned at the time of admission to the Study Course, will follow the student throughout their entire study path, remaining available with a weekly reception schedule easily accessible for information, clarifications and advice. In addition, at the end of each exam session, it will be the tutor's responsibility to arrange meetings with the student to evaluate the results achieved after each semester of lessons, and if such results are not satisfactory, to help them understand the reasons and implement corrective measures. Furthermore, annually, student tutors are selected to act as a direct link with the CdS, Department and University structures.

Training Periods Association The information, assistance and support services available to students for curricular internships (which require 3 to 6 CFU) are offered by the Course of Study through the course coordinator (Prof. Antonella Di Nallo) and the Department's administrative coordinator (Dr. Cristina Ricciardi). Students can propose themselves for an internship or apply to carry out an internship at public bodies and private companies with which the Course of Study has established specific conventions. At the end of the internship, both the student intern and the tutor responsible at the organization complete an evaluation form of the experience.
In 2019, conventions with external bodies for curricular internships increased in number and quality. Both student interns and host organizations are required to complete an evaluation form.
From March 2020, due to the Covid-19 health emergency, internships were suspended as per DPCM and D.R.
In 2021, the situation of suspension of in-person internships continued.
Starting from the beginning of the 2021-2022 academic year, the pandemic situation allowed a gradual return to internship activities. In 2021, there were 11 interns, and in 2022, the number of students requesting an internship increased. The Course of Study has established 24 conventions with external bodies/organizations.
In 2022, a very positive situation was recorded. Conventions that were 21 in number during the calendar year 2022 were renewed, and today there are 23. New conventions were also established with schools and comprehensive schools to facilitate internships in schools. Internships are always supported by a Course of Study tutor and a tutor at the organization where the internship takes place, who evaluates the student intern (see attached form). The number of interns has increased, and from 2022 to date, 20 students have completed an internship.
In 2023, a substantial continuity with the previous year's trend was recorded. The Course of Study approved 4 new Internship Conventions, bringing the total to 25 active Conventions. The new conventions are:
1. CHIETI STATE ARCHIVE (CONVENTION N. 107 DATED 21/03/2023)
2. PESCARA CLASSICAL LYCEUM (CONVENTION N. 108 DATED 21/03/2023)
3. G. B. VICO NATIONAL BOARDING SCHOOL AND ASSOCIATED SCHOOLS (CONVENTION N. 110 DATED 12/04/2023)
4. PESCARA 7 COMPREHENSIVE SCHOOL (CONVENTION N. 111 DATED 09/05/2023)
The interns (5 students) correctly completed their curricular internship activities for 3 or 6 CFU, corresponding to 75 or 150 hours. Among the chosen locations are Foundations, Theater Deputations, Municipalities, and Lyceums.
The evaluation tests from company tutors, promptly received on the form provided by the Course of Study, indicate the achievement of the predefined objectives and an excellent relationship with the university tutor and the relevant offices.
The student interns' reports were attentive, recording a good level of expansion of acquired skills and learning of practical abilities essential for entering the workforce (from the report by Dr. Cristina Ricciardi, Internship Coordinator, DiLASS).

Workplace Guidance
2019
Exit orientation is organized according to the intervention lines provided by the University's Post-Graduation Orientation Program named START. The word START is used as an acronym for Stage, Internships, Advanced Training, Research, Territory. Active since 2005, the START Program was established to consolidate an effective network of relationships between the university, businesses, and research systems, facilitating the development of a virtuous process of relationships and services aimed at:
- facilitating the 'communication' between business needs, employment insertion processes, and institutional impacts,
- providing substance and continuity to the transition phase to employment for qualified knowledge resources, enabling the local and national economic/productive system to meet the continuous challenges of the market. Contact the Service.
In particular, the student support activities include:
- front-office: service managed by Placement, offering information, competition notices, scholarships, extracurricular internships, useful links, periodicals, CV preparation, and employment prospects.
- University Placement service promoting seminars, notices, career days, internships, and job offers, also through SMS and/or dedicated mailing lists for businesses and students/graduates of the Departments, as well as via popular social networks.
- website providing free access to CVs of approximately 80,000 students and graduates from the last six years who authorized the publication of their data. Simultaneously, companies, organizations, and private employers can consult the database and, through the interconnection between CURRICULA and JOB, request Placement Operators' support for detailed searches to identify specific professional profiles and/or post job/stage offers for free.
-workshop on workplace orientation: in collaboration with Businesses and other partners, the Placement service organizes workshops for students, graduates, and PhD students. Within the workshops, CV preparation and job interview management workshops, European citizenship, business start-up, using social networks for job search and personal branding are also proposed. The intention is to strengthen the cross-disciplinary cultural level of university students, enabling them to expand their empowerment toolset.
Finally, the Course offers students about to graduate the opportunity to attend meetings with stakeholders to discuss with representatives of the working world.

Student opinions
2018
The online survey of student opinions on teaching activities conducted in the A.Y. 2016-2017 produced a rather high overall value for the Study Program in Letters, with a score of 3.49, increasing by 0.01 compared to the A.Y. 2015-2016. This summary of student evaluations for the Study Program in Linguistics, Linguistics and Literary Traditions is absolutely reassuring. It is evident that students provide highly positive evaluations regarding the organization and quality of teaching. The only case where the response 'definitely yes' was not the majority concerns preliminary knowledge for understanding the topics covered in class, which many students consider inadequate; the overall score for this question is the lowest at 3.27; the highest score relates to the availability of teachers during lectures and office hours: 3.66.
2019
The evaluation by attending students highlights appreciation for the teaching offer of the Study Program in Linguistics, Linguistics and Literary Traditions, as the 'Analytical Evaluation Summary' score for the A.Y. 2018-19 is 3.54, indicating a substantially stable situation compared to the previous A.Y. (3.57). Generally, there is a positive increase in evaluations regarding the interest generated by the topics (3.59), the coherence of the courses with what was declared (3.60), the punctuality of activities (3.56), the ability to explain topics (3.60), and the motivation of teachers (3.62). As for the teaching of individual teachers, it is also considered entirely satisfactory. For non-attending students, a stable situation is also recorded with a score of 3.36 compared to 3.40 of the previous A.Y.
2020
Comparing the student evaluation data in the analytical summary immediately shows an increase in the average score, which is 3.58, rising from 3.54 of the previous A.Y. Specifically, interest in courses is 3.61 against 3.59 of 2019; the study load proportional to assigned CFU is 3.46 against 3.43; the adequacy of teaching materials is 3.56 against 3.46; the coherence of course delivery with what was declared on the website is 3.64 against 3.60; respect for lecture schedules is 3.66 against 3.56; clarity in defining exam procedures is 3.57 against 3.52; teacher motivation is 3.63 against 3.62; adequacy of topic exposition is 3.64 against 3.60; teacher availability for clarifications during lectures/office hours is 3.77 against 3.71. The only data not within the average evaluation is the usefulness of integrated activities for learning the subject (128 students consider them not useful). For non-attending students, the trend is also upward (3.40 against 3.36). Overall, the evaluation shows an increase that testifies to student satisfaction with the organization and activities of the Study Program.
The results of student/alumni opinions were discussed by the Study Program on September 23, 2020.
2021
The evaluation of the Study Program by students for the A.Y. 2020-21 is particularly flattering, as the increase in the average score (3.63 compared to 3.58 of the previous year) must be considered in the context of the pandemic situation due to Covid-19, which imposed distance learning for most of the academic year. The increase of 0.5 is in fact a significant achievement. Specifically, all 11 items show an increase: the interest in courses has a slight increase of 3.62 compared to 3.61 of the previous year; the preliminary knowledge for understanding is rated 3.37 against 3.32; the proportionality of study load to assigned CFU is 3.53 against 3.46; the adequacy of teaching materials is rated 3.63 against the previous 3.56; the coherence of course delivery with what was declared on the website is 3.69 against 3.64; respect for schedules shows an increase of 0.10, i.e., 3.76 against 3.66; clarity in defining exam procedures is 3.59 against 3.57; teacher motivation is 3.66 against 3.63; adequacy of topic exposition is 3.67 against 3.64; teacher availability for clarifications during lectures/office hours is 3.79 against 3.77. As can be observed, all items show an increase, interpreted as a growing student satisfaction with the Study Program.
The student/alumni opinion data will be discussed in the first suitable council after the data publication.
The Study Program did not highlight any particular issues except for delays in exam certification, as noted by the student representative at the meeting on April 24, 2021.
Regarding the management of student complaints, the Study Program established, since the Course Council meeting on June 4, 2020, the role of a 'Student Guarantor' and publicized it on the Study Program website (https://www.dilass.unich.it/node/8681).
2022
Student evaluation for the academic year 2021-2022 is at very positive values, although declining compared to the previous year. The score is 3.55, decreasing from 3.63 of the previous year.
A decrease is recorded for all questionnaire items prior to exams, including the perception of teaching load as disproportionate (3.53 against 3.42) and the adequacy of teaching materials (3.63 against 3.51). For non-attending students, who constitute a significant portion of enrolled students, the score is 3.42, matching the previous A.Y. (3.46). Although not final data (update expected October 31, 2022), the overall score is still considered positive and within the Study Program's norm. The Almalaurea and University data on student opinions will be discussed in the Study Program in September 2022.
Regarding the management of student complaints, the Study Program maintains the role of the 'Student Guarantor' publicized on the Study Program website (https://www.dilass.unich.it/node/8681).
2023
The student opinion survey has shown improvement compared to the previous year. The average score of the Study Program is indeed 3.68 (3.55 of the previous year), compared to a Humanities Area average of 3.54 and a University average of 3.44, practically unchanged. The item with the lowest score is D1 (Are the preliminary knowledge possessed sufficient for understanding the topics in the exam program?) at 3.51 (Area 3.33 and University 3.31), which is still above the area and University averages. Overall, the Study Program achieves very positive values, although not final data (update expected October 31, 2023). Ability to apply knowledge and understanding (applying knowledge and understanding)
Graduates are able to apply their knowledge and understanding by demonstrating the ability to analyze philologically and critically texts from the linguistic and literary tradition of classical, medieval, modern, and contemporary eras. The teaching tools used to achieve these results consist of frontal lessons, exercises, seminars, which involve the use of specialized texts.
The achievement of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding mentioned above occurs through critical reflection on texts proposed for individual study, stimulated by classroom activities.
Verification of the achievement of the ability to apply knowledge and understanding occurs mainly through exams and intermediate assessment tests in oral and/or written form, oral presentations.
Knowledge and understanding are acquired and verified within the linguistic, philological, and literary training activities.
Learning skills (learning skills)
Graduates must have developed learning skills that allow them to continue studying, mostly independently or with a high level of responsibility. Tutoring activities contribute to guiding students toward autonomy in research. The achievement of expected results will be constantly verified through laboratories, internships, traineeships, and reports on specific topics. The thesis elaboration marks the end of the training path and will also provide the tools for subsequent updating of their scientific knowledge.
Knowledge and understanding (knowledge and understanding)
The final title of Master of Arts in Philology, Linguistics and Literary Traditions will be awarded to students who have acquired in-depth and updated methodological, historical, and critical training in linguistic and literary studies of the classical, medieval, modern, and contemporary eras and have demonstrated direct experience with original texts and documents.
The achievement of the proposed training objectives will be supported by both frontal lessons, seminar activities, and participation in specialized conferences and congresses. The final phase of the training process will be the writing of a monographic thesis that involves the application of research methodology tools, the ability to use specific bibliographic resources, and the personal re-elaboration of acquired disciplinary content. The achievement of these results is entrusted to frontal lessons, exercises, seminars on monographic topics related to the main disciplines of the course and is verified through written and/or oral tests.
Master's graduates must demonstrate knowledge of, and the ability to analyze philologically and critically, texts from the linguistic and literary tradition of the classical, medieval, modern, and contemporary eras. The teaching tools used to achieve these results consist of frontal lessons, exercises, seminars, which involve the use of specialized texts, modernly equipped, the result of advanced research.

Brief course description The Master's course in Philology, Linguistics and Literary Traditions aims to provide a solid linguistic, literary, and historical culture through the deepening of knowledge acquired with the undergraduate degree in the two teaching paths of Modern Philology and Philology and Literatures of the Ancient World, corresponding respectively to the two classes LM-14 and LM-15. The main objective is to develop a methodologically deep awareness that leads to a highly qualified and versatile intellectual formation, developing in students the ability to move easily in the multiple expressions of the classical world or, according to their choice, the modern and contemporary world. The two paths offer a wide variety of literary, philological, linguistic, and historical courses often complementary to each other, allowing for the acquisition of solid specialized knowledge and effective analytical tools. This training offer ensures adequate competencies in the fields of communication and conservation of cultural heritage, classification and processing of information related to various fields of work, from teaching in schools to professions in the publishing, cultural industry, and public and private cultural institutions. It also fosters predisposition to scientific research, laying the foundation for access to PhD programs and second-level Master's degrees. Teaching activities include frontal lessons, exercises, study seminars, assisted study, laboratories, and training internships at public and private structures. At the end of the path, graduates possess a deep, theoretical, and methodological preparation in the fields of philology, linguistics, literatures, and history; they possess the critical ability to face the text, from its constitution to its linguistic and semiotic aspects, to its literary and historical interpretation and evaluation.

Specific course objectives and description of the training path The Interdisciplinary Master's course in Philology, Linguistics and Literary Traditions (LM14-LM15) aims to provide students with a broad cultural formation in the fields of languages, literatures, and classical and modern cultures, and to train highly qualified intellectual personnel capable of providing original contributions in the fields of research, communication, and conservation of cultural heritage, and equally capable of being profitably used for the classification and processing of information in various professional and work fields, thanks to the versatility resulting from the solid and articulated preparation provided by the course.
The merger of the two degree classes into a single interdisciplinary course, motivated by the existence of a common methodology and tradition of studies at least in part, has the advantage, from a cultural point of view, of highlighting the fundamental unity of themes that traverse Western culture, from classical roots to modern and contemporary developments. The course allows for a critical-literary, historical, philological, and linguistic preparation through direct contact with the main authors and the most important works of the literary tradition, also in relation to other fields of artistic expression such as visual arts and performance. The course first aims to provide the necessary tools for philological and linguistic investigation, together with the indispensable competencies for the interpretation of literary texts and the exegetical and critical use of sources in classical and modern contexts. On this common background, and considering the centrality of philological study in the course structure, the division into classical and modern classes (which the student must indicate at enrollment) will allow the acquisition of specific competencies and particular theoretical and methodological tools. In the classical path, the course aims to acquire full and complete knowledge of Greek and Latin languages and literatures and the history of antiquity and its artistic and material culture. In the modern path, it aims to achieve full mastery of Italian literary history and Italian linguistic history, viewed in their relationship with historical, artistic, and cultural development. The course also ensures the acquisition of updated knowledge of the research techniques necessary for the retrieval, exegesis, and critical use of sources.
The course also provides the possibility of acquiring 24 CFU in anthropo-psychopedagogical subjects and teaching methodologies and technologies according to the new regulations regarding teacher training. Graduates will also be able to use at least one European Union language besides Italian (B2 level) in written and oral form, with reference to specific disciplinary lexicons, and must be able to use the main information technology and telematic communication tools in their specific areas of competence.
The formation of a common basic training base for all students enrolled in the interdisciplinary Master's course is achieved through the activation of disciplinary sectors common to the two Master's degree curricula, integrated with a suitable selection of related or complementary disciplines. Laboratories will also be offered to reach the required language level.

Territorial social partners have been periodically consulted since the course was established. Regarding the course's training objectives, officials of Libraries and Archives, public and private, owners and delegates of Publishing Houses and Bookstores, representatives of Research Organizations and non-profit cultural associations, representatives of the Press and Directors of the Regional School Office have been contacted. The latest consultation dates back to 2016 and was organized by the Department with the participation of various territorial entities (see SUA 2016 A.2.b). To ensure greater continuity in relations with organizations and greater promptness in corrective interventions that may be necessary, the course intends to proceed as follows: starting from the current academic year, the Course President will initiate periodic consultations with representative organizations, at national and international level, of goods and service production and professions, specific consultations based on the peculiar training objectives of the Course.
These consultations will take place, at least by July of each year before the start of the following academic year. The subject of these consultations will be proposals for modifying the curriculum and/or didactic regulations for the next academic year, to update the study path based, as much as possible, on the requests of the job market. More precisely, it is planned to send via email a document with a synthetic presentation of the course's training objectives, which interlocutors will be invited to evaluate, entering into the specifics of the training dynamics.

A reinforcement in this direction could favor greater appeal from the cultural industry.

Present were Prof. Cimini, Soccio, and Di Nallo and representatives of the following organizations: Etipublica Public Promotion Association (Pescara); Archaeological, Fine Arts and Landscape Superintendency of Abruzzo (Chieti), National Center for Dannunzian Studies (Pescara), Publishing House Rocco Carabba (Lanciano), Tiboni Foundation for Culture (Pescara), Marrucino Theater (Chieti), Comprehensive Institute No. 4 of Chieti, Provincial Voluntary Service Center of Chieti, Spazio MATTA - Artists for the Matta of Pescara. The debate focused on the importance of strengthening the link between the University and the job market to obtain suggestions on how to orient student training and how to organize work experiences during the university path. From the fruitful meeting, it emerged that the versatility of humanistic knowledge is a primary value but must be combined with higher communication skills, both written and oral, and greater relational abilities. This allows graduates of the courses in Letters and Philology, Linguistics and Literary Traditions to access teaching, specific post-graduation training paths (PhD and second-level Master's), but also employment in business, both public and private.
Attached are the documents related to the two meetings.
2019
In 2019, only one meeting was held on December 2, 2019, with stakeholders interested in the courses of the Department of Letters, Arts and Social Sciences. Present were the Department Director, the presidents of the four courses, the contact for relations with stakeholders, and the contact for curricular internships who drafted the minutes. The meeting was fruitful, as it discussed the usefulness of curricular internships, the possibility of improving the offer, and the opportunities they provide for students both in terms of training and future prospects. It emerged that the level of students is high but they need to be directed towards internships that are more suitable for their preparation and aspirations, as the starting point for a future project in the job market.

Entry, path, and exit data
2017
In the last two years, the course in Philology, Linguistics and Literary Traditions has recorded a progressive decrease in the number of enrollments (97 in 2015-2016, 92 in 2016-2017) compared to the previous three years (104 in 2012-2013, 114 in 2013-2014, 110 in 2014-2015); it is likely that this decline is in line with the national decline in enrollments at the university level, particularly in humanities. Most of them come from the Abruzzo region (9.78% from Chieti; 47.83% from other municipalities of the Chieti province; 19.57% from other provinces of the region), but a consistent number of students also come from other regions (22.83%), especially Molise and Puglia. Almost all have obtained the undergraduate degree at our university; only 4 of the enrolled students come from another Italian university. The undergraduate degree grade is mostly above 106, with 23 110 and honors (only 18 of the enrolled students entered with a grade below 100). Regarding students enrolled in the second year, 62/97 have acquired more than 40 CFU; 26 between 21 and 40 CFU, and only 9 less than 20 (4 with no CFU); the data is reassuring and has improved compared to previous years; 86.60% has an average above 28/30.
2019
In the academic years 2017-2018 and 2018-2019, the course in Philology, Linguistics and Literary Traditions records the same number of new students, i.e., 83, further decreasing compared to the previous survey. Most of them come from the Abruzzo region (91), while others (21) come from neighboring regions. In this survey, students have mostly obtained the undergraduate degree at the G. d'Annunzio University of Chieti and Pescara (90.36%). The degree grade is 110 and honors for 51 students, 110 for 4 students, between 105 and 110 for 13 students, and below 105 for 13 students. The average grade for exams taken remains unchanged at 28.25/30.
2020
In the academic year 2019-20, the number of new enrollments/registrations has increased significantly. There are 113 new enrollments against 83 in the previous year, with a total of 236 enrolled against 204 in 2018-2019. Most of them come from the Abruzzo region (92), have obtained their diploma at high schools (87). The degree grade is 110 and honors for 84 students, 110 for 3 students, between 105 and 100 for 23 students, and 105 for 4 students. 83.13% of students achieve a grade between 28 and 30.
Entry, path, and exit data were commented on in the Course Council on September 23, 2020, and in the GAQ meetings of September 3, 2020, and October 7, 2020. In particular, meetings highlighted a criticality regarding integrated exams and their management. There is a need to reduce integrated exams in the teaching offer and to have unique management modalities.
2021
In the academic year 2020-21, the number of new enrollments remained substantially unchanged (111) with a total of 282 enrolled—compared to 113 new enrollments and 236 enrolled in the previous academic year. Of the new enrollments, 74 come from the Abruzzo region, 37 from other regions of Italy. The degree grade is 110 and honors for 32 students (of which 20 in course, 8 one year late, and 4 two or more years late); 110 for 3 students (of which 2 in course and 1 two or more years late); between 105 and 110 for 7 students (of which 3 in course and 4 one year late); 105 for 4 students (of which 1 in course, 1 one year late, and 2 two or more years late). The percentage of students continuing to the second year is 93.69%. The average grade for exams is 28.55.
Data will be commented on in the first useful council after publication.
2022
In the academic year 2021-2022, the number of new enrollments decreased (90) with a total of 273 enrolled. Of the new enrollments, 15 come from the same municipality, 42 from other municipalities of the province, 14 from another province, and 18 from another region (1 from abroad). Regarding school origin, 68 come from high schools, 7 from technical institutes, 12 from magistrali, and 4 from other institutes. The average grade of the undergraduate degree for students entering in 2021 is 105.3 (Almalaurea data). The percentage of students continuing to the second year is 92.31%. 82.69% of students have an exam average between 28 and 30. In 2021, the degree grade was 110 and honors for 59 students, 110 for 5 students, between 105 and 110 for 10 students, and 105 for 7 students. Data will be commented on in the Course Council of September 2022.
2023
In the academic year 2022-2023, the number of new enrollments increased to 93 with a total of 250 enrolled, of which 172 in course and 78 out of course. Of the new enrollments, 18 come from the same municipality, 39 from other municipalities of the province, 12 from another province, and 24 from other regions. Regarding school origin, 57 come from high schools, 16 from technical institutes, 18 from magistrali, and 2 from other institutes. The percentage of students continuing to the second year is 86.21% for LM14 and 50% for LM15. Characteristics of the final exam The final exam consists of preparing and discussing a research-based thesis, prepared by the student under the guidance of a supervising professor, belonging to a SSD within which the student has passed at least one exam. The weight of the final exam corresponds to 18 CFU.
Final exam implementation The final exam consists of preparing and discussing a research-based thesis, prepared by the student under the guidance of a supervising professor, belonging to a SSD within which the student has passed, or had validated if recognized for career purposes, at least one exam. The thesis supervisor must be a professor active in the SSD of the discipline in which the student graduates; in case of professors no longer in service, the topic of the exam must be agreed upon and deposited in the Secretariat before the start of the retirement period. The weight of the final exam corresponds to 18 CFU.
The final exam is evaluated by a commission appointed by the Department Director, who also sets the work calendar. The judging commission is composed of a minimum of seven professors including the President. The majority of the commission members must be professors of the university. The President of the Commission is, among the members, the first-level professor with the greatest seniority or, in the absence, the associate professor with the greatest seniority. The President must ensure the full regularity of the exam and the adherence of the final evaluations to the general criteria established by the bodies responsible for the course.
The commission awards up to a maximum of 6 points for the final exam, with reference criteria being the ability to synthesize, scientific competence, coherence of argumentation, and expressive clarity demonstrated by the candidate in the written work and oral presentation. Students who have completed a study experience within the ERASMUS program and international agreements (OVERSEAS) are awarded an additional 1 point. The judging commission expresses the overall grade in hundredths, taking into account the curriculum and the final exam, and, unanimously, may award the highest grade with honors. The minimum grade to pass the exam is 66 out of 100.

The Faculty has adequate, suitable, and effective equipped spaces, and following a program in an advanced phase of deep restructuring of the Chieti Campus, new teaching and scientific spaces will be acquired in the short term, fully commensurate with the new programming and the prospects of its complete implementation. The Faculty can rely on a specific teaching staff for basic and characterizing disciplines, widely adequate. The proposed curriculum, significantly improved in terms of compactness, transparency, and effectiveness, can contribute to the goals of rationalization and qualification of the university's teaching offer and also acquire greater attraction capacity.

Admission Procedures The course is quota-controlled and by May 15th of each year the Teaching Council proposes to the Department Council the maximum number of students to enroll in the first year. For the 2024-2025 academic year, the sustainable student intake is 173 units; it has been decided to set a quota of 160 students, of whom 158 are Italian, EU, and non-EU citizens residing in Italy, and 2 are non-EU citizens residing abroad (Art. 26 L.n. 189 of July 30, 2002).
To enroll in the Pharmacy Bachelor's Degree, a five-year secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent under current regulations is required. Candidates, up to a maximum of 160 units, will be selected based on a merit ranking determined by the secondary school diploma grade, with priority given to the chronological order of pre-registration to the ranking, following the procedures outlined in the official call.
Admission, pre-registration, enrollment, and transfer procedures from other degree courses will be adequately advertised on the University website (https://www.unich.it) and on the teaching structure noticeboards.
After enrollment, Additional Educational Requirements (OFA) will be defined through multiple-choice questions developed by teachers covering topics in Chemistry, Biology, Physics, and Mathematics. The recovery of OFA must be completed within the first year of the course.
Additional Educational Requirements (OFA)
Verification of Required Knowledge The initial knowledge verification test (mandatory per DM 270/04) is administered to identify any educational gaps among new students and organize necessary recovery activities (in addition to the standard course activities), ensuring academic support for students assigned OFA based on the initial knowledge test results.
Students transferring from other institutions, changing study programs, reactivating careers, or enrolling in a subsequent year with career abbreviation will be excluded from the initial knowledge verification. All information regarding the initial knowledge verification test (date, time, location, number of questions, duration, registration procedures, scoring criteria for correct, incorrect, or unanswered questions, etc.) will be published on the University website (https://www.unich.it) and on the teaching structure noticeboards.
OFA-related questions cover the following disciplines:
- Chemistry:
States of aggregation of matter. Heterogeneous and homogeneous systems. Compounds and elements. Ionic and molecular compounds. Atomic composition (electrons, neutrons, protons). Atomic number and mass number. Atomic weight and molecular weight. Chemical reactions and stoichiometry (balancing and elementary stoichiometric calculations). Mole concept. Avogadro's number. Solutions. Solution concentration. Acid and base concepts. Acidity, neutrality, and basicity of aqueous solutions. pH. Carbohydrates. Lipids. Amino acids and proteins. Nucleic acids.
- Physics:
Direct and indirect measurements. Fundamental and derived quantities. Physical dimensions of quantities. Decimal metric system. International System of Units (SI). Units of measurement (names and relationships between fundamental and derived units). Multiples and submultiples. Kinematic quantities. Uniform linear motion. Uniformly accelerated linear motion. Uniform circular motion. Simple harmonic motion. Vectors and vector operations. Forces, moments of forces. Vector composition of forces. Definitions of mass and weight. Acceleration due to gravity. Density and specific weight. Law of universal gravitation. Work. Kinetic energy. Potential energy. Pressure and its units of measurement. Archimedes' principle. Heat propagation mechanisms. Ideal gas laws. State changes. Basic concepts on acoustic and optical phenomena (reflection, refraction, dispersion). Electrostatics and electrodynamics. Electric field and potential. Electrical resistance and resistivity. Electrical work and power. Effects of electric currents.
- Mathematics:
Natural, integer, rational, and real numbers and their ordering and comparison. Algebraic operations and their properties. Ratios and percentages. Powers and their properties. Scientific notation. Radicals and their properties. Logarithms (base 10 and base e) and their properties. Algebraic expressions. First and second-degree algebraic equations. Inequalities. Fundamental concepts on functions and their graphical representation. Measurement of lengths, areas, and volumes. Angle measurement in degrees and radians. Sine, cosine, tangent of an angle and their notable values. Cartesian coordinate system in the plane. Equation of a line. Conditions for parallelism and perpendicularity. Distance from a point to a line. Equation of a circle, parabola, hyperbola, ellipse and their representation in the Cartesian plane.
- Biology:
Organic molecules present in living organisms and their functions. Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. Animal and plant cells. Cell membrane and its functions. Cellular structures and their functions. Cell division: mitosis and meiosis. Chromosomal complement. Animal and plant tissues. Photosynthesis. Glycolysis. Aerobic respiration. Fermentation. Sexual and asexual reproduction. Genes and DNA. Genetic code and its translation. Protein synthesis. Anatomy of major organ systems and their functions and interactions. General knowledge on viruses, bacteria, and fungi. Main plant organs and systems and their functions.
For the verification of knowledge possession, the test consists of multiple-choice questions equally distributed across Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, and Biology disciplines.
How Additional Educational Requirements (OFA) are Determined
The initial knowledge verification test will be administered after enrollment. Additional Educational Requirements (OFA) will be assigned exclusively to students who scored less than 50% correct answers in each disciplinary area (Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, Biology) in the verification test.
Students who have taken the TOLC-F test in 2023 or 2024 will have their test results considered valid for the initial knowledge verification, provided they submit the relevant documentation.
OFA must be completed within the first year through the recovery methods established by the Course Director and the teachers of the relevant disciplines.
Completing OFA is mandatory to access official exams in the corresponding courses as per the Study Plan.
Recovery Methods Based on the initial knowledge verification, if necessary, the Bachelor's Degree course will activate additional recovery courses beyond the official course lectures in each disciplinary area where students have educational gaps. Teachers of the disciplines subject to OFA will schedule 1 or 2 weekly hours for recovery. Attendance at the recovery course is mandatory. Students attending recovery courses are not exempt from attending official courses. The educational gap is considered filled upon passing a written verification test.
Failure to complete OFA by October 31st of the year following enrollment will prevent students from taking exams for subsequent years unless they have earned at least 18 CFU from the first-year courses in the basic and characterizing disciplines.

Program, texts and objectives Communication skills
Master's degree graduates in Pharmacy must: - provide healthcare consultation, exercising a connecting role between patient, doctor and public health facilities, collaborating in drug monitoring in the territory; - demonstrate relational and organizational skills in pharmacy management; - be able to engage, in an industrial context, with biologists and doctors; - be capable of communicating, both in writing and orally, also in English. These objectives are achieved through professionalizing seminars, pharmacy management simulations, practical-professional internship and language tutoring activities specifically oriented towards professional topics.
