UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITY OF CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [L500] ECO-SUSTAINABLE TECHNOLOGIES AND ENVIRONMENTAL TOXICOLOGY
TYPE:
CURRICULUM:
SECTION: Career Guidance
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/1865

Career Guidance The university has established a centralized Orientation and Placement service aimed at supporting the employment of its graduates.
Additionally, a guidance committee has been established within the Degree Program, led by the Internship Coordinator, Prof. Antonio Di Stefano, to facilitate students' internship pathways, enabling a satisfactory percentage to graduate during their studies. The committee's task is to systematically consult professional, technical-scientific organizations and companies in the sector, guide students toward training activities aligned with the Degree Program's objectives, and identify academic supervisors based on professional competencies to accompany students throughout their internship. Often, internships conducted at external institutions lead to actual employment contracts. Academic supervisors promote collaboration between the university and external institutions to establish a constructive and lasting trust relationship.
On April 8, 2021, Prof. Antonio Di Stefano, delegate for the third mission of the Department of Pharmacy, together with the Degree Program President TESTA, Prof. Ivana Cacciatore, and Dr. Lisa Marinelli and Michele Ciulla, organized via MICROSOFT TEAMS a day of meetings with the company RANSTAD and some national 'Pharma' industries. The event was dedicated to students, graduates, and alumni of the Pharmacy Study and Degree Programs, aiming to guide participants in drafting presentation CVs and proposing the correct approach for job interviews. Approximately 70 students participated, predominantly from the final years of the Pharmacy Study Programs (40%) and CTF (45%), and 7% of first-year TESTA Degree Program students.

Student opinions A.Y. 2020/21
The analysis reported relates to the 2020/21 Cohort that attended the first year of the Degree Program TESTA and the data regarding student opinions on teaching for the academic year 2020-21 are updated as of 31-07-2021 (Source PQA at link http://core.unich.it).
The number of questionnaires completed by attending students is 107 out of 308 theoretical (34.74%) in the first year of observation with 7 courses covered for both semesters. In A.Y. 2020/21, the general comment on the trend of judgments provided by attending students on the various courses of the program is globally positive, with good satisfaction regarding the teaching delivered, the qualification of the teachers, and the schedules and availability of teachers for clarifications. All this is confirmed by an average score of 3.49, a value higher than the University average (3.35_data PQA_opinion survey students 2019-2020_Table 3.a).
In particular, from the analysis of individual questions, it emerges high student satisfaction regarding teacher professionalism (punctuality in class: 3.78, availability during office hours: 3.84, consistency with the program: 3.70, clarity of exposition: 3.59). The judgment reported in the 107 questionnaires indicates that students consider it appropriate to maintain the current teaching load. The point requiring attention primarily concerns the preliminary knowledge possessed by students for understanding the program content (2.74). Compared to the University average and the averages for Health Area Degree Programs (3.30_data PQA_opinion survey students 2019-2020_Table 3.a), the score obtained by the Degree Program in TESTA (3.49) is higher.
Very interesting is the student evaluation of courses belonging to CUN areas of chemical and biological sciences: 3.54 and 3.48, respectively. No significant differences are evident.

Analysis 2022/23
The analysis reported relates to students who attended the TESTA Degree Program and the data regarding student opinions on teaching for the academic year 2022-23 are updated as of 31-07-2023 (Source PQA at link http://core.unich.it).
The number of questionnaires completed by attending students is 678 with 38 training activities covered for both semesters. The percentage of questionnaires, which has significantly increased compared to the previous year (390 with 15 courses covered), is also due to the activation of the third year of the Degree Program.
In A.Y. 2022/23, the general comment on the trend of judgments provided by attending students on the various courses of the program is globally positive, with good satisfaction regarding the teaching delivered, the qualification of the teachers, and the schedules and availability of teachers for clarifications.
Regarding the A.Y. 2022/23 Macro-indicators concerning teaching effectiveness (3.48) and organizational logistical aspects (3.50) of the Degree Program, they are in line with the Health Area averages (3.43) and University averages (3.48). Slightly lower is the overall satisfaction of the Degree Program (3.27) compared to Health Area (3.32) and University (3.35).
Students have evaluated very positively teacher punctuality (3.66), teacher availability (3.66), and clarity in examination procedures (3.46), all evaluations increased compared to previous years.
The judgment reported by students in the 678 questionnaires regarding the preliminary knowledge possessed by students for understanding the program content has significantly increased in A.Y. 2022/23, reaching 3.26 compared to 2.99 in A.Y. 2021/22 and 2.79 in A.Y. 2020/21. This increase is likely due to the actions taken by the Degree Program regarding the strengthening of introductory courses related to Additional Mandatory Courses and targeted orientation primarily towards scientific high schools.
The evaluation that is less high concerns the proportionality between study load and credits (3.16), in line with the previous year (3.13). Regarding this point, meetings were held by the Degree Program Chair to harmonize course content and the proportionality of CFU per course. Compared to last year, the interest stimulated by the teacher in the disciplines remains around the same value of 3.34.
The average evaluation of the Degree Program (3.43) in A.Y. 2022/23 is higher than the previous year (3.39) and in line with the average evaluation of Health Area Degree Programs at the University (3.4).

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding (applying knowledge and understanding)
The graduate in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology will be able to:
- interpret and predict the structure, physical properties, and chemical behavior of organic molecules, with particular reference to organic and inorganic pollutants;
- apply methodologies for the preparation and analytical characterization of samples collected from the environment (soil, water, air), interpret spectroscopic data, and prepare analytical reports;
- implement tools for verifying the environmental impact of chemical and pharmaceutical industrial processes and plan possible corrective actions;
- indicate new approaches for the industrial synthesis of chemical products through low-impact environmental processes (Green Chemistry);
- recognize and undertake corrective actions on factors influencing microbial development on matrices of different nature;
- apply experimental procedures for determining the composition or chemical-physical properties of a food product;
- apply the most suitable preventive measures regarding occupational injuries and diseases and develop skills in managing exposure to chemical agents;
- evaluate the toxicity of drugs and other substances in relation to their presence in the environment;
- recognize mechanisms and characteristics of radioactive decays, perform radioactivity measurements;
- apply the most suitable preventive measures regarding occupational injuries and diseases.
- set up circular economy models and identify the main information necessary to carry out environmental sustainability assessments, and evaluate the related economic impacts through the appropriate tools;
- apply the EMA guidelines on Environmental Risk Assessment (EMEA/CHMP/SWP/4447/00 corr 2) within a pharmaceutical plant and in relation to production processes;
The graduate in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology acquires the described competencies through: frontal lessons, exercises, laboratory activities, independent study, seminars, field practical activities, free courses, participation in external seminars, conferences, and meetings.
The acquisition of competencies is verified through: written tests, oral exams, laboratory practical tests, classroom discussions, reports to be submitted to the teacher.
Learning skills (learning skills)
In terms of acquiring adequate competencies related to learning skills, of fundamental importance will be:
- the ability to autonomously and guidedly update one's own knowledge, regarding technical-scientific and methodological innovations, in particular for professionalizing disciplines;
- understanding scientific articles in English and bibliographic consultations;
- the ability to consult databases and other online information, through which to ideate and support arguments and solve problems in one's field of study.
- the ability to stay updated on national and community regulations of specific professional sectors such as the sector of chemical safety and environmental protection, the sector of food protection, or the regulatory section concerning the production of medicines.
Learning skills are acquired throughout the study path, with particular regard to the teachings and individual study in the legal-regulatory field, related to the consultation of disciplinary databases.
Learning skills are also evaluated through continuous verification forms during training activities, as it will be required to present autonomously researched data organized into reports to be submitted to the teacher, and through the tutoring activity in the development of projects and through the evaluation of the self-learning skills acquired during the final project activity. The development of adequate learning skills will be necessary to undertake subsequent studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Knowledge and understanding (knowledge and understanding)
The graduate in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology will be able to acquire:
- knowledge of basic disciplines such as mathematics, physics, general chemistry, and organic chemistry, with their respective methodologies and applications relevant in environmental, biological, and chemical fields;
- basic knowledge of anatomy, biology, and pathology with particular reference to environmentally originated pathologies;
- theoretical and practical aspects of analytical chemistry and analysis of medicines, with reference to spectroscopic techniques and sample preparation for the determination of inorganic and organic analytes;
- knowledge of the general principles governing the production of all forms of pharmaceuticals, both sterile and non-sterile, focusing on the dynamics of containing potential environmental contamination;
- basic knowledge for understanding the most important chemical transformations occurring in air, water, and soil;
- in-depth understanding of the function of drugs in physiological and pathological processes and their role as environmental or food contaminants;
- basic notions of microbiology, with particular reference to the impact of microorganisms in the biotechnology, food, and industrial sectors;
- knowledge of the use of GMOs in the pharmaceutical industry for the production of recombinant proteins and drugs;
- basic knowledge of radioactivity and the laws of radioactive decay and the basis for understanding the interaction between radiation and matter and therefore how they can be detected;
- knowledge related to nutrient classes, notions on the chemistry of fermented products, food preservation, and undesirable and toxic substances.
- knowledge of technologies for the recovery and valorization of industrial waste and principles of environmental monitoring, with particular reference to circular economy and the economic sustainability of recycling plants;
- basic knowledge of the Italian State Organization, regulations, and subjects involved in health and safety protection in workplaces, as well as regulatory bodies for national and international medicines, pharmacovigilance and regulations, and environmental impact assessment regulations for medicines (Environmental Risk Assessment, ERA).
The graduate in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology acquires the described knowledge through: frontal lessons, exercises, laboratory activities, independent study, seminars, field practical activities, free courses, participation in external seminars, conferences, and meetings.
The acquisition of knowledge is verified through: written tests, oral exams, laboratory practical tests, classroom discussions, reports to be submitted to the teacher.

Brief course description The three-year Degree Course in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology (TESTA) was activated in the academic year 2020/21 at the Department of Pharmacy of the University of Chieti-Pescara 'G. d'Annunzio'.
TESTA graduates are fundamental to promote scientific and cultural training aimed at protecting the environment. The distinctive characteristic of this course compared to others aimed at the environment is the attention dedicated to the pharmaceutical, chemical, and food sectors. Thanks to the training path, graduates will acquire the necessary competencies to evaluate environmental risks related to the production and disposal of waste in the pharmaceutical, chemical, and food sectors, enabling them to operate successfully within these industries.
EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVES:
The TESTA Degree Course aims to prepare professionals capable of applying the technical and scientific knowledge acquired in a wide range of sectors, including environmental chemical analysis, environmental toxicology, production and control of chemical and pharmaceutical processes, circular economy, recycling, and valorization of industrial waste.
COURSE STRUCTURE:
The TESTA Degree Course is structured over three years: the first year centered around a core of fundamental subjects to provide a basic preparation, and the second and third years based on more specific and professionalizing disciplines. During the three years of the course, students participate in lessons, exercises, laboratories, elective courses, seminars, conferences, meetings, and field practical experiences.
ACQUIRED COMPETENCIES:
The graduate will be able to perform functions in technical or professional roles in environmental protection, including:
- Preparation of protocols for chemical, microbiological, and eco-toxicological analyses on environment and atmosphere (waters, foods, wastes, soils, and air);
- Preparation of protocols for monitoring waters, air, soil, and foods to detect potential contaminants;
- Execution of chemical controls according to the most modern certified quality systems, toxicological, and microbiological for the protection of food and industrial environment (water, air, soil);
- Ability to apply standardized sampling methodologies and certified instrumental analytical methodologies for the detection, recognition, and quantification of toxins and contaminants in different matrices included in the work context functions;
- Planning of preventive and educational interventions for population health in relation to toxicological aspects derived from chemical and biological pollution.
PROFESSIONAL PROFILE:
The TESTA graduate will be able to apply the acquired competencies in the fields of chemical-toxicological analyses, chemical-pharmaceutical sector, production and control of chemical processes, and environmental sustainability with particular reference to circular economy.
EMPLOYMENT OUTLOOKS:
The Three-year TESTA Degree Course prepares for the profession of:
Chemical Technicians Technicians in the field of chemical/toxicological analyses Technicians for the operation and control of chemical plants Environmental Control Technicians Waste collection and environmental remediation Technicians Biochemical Laboratory Technicians Food Products Technicians Registration in the Chemicals Register Section B.
External effectiveness As of 1.09.2023, no student has obtained the degree, therefore data on graduates entering the job market are not available.
Specific educational objectives of the course and description of the training path One of the fundamental determinants of the TESTA Course is the relationship with the environment, with particular reference to preserving the territory and the organisms that inhabit it, maintaining biodiversity, and the health status of the human population. At the same time, one of the main goals is to identify technological solutions capable of combining industrial production with ecological sustainability, with particular reference to circular economy. All this is reflected in the professional and cultural profiles that the course intends to form, namely professional technicians capable of implementing the technical-scientific knowledge acquired in numerous application fields related to environmental toxicology, production and control of chemical and pharmaceutical processes, ecology, and management of industrial waste and territory control.
Territory control from a toxicological perspective thus becomes one of the main objectives of the graduate in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology, as through the acquired competencies they will be able to conduct research and analyses on the territory and potential contaminants, implementing control and evaluation of potential pollutants in waters, soil, and air. In addition to potential contaminants, the identification of existing environmental criticalities can help seek new strategies to define the changes to apply and the eventual environmental recovery. Such recovery and restoration of environmental conditions is of fundamental importance, as the environment must be considered a factor that can directly influence health.
The concept of environmental recovery, eco-sustainability, and territory control is certainly linked to the production and control of chemical and pharmaceutical processes, among the main responsible for the release of environmental contaminants that still possess biological activity, as well as active pharmaceutical ingredients or their metabolites/derivatives. Professionals that the course intends to form will have the opportunity to collaborate and assist specialists in controlling and managing the operation and safety of chemical flow processes and pharmaceutical and food production. The emphasis will be placed not only on controlling chemical processes but especially on circular economy, eco-sustainability, and the valorization of by-products from chemical and pharmaceutical industries. Indeed, the main objective will also be to provide in-depth knowledge of the methodologies applied for waste recycling in order to design, develop, and evaluate systems for controlling and detecting information on various types of environmental pollution. Such competencies can be put into practice within chemical and pharmaceutical companies, in laboratories of public and private structures, in Universities, in Research Institutes, and in the National Health Service.
The greater attention to the pharmaceutical sector characterizes and distinguishes the TESTA Course from other degree courses belonging to class L-29, as the proposed training path will allow the graduate to evaluate the environmental risk related to the production and release into the environment of pharmaceutical production waste, active ingredients, or final formulations, operating within chemical-pharmaceutical industries in relation to EMA guidelines on Environmental Risk Assessment (EMEA/CHMP/SWP/4447/00 corr 2). The objective is particularly important to limit the environmental impact consequent to the market release and use of human medicines. The graduate in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology will therefore be able to contribute concretely to the necessary obligations to prepare the documentation to be submitted to Regulatory Authorities (in the request for Marketing Authorization of a new drug or for modifications to existing drugs), to demonstrate having carried out the environmental impact assessment and adopted the preventive measures provided.
The Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology Degree Course is structured over three years: two semesters intended to provide a basic preparation and four semesters of a more specifically professionalizing nature, during which lessons, exercises, laboratories, seminars, field practical activities, free courses, participation in external seminars, conferences, and meetings are scheduled. The didactic structure of the Degree Course includes a group of basic disciplines, followed by disciplines of a professional nature. The course aims to provide the graduate with adequate scientific-technical training to enable direct insertion into the job market. Each discipline will be evaluated by teachers through in-course and final assessments, through the administration of written tests or oral assessments, or a combination of both. The examination methods will be detailedly described by each teacher in class, as well as illustrated in the corresponding Course Sheet.
At the end of the path, it is possible to carry out a professional internship of at least 150 hours for the recognition of 6 CFU, at laboratories of Companies or Convened Structures. Alternatively, the student may choose a research thesis path to be carried out within the Department or at External Companies and Structures. The internship activity will take place not before the third year attendance according to the modalities indicated in the study regulations. The Course of Study, together with the training internships at companies, public structures, and laboratories, also provides for study stays abroad within the framework of international agreements. Knowledge of a foreign language, preferably scientific English, is also required.

The present members agreed to provide a brief description of the proposals before proceeding to discuss the item on the agenda.
Consultation with representative organizations - at national and international level - of goods and services production, professions (Course establishment)
On April 15, 2019, the Establishing Committee for the TESTA Course, appointed by the Department of Pharmacy Council in 2018, met to evaluate the strategic plan for expanding the training offer with a shared training path of clear interest to companies operating in the regional and national territory. In the same meeting, the name 'Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology' was chosen for the Course to account for current industrial production needs for a 'circular' production fully protecting the environment. During the discussion, the concrete availability of Fater SpA to contribute to the delivery of some professionalizing subjects to be included in the study program was highlighted. It was also proposed to introduce highly qualified professional company teachers, and periods of training abroad and internships on the national and international territory were outlined.
Consultations were carried out with the main stakeholders: Teachers, Directors of chemical and pharmaceutical companies, as well as the Order of Chemists and Physicists of Lazio, Umbria, Abruzzo, and Molise, through meetings of the Establishing Committee formed by teachers and an industrial sector representative, and through the administration of questionnaires to industrial realities of the territory to evaluate training requests and needs to form graduates capable of performing specific functions in technical or professional roles in environmental protection.
Among the consulted organizations, the Order of Chemists and Physicists of Lazio, Umbria, Abruzzo, and Molise, through the interregional delegate, on November 25, 2019, evaluated the activation of the Course with a very positive opinion, proposing to consider, among the educational objectives, also topics related to the management of plants not only pharmaceutical but also for example for purification and thermal valorization in the environmental field, as well as considering in-depth on the classification of substances according to REACH and CLP regulations and the management of safety data sheets (MSDS), without neglecting regulatory references in the field of environmental authorizations for plant operation. The Order suggested to integrate the expressed indications within elective courses (3 CFU each) within the waste management of laboratories and forensic chemistry and toxicology, promptly received by the Establishing Committee.
The judgment expressed by Fater SpA during the Establishing Committee meetings, by the Analytic Hierarchy Bio Refinery Process (AHP) Development Leader, was widely favorable towards the current degree project, emphasizing that the current structure is suitable for adequate preparation of the required professional figures, especially specialized in the analysis and use of bioproducts extracted or recovered for direct industrial applications, essential for implementing eco-sustainable approaches in an economy based on recycling and valorization of industrial waste to be redirected to the production of medicated medical devices. The Establishing Committee accepted the reflections of the Fater SpA representative, proposing the establishment of an (affiliated) course named 'Recycling and Valorization of Waste and Circular Economy'.
Among the industrial realities, the judgment of Dompé Pharmaceuticals SpA was noted, which expressed its opinion through the completion of a questionnaire on July 24, 2019 by the Biotech Director of the L'Aquila plant. In particular, the opinion was positive regarding the course name and the proposed employment outlooks, considering that the professional figures the course aims to form respond to the needs of the company represented. Positive results of learning were considered in all reference areas, as well as being responsive to the competencies required for the formation of the professional figures provided by the course.
The pharmaceutical company BSP Pharmaceuticals with headquarters in Latina was involved through the completion of questionnaires on July 23 and 29, 2019 by the following professionals: Environmental, Health & Safety Director (EHS) & Qualified Person, Corporate Quality Operations Director, and Plant Director. The professionals consulted expressed a favorable opinion regarding the course name, while for the proposed employment outlooks, emphasis was placed on greater attention to professional toxicology and deeper insight regarding WHO guidelines on environmental risk assessment in the pharmaceutical field. Positive learning results were considered in all reference areas, and among the suggestions proposed, the need for greater focus on systems for preventing environmental contamination and the ability to prepare protocols and environmental risk assessment (ERA) reports was highlighted. Particular attention was recommended on the evaluation of products released into the environment in relation to climate change and ecosystem changes, on the implementation of knowledge and consequences related to human exposure to environmental pollutants, as well as deepening knowledge of computational toxicology. Finally, it was proposed to develop some courses in English to facilitate opportunities abroad and to prepare company presentations within the Course.
Taking into account the indications of the company executives, the Establishing Committee took charge of introducing within the disciplines of chemical, biological, and medical sectors, training aspects that reflect the suggestions emerging in various sections of the questionnaire.
The questionnaires completed by the responsible persons of the consulted industrial realities can be viewed at the address Consultation with representative organizations - at national and international level - of goods and services production, professions (Subsequent consultations)

Entry, path, and exit data The statistical data relating to the first and second cohort of students enrolled in the TESTA Course are for the academic years 2020-21 and 2021-22 and are updated to August 29, 2022 (Source S.I.Ca.S. at link http://gestapp.unich.it).
COHORT 2020-21
The students enrolled in the TESTA Course for the academic year 2020-21 were 43, of which 32 pure enrollments and 3 transfers (Tab. 1_S.I.Ca.S.). For the academic year 2020-21, 51 new careers were registered, but 7 students enrolled before January 31, 2021, withdrew, and one student transferred to another course (Tab. 2, 2-bis_S.I.Ca.S.).
The students enrolled in the 2020-21 cohort are predominantly female (60.5%) compared to male (39.5%). 58.1% of the enrolled students are 19 years old or younger, 16.3% are between 20-22 years old, 7% between 23-24 years old, and 18.6% over 25 years old (Tab. 3_S.I.Ca.S.).
34.9% of the enrolled students come from the same municipality, 34.9% from another municipality in the province, 21% from another province in the region, and 9.2% from outside the region (Tab. 4_S.I.Ca.S.). The S.I.Ca.S. data in Table 4-Ter show that 39 students are from the Abruzzo region (90.8%), 2 from Molise (4.6%), 1 from Campania (2.3%), and 1 from Sicily (2.3%).
The high school diploma obtained at the high schools is held by 46.51% of the enrolled students (of which 30.2% holds the scientific high school diploma and 9.3% the classical high school diploma), at technical institutes by 30.3%, at magistral schools by 13.95%, and at other schools by 7% (Tab. 5 and Tab. 5 Bis_S.I.Ca.S.).
The diploma grade of 100 and honors is reported by 2.3% of the enrolled students, 100 by 9.3% of the enrolled students, between 80 and 99 by 35% of the enrolled students, and up to 80 by 49% of the enrolled students (Tab. 6_S.I.Ca.S.).

Characteristics of the final exam The degree in Eco-sustainable Technologies and Environmental Toxicology is obtained after passing a final exam, which constitutes an individual training moment to complete the path carried out. During the final exam, the student presents and discusses their thesis project, also of an experimental nature, related to the educational objectives of the Course, which is written under the supervision of a faculty teacher. The final exam can be taken in English, and the final thesis can be presented in the same language.
Method of conducting the final exam The final exam can be taken in English, and the final thesis, whether compilative or experimental, can be presented in the same language.
However, a favorable and motivated opinion from the Course Council is necessary, guaranteeing the possibility of effectively evaluating the thesis due to sufficient competencies within the faculty body. In any case, the thesis and the thesis written in a foreign language must be accompanied by an adequate summary (abstract) in Italian.
The Degree Examination Committee is composed of a minimum of five and a maximum of seven members; it includes First and Second Class Teachers, Researchers, Contract Teachers, and professionals from external companies.
The final grade, expressed in hundredths, takes into account the weighted average of the grades obtained during the study course, plus:
A) a percentage up to a maximum of 10% in reference to the grade in hundredths obtained from the average of the student's career grades, and conditioned by the quality of the activity performed;
Additional points may be assigned by the Degree Committee:
B) 1 point if the student graduates during the course;
C) 0-1 point (at the discretion of the committee) if the student has had an international mobility within their study path;
D) 0-2 points for an experimental thesis.
The award of the honor (lode) is at the discretion of the Committee, taking into account the student's previous career and the thesis work.
The award of the honor requires the unanimous decision of the Committee. If the graduate has obtained, during the course, an average grade of at least 107/110 in the profit exams, the Committee may propose a mention for 'pregevole curriculum studiorum' to be approved unanimously.
The Degree Exam is normally held in the months of July, October, November, March, and April.
Procedures for requesting, characteristics, and obtaining the degree title.
The student must prepare a compilative or experimental thesis agreed with a Department teacher or from other Departments, or with a teacher from another Italian or foreign University, or with a researcher from other public or private institutions, following the signing of a convention or recognition of the visiting student status.
The thesis request must be submitted to the Course Director after obtaining at least 117 CFU, at the beginning of each month after all exam sessions, normally on the first Wednesday of March, April, May, June, July, September, October, November, and December. The supervisor and co-supervisor are appointed by the Course Council.
The discussion of a compilative thesis must take place at least three months after the appointment of the supervisor.
The discussion of an experimental thesis must take place at least six months after the appointment of the supervisor.
To be admitted to take the Degree Exam, the student must have obtained, in total, 171 CFU in the case of an experimental thesis, or 177 CFU in the case of a compilative thesis; must have submitted to the student office: - a request to the Rector at least 90 days before the graduation session - a final copy of the Thesis at least 15 days before the graduation session.
Summary of the technical report of the evaluation nucleus - SUA Sheet The design of the Course was carried out with appropriate timing and attention. The cultural and professional profiles of the figure the Course intends to form are clearly defined. The direct consultation of stakeholders is adequate at the local level, although not entirely at the national level.
The functions and competencies are described with sufficient precision and coherence with the professional profiles. The path is sufficiently coherent with the professional profile.
The course provides an admission test: the necessary knowledge for admission are defined in detail, as well as the modalities. OFA are correctly assigned in the main subjects (mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology) based on not reaching a minimum score in the corresponding questions of the test, and support courses are also provided for each subject.
The structural resources and teaching staff appear adequate. The monitoring of the Course is consistent with the University's AQ system.

Access Requirements Required knowledge for access Candidates who hold a secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as suitable may be admitted to the Biomedical Laboratory Techniques Study Program.
The prerequisites required for students enrolling in the course should include good interpersonal skills, teamwork abilities, and the capacity to analyze and solve problems.
An adequate preparation in biology and chemistry is required to be admitted to the Biomedical Laboratory Techniques Study Program. Students admitted to the course with a level below the predefined minimum grade will be required to attend preparatory teaching activities during the first semester of the first year, which must be compulsorily followed by students in debt. The assessment of results achieved in the preparatory teaching activities will be conducted within the evaluation of the corresponding courses.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITY OF CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [L605] BIOMEDICAL LABORATORY TECHNIQUES
SECTION: Admission Procedures
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/612

Admission Procedures Candidates with a Five-Year Upper Secondary School Diploma or an equivalent foreign qualification may be admitted to the Course of Study in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques. Admission to the first year is regulated and requires passing a multiple-choice admission test on topics specified by the Ministry. The test is held only if the number of applications exceeds available places. Admission to subsequent years for students from the same Course of Study at other universities is subject to available places within the previously approved regulated number by the Course of Study Council. Admitted students must demonstrate competence in Biology, Chemistry, and Physics. Any additional educational obligations (OFA) will be assigned based on the admission test results. In particular, candidates who score below 25% of the maximum score in Biology, Chemistry, and Physics on the entrance test will be enrolled with OFA. Students enrolled in the Course of Study in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques with OFA will be informed via email or direct meetings. Fulfilling OFA involves individual seminar-style training activities assigned for each discipline in which the student has a deficiency. OFA must be completed by the end of the first semester of the first year, and completion will be certified by the relevant discipline instructors through an oral verification test. Fulfilling OFA is required to take second-year exams. While enrollment in the second year is permitted, it will not be possible to take second-year exams before fulfilling the assigned OFA.

Program, texts and objectives Note regarding the selected sectors and credits for characteristic activities The VET/06 sector has been included among the characteristic disciplines Communication skills
The graduate in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques must be able to:
- demonstrate communication and listening skills towards users and various healthcare professionals with whom they interact in the workplace or occasionally come into contact, using both written and verbal communication forms. In particular, they must demonstrate the ability to complete dedicated forms, communicating clearly, concisely, and professionally in both verbal and written form, technically and grammatically accurate, in order to convey ideas, pose problems and find appropriate solutions.
- establish effective and collaborative relationships with other healthcare professionals, being aware of the specificities of different professional roles;
- demonstrate the ability to use information and computer technologies in their work environment.
Teaching tools: frontal lectures in the classroom, internship, reading and interpretation of international literature.
Assessment methods: oral reports on communication aspects; periodic meetings with tutors and the coordinator; oral and written presentation of projects.

SECTION: Critical Judgment (making judgements)
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/612

Critical Judgment (making judgements)
The biomedical laboratory techniques graduate must:
- demonstrate responsibility for their area of competence, performing technical-professional tasks autonomously in direct collaboration with other laboratory-qualified personnel responsible for various operational duties;
- exercise critical thinking to deliver effective technical diagnostic services;
- be responsible, in laboratory settings, for the correct execution of analytical procedures and their own work within specific functions, in accordance with protocols defined by responsible managers, and verify that delivered services meet predefined indicators and standards set by the facility manager;
- demonstrate the ability to consider other operators in the exercise of their actions;
- participate in the planning and organization of work within the facility where they operate.
- apply ethical principles in their professional conduct.
Teaching Methods: lectures, teaching laboratories, practical laboratory and/or equipped room lessons, internship, reading and interpretation of international literature.
Assessment Methods: written and oral reports on technical/professional aspects, discussion of clinically relevant practical cases.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITÀ DEGLI STUDI GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO – CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [L605] BIOMEDICAL LABORATORY TECHNIQUES
SECTION: Incoming Orientation
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/612

Incoming Orientation During the week of the start of lectures for the Study Program, a morning is dedicated to first-year students to explain in detail the purposes and structure of the Course. During this meeting, the Course Director and the Orientation Coordinator, Prof.ssa Susi Zara, appointed by the Course Council, illustrate the training path.
Students are informed that each teacher sets up office hours to personally address, with those who wish, issues related to the specific discipline, providing all necessary support. Additionally, all teachers are available to speak with students after lectures, either in groups or individually, to resolve issues related to teaching or of a personal nature.
During the meeting, the procedure to accelerate the recognition of CFU and/or exams in case of transfers or changes from other Universities or Study Programs is explained. Information is also provided on the location of classrooms and laboratories where lectures and training internships will take place. The name of the Professional Training Director (i.e., Dr. Maria Rita Marino) is provided, to whom students can turn for assistance with learning difficulties or issues in the professional internship path.
At the beginning of the second semester of the first year, when students start their internship period in hospital laboratories, the Internship Coordinators, together with the Professional Training Director and the Department Manager, welcome students to provide further explanations on the internship procedures and practical behavioral guidelines to follow.
After meetings with the Course Director, the Orientation Coordinator, and the Professional Training Director, a questionnaire is administered to new students to evaluate their satisfaction with the information received and its usefulness. Additionally, the Course Director monitors first-year student dropout rates to identify potential adaptation issues related to insufficient orientation.
In addition to the orientation meetings organized by the Study Program, the incoming orientation activity is managed centrally by the University. The University ensures students a continuous orientation process, starting from secondary school, continuing throughout their time at the University, and concluding by facilitating graduates' entry into the workforce. In particular, the Study Program actively participates in the annual Open Day event, held at the Chieti campus and involving all secondary schools in the Abruzzo region and neighboring areas. The main objective of Open Day is to support students in choosing the academic course most suitable for their aptitudes.
During Open Day, we offer seminars, meetings with our students, and guided tours of the research laboratories of the Department of Medical, Oral and Biotechnological Sciences and the CAST. Students have the opportunity to meet teachers, who stimulate interest and curiosity about biomedical disciplines while providing detailed information about the Course.
We also participate in the Student Fair, whose main objective is to create the first contact with students in their fourth and fifth years of secondary school to guide them toward a conscious choice of university studies. During the Fair, students can directly meet the Course Director and/or Prof.ssa Susi Zara, the Orientation Coordinator, to deepen their knowledge of the Biomedical Laboratory Techniques Study Program and understand its opportunities.
Additionally, we participate in meetings organized by the University at secondary schools, with the aim of guiding students on the opportunities arising from transitioning from high school to the professional training of the Study Program.

Orienting and ongoing tutoring The names of the President and Tutor instructors are listed on the Course of Study website, who are available daily to assist students in resolving any issues they may encounter during their educational path. Since the number of enrolled students per year never exceeds thirty, contact occurs in a fluid and continuous manner. During office hours, the instructor's commitment is aimed at assisting the student in resolving problems they present during the meeting.
The Course President also periodically evaluates, through the INGRID monitoring platform, any courses that represent critical points in the students' educational path. If criticalities arise, the President convenes the instructors of the relevant courses together with the members of the Course of Study Teaching Committee to agree on corrective measures to implement.
Particular importance is given to the relationship between Student and Laboratory Tutor during daily professional internship. The National Commission of the Degree Course in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques has recently drafted a document on the importance of student evaluation of the quality of internship environments (see attached PDF file). The Course of Study uses this evaluation form, administered annually to students, to monitor their perception and level of satisfaction with the professional internship experience, with the aim of activating improvement strategies if necessary.
The Course of Study also promotes ongoing student orientation through the support of Student-Tutors provided by the Department of Medical, Oral and Biotechnological Sciences (DSMOB). These students are selected through a specific call to carry out preparatory and recovery didactic-integrative activities for students of our Course who face difficulties in acquiring knowledge and passing exams. The Course President identifies through the INGRID monitoring platform any courses that represent criticalities for students. Once identified, the President convenes the instructors of the relevant courses together with the members of the Course of Study Teaching Committee to agree on the support activities that the Student-Tutor will carry out for students who request them. During the 2023-2024 academic year, the Course of Study had Mr. Francesco Rosucci as Student-Tutor, a student of our university enrolled in the sixth year of the Degree Course in Medicine and Surgery.

SECTION: Career Guidance
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/612

Career Guidance The Course organizes extracurricular seminars conducted by professionals from the National Health Service (SSN), Governmental Institutes, and Scientific Associations of healthcare professions to train and prepare students for the demands of the job market. Specifically, these seminar activities are organized by the Course in collaboration with the Istituto Zooprofilattico Sperimentale del Lazio e della Toscana (IZSLT), the Consiglio per la Ricerca in Agricoltura e l'Analisi dell'Economia Agraria (CREA), and the Associazione Italiana dei Tecnici di Istologia e Citologia (AITIC) (see the file of seminar activities organized for the 2023-2024 academic year for students enrolled in the third year of the course). An additional support for career orientation is provided by the modification of the Course's academic structure, which since the 2021-2022 academic year has introduced disciplines within the SSD Vet/04 (i.e., 'Animal Food Inspection'), Vet/06 ('Parasitology and Parasitic Diseases of Food') and Agr/15 (i.e., 'Food Science and Technology'). This is done with the aim of further enhancing employability not only in the biomedical sector (recent data from AlmaLaurea shows an employment rate for our biomedical laboratory techniques graduates exceeding 90% one year after graduation, with most employed in the public sector, both in the SSN and in university biomedical research), but also in the agri-food and veterinary sectors.

To improve the management of student careers, the Course systematically and periodically analyzes and monitors the employment outcomes of its graduates, primarily using data provided by AlmaLaurea.

Additionally, the Course continuously encourages students to utilize the University's placement service for career orientation. To increase employment and employability of its students, the 'G. d'Annunzio' University has established a comprehensive placement structure. In accordance with Law 30/03, known as the Biagi Law, Italian universities can now carry out job intermediary activities, collaborating with public employment centers and private operators to provide new employment services. The 'd'Annunzio' University has promptly activated in this regard, offering a centralized placement service to its graduates and local businesses. To this end, the 'd'Annunzio' University launched the S.T.A.R.T. project (Internships, Traineeships, Advanced Training, Research, Territory and Placement), aiming to facilitate the meeting between universities, businesses, and research systems to develop and consolidate an effective relationship and service system. This system aims to facilitate communication between business needs, employment integration processes, and training plans, while providing support during the transition to work for knowledge resources. The University is therefore able to offer businesses seeking young workforce resources, both through employment contracts and through training and orientation internships, not only direct contact with the desired professional figure, but also support services to identify the most suitable professional profiles for specific needs.

Student Opinions During the 2022-2023 academic year, 751 questionnaires were collected from our students, with the number of training activities involved in the survey amounting to 44 out of 44 total activities (100% coverage) present in the Study Program. The overall average score assigned to the Study Program in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques was 3.45 points, exceeding the University's average (i.e., 3.44 points) and the average score of Study Programs in the Health Area (i.e., 3.40 points) (the summary graph of these scores is provided in the PDF file of Table B6). Specifically, the "Overall Satisfaction" score given by our students towards the Study Program in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques (i.e., 3.34 points) is largely aligned with the score students gave to the University (i.e., 3.35 points) and to the Study Programs in the Health Area (i.e., 3.32 points). However, the score recorded by our Study Program regarding "Logistical and Organizational Aspects" (i.e., 3.51 points) and "Teaching Effectiveness" (3.50 points) was higher than the scores recorded by the University (i.e., 3.48 points: for both "Logistical and Organizational Aspects" and "Teaching Effectiveness") and by the Study Programs in the Health Area (i.e., 3.43 points: for both "Logistical and Organizational Aspects" and "Teaching Effectiveness") (the summary graph of these scores is provided in the PDF file of Table B6).

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding (applying knowledge and understanding)
The student and graduate in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques will utilize the acquired basic knowledge and be supported by it in every laboratory procedure that involves the application of established techniques or the development of new methodologies. Knowledge of the etiology of pathological processes, the related pathogenic mechanism, the reactions to pathogens, and the consequences for the organism constitute a fundamental prerequisite for understanding the diagnostic methods used in various areas of Laboratory Medicine. Will be able to:
- Analyze instrumental procedures and understand errors in relation to biological operational descriptions.
- Apply techniques to understand cellular and tissue alterations, the specific mechanisms of the immune response in neoplastic transformation.
- Apply techniques related to the main hormonal regulation mechanisms.
- Apply specific and indispensable competencies for the appropriate use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) as required by current regulations, both regarding the handling of organic material and its correct disposal, as well as the safe use of laboratory reagents.
- Use basic computer science principles in the laboratory area, with particular reference to the storage of data and clinical health reports.
- Apply knowledge to understand and apply information search processes on the Web.
- Translate the principles of psychology related to emotions, motivational states, and their influence on behavior in the workplace.
- Manage the acquisition of cellular and tissue material, verify its consistency in terms of good preservation, and process it in the most appropriate way for resolving the diagnostic question.
- Apply histocytological, immunohistocytological, and molecular techniques on biological tissue and cellular samples, knowing their potential and utility in the preventive and predictive diagnosis of neoplastic diseases, with particular attention to current laboratory protocols and required quality controls.
- Critically analyze results and implement all improvement strategies that allow the pathologist to formulate a diagnosis more responsive to the clinical question posed.
- Apply techniques in the field of microbiology, with particular attention to the bacteriological field, and in the pathways to be used for infection diagnosis.
- Apply current microbiology techniques necessary to grow, classify, and identify bacteria; with both traditional and innovative procedures dedicated to the search for viruses and/or their components in various biological materials.
- Apply techniques used in virology diagnostic and research laboratories regarding DNA and RNA viruses; apply laboratory techniques to highlight pathogenic fungi and reveal the presence of pathogenic protozoa for humans in various pathological materials.
- Apply parasitological techniques used in veterinary diagnostic laboratories to diagnose animal infestation and/or in animal-derived foods.
- Apply techniques related to the general principles of diseases caused by infectious agents, possessing essential knowledge to identify etiology, epidemiology, clinical aspects, diagnostic principles, and therapeutic and preventive guidelines for major infectious diseases.
- Apply methods for critical evaluation and clinical interpretation of the results of major laboratory diagnostic investigations.
- Apply criteria for critical and interpretative evaluation of the results of laboratory methods used.
- Apply criteria for critical evaluation and interpretation of the results of major laboratory diagnostic investigations in liver diseases, cardiovascular diseases, hemostasis, and hereditary constitutional diseases, as well as molecular techniques engaged in the diagnosis of neoplasms.
- Apply the main diagnostic methods and techniques used in the Immunohematology laboratory.

Learning Skills (learning skills)
The student will be able to:
- Self-assess one's competencies, knowing how to identify one's development and learning needs, as well as plan, organize, and develop one's actions.
- Share knowledge within work teams.
- Conduct independent study.
- Research information necessary to resolve problems or uncertainties in professional practice, using both primary sources (research studies) and secondary sources (guidelines, systematic reviews).
These abilities will be achieved in their entirety and fully through the mandatory attendance of the Professional Internship and didactic laboratory activities, under the guidance of a tutor.
Teaching tools: classroom lectures, seminars, internship.
Verification methods: the evaluation of learning abilities will be carried out through theoretical-practical exams, discussion on specific technical/professional aspects related to clinical cases; written and oral reports on these technical/professional aspects; research and production of teaching materials.

Knowledge and Understanding (knowledge and understanding)
The student, through basic prerequisite disciplines, knows and understands:
- The principles of Medical Physics, Applied Biology, Medical Genetics, Human Anatomy and Histology, Medical Chemistry and Systematic and Applied Biochemistry.
- Human Physiology and General Pathology.
- Basic principles of Computer Science, Information Processing, and Medical Statistics, in the area of Laboratory Medicine, with particular reference to the management of current Systems.
- Principles of General Psychology, Labor Law, and Organization of Health Services in Laboratory Medicine.
- Principles of Research Methodology and HTA.
- Principles of Ethics and Professional Deontology.
- Principles of Safety and Quality in Laboratory Medicine as a constitutive part of the citizen's right to health.

In the Pathological Anatomy Learning Area, the student knows and understands:
- The pathological anatomy of the most frequent human neoplastic forms.
- Basic knowledge of molecular biology and current techniques for molecular diagnosis in pathological anatomy.
- Methodological foundations of histological and cytological techniques used in clinical anatomo-pathological practice.
- Types of diagnostic anatomo-pathological exams.
- Tissue and cytological sampling methods.
- Types of biological material preservation.
- The method of liquid-phase collection of cytological samples.
- Procedures for accepting cytological and biopsy material.
- Macroscopic examination of the surgical piece, with reference to the rapid examination.
- General principles of the main fixation, processing, embedding of material in paraffin, and cutting techniques.
- Protocols for preparation, cutting, and staining according to international guidelines.
- Staining methods for histological slides, pathological anatomy of the most frequent human neoplastic forms.
- Logistical, instrumental requirements, and quality control procedures for the diagnostic use of histocytological techniques.
- The pathological anatomy report.
- How to prepare a histological sample on which to perform immunohistochemical staining.
- Types of antibodies and methods of production of monoclonal and polyclonal antibodies.
- Techniques for antigen identification and localization: conjugation of antibodies with fluorescent and enzyme tracers.
- Antigen unmasking or recovery techniques.
- Applications of immunohistochemistry in Pathological Anatomy.
- Methods for preparing histological samples using Tissue-MicroArray (TMA).
- Automated methods for preparing and reading histological preparations.
- Role of molecular biology techniques in anatomo-pathological diagnosis, with particular reference to FISH and CISH preparation methods.
- Methods for extracting DNA and RNA from biological samples of blood, cytological, and tissue origin using manual and standardized techniques.
- Methods for determining the mutational status: PCR, real-time, and gene sequencing.
- Sanger sequencing: manual and automated via capillary.
- Pyrosequencing.
- Targeted molecular therapies in oncology: molecular biology techniques for evaluating the expression of 'theranostic' molecular markers.
- Cytological techniques, smear, thin layer, cytocentrifugation, and cell block; automation systems: Thin prep processor, fixation, and staining.
- Diagnostic interpretation of microscope preparations, benignity criteria, reporting systems in urinary cytology; cytology of effusions, pulmonary cytology, fine-needle aspiration cytology.
- Cervicovaginal cytology, population screening, from Pat Test to HPV DNA TEST, natural history of HPV infections, cytology of HPV-induced lesions, and Bethesda reporting system.

In the Microbiology Learning Area, the student knows and understands:
- The concept of species and the classification of microorganisms.
- Description, pathogenesis, laboratory diagnosis, control measures, and prevention of the most medically significant bacteria.
- Description, pathogenesis, laboratory diagnosis, control measures, and prevention of the main viruses responsible for diseases in humans and Prions.
- The shape and structure of the bacterial cell and spore.
- Bacterial reproduction, metabolism, pathogenic action, mutations, and recombination.
- General principles, mechanism of action, and resistance to antimicrobial agents.
- Structure and classification of animal viruses, viral replication strategy, and pathogenic action.
- Hospital-acquired infections.
- The importance of adopting Procedures; Operating Instructions; Traceability of the analytical process in a certified Microbiology laboratory.

In the Clinical Pathology Learning Area, the student knows and understands:
- Planning and implementation of technical-diagnostic activities strictly related to alterations and possible pathological interactions related to the treated pathologies.
- Correct use of complex laboratory equipment necessary for conducting specific examinations on the topics covered.
- Critical evaluation, based on acquired knowledge and experience, of the results obtained by applying specific Laboratory Methods.
- Results obtained within the respective Quality Control.
- Laboratory Methods of dynamic-functional tests, necessary for evaluating physiological and pathological hormonal metabolism.
- The meaning of the main tests indicating altered function of the excretory organ.
- Correct use of molecular techniques for studying gene functions.
- Correlation between gene expression and clinical parameters in tumor progression.
- Correct use of in vitro and in vivo techniques for studying molecular mechanisms involved in controlling tumor progression.
- Biotechnological analyses for Medicine and Personalized Therapy.

In the Immunoematology Learning Area, the student knows and understands:
- Physiology and morphology of blood cells, Hematopoiesis, Acute and Chronic Leukemias, Lymphomas, Anemias, Hemostasis Pathophysiology, Coagulopathies.
- Collection, production, Quality Control, and preservation of blood components and derived plasma.
- Organization and Institutional Accreditation of a Blood Transfusion Center.
- The AB0 system, the Rh system, and other blood groups, Blood Group Genetics, and Detection Techniques.
- Autoimmune hemolytic disease and Neonatal hemolytic disease.
- Platelet antigens and their relevance in transfusion medicine.

Brief Course Description
The Study Course (CdS) in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques (TLB) belongs to Class 3 of degrees in Technical Health Professions (L/SNT3). Its objective is to train health professionals capable of performing diagnostic procedures on biological materials with professional autonomy and authority, in accordance with Law 10 August 2000, n. 251, and in implementation of the regulations concerning the identification of figures and their professional profiles defined by a decree of the Minister of Health (D.M. n. 745 of September 1994) and subsequent integrations and modifications. The courses, professional internships carried out in hospital laboratories, and thesis internships at university biomedical research laboratories enrich the graduate's skills, who finds employment in the pharmaceutical industry with a diagnostic and cosmetic focus, in the agro-food and animal husbandry industry, as well as in laboratories of the armed forces and in those of public and private biomedical research institutions. The CdS is conducted over three years, with a total of 180 CFU and 20 exams. The final exam has the value of a State Exam enabling professional practice. The degree allows access to Master's Degree Courses in the Class of Sciences of Technical Health Professions (LM/SNT3) and the Master's Degree Course in Nutrition and Health Sciences (LM/61), without academic debts, to first-level Master's programs, and to Advanced Courses.

External Effectiveness
For the employment statistics of our CdS graduates one year after obtaining their first-level degree, we used AlmaLaurea data presented on June 12, 2023. Graduates who consented to be interviewed for statistical research purposes were 13 out of 17 total graduates. 61.5% of them enrolled in a second-level degree course after their first-level degree, significantly higher than the national average for the technical health professions degree class (L/SNT3, SNT/3), which is 25.9%. The percentage of interviewed graduates who declared being employed in work activities or performing paid training activities was 92.3% (12 out of 13 interviewed graduates). This percentage is higher than the national average for the L/SNT3 class, which is 74.1%. The attached PDF file shows the employment and training status of our graduates.

The employment characteristics of the graduates are:
- 61.5% enrolled in a second-level degree course after their first-level degree.
- 92.3% employed in work activities or performing paid training activities.
- Satisfaction rating consistently higher than the national average.

The Study Course has adequate teaching and structural resources to support the new programming and its full implementation. The Study Course covers a field of clear professional relevance. The proposed curriculum is significantly improved in terms of coherence, transparency, and effectiveness, contributing to the goals of rationalization and qualification of the University's educational offer.

Admission procedures The number of students admitted to the Master's Degree Programme in Cardiovascular Pathophysiology and Cardiovascular Perfusion Techniques is planned in relation to the actual availability of teaching staff, suitable facilities and teaching equipment, and services operating in the local structures of the National Health Service or in Regional structures contracted with the University. Candidates who hold a secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent may be admitted to the Degree Programme in Cardiovascular Pathophysiology and Cardiovascular Perfusion Techniques. Students admitted to the Programme who score below 25% of the maximum score in Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics and Physics in the entrance test will be assigned Additional Educational Requirements (OFA). The annual list of students required to complete the OFA will be published on the online site of the School of Medicine and Health Sciences at https://scuolamedicina.unich.it or www.med.unich.it, in the section reserved for the Programme. Completion of the OFA involves individual assignments of seminar-style training activities for each discipline in which the student has shown deficiency. Assessment will be conducted through the successful completion of a final exam, which must be taken within the first year of the Programme. As specified in Article 49, paragraph 3, point b of the University Academic Regulations, students who have not completed the Additional Educational Requirements as stated in Article 28 of the University Academic Regulations are not permitted to enroll in second-year courses. Therefore, while enrollment in the second year is permitted, it will not be possible to take second-year exams before completing the assigned OFA.

Programme, texts and objectives Communication skills
The graduate in cardiovascular pathophysiology techniques must be able to:
- Establish professional relationships and collaborate with other healthcare professionals, being aware of the specificities of different professional roles
- Demonstrate effective communication skills with users and in relationships with other professionals
- Assume leadership roles towards colleagues and students, including delegation and supervision of clinical activities provided by others, ensuring compliance with quality and safety standards in planning and managing care
- Effectively communicate technical and clinical assessments and decisions using verbal, non-verbal and written methods within interdisciplinary healthcare teams
- Collaborate with the care team to implement and develop protocols and guidelines
- Effectively communicate with patients, families and other professionals to provide optimal healthcare.

Teaching methodologies and activities, didactic tools to develop expected outcomes:
- Frontal lessons, videos and critical analysis of films, simulations, narratives, testimonies
- Discussion of cases and paradigmatic relational situations in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions, internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various contexts with debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess relational experiences with users and the team.

Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes:
- Observation of film or written frames, dialogues with structured grids;
- Assessment feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation forms and clinical reports).

Judgment autonomy
The graduate in cardiovascular pathophysiology techniques must demonstrate the ability to:
- Apply ethical principles in their professional behavior
- Assume responsibility for their work during professional practice in accordance with the professional profile and the Code of Ethics
- Recognize differences in competencies and responsibilities between the graduated cardiovascular pathophysiology technician and other healthcare professionals
- Demonstrate initiative and autonomy defined in their work activities Teaching methods and learning activities, teaching tools to develop expected outcomes:
- Frontal lessons, guided reading and application, case discussion in small groups with presentations in plenary sessions, internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various contexts and progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility, debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess professional practice experiences.
Assessment tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes
- Written and oral exams, staged case tests,
- Evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation forms and clinical reports on professional practice)
- Structured objective exam in 'blocks' 'flowchart'.

Orientation in Entry The "G. d'Annunzio" University, through its Orientation, Placement, Student Rights and Disability Sector, provides support to Upper Secondary School students in making the challenging choice of the most suitable academic course for their abilities, assisting them in university studies to prevent initial evaluation errors from causing delays or abandonment of the chosen path, and ultimately facilitating their entry into the job market and professions. Orientation encompasses a set of services offered by the University of Chieti-Pescara "Gabriele d'Annunzio" to improve students' relationship with the University, accompanying them throughout their academic journey from choosing a study direction to entering the workforce through specific and targeted activities for prospective students, enrolled students, and graduates.
The service is coordinated by a Rector's delegate for orientation, appointed by the School of Medicine and Health Sciences (Prof. Giustino Orlando), assisted by the interim Sector Manager (Mr. Marco Costantini) and a delegate from the Department of the Study Program, appointed by the Department Director. Entry-level orientation services include periodic public presentations of the educational offer, inviting Upper Secondary School students from the territory and from out-of-region schools upon request, as well as participation in orientation fairs organized by various national entities.
Orientation services are provided by organizing presentations of the Educational Offer, coordinating University orientation with Department orientation, and involving Upper Secondary School students in meetings and seminars at school institutions:
Open Day: Annual event held at the Chieti and Pescara campuses, inviting all Upper Secondary Schools in the Abruzzo region and neighboring regions. During this event, the University presents its wide range of study paths within an Educational Offer structured into 4 main academic areas (Health Sciences, Scientific, Social and Humanities) and organized into 68 Study Programs offered by 14 Departments.
- Student Fairs and Exhibitions: Events where direct meetings with Department and Study Program professors are possible to deepen knowledge of the University and understand its opportunities.
The University organizes its own Student Fair but also actively participates in Student Fairs organized by other cities throughout the academic year (e.g., Macerata, Fermo, Ascoli Piceno, Bari, etc.), as well as abroad (e.g., University of Tirana).
- School Visits: Presentations of Study Programs and seminars organized by Departments or the Study Program itself to guide students from Upper Secondary School to university studies.
- Urban Box: The "d'Annunzio" University has signed an agreement with the City of Pescara for the use of the Urban Box in Piazza della Rinascita as a meeting point with young people and citizens. The Urban Box serves as a showcase facing the city of Pescara, where the University's Educational Offer is presented interactively through videos, brochures, and staff.
- PNRR 2026 Orientation: Following requests from Upper Secondary Schools to activate PNRR School-University Orientation agreements, orientation courses are offered at the University. From the start of the academic year until May, 15-hour orientation courses for different schools are scheduled, held in person and following two modalities: one day of course held at the Chieti campus, featuring a module explaining the university system and TOLC, and two separate modules presenting all Health Sciences and Scientific Study Programs. The second day of course, held at the Pescara campus, involves courses aimed at presenting Social-Humanities Study Programs and all tools for choosing a university path. At the end of the course, the AlmaOrientati questionnaire is administered to better understand each student's individual profile. Based on the results, students can further explore their test results with the support of experts from each of the four areas present at the Pescara campus.
- Universities Unveiled: CRUI has decided to establish the National University Day on March 20, coinciding with International Happiness Day and within the Minerva Week, a period dedicated to celebrating knowledge and education. For this occasion, the University participated with meetings, workshops, and debates organized on campus open to all citizens.
Through collaboration with a group of professors, the orientation service is also responsible for producing both printed and online versions of the Student Guide, an invaluable information tool and first step in self-orientation, as well as supporting Upper Secondary School students transitioning to university and new enrollees.
The Study Program representatives, who participate in numerous orientation events held across the territory, invite graduating students and students in their fourth year of Upper Secondary School to complete the AlmaOrientati questionnaire available on the University's Orientation Portal, a useful tool to help future enrollees monitor their knowledge of the university world and reflect on self-orientation.
The University provides for free a mobile application specifically developed to more easily access the Orientation Services offered by the University of Chieti-Pescara "Gabriele d'Annunzio". Through this application (App Ud'A Orienta), it is possible to learn about the Educational Offer, discover services, inquire about fees, receive updated information on Open Days and all the numerous Orientation initiatives offered by the University.
To support the activities carried out by the University, the Study Program has sought to identify additional initiatives to provide clear, simple, and immediate responses to the information requests of families and prospective students.

Student Opinions The census based on the pre-exam questionnaire administered to students of the Study Program in Techniques of Cardiovascular Physiopathology and Cardiovascular Perfusion (L-SNT-3) for the academic year 2022/2023 provided an average score for all evaluated courses equal to 3.46
The value is lower than that of the academic year 2021/202 (3.56) and equal to the year 2020/2021 (3.46)
From the analysis of the analytical sheet of the macroindicators, it emerges that the Course presents an average (3.46) decline compared to last year 2021/2022 (3.56), but remains higher than the University's percentage (3.43) and the Health Area (3.39).
Regarding the index related to the preliminary knowledge possessed, the same are considered sufficient with a slight reduction in the average value (3.23) compared to previous years 3.28 (2021/2022) and higher than 2020/2021 (3.22). The percentage related to the perceived study load is similar (3.39) compared to the previous academic year (3.40) and higher than the 3.30 of the academic year 2020/2021. The same trend for results regarding the adequacy of the provided teaching material (3.37) compared to 3.47 (2021/2022).
Analyzing the scores received by individual courses (min=1, max=4) divided into levels (A= from 3.5 to 4 inclusive; B= from 3 to 3.5 not inclusive; C= from 2.5 to 3 not inclusive, and D= from 1 to 2.5 not inclusive), it emerges that 49 courses were evaluated in the current academic year 2021/2022.
The percentage of courses in Level A (55.55%) has been maintained (55% of the year 2021/2022 and approximately 34% of the year 2020/2021). Courses that received a Level B score constitute 42% for the academic year 2022/2023 compared to 40.8% of the academic year 2021/2022 and 62.8% of 2020/2021.
Courses evaluated at Level C represent 7.9% compared to 4% in 2021/22.
Also in the academic year 2022/2023, as in the previous year, no course was evaluated at Level D.
Although the values remain higher than those of the University and the Health Area, the reduction in some parameters used can be attributed to the post-Covid resumption of in-person teaching activities, including laboratories, and the presence of new teachers who must still interact with the Course and new students. Moreover, school learning and remote lessons during the Covid period may be responsible for the reduction in the index related to the preliminary knowledge possessed and also the level of interest in the studied topics. It is important, however, to resort to further strategies and corrective actions to be implemented by the CDS, the Parity Committee of Teachers-Students, and the AQ Management Group.
