GRADUATE OPINIONS From the Alma Laurea survey in the 2022 survey year, 18 graduates were interviewed compared to 7 in 2021.
From the data analysis, it emerges that 50% considered the study load of the courses appropriate to the duration of the Course, a percentage higher than the total class of Universities (50% vs 43.8%), with a slight decline in satisfaction regarding teacher-student relationships compared to the previous year (always or almost always adequate and often adequate respectively at 83.4% compared to 85.7% in Academic Year 2021/2022).
The overall evaluation of classrooms remains positive, although reduced compared to Academic Year 2021/2022 (always or almost always adequate and often adequate respectively at 22.2% and 55.6% compared to 42.9% and 57.1% in the previous academic year); this variation may be correlated with the health emergency and the difficult resumption of in-person activities post-COVID-19.
Although only 22% of students used the computer stations in Academic Year 2022/2023, these were rated adequate in 100% of cases compared to 25% in 2021/2022. There was also an improvement in the evaluation of equipment for other teaching activities (always or almost always adequate and often adequate at 76.9% compared to 66.7% in the previous academic year). The data suggests targeted actions to improve students' awareness of the potential offered by the Course.
With regard to overall course satisfaction, a decrease was observed compared to the previous Academic Year (definitely yes + more yes than no at 83.4% vs 90.3%). This data, not emerging from frequent meetings with the Student-Teacher Parity Commission, can also be interpreted based on the analysis of the interviewed cohort, which faced difficulties in organizing internships during the COVID period and the challenging recovery required for some students outside the course.
The CDS will continue to identify strategies to improve these parameters, considering the positive feedback from the Parity Commission, particularly focusing on internships that faced significant difficulties during the COVID era and strategies to be developed in the cyclical review.

BRIEF COURSE DESCRIPTION
The Bachelor's Degree in Techniques of Cardiovascular Pathophysiology and Cardiovascular Perfusion qualifies for the profession of Cardiovascular Pathophysiology and Cardiovascular Perfusion Technician. This profession is governed by the Ministry of Health Decree of July 27, 1998, No. 316, and subsequent amendments.
Graduates must possess the necessary scientific foundations and theoretical-practical preparation to be qualified to practice the profession of Cardiovascular Pathophysiology and Cardiovascular Perfusion Technician and the methodology and culture required for continuous professional development. They must have a level of professional, decision-making, and operational autonomy derived from theoretical and practical training, including the acquisition of behavioral competencies, achieved within the specific work context, to ensure full mastery of all necessary competencies and their immediate applicability in the workplace. The objective of the Bachelor's Degree in Techniques of Cardiovascular Pathophysiology and Cardiovascular Perfusion is to provide specific technical preparation, supporting medical staff.
The Course provides fundamental biomedical and technical knowledge to form the professional figure, through in-depth study during the training path, alongside basic subjects, in various fields such as cardiology, vascular diagnostics, general, thoracic, and cardiac surgery, vascular diagnostics, cardiac surgery, pulmonology, oncology, intensive care, dialysis, and emergency procedures for managing devices that support and/or replace cardiac and/or respiratory functions.
This is a highly specialized figure with numerous professional profiles: hemodynamics technician, extracorporeal circulation technician, sonographer, electrophysiology technician.
Upon completion of the training path, the graduate must possess knowledge and skills to:
- Manage computer systems for transmitting and managing cardiac exams
- Manage the technical execution of the complete echocardiographic exam, including quantitative and echoflowmetric evaluation of the cardiac and/or vascular system
- Perform instrumental control of patients with implantable pacemaker and automatic defibrillator devices
- Perform instrumental diagnostic procedures in outpatient settings and/or with the aid of telemedicine and cardiac telemetry tools
- Conduct tests for evaluating cardiorespiratory function (spirometry)
- Manage cardiovascular and respiratory assistance
- Use normothermic and hyperthermic extracorporeal techniques for antiblastic, pelvic, peritoneal, thoracic, limb, and liver therapy
- Apply organ preservation protocols and transportation management
- Apply extracorporeal dialysis techniques
- Manage intraoperative plasmaferesis techniques, preparation of platelet gel, and fibrin glue
- Oversee the operation and maintenance of equipment related to extracorporeal circulation techniques, hemodynamic techniques, and non-invasive cardiology
- Manage electrocardiography, exercise electrocardiography, dynamic electrocardiography (Holter), and event storage systems for brady-tachyarrhythmias
- Ensure the correct application of required support techniques
- Ensure the correct application of required diagnostic and therapeutic prescriptions
- Independently manage extracorporeal circulation techniques and hemodynamics of patients artificially supported by the heart-lung machine
- Ensure blood oxygenation and systemic perfusion
- Apply cerebral protection techniques in procedures involving cerebral vessels
- Document extracorporeal circulation data on the clinical chart
- Make decisions consistent with legal, ethical, and deontological dimensions regulating healthcare organization and professional responsibility
- Participate in the development of guidelines to be applied to procedures, respecting the quality-safety principle (clinical risk management)
- Use tools and methodologies for quality assessment and review
- Ensure patients and significant others receive relevant and up-to-date information about their health status
- Collaborate in teaching and tutoring activities, both in basic and continuous training
- Recognize and respect the roles and competencies of oneself and other members of the care team, establishing collaborative relationships
- Interact and actively collaborate with interprofessional teams
- Implement health education interventions for healthy individuals and prevention interventions
All theoretical knowledge provided to students is essential for the professional internship practice, which requires approximately 1500 hours over the three-year period and represents the necessary effort for students to achieve the expected competencies.

SPECIFIC COURSE LEARNING OBJECTIVES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE TRAINING PATH
Upon completion of the three-year path, the graduate must be able to:
- Conduct tests for evaluating cardiorespiratory function (spirometry)
- Manage computer systems for transmitting and managing cardiac exams
- Manage the technical execution of the complete echocardiographic exam, including quantitative and echoflowmetric evaluation of the cardiac and/or vascular system
- Perform instrumental control of patients with implantable pacemaker and automatic defibrillator devices
- Perform instrumental diagnostic procedures in outpatient settings and/or with the aid of telemedicine and cardiac telemetry tools
- Manage cardiovascular and respiratory assistance related to techniques, technologies, and devices used in short, medium, and long term, including ECMO and mechanical support systems for cardiac function
- Use normothermic and hyperthermic extracorporeal techniques for antiblastic, pelvic, peritoneal, thoracic, limb, and liver therapy
- Apply organ preservation protocols and transportation management
- Apply extracorporeal dialysis techniques
- Manage intraoperative plasmaferesis techniques, preparation of platelet gel, and fibrin glue
- Oversee the operation and maintenance of equipment related to extracorporeal circulation techniques, mechanical support for cardiac and/or respiratory function, hemodynamic techniques, interventional cardiology, and non-invasive cardiology
- Manage electrocardiography, exercise electrocardiography, dynamic electrocardiography (Holter), and event storage systems for brady-tachyarrhythmias
- Ensure the correct application of required support techniques
- Ensure the correct application of required diagnostic and therapeutic prescriptions
- Independently manage extracorporeal circulation techniques and hemodynamics of patients artificially supported by the heart-lung machine
- Ensure blood oxygenation and systemic perfusion
- Apply cerebral protection techniques in procedures involving cerebral vessels
- Document extracorporeal circulation data and cardiovascular-respiratory assistance monitoring data on the clinical chart, both in paper and electronic format
- Make decisions consistent with legal, ethical, and deontological dimensions regulating healthcare organization and professional responsibility
- Participate in the development of guidelines to be applied to procedures, respecting the quality-safety principle (clinical risk management)
- Use tools and methodologies for quality assessment and review
- Ensure patients and significant others receive relevant and up-to-date information about their health status
- Collaborate in teaching and tutoring activities, both in basic and continuous training
- Recognize and respect the roles and competencies of oneself and other members of the care team, establishing collaborative relationships
- Interact and actively collaborate with interprofessional teams
- Implement health education interventions for healthy individuals and prevention interventions
- Manage clinical and instrumental patient data collection and analysis systems
- Perform and interpret hemostasis diagnostics (coagulation and platelet function) for managing mechanical support of cardiac and/or respiratory function
- Acquire competencies related to blood and blood product management, including indications and complications, through knowledge of phenotypic typing and relevant laboratory tests
- Acquire knowledge and competencies for safe workplace management to draft and apply protocols and procedures

FINAL EXAM CHARACTERISTICS
According to Article 7 of the Interministerial Decree of February 19, 2009, the final exam consists of:
a) a practical exam where the student must demonstrate acquisition of theoretical, practical, and technical skills specific to the professional profile;
b) preparation and defense of a thesis.

The exam is organized by the Minister of Education, University, and Research, in agreement with the Minister of Labor, Health, and Social Policies, in two national sessions.

FINAL EXAM PROCEDURE
The student, upon completion of their training, takes the graduation exam, which the Study Program Council prepares according to the Interministerial Decree of February 19, 2009, Article 7. The graduation exam, consisting of practical skills demonstration (Technical-Practical Exam) and thesis preparation (Thesis Defense), is organized in two national sessions, typically in October/November and March/April. The graduation exam committee consists of at least 7 and no more than 11 members, appointed by the School President on the proposal of the Study Program Council. Two members are appointed by the Professional College, if it exists, or by professional associations designated by a specific decree of the Minister of Health based on local representation, and their names are communicated by the Study Program Director to the Student Secretariat at least 30 days before the session start date. Considering the control role of these members, they must not be teachers of the same Course. Additionally, an expert from the Ministry of Health is usually appointed as an external member who does not form part of the committee but provides a procedural opinion on the exam's appropriateness, to be included in the minutes. In the case where the Ministry does not appoint experts, the Rector may exercise the substitute power.
To be admitted to the graduation exam, the student must:
a) complete all Integrated Courses and pass the related exams
b) earn a total of 180 CFU over the three years
c) pass the mandatory professional training internship, evaluated and certified at the end of each year
d) submit the application to the Rector, along with a copy of the thesis, to the Student Secretariat at least 30 days before the exam
e) pass the final practical exam
Specifically, to discuss the thesis, the student must pass the Technical-Practical Exam in the same session as the thesis defense. The final grade is expressed in hundredths with possible honors and is calculated as the sum of:
- the weighted average of exam grades, converted to 110, and the evaluation of the mandatory professional training internship
- the sum of the scores from the practical exam (0-4 points) and thesis defense (0-6 points).
The thesis evaluation is based on:
- scientific quality and originality
- accuracy of the methodology
- level of in-depth work
- critical contribution of the graduate.
The graduation committee may award additional points for:
- honors obtained in exams (0.2 points per honor, up to a maximum of 1 point)
- participation in Erasmus or international mobility programs (up to 1 additional point)
- graduation within the normal course duration (1 additional point).
Honors may be awarded with a unanimous committee decision to candidates scoring above 110.
The topics for thesis defense, whether compilative or experimental, are agreed upon by students with their thesis advisors. It is the student's responsibility to prepare the thesis with guidance, research sources, ensure data confidentiality, develop data collection tools, and process and write the collected data.
The Co-advisor may not be part of the teaching staff but must have in-depth knowledge of the thesis topic and collaborate with the student in completing tasks assigned by the Advisor.
The final exam may be taken in a foreign language, previously agreed with the Study Program Director. In this case, an extended summary in Italian must also be prepared.

Admission Procedures Admission to the Study Program is granted upon passing a specific examination based on ministerial decrees regarding the procedures and content of entrance examinations for university courses with national programmed access.
The procedures for conducting the examination are specified in the ministerial decree and in the Study Program.
Additional Educational Obligations (OFA) are required for candidates scoring below a specified threshold. For the purpose of verifying initial knowledge, only the answers to the entrance test questions related to the following subjects are considered:
- Biology
- Chemistry
- Physics and Mathematics Questions related to general culture and logical reasoning are not taken into account.
For the disciplinary areas listed above, where recovery activities are provided, students who score below 25% of the maximum score in individual subjects will be assigned OFA to be completed obligatorily within the first year through the methods established by the Course Director and the instructors of the relevant disciplines. Students will be duly informed via email and through direct meetings regarding the deficiencies in their preparation and the activities provided to facilitate their recovery. Completing the OFA within the first year is mandatory to be eligible for the official examinations specified in the Study Program. To this end, students may utilize dedicated tutorial hours for exercises in each disciplinary area where educational debts have been incurred. The educational debt will be considered fulfilled upon passing the examination specified in the Study Program, in agreement with the instructors of the disciplines listed above.
The Additional Educational Obligation does not affect the number of credits the student must earn in their study path or their average grade. Furthermore, pursuant to Article 49, paragraph 3, point b of the University Academic Regulations, students who do not fulfill the Additional Educational Obligations as stated in Article 28 of the Academic Regulations are not permitted to enroll in the second year. Therefore, while second-year enrollment is permitted, it will not be possible to take second-year examinations before completing the assigned OFA.

Program, Texts and Objectives Communication Skills
Graduates will be able to establish and maintain positive communication relationships for both general and technical communications, and will be able to analyze and present acquired data and disseminate scientific information on current topics. The ability to relate is fundamental in this type of work, therefore they will be able to:
1) Listen carefully to extract and synthesize relevant information on all issues, understanding their content.
2) Communicate effectively with colleagues, the community, other sectors, and the media.
3) Interact with other professional figures involved in prevention through efficient group work.
4) Demonstrate basic skills and correct attitudes in teaching others regarding on-the-job training.
5) Communicate effectively both orally and in writing.
Communication skills will be assessed through specific oral or written tests for each course and internship, as well as in the final examination.

SECTION: Judgment autonomy
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/610

Judgment autonomy (making judgements)
Graduates must have the ability to integrate knowledge and manage complexity, as well as to form judgments based on limited or incomplete information, including reflection on the social and ethical responsibilities related to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Therefore, they must be able to:
1) Demonstrate in professional activities a critical approach, constructive skepticism, and a creative, research-oriented attitude.
2) Consider the importance and limitations of scientific thinking based on information obtained from various sources, to manage prevention.
3) Form personal judgments to solve analytical and complex problems ("problem solving") and independently seek scientific information, without waiting for it to be provided.
4) Identify the essential elements of the prevention technician profession, including moral and ethical principles and legal responsibilities underlying the profession.
5) Respect professional values including excellence, responsibility, reliability, honesty, integrity, and commitment to following scientific methods and current regulations.
6) Respond personally to the need for continuous professional improvement, aware of their own limitations, including those of their technical, scientific, and legal knowledge.
7) Respect colleagues and other prevention professionals, demonstrating the ability to establish collaborative relationships with them.
They will also be able to independently judge the impact of environmental and working conditions not only on health, but also in terms of psychological and socioeconomic well-being, be aware of risks present in living and working environments, as well as of behavioral norms and aspects related to safety and environmental issues.
Judgment autonomy is achieved through classroom lectures and training internships and is verified in examination tests for each course, internships, and the final exam.

Entry Orientation Every year the University offers students from secondary schools numerous initiatives aimed at guiding them toward a conscious choice of study program and providing detailed information about the educational offerings, facilities, and services of the University.
Entry Orientation is coordinated by the University's Orientation Coordinator, the Coordinator for Orientation of the School of Medicine and Health Sciences, supported by the Orientation, Tutoring, Placement, Student Rights, and Disability Office. The Program's Orientation Representatives (Prof.ssa Rosa Mancinelli and Prof. Franco Mezzanotte) collaborate with the Department and School Orientation Representatives to participate in the main University-organized Orientation activities:
1. "A Day as a Matriculant" during which the outgoing Orientation activities take place at secondary schools;
2. "A Day with D'Annunzio" within the framework of the "University Unveiled" initiative;
3. the Open Day on campus. During the day, the Program's Orientation Representatives, the Program Director, the Professional Training Directors, and students representing each academic year are in the classroom to illustrate the Program's characteristics, educational objectives, organization of teaching activities (number of exams, CFU, academic calendars, etc.), and professional opportunities. Additionally, students can visit teaching facilities, the campus, and receive information about accommodation, services, and dining.
4. Night of Research, where the Program participates with its booth and demonstration activities and in-depth seminars.
The Program organizes specific Orientation meetings to present the Program's characteristics, upon request from school principals. For the current academic year, meetings are being organized at several Institutes to illustrate access modalities to the Program, the duration of the study program, the theoretical training path, and the modalities of professional training internships in healthcare companies, public institutions, and private companies, as well as professional opportunities and the possibility to continue education by enrolling in the Master's Degree Program in Preventive Health Professions or Master's programs.
At the beginning of the academic year, after all enrollments are completed, first-year students are summoned by the Program Director to a dedicated meeting where the Program's purposes and structure are explained in detail. Information is provided on the location of classrooms and laboratories where lectures and professional training internships will take place. A customized Program presentation brochure is distributed to attending students.

International Mobility Office Although students at the Chieti-Pescara University have multiple opportunities for international mobility for study and internships, both in Europe and outside Europe, for students in Techniques of Prevention in the Environment and Workplaces, some difficulties are encountered, especially regarding the absence at the international level of a specific equivalent study program to ours in terms of educational offerings, with which to carry out fruitful exchanges within a specific professional framework. Indeed, currently, no student of the CdS has taken advantage of the opportunity for study abroad.
The Chieti-Pescara University adheres to international networks and signs cooperation agreements with universities in countries all over the world; in particular, within the Erasmus+ Programme and framework agreements with universities in countries outside the European Union.
The CdS in TPALL is included in the LLP Erasmus mobility program.
The CdS informs students of the possibility to carry out recognized internships, organized by the University, at companies, firms, professional offices, and training and research centers in EU and non-EU countries, through the Erasmus+ programme which provides funding from community funds.
At the beginning of each academic year, it is reminded that the University Language Centre organizes language courses for University students, issuing a final certificate after passing the assessment.
Currently, the CdS has received an expression of interest for incoming mobility from IES San Severiano, Cadiz, Spain. Thanks to the support of the Internationalization and Erasmus Department, the Erasmus coordinator of the CdS, Professor Rosa Mancinelli, is activating an Erasmus agreement.
With the recent decree regarding mobility programs on national territory, which allows students to enrich themselves culturally by participating in study courses and internships at national academic institutions, we hope to successfully raise student awareness.
The president and Erasmus coordinator of the CdS also pursue an awareness-raising action among teachers for Erasmus mobility dedicated to teachers. For more details on international mobility programs - requirements, deadlines and participation procedures - the International Relations Office, Erasmus, agreements, Incoming Students is active.

Opinions of Graduates From the analysis of ALMALAUREA data, derived from questionnaires completed by graduates in 2022/23, the following emerges:
approximately 67% consider themselves satisfied with the organization of the Course of Study and approximately 75% regarding relations with professors. 50% of respondents rate the academic load as adequate, a figure in line with the previous year (57%). Most graduates appreciate the organization of exams, a fact that supports the President's ongoing efforts to reorganize integrated courses, aiming to improve relations between professors and students. 58% of respondents would enroll again in the same Course of Study, but only 25% in the same University, a slight decrease compared to last year.
Learning Skills
The Course of Study, through frontal lectures, specific internships, and the professional laboratory, aims to develop the ability to learn, enabling graduates to continue their studies independently in the field and update themselves. In particular, they will be able to:
1) Collect, organize, and correctly interpret health, legislative, and technical information from various resources and databases.
2) Gather information on specific cases during investigations into accidents, food poisoning, animal-origin foods, and environmental hygiene.
3) Use technology associated with information and communication as a valid support for good prevention practices.
4) Understand the application and also the limitations of information technology.
5) Manage a good archive of their technical-health practice for subsequent analysis and improvement.
The learning ability will be assessed through specific written and/or oral tests, during internships, in the laboratory, and in the final exam.

Brief Course Description The Course of Study (CdS) in Techniques of Prevention in the Environment and in the Workplace (enabling the health profession of Techniques of Prevention in the Environment and in the Workplace) belongs to Class 4 of Health Prevention Professions Degrees (L/SNT4) and aims to train health professionals who, in accordance with Article 4 of Law 10 August 2000, No. 251, independently carry out prevention, verification, and control activities in environmental and workplace hygiene, food and beverage hygiene, public and veterinary health. Such activities must be conducted within the scope of professional responsibility.
The Course is structured over three years and requires the acquisition of 180 CFU in total for the degree. The number of exams is 25 (including Seminars, Professional Internships, Optional Teaching Activities, and Laboratories). Topics range from basic knowledge of medical-biological, legal, and technical disciplines to more professional topics.
The final exam has the value of a State Exam enabling professional practice.
The degree title allows access to Master's Degree Programs in Class 4 of Health Technical Professions LM/SNT4, without academic debts (Article 4, Paragraph 3, D.I. 19 February 2009), to Level 1 Master's Programs, and to Specialization Courses.
The first year of the Course was activated at our University in the academic year 2002/2003.
External Effectiveness The Interuniversity Consortium ALMALAUREA conducted a survey on the employment status of graduates in Techniques of Prevention in the Environment and in the Workplace for the academic year 2022/23. Only 20% are enrolled in a two-year Master's program. This figure might be explained by the demand for this profession in the labor market.
One year after graduation, 40% are employed. The work activity is predominantly in the private sector (in line with previous analysis), with high use of skills acquired during the study path and an average monthly salary of 1,500 euros, with 50% of respondents having an indefinite-term contract.
Specific Educational Objectives and Training Path Description Graduates must achieve the following specific cultural and professional competencies:
- Knowledge of the principles of chemistry and physics necessary for interpreting environmental monitoring data in living and working environments;
- Knowledge of the principles of anatomy, physiology, histology, and general pathology necessary for understanding common pathologies, particularly occupational ones;
- Ability to correctly apply environmental sampling methodologies for chemical pollutants;
- Ability to correctly measure physical agents as required by current regulations;
- Ability to control the quality of foods and beverages intended for consumption;
- Adequate knowledge of occupational and environmental toxicology;
- Knowledge of medical-surgical sciences enabling understanding of the etiopathogenesis of diseases, particularly occupational ones;
- Knowledge of microbiological techniques;
- Knowledge of the principles underlying labor law;
- Knowledge of the principles underlying criminal law concerning environmental property crimes and violations of hygiene and safety regulations in living and working environments and food;
- Ability to assess the need for investigations and inquiries for occupational accidents and diseases;
- Ability and sensitivity to evaluate psychological issues within communities and work organizations;
- Knowledge of the fundamental concepts of health organization;
- Knowledge, from a preventive perspective, of common disease patterns, particularly occupational ones;
- Knowledge, from a preventive perspective, of accident phenomena;
- Knowledge, from a preventive perspective, of infectious diseases;
- Knowledge of the fundamental methodological elements of epidemiology;
- Knowledge of ergonomic issues, particularly regarding the relationship between work and vision;
- Knowledge of common industrial technologies;
- Ability to use statistics to evaluate biological and environmental monitoring data;
- Ability to propose sufficiently validated and recognized methods in ergonomics, hygiene, and toxicology;
- Learning of the basics of research methodology and the ability to apply results in public health prevention;
- Ability to identify, prevent, and address occupational risks in various work situations and assess their health effects;
- Knowledge of the essential elements of business organization, particularly health services;
- Ability to act consistently with the legal, ethical, and deontological principles of the profession during supervision and control activities as part of the training program;
- Knowledge of fundamental regulations regarding hygiene and safety in living and working environments;
- Computer skills useful for managing information systems of services and for self-education.
The bachelor's degree in techniques of prevention in the environment and in the workplace requires 180 credit units spread over three years of study, with at least 60 CFU to be acquired in training activities aimed at developing specific professional skills (internship).
Internship:
For internships focused on Hygiene and Safety in the Workplace (both public and private sectors), specific technical skills will be emphasized to organize and evaluate analytical risk paths related to work activities, implementing appropriate preventive and protective measures to safeguard safety. This requires, in addition to knowledge of current safety regulations, specific training in business organization, management, and quality assurance. Practical experiences will be specifically designed to achieve the following objectives:
- Application of current regulations on Hygiene and Safety in the Workplace, aimed at carrying out supervision and control activities and collaborating on occupational accidents and diseases.
- Ability to prepare a plan to assess risks within a work environment.
- Evaluation of the significance of environmental and biological monitoring investigations in the workplace.
- Ability to identify preventive and protective measures to contain risks.
- Use of tools to evaluate the effectiveness of adopted measures.
- Knowledge of quality and safety management systems at the business level (ISO series) and the environmental impact of activities, products, and services (ISO series).
For internships focused on Environmental Hygiene, Food and Beverage Hygiene, Public Health, and Veterinary Hygiene:
- Application of current regulations on environmental protection, aimed at carrying out supervision and control activities, also using monitoring tools for air, water, and soil quality.
- Ability to identify, based on results, appropriate preventive measures to protect the environment and verify their effectiveness.
- Application of current regulations on food and beverage quality intended for consumption and cosmetic products.
- Ability to analyze food production cycles, identify critical control points, and prepare measures to safeguard hygiene and quality of beverages and foods, including those of animal origin.
- Knowledge of quality and safety management systems at the business level (ISO series) and the environmental impact of activities, products, and services (ISO series).
- Acquire the ability to analyze and solve problems related to issuing opinions for authorization in environmental hygiene, food hygiene, and public and veterinary health;
- Acquire the ability to assess the need for investigations and detect irregularities during supervision activities in living and working environments; possession of teaching skills oriented toward informing and training staff.
- Acquire the ability to conduct site visits, inspections, and sampling at various production units.
- Ability to draft main Administrative and Judicial Police Acts.
The training path, based on the specific objectives described above, is implemented through the learning of basic disciplines, such as physics (FIS/07), chemistry (CHIM/03 and CHIM/06), mathematics, statistics, and informatics (MAT/04, MED/01, INF/01), biology (BIO/13), biochemistry (BIO/10), anatomy (BIO/16), histology (BIO/17), physiology (BIO/09), general pathology (MED/04), microbiology (MED/07), and subsequently through the learning of more specific disciplines, such as food chemistry (CHIM/10), environmental technical physics (ING-IND/11), ecology (BIO/07), General and Applied Hygiene (MED/42), and Sociology of Environment and Territory (SPS/10).
Particular attention is given, within the core courses and internships, to evidence-based prevention, providing theoretical-practical tools that enable professional autonomy and the capacity for continuous scientific self-updating.
Cultural training is enriched by courses in humanities and psychopedagogy (General Sociology SPS/07, General Psychology M-PSI/01) to ensure the acquisition of behavioral, relational, and communication skills necessary for navigating a complex work environment.
Special attention is given to prevention sciences in health services (General and Applied Hygiene MED/42, Legal Medicine MED/43, Occupational Medicine MED/44, Radioprotection) and first aid (Internal Medicine MED/09, Anesthesiology MED/41). Health management sciences are developed particularly regarding public law (IUS/09) and labor law (IUS/07). Students are provided with an English language course also aimed at understanding scientific literature. Courses are structured into modules and are delivered through frontal lectures, classroom exercises, or laboratory sessions. Learning outcomes are assessed through in-course tests (also serving as self-assessment for students) and a final oral or written exam, which verifies the achievement of the set objectives, unique and simultaneous for each course, necessary for acquiring credit units. Learning outcomes of laboratory, English, and some internship courses result in a pass. Students have access to 6 credits for preparing the final exam at facilities dedicated to training; this activity can also be carried out at non-university facilities, such as hospitals, health services, or private entities.
The bachelor's degree in Techniques of Prevention in the Environment and in the Workplace requires 180 total credit units, spread over three years of study, with at least 60 to be acquired in training activities aimed at developing specific professional skills (internship).
Opinions of Entities and Companies with Internship/Training Agreements The students enrolled in the Course of Study carried out internships in the academic year 2022/23 at:
ASL of Lanciano Vasto Chieti ASL of Pescara Private Companies in the Territory:
CEIT Fater Project Safety CSL Center for Worker Safety Inca Consult Marfisi ASSO API FED API Studio 81
All tutors from the above-mentioned structures were invited to complete an evaluation questionnaire on the student's performance during the 2022/23 academic year to verify the effectiveness of the Course of Study in imparting work-ready skills. At the end of the questionnaire, each tutor was asked to list any suggestions aimed at improving the Course of Study's curriculum to make it more professional.
No suggestions were provided by ASL tutors, who considered students capable of handling the proposed work. Some private company tutors propose including technical case studies in teaching modules to allow students to arrive at internship sites having already developed basic problem-solving skills.
Public and private sector tutors believe students are able to ask questions, have a critical spirit, and adopt a proactive attitude.
Students were administered a questionnaire asking them to rate, on a scale of 5 levels (nothing-much), their acquired competencies and awareness of their role, their relationship with the tutor and colleagues, and their autonomy during the internship. Most students rated their internship satisfaction as 'much' and 'very much'. In particular, students who completed internships in private companies appreciated the opportunity to draft risk assessment documents. Students who completed internships at the ASL Prevention Departments highlighted the importance of a welcoming work environment for productive work.
Finally, the Course of Study President commits to organizing, with the help of tutors and other local experts, seminars, workshops, and ADOs to address gaps identified by tutors during internship activities regarding topics covered in the curriculum.
Consultation with Representative Organizations - at National and International Levels - of Goods and Service Production, Professions (Course Establishment)
The course should provide students with competencies in:
- Conducting investigative activities for issuing authorizations or technical-sanitary no-objection for activities subject to control;
- Verifying and reporting irregularities and issuing opinions within their competence;
- Supervision and control of living and working environments and assessing the need for investigations and inquiries for occupational accidents and diseases;
- Supervision and control of the compliance of facilities and environments with connected activities and the safety conditions of equipment;
- Supervision and control of food and beverage quality intended for consumption and assessing the need for subsequent specialized investigations;
- Supervision and control of veterinary hygiene within their competence and assessing the need for subsequent investigations;
- Supervision and control of cosmetic products;
- Collaboration with judicial administration for investigations into environmental property crimes, hygiene and safety conditions in workplaces, and food;
- Supervision and control of all else provided by laws and regulations in the field of health and environmental prevention, within their competence;
The training path must also consider that prevention technicians are responsible for organizing and planning, executing, and ensuring the quality of acts carried out in the exercise of their professional activity; they participate in study, teaching, and professional consulting activities in health services and places requiring their professional competence.
Consultation with Representative Organizations - at National and International Levels - of Goods and Service Production, Professions (Subsequent Consultations)
The Course of Study organizes an annual consultation meeting with social partners, inviting sector representatives or Public Bodies (Prevention Department/ARTA). At the time of completing this form, the most recent consultation took place on 07/03/2024, attended by the Course of Study President, one of the Course of Study's reference professors, representatives of the ASL Pescara and Chieti Prevention Departments, and the President of the Regional Board of Prevention Technicians. The Acting Head of the ASL Pescara Prevention Department delegated the ASL Pescara representative (the meeting minutes are attached).
The Degree Course aims to maintain and enhance contacts with business associations and productive sectors in the region that can benefit from the graduate's professional profile, by organizing periodic meetings attended by the Degree Course President, GdAQ members, Prevention Department heads of ASL Chieti and ASL Pescara (training sites of the CL), and representatives of private professional structures, to discuss updating the training offer, adequacy of professional internships, correspondence of the Course of Study with workplace expectations, and verify employment opportunities for graduates.
Previous years' consultation outcomes have proven important in revising the Course of Study's educational profiles in response to local companies' demands and in training qualified young people who can improve prevention culture in the environment and workplaces.
Some stakeholders, despite not attending the meeting due to commitments, reiterated the need for qualified young people in our territory and offered to propose internships to expand competencies.
To facilitate the collection of suggestions and opinions from companies and host entities for students in Techniques of Prevention in the Environment and in the Workplace, the Course of Study proposes exchanging questionnaires via email to overcome logistical-organizational difficulties that make it hard to attend social partner consultation meetings.
Entry, Path, and Exit Data Entry data show a consistent trend in student origins, predominantly from Abruzzo provinces. Only a minority (2) come from other regions.
57% of new students come from technical or professional institutes.
29 new students enrolled in 2022, of which 23 are pure.
64% of students progressed to the second year in the same Course of Study; 39% enrolled in the second year having earned more than 40 CFU.
In 2022, the average exams taken by the 2020 cohort was 1.07, and the average CFU earned was 22%. These data are partial, as the autumn exam session is missing.
Currently, there are 75 enrolled students across three years, with 60 in progress.
Exit data show that out of 17 graduates, only 2 obtained the degree beyond the course duration. Most (10) obtained the degree on time. 4 graduates received the degree with honors.
Characteristics of the Final Exam The final exam, worth 6 CFU, consists of a practical test (failure to pass prevents completion of the final exam) where the student must demonstrate acquisition of theoretical-practical and technical-operative knowledge and skills specific to the professional profile, and the preparation and discussion of a thesis (see D.I. 19 February 2009, Article 7).
The final grade, expressed in hundredths, is determined by the following parameters:
a) The weighted average of grades obtained in curricular exams, elective teaching activities, and internship, expressed in hundredths;
b) Points awarded by the Graduation Committee during the thesis discussion, obtained by summing individual scores from committee members;
c) The score achieved in the practical test.
The honors proposed by the Graduation Committee President can be awarded with unanimous committee agreement to candidates scoring above 110.
Final Exam Execution Method The final exam is conducted, in accordance with Article 7 of the D.I. of 19 February 2009, in two sessions: the first, typically in October/November, called Regular; the second in March/April, called Extraordinary. The final exam covers:
a. A practical test where the student must demonstrate acquisition of theoretical-practical and technical-operative knowledge and skills specific to the professional profile;
The practical test involves preparing two technical-practical documents: a workplace safety test requiring the candidate to assess occupational risks for a homogeneous group of workers with specific characteristics; a public health veterinary hygiene or food hygiene test requiring the candidate to illustrate correct sampling methods in the food sector or investigation procedures in the livestock sector.
b. Preparation and discussion of a thesis, with supervision from a Degree Course professor designated as Supervisor, and possibly external co-supervisors.
The thesis aims to engage the student in formalization, design, and research work that substantially contributes to completing their professional and scientific training. The thesis content must relate to themes or disciplines closely related to the professional profile of the Prevention Technician in the Environment and in the Workplace.
Thesis topics generally focus on:
- Inspection of animal-origin foods
- Handling, storage, and management of foods
- Health and safety in workplaces
- Public health hygiene
- Environmental protection through monitoring of matrices.
Thesis evaluation is based on the following criteria: level of depth and scientific relevance of the work, critical contribution of the graduate, accuracy of the methodology used, and presentation/discussion of the document.
The final degree score, expressed in hundredths with possible honors, is composed of:
a. The weighted average of grades obtained in profit exams;
b. The sum of evaluations obtained in the practical test (from 18/30 to 22/30 = 1 point; 23/30 to 25/30 = 2 points; 26/30 to 28/30 = 3 points; 29/30 to 30/30 = 4 points; honors = 5 points);
c. The grade awarded for the thesis discussion (0 to 5 points for a compilation thesis and 0 to 7 points for an experimental thesis).
Students may prepare the thesis in English. The deadline for submitting the graduation application and related documentation will be indicated on the Degree Course website.
The Final Exam Committee consists of at least 7 and no more than 11 members, appointed by the Rector on the proposal of the Course Council, two of whom are designated by the professional college or sector associations, chosen from their members.
The dates of sessions are communicated in advance to the Ministries of University, Scientific Research, and Health, which may send experts as representatives to individual sessions. In case of failure to designate the aforementioned members, the Rector exercises the substitute power. The President of the Committee is held by the Course of Study President, who may appoint a substitute from among the permanent professors of the Course of Study in case of absence. The Committee composition cannot change during the two evaluation phases of the same session. In case of serious impediment, a member may be replaced by a previously appointed substitute.

Admission procedures Students who have obtained a high school diploma from Italian or foreign secondary schools (subject to verification of the equivalence of the qualification and Italian language proficiency) may enroll in the Bachelor's degree program. The adequacy of the applicants' background will be verified through written tests.
Students who have achieved a high school diploma grade of 70/100 or higher, or 38/60 or higher according to the old grading systems, are admitted to the Bachelor's degree program without the need for verification tests. Students who have obtained a grade between 60/100 and 69/100, or between 36/60 and 37/60, will be called for an initial preparation adequacy verification test (CRA). If educational gaps are identified, these must be addressed by students within the first year through regular and/or supplementary curricular activities (O.F.A.). Students required to complete O.F.A. may attend lectures and take profit exams only in the first year.
The O.F.A. recovery will consist of multiple-choice questions on topics belonging to the following disciplinary areas:
sps/07 - sps/08 - sps/09 - sps/12: sociological disciplines; m-sto/04: historical, geographical, and psycho-pedagogical disciplines.
The O.F.A. recovery will be distributed throughout the academic year.
Students who:
1. fail to complete the O.F.A. within the first year of the program
2. do not earn 18 CFU from the basic and characterizing courses of the first year
will not be allowed to take exams in the second year.
The program duration is three years for a total of 180 CFU.

Syllabus, texts and objectives Note regarding credits for other activities NOTE on the observations made regarding the designation of the Study Program:
a) the new proposed designation 'Sociology and Criminology' is merely a simplification and rationalization of the existing designation 'Sociology, Social Research and Criminology';
b) the proposed designation is not misleading because 1) it does not refer to different classes of Degree since there is no specific class of Degree in Criminology; 2) it denotes, in line with the educational objectives of the Study Program, a strictly sociological approach to criminological issues in accordance with the epistemological status of Sociology itself;
c) it is also noted that other L-40 Degree Programs have designations explicitly referencing Sociology and Criminology;
d) the suggestion to change the name to 'Sociology of Deviance' does not seem appropriate because it simply corresponds to a scientific-disciplinary sector within the Study Program.

SECTION: Communication Skills
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/661

Communication Skills (communication skills)
All teachings will guide students toward acquiring awareness of the social importance of communication and toward enhancing individual communication and interpretative skills. In particular, students, reflecting on the quality and effectiveness of different presentation choices, will learn to identify the various communication techniques used in the multimedia society (through the use of computer and telecommunication tools), but will also learn to identify the means and skills available to subjects operating within limited social groups. Through specific teachings, students will become aware of the importance of interpreting data, facts, and texts in the information society and the importance of linguistic and extralinguistic preconceptions in the production of texts, speeches, and multimedia objects intended to fulfill communication tasks. Students will also be directed toward the concrete utilization of the various communication tools currently available, also in order to develop their ability to choose, on each occasion, the most suitable communication strategies and channels in relation to the concrete content to be transmitted. The course will achieve these objectives also through the extensive disciplinary space reserved for the specific study of themes related to the sociology of cultural and communication processes. The acquired competencies will be used both at a theoretical and practical level for drafting projects and operational plans, as well as for preparing communications and service documents aimed at risk management and safety practices.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITÀ DEGLI STUDI GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO – CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [695N] SOCIOLOGY AND CRIMINOLOGY
SECTION: Judgment autonomy (making judgements)
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/661

Judgment autonomy (making judgements)
The entire course structure aims at developing critical abilities and judgment autonomy of graduates capable of acting independently within operational and/or research groups interested in improving social contexts. In particular, judgment autonomy will be achieved mainly through courses concerning the critical historical study of the theoretical and philosophical foundations of social sciences and research methodology, as well as through students' design of operational and/or research projects during which teachers will foster the autonomous ability to collect, interpret and manage data and mature reflection on social issues, particularly related to communication problems and security policies. Regarding skills aimed at collecting, analyzing and reprocessing information to manage risk situations, judgment autonomy will be pursued through laboratory initiatives involving teachers and experts.

Career Guidance Regarding post-graduation career orientation activities, the Study Course structures coordinate with the University Career Service, which most graduates access.
The Study Course has activated an Outgoing Career Guidance service that periodically organizes workshops on the behavioral skills necessary for entering the job market and meetings with professions aimed at introducing graduates to the various professional profiles they can aspire to with their acquired skills.
During the 2021-2022 academic year, the customary 'Meetings with Professions' with local and national representatives of the business world resumed. In this context, a career day was held in July 2022, featuring participation from institutions and companies that described to students the main job opportunities. After simulating interviews, they collected student applications. The same initiative is scheduled for May 21, 2024. Furthermore, to enhance the employment and employability of its students, the 'd'Annunzio' University has established a full-fledged placement service. As known, under Law 30/03 (commonly referred to as the Biagi Law), Italian universities can now carry out job intermediary activities, complementing public employment centers and private operators in providing new employment services (Start Program). Among the services available to recent graduates are:
• BASIC AND SPECIALIZED CONSULTING FOR STUDENTS, BUSINESSES, AND GRADUATES: The front-office activities managed by the Placement include providing information on various services dedicated to graduates and businesses, as well as on key topics relevant to different target groups (contract types, labor market regulations, production and business systems, CV preparation, employment prospects). Individual meetings with graduates are held to identify and analyze their skills, initiating the drafting of a professional project. Meetings with business representatives are organized to analyze professional needs. The University Placement promotes seminars, calls, career days, internships, and job offers through SMS and/or dedicated mailing lists for businesses and students/graduates of the Departments, as well as via popular social networks.
• SERVICES FOR BUSINESSES AND GRADUATES - JOB INTERMEDIATION: To enhance the employment and employability of its students, based on guidelines in Law 30/03, the 'd'Annunzio' University has established a full-fledged placement structure. The University can therefore offer, to those seeking young talent for their organization—whether through employment contracts or training and orientation internships—not only a direct connection to the sought professional profile, but also support services to facilitate the identification of professionals matching specific needs. The service is managed using the online platform JOB (http://job.unich.it), designed to meet the specific intermediary needs of d'Annunzio. In compliance with recent regulations (Law No. 183/2010 - 'Work Package' and Law No. 111/2011), the University has further enhanced its technical tools for job intermediary services with the CURRICULA application. Available on the University website, CURRICULA provides free access to CVs of approximately 80,000 students and graduates from the last six years who have authorized the publication of their data. Simultaneously, businesses, institutions, organizations, and private employers can consult the database and, through the interconnection between CURRICULA and JOB (currently being integrated with the national Clic Lavoro system), request Placement Operators' support for detailed searches to identify specific professional profiles and/or post free job/internship offers, also dedicated to students seeking financial support during their studies.
• CAREER GUIDANCE FOR BUSINESS START-UP AND MICRO-CREDIT: Within the Standard Setting procedure, the University has made available, for the benefit of Students, Graduates, and PhD Candidates, the Career Guidance for Business Start-up service. To this end, a dialogue process with local and national stakeholders has been initiated to identify collaboration dynamics. The Placement, with this new service, aims to provide initial guidance to those interested in an entrepreneurial career and, based on the outcomes of the initial guidance meetings, refer them to other services available in the territory that may be useful to the student/graduate. More details
• Micro-Credit Office. To facilitate young entrepreneurs in identifying initial financial resources, the University Placement Service offers Micro-Credit guidance. The 'd'Annunzio' University has joined the 'Micro-Work' project, which aims to build a permanent micro-credit network based on public-private collaboration, with the goal of strengthening micro-credit as an active labor policy tool.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITY OF CHIETI/PESCARA GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO STUDIES
COURSE: [695N] SOCIOLOGY AND CRIMINOLOGY
SECTION: Student Opinions
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/661

Student Opinions From the data collected from the 2022-2023 student opinion survey, it is possible to observe a decidedly appreciable rating in all items. Indeed, on a scale from 1 to 4, 14 courses (45.1%) fall into level A (from 3.5 to 4), while the remaining 17 are included in level B (from 3 to 3.5). Regarding the various aspects of teaching, the items that most satisfied students refer to teachers' availability to provide clarifications during lectures and office hours (3.58), respect for lecture schedule times (3.51), and interest in the topics covered in the courses (3.40). Other positive evaluations concern the consistency between what is stated on the website and the actual course delivery (3.50) and the teacher's ability to stimulate/motivate interest in the subject (3.39). These results, although positive, are slightly below the university and general social area averages. The most important data to consider is the preliminary knowledge (D3), which has an average score of 3.25 out of 4, compared to 3.31 for the university and 3.32 for the area. In this regard, the CDS has decided to use the TECO-T tool as a barometer of students' acquired transversal competencies.

Additionally, to manage student complaints and observations, the CDS has publicized on the degree course website the link to the university's complaint management system and has appointed a Student Ombudsman, a teacher from the same course.

Regarding the findings from the February 2022 CPDS, the usual issues persist: regarding available spaces, a well-known issue is the inadequacy of classrooms given the reduced restrictions on in-person teaching. The evaluation of the adequacy of computer workstations is also considered negatively inadequate. In this regard, the CDS intends to continue dialogue with the university to obtain more suitable spaces for a course among the largest at the Chieti-Pescara university.

N.B.
The student opinion results will be discussed at the first useful degree course council, presumably by the first half of September 2023. Subsequently, the minutes attachment can be added.

UNIVERSITÀ: UNIVERSITÀ DEGLI STUDI GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO – CHIETI/PESCARA
CORSO: [695N] SOCIOLOGIA E CRIMINOLOGIA
SEZIONE: Opinioni dei laureati
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/661

Opinioni dei laureati La gran parte dei laureati è costituita da donne (80,5%), anche se il loro numero è lievemente diminuito di circa 4 punti percentuali rispetto al precedente anno. L'età media dei laureati è di 24,4 anni, anche se il 47,6% dei laureati presenta un'età inferiore ai 23 anni. Il 73,6% (dato in decremento, relativamente a quello dell'anno scorso 82,4%) dei rispondenti proviene da un liceo (in prevalenza dal liceo delle scienze umane e dal liceo scientifico) e per l'82,6% si è trattata della prima esperienza universitaria. La media degli esami sostenuti è di 24,9/30 ed il voto medio di laurea di 98,5/110 (dati, questi ultimi, in leggero aumento rispetto alla precedente rilevazione).
Dall'analisi dei dati sui laureati intervistati (224 su 231), si rileva una generale soddisfazione per il corso di laurea scelto: infatti, sommando i 'Decisamente si' e i 'Più si che no', ben l'84,8% dei laureati si ritiene complessivamente soddisfatto. Di questi il 38,4% (dato in leggera crescita) si definisce decisamente soddisfatto. Per quanto concerne il rapporto con i docenti il livello di soddisfazione degli ex studenti si attesta sull'85,7% (dato in leggero aumento). Anche il carico di studio è giudicato equilibrato (87,5% sommando i 'Decisamente si' e i 'Più si che no'), anche se lievemente inferiore al precedente dato (91,2%). Più della metà (il 64,3 56,8%), si iscriverebbe di nuovo allo stesso corso, presso l'Ateneo di Chieti-Pescara (dato migliorato di circa 7 punti percentuali rispetto al precedente anno).
Per quanto concerne il giudizio espresso sull'adeguatezza delle aule, solo il 30% dei laureati si afferma come esse siano sempre o quasi sempre adeguate. Difatti, quello degli spazi per la didattica rappresenta un problema annoso e strutturale, messo in evidenza – in molte occasioni - dal Consiglio di corso di laurea. La valutazione dell'adeguatezza delle postazioni informatiche è giudicata negativamente ('in numero inadeguato') dal 49,5% dei laureati, confermando la criticità emersa negli anni precedenti. Poco più della metà (55,8%) ha utilizzato attrezzature per le altre attività didattiche. Per quanto concerne i servizi di orientamento in uscita, sommando i 'Decisamente si' e i 'Più si che no', ben il 67,7% dei laureati si ritiene complessivamente soddisfatto. Il 67,9% intende proseguire gli studi iscrivendosi ad una laurea magistrale e, di questi, il 46,1% intende farlo rimanendo nel medesimo Ateneo.
N.B.
I risultati delle opinioni dei laureati verranno discussi nel primo Consiglio di corso di laurea utile, presumibilmente entro la prima metà di settembre 2023. In seguito, si potrà procedere con l'inserimento dell'allegato del verbale.
Capacità di apprendimento (learning skills)
Il corso si propone di lasciar sviluppare l'autonoma capacità di apprendimento soprattutto attraverso strategie educative basate sull'uso cosciente della relazione dialogica, sul metodo dei progetti e, dunque, su pratiche, anche seminariali, di mutuo insegnamento all'interno di gruppi di studio che potranno valutare i risultati ottenuti mediante strumenti di autoverifica basati sulla rilevazione dell'impatto dei progetti sull'ambiente sociale che essi intendono studiare e/o modificare.
I risultati attesi in relazione alle conoscenze, alle capacità di comprensione e di applicazione dei saperi, all'autonomia di giudizio, alle abilità comunicative e alle capacità di apprendimento verranno periodicamente verificati attraverso modalità tradizionali di valutazione all'interno dei singoli insegnamenti ed anche attraverso confronti formativi (stimolati dalle attività di tirocinio) fra docenti, studenti e rappresentanti di associazioni, enti e istituzioni impegnate, a vario titolo, per il miglioramento di gruppi e contesti sociali Organizzazione e responsabilità della AQ a livello del Corso di Studio Presidente del Cds, Prof. Claudio Tuozzolo, ai sensi dell'art. 56 dello Statuto di Ateneo, viene eletto dal Consiglio di SC fra i professori di ruolo che ne fanno parte e dura in carica per tre anni. Ha la responsabilità del funzionamento del Corso di SC e ne convoca e presiede le riunioni ordinarie e straordinarie del Consiglio del CdS.
Il Gruppo di Riesame è composto dal Prof. Andrea Antonilli; Prof.ssa Marta Ferrara; ; Prof. Piergiorgio Della Pelle; Prof.ssa Thea Rossi; Prof.ssa Vanessa Russo; Dott.ssa Raffaella De Girolamo; Marco Massaro (rappresentante studenti).
l Gruppo di Riesame (GdR) è una commissione del CdS la cui attività principale consiste nell'analisi dei risultati dei processi formativi del corso, con la finalità di individuare i punti critici e le possibili azioni di miglioramento. Il GdR è responsabile della Scheda di Monitoraggio Annuale (SMA) basata su una analisi degli Indicatori forniti da Anvur, e della redazione periodica del Rapporto di Riesame Ciclico. Il GdR opera come commissione istruttoria del Consiglio di CdS cui è sottoposta l'approvazione dei suoi principali atti.
In particolare, il GdR è responsabile di monitorare e valutare: l'attrattività e gli abbandoni del CdS; la regolarità delle carriere e di tempi necessari alla laurea; l'efficacia esterna del CdS in termini di occupabilità dei laureati e/o loro proseguimento nella formazione universitaria; il livello di internazionalizzazione del CdS.
Commissione Paritetica opera presso la Scuola ed è costituita da una rappresentanza di docenti e studenti iscritti ai Corsi della Scuola. (La Prof. Oliverio è il membro della Commissione Paritetica indicato dal CdS). La Commissione svolge attività di monitoraggio continuo dell'offerta formativa e della qualità della didattica, nonché dell'attività di servizio agli studenti da parte dei docenti e individua indicatori per la valutazione dei risultati delle suddette attività.
Essa, a seguito dell'attività di monitoraggio svolta, provvede a redigere una relazione annuale contenente valutazioni e proposte al Nucleo di Valutazione sul miglioramento della qualità e dell'efficacia delle Strutture didattiche, anche in riferimento ai risultati ottenuti nell'apprendimento, in rapporto alle prospettive occupazionali e di sviluppo personale e professionale, nonché alle esigenze del sistema economico e produttivo. La Commissione Paritetica redige annualmente la Relazione Annuale.
La Relazione Annuale valuta se:
1. il progetto del CdS mantenga la dovuta attenzione alle funzioni e competenze richieste dalle prospettive occupazionali e di sviluppo personale e professionale, individuate tenuto conto delle esigenze del sistema economico e produttivo;
2. i risultati di apprendimento attesi siano efficaci in relazione alle funzioni e competenze di riferimento (coerenza tra le attività formative programmate e gli specifici obiettivi formativi programmati);
3. l'attività didattica dei docenti, i metodi di trasmissione delle conoscenze e delle abilità, i materiali e gli ausili didattici, i laboratori, le aule, le attrezzature e i servizi agli studenti svolti da docenti e ricercatori siano efficaci per raggiungere gli obiettivi di apprendimento al livello desiderato;
4. i metodi di esame consentano di accertare correttamente i risultati ottenuti in relazione ai risultati di apprendimento attesi;
5. al Riesame Annuale conseguano efficaci interventi di correzione e miglioramento da parte dei CdS negli anni successivi;
6. i questionari relativi alla soddisfazione degli studenti siano efficacemente gestiti, analizzati e utilizzati per il miglioramento della didattica;
7. siano rese effettivamente disponibili al pubblico informazioni aggiornate, imparziali, obiettive, quantitative e qualitative, su ciascun CdS offerto, mediante una pubblicazione regolare e accessibile delle parti pubbliche della SUA-CdS.
