SECTION: Opinions of Graduates
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/1903

Opinions of Graduates The first cohort of this degree program will graduate in the 2023-2024 academic year; the first graduation session will take place in July 2024.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding (applying knowledge and understanding)
The graduate in Technical Professions for Construction and Territory will be able to analyze territorial, urbanistic, and landscape-environmental issues, being capable of choosing the most suitable techniques for their survey and representation. In addition to traditional techniques, they will be able to use cutting-edge information technologies.
They will be able to carry out support activities for monitoring and diagnosing structures, infrastructure, and territory. They will also be able to understand and analyze, through a scientific approach, basic engineering problems, with reference to geotechnical, structural, and architectural aspects.
The graduate will have the ability to conduct land and property valuation assessments and will also master the administrative and technical procedures required to intervene in the territory. They will be able to independently manage or provide consultancy regarding the preparation of building permits, technical specifications, maintenance plans, technical drawings, and forensic technical consultancy activities.
The graduate will have the ability to independently assess the fulfillment of safety and organization requirements for construction sites and will be able to hold the title of Construction Site Safety Coordinator D. Lgs. 81/08 and subsequent amendments.
The abilities to apply knowledge and understanding mentioned above are acquired through attendance at theoretical courses, study of recommended teaching materials, discussion and dialogue with professors, laboratory activities, and internships.
The actual understanding of in-depth subjects and the ability to solve specific problems will be assessed through oral and/or written exams.
Learning Skills (learning skills)
The graduate in Technical Professions for Construction and Territory will be able to update themselves on methods, tools, and techniques required in the management and recovery of existing real estate and infrastructure. Additionally, they will be capable of handling the design and execution of simple works falling under civil and environmental engineering. These learning abilities will be demonstrated by achieving curricular objectives within the framework of the assessments provided in the Degree Program.
The development of learning abilities will be supported by all training activities of the study program: individual study, preparation of individual and group projects, bibliographic research, activities carried out during exercises and laboratories, learning through dialogue with academic and company tutors during internships, and preparation for the final exam. In particular, during the study path, students will develop awareness of the importance of autonomous and mature learning, which is indispensable for professional practice.
The ability to learn is assessed through verification methods throughout the entire training process.
Knowledge and Understanding (knowledge and understanding)
This Professional Degree Program will enable graduates to acquire knowledge and understanding in the field of construction and civil and rural infrastructure.
In particular, the graduate will know techniques for surveying, analyzing, representing, and managing territorial, urbanistic, and landscape-environmental issues at various scales. In addition to traditional techniques, they will deepen cutting-edge information technologies.
The graduate will possess knowledge for monitoring and diagnosing structures, infrastructure, and territory. They will also be able to understand and analyze, through a rigorous scientific approach, basic civil engineering problems, with reference to geotechnical, structural, and architectural aspects.
The graduate will have knowledge of land and property valuation and will acquire knowledge of law and procedures required to manage the administrative process for preparing building permits, technical specifications, maintenance plans, technical drawings, and forensic technical consultancy activities.
The graduate will know the safety and organization requirements for construction sites.
They will also have acquired adequate knowledge and understanding, in written and oral form, of at least one European Union language other than Italian.
Knowledge and understanding can be applied across four learning areas:
1) Basic training;
2) Interdisciplinary technical-professional training;
3) Construction;
4) Territory.
Organization and Responsibility of Quality Assurance at the Course Level The Quality Assurance of the Course is organized according to the structure illustrated in the attached PDF file.
Program of Work and Implementation Deadlines The program of work, including implementation deadlines for various initiatives, is reported in the attached PDF file.
Brief Description of Related and Complementary Activities Regarding related and complementary activities, it is considered necessary to complete the training path, beyond basic and characteristic subjects, by deepening the study of physical geography and geomorphology, whose knowledge contributes to the formation of a Competent Graduate Technician in assessing geomorphological risks and environmental resources based on analysis methods and techniques such as photointerpretation, remote sensing, and geomorphological surveys and processing using models; in assessing environmental impact and nature conservation; in developing cartographic methods and techniques, also using territorial information systems, for representing data and processing them with particular attention to exogenous processes, geomorphological assets, and environmental issues.
Course Description Briefly The Study Program in Technical Professions for Construction and Territory is a professionalizing program aimed at training qualified, versatile technicians in the field of construction and civil and rural infrastructure (Geometers or Building Engineers). Graduates can register with the College of Geometers or the College of Industrial Engineers and, therefore, practice the profession of Licensed Geometer or Licensed Building Engineer.
The three-year training path is designed to deepen, beyond basic disciplines, professional knowledge useful for forming a highly qualified technician in the fields of valuation, surveying, construction site safety, and building, territory management, urban planning, and public and private works law. Practical skills are refined through numerous hours of laboratory and internship activities, which occupy the entire third year.
The final exam has the value of professional qualification for Licensed Geometers or Licensed Building Engineers (DDL 28-10-2021).
The graduation committee includes two representatives of the competent Provincial College.
Continuing studies in master's degrees is not a natural outcome for this Degree Program.
External Effectiveness The first cohort of the Course has not yet completed the study path; the first graduation session will take place in July 2024.
Specific Educational Objectives of the Course and Description of the Training Path The educational objectives of this professionalizing degree program are consistent with the qualifying educational objectives of class L-P01 Technical Professions for Construction and Territory, as described in DM 446/2020 and subsequent amendments, as reported in the interministerial decree No. 682 of 24/05/2023.
The training path includes activities aimed at acquiring:
• Basic knowledge in the fields of chemistry, physics, mathematics, and informatics, tailored to the specific technical figure to be formed;
• Knowledge in the fields of construction, infrastructure, and territory;
• Knowledge in the fields of private and administrative law;
• Knowledge in the fields of surveying, geomatics, and valuation.
Graduates in the class must:
• Be able to address and solve technical business problems;
• Know the principles and scope of professional activities and their related regulations and ethics;
• Possess the basic cognitive tools for continuous updating of their knowledge, also using information technology tools.
Regarding basic training activities, students are provided with the necessary basic knowledge to equip them with tools for solving problems and measuring and interpreting data.
Within the characteristic training activities:
• The study of digital representation of buildings and territory through drawing, surveying, and CAD modeling, using both traditional techniques and available advanced technologies (ICAR/17). The deepening of these topics is also integrated with laboratory activities.
• Within architecture and urban planning, the study of architectural and urban composition with specific reference to a small building (ICAR/14), and the analysis of techniques for producing, reading, and comparing urban planning documentation at various levels and scales.
• Within construction and environment, attention is focused on the knowledge required to adequately control complex transformations in the building and territorial layout resulting from social and economic development processes. In this context, the study of knowledge elements for assessing structural and geotechnical aspects (ICAR/07, ICAR/08, and ICAR/09), the valuation of real estate assets on the territory (ICAR/22), and the organization and safety of construction sites (ICAR/11) with the issuance of the title of Construction Site Safety Coordinator D. Lgs. 81/08 and subsequent amendments. Courses will be integrated with laboratory activities to be carried out in the field and/or at construction sites.
• The study of geodesy, surveying, and cadastral activities is deepened (ICAR/06). The deepening of these topics is also integrated with field laboratory activities.
• Finally, the graduate's knowledge is reinforced regarding aspects of technical legislation for public and private works (IUS/10).
Regarding related and complementary activities, the deepening of physical geography and geomorphology studies (GEO/04) is provided.
Students also have the opportunity to take advantage of the free training offer to deepen cross-cutting themes applicable to all areas where the graduate technician will be called to operate (ICAR/02, ING-IND/11, etc.).
In addition to frontal teaching and laboratory activities, a practical-evaluative internship period is provided, which must be carried out at companies, firms, professional studios, public administrations, public or private bodies, including third-sector organizations, or professional colleges. In particular, the practical-evaluative internship aims to enable students to acquire and apply knowledge, skills, and professional abilities, including: topographic and architectural surveying; digital methodologies for supporting planning and design; support for monitoring and diagnosing structures, infrastructure, territory, and auxiliary facilities; management of cadastral, demarcation, and local authority databases; agricultural activities and rural development; valuation assessments; work accounting; construction site and workplace safety; energy certification and sustainability and health certification of environments; preparation of building permits, technical specifications, maintenance plans, technical drawings, and forensic technical consultancy activities; design, work management, and supervision of architectural, structural, distributional, and installation aspects related to modest constructions; principles of professional activities; regulations and ethics.
Opinions of Entities and Companies with Internship/Practical Training Agreements The students of the first cohort of the study program are currently completing their internship during the 2023-24 academic year.

Regarding the proposals advanced by the 'G. d'Annunzio' University of Chieti-Pescara, Prof. Sergio Caputi noted that:
-The Study Program in Technical Professions for Construction and Territory for the Geometer Profession is a professionalizing program aimed at training qualified, versatile technicians in the field of construction and civil and rural infrastructure. Graduates can register with the College of Geometers and, therefore, practice the profession of Licensed Geometer.
The three-year training path is designed to deepen, beyond basic disciplines, professional knowledge useful for forming a highly qualified technician in the fields of valuation, surveying, construction site safety, and building, territory management, urban planning, and public and private works law. Practical skills are refined through numerous hours of laboratory and internship activities, which occupy the entire third year. Continuing studies in master's degrees is not a natural outcome for this Degree Program. Specifically, graduates in the program must:
 Have acquired a sufficient preparation in basic disciplines, with particular attention to understanding the phases underlying the processes of design, realization, and management of building and infrastructure works in the civil, rural sector, and territory management;
 Possess adequate preparation in reference applied disciplines and a sufficient set of essential operational knowledge to operate independently in various fields such as: i) topographic, cartographic, and architectural surveying, including subsequent restitution, also cartographic and georeferenced, using the most advanced available technologies for surveying and restitution; ii) activities based on the use of digital methodologies for supporting urban planning and architectural design; iii) support activities for monitoring and diagnosing structures, infrastructure, and territory, as well as auxiliary facilities; iv) activities related to the management and updating of databases: cadastral, demarcation, and local authorities; v) agricultural activities and rural development; vi) valuation assessments; vii) safety in managing construction sites and workplaces, with preparation of permits for design and execution; viii) activities of analysis and monitoring aimed at energy efficiency, energy certification, and certification of sustainability and health of environments; ix) preparation of building permits, technical specifications, maintenance plans, technical drawings, and forensic technical consultancy activities; x) design, work management, and supervision of architectural, structural, distributional, and installation aspects related to modest constructions;
 Appropriately know the aspects related to technical and economic feasibility, cost calculation, and the production and realization process of construction works, auxiliary facilities, and territorial transformations with their functional elements;
 Know the principles and scope of professional activities and their related regulations and ethics;
 Possess the basic cognitive tools for continuous updating of their knowledge;
 Be able to effectively use, in written and oral form, at least one European Union language other than Italian, within their specific field of competence and for general information exchange;
 Possess adequate competencies and tools for managing and communicating information and for carrying out group work with defined levels of autonomy.
The training path includes activities aimed at acquiring:
 Basic knowledge in the fields of chemistry, physics, mathematics, and informatics, tailored to the specific technical figure to be formed;
 Knowledge in the fields of construction, infrastructure, and territory;
 Knowledge in the fields of private and administrative law;
 Knowledge in the fields of surveying, geomatics, and valuation.
The graduate technician must:
 Be able to address and solve technical business problems;
 Know the principles and scope of professional activities and their related regulations and ethics;
 Possess the basic cognitive tools for continuous updating of their knowledge, also using information technology tools.
The training path is structured in line with DM 446/2020 and provides training activities delivered in the areas of basic, characteristic, and related/integrated disciplines. These activities are integrated with laboratory and internship training activities aimed at preparing graduates to solve practical basic engineering problems they may face in their future professional experience. Graduate technicians will possess knowledge suitable for technical roles in both public and private sectors. The main expected employment outcomes for graduates of this class are: i) independent professional activities; ii) employees in technical roles in engineering companies, legal or economic-commercial firms, construction companies, real estate management entities, and public bodies for territory management and control; iii) employees in technical roles in public administrations.
Continuing studies in master's degrees is not a natural outcome for courses of this class.
This Professional Degree Program will enable graduates to acquire knowledge and understanding in the field of construction and civil and rural infrastructure.

Consultation with Representative Organizations - at National and International Levels - of Goods and Service Production, Professions (Course Establishment)
The content and structure of the training path were defined through analysis of regulatory sources, evaluation of sector studies and research (National Council of Geometers, Confindustria, etc.), and direct consultation with stakeholders, as required by Article 11, Paragraph 4 of DM No. 270/2004.
On July 24, 2019, a meeting was held between two professors from the Department of Engineering and Geology (the dean and a researcher), a representative of the Pescara Province College of Geometers, and a professional from the Pescara Engineering Order, as well as a retired professor at the Pescara CAT Technical Institute, to examine the proposal for the new Study Program. From the initial consultation, strong interest was expressed, particularly by the Secretary of the Pescara Province College of Geometers, in establishing the new Study Program capable of addressing needs emerging from recent regulatory renewal. The constructive discussion that followed led to refining the initial proposal, particularly by introducing an exam on construction site organization and safety to obtain the title of Construction Site Safety Coordinator D.Lgs. 81/08 and subsequent amendments; and led to the final choice of the educational framework. On November 5, 2019, the first draft of the study plan was presented in the presence of the same professionals. Following the issuance of DM 446 of August 12, 2020, a further meeting was held on October 14, 2020, to update the proposal based on new regulations.
The interest of the Colleges of Geometers was renewed and formalized through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between the Department of Engineering and Geology of the G. d'Annunzio University of Chieti-Pescara and the Provincial Colleges of Geometers and Licensed Geometers of the provinces of Chieti, Pescara, and Teramo on January 5, 2021. Specifically, in the agreement, the parties commit to identifying the providers of training activities within the curricular internships for each cohort, to ensure all graduates complete the training internship and the associated thesis.
Consultations with social partners also involved the Pescara CAT Technical Institute, officials of the Pescara Civil Engineering Office, some professionals from the provinces of Chieti and Pescara, and construction companies operating in the territory. In particular, the positive opinion expressed by representatives of the labor market, both public and private, regarding the establishment of the new degree program was considered a strong positive signal for potential employment outcomes. It was also noted that all stakeholders fully agreed with the proposed study plan, recognized as fully aligned with DM 446 and responsive to the training needs required for the Licensed Geometer professional figure. It is noted that, in response to the health emergency related to the Covid-19 pandemic, teleconferences were held in the second half of November 2020.
Minutes of all meetings are attached to this document.
From the plurality of opinions collected, a common need emerged to activate a training path for technicians in the fields of construction and territory that can serve as a natural continuation of the path previously provided by technical institutes in the technological sector with a focus on Construction, Environment, and Territory (CAT) and allow registration on the Register of Licensed Geometers (once the enabling DDLs come into effect).
Subsequent consultations will be annual, and it is planned to establish a Steering Committee to systematically listen to stakeholders, both for external monitoring and to remain aligned with labor market evolution.
The Committee will consist of:
- Head of the Study Program
- Director of the INGEO Department with coordination functions;
- Student representatives
- Representatives of professional orders (Geometers, Engineers, Architects) from neighboring provinces.
- Representatives of CAT schools from neighboring provinces;
- President or delegate of Confindustria.
Operational and decision-making meetings will be held at the Department of Engineering and Geology and will be expanded to the AQ Management Group.

Characteristics of the Final Exam Admission to the final exam will be permitted only for students who have acquired all credits from the passing exams and other training activities required for the Degree Program.
The final exam, worth 3 CFU, includes the presentation of a problem resolution developed during internship activities, demonstrating the student's ability to apply knowledge acquired during the study program under the supervision of one or more internal professors and, if applicable, external professional or company figures.
Pursuant to Articles 2 and 3 of Law November 8, 2021, No. 163, the final exam for the professionalizing degree in Technical Professions for Construction and Territory - class L-P01 qualifies for the practice of the professions related to the individual study programs, namely Licensed Geometer or Licensed Industrial Engineer.
For this purpose, the final exam includes the performance of a practical evaluation of professional skills acquired during the internship, aimed at verifying the candidate's suitability for the practice of the profession, which precedes the final exam.
Final Exam Procedure The final exam for the professionalizing degree includes the performance of a Practical Evaluation Test (PET) that precedes the final exam.
Practical Evaluation Test (PET)
The PET aims to verify the acquisition, during the Practical Evaluative Internship (PEI), of the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary for the independent practice of the Licensed Geometer profession.
The PET consists of an examination of the profession's discipline and the resolution of one or more practical problems consistent with those analyzed during the PEI.
The PET judging committee has a balanced composition and consists of at least four members. Half of the committee members are university professors, one of whom serves as President, appointed by the Course Council, and the other half are professionals with proven experience, appointed by the competent professional bodies, with at least five years of practice in the profession chosen by the student.
The student passes the PET by obtaining a suitability judgment, which does not contribute to determining the graduation grade, and proceeds to the defense of the thesis.
Final Exam The final exam includes the presentation of a written report (thesis) and an oral discussion in the presence of a committee composed of professors and the internship tutor.
The candidate is assigned a specific time for presenting their work. The graduation committee formulates its judgment at the end of a block of presentations that occupy a time frame not exceeding half a day.
The thesis committee consists of the thesis advisors, internship tutors, and other professors of the Degree Program up to the minimum number of committee members required by the University's Academic Regulations.
Honors may be awarded, upon unanimous decision of the committee, in cases where the total score, sum of the average of passed exams and the final exam score, is at least 110/110.
The proclamation takes place in a public session.
Pursuant to the DDL 'Provisions on University Qualifying Titles' of October 28, 2021, the final exam has the value of professional qualification for Licensed Geometers or Licensed Industrial Engineers. Therefore, the committee is integrated by two representatives of the competent Provincial College.
Summary of the Technical Report of the Evaluation Unit - SUA Sheet The activation of the Degree Program, following the issuance of DM August 12, 2020, defining the modalities for activating professional-oriented paths, contributes to enhancing the University's training offer.
The design of the Course was carried out with appropriate timing and attention. The cultural and professional profiles of the figure the Course aims to form are clearly defined. Direct consultation with stakeholders is adequate at the local level, though not entirely at the national level.
Functions and competencies are described with sufficient precision and coherence with professional profiles. Regarding the disciplinary competencies of the members of the Evaluation Unit, the path appears sufficiently coherent with the formed professional profiles.
The structural resources and teaching staff appear adequate. Monitoring of the Course is consistent with the University's Quality Assurance system.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITÀ DEGLI STUDI GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO – CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [L604] OBSTETRICS
SECTION: Admission Procedures
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/615

Admission Procedures Students admitted to the degree program who score below 20% of the maximum score in Mathematics, Physics, Biology, and Chemistry in the admission test will be assigned Additional Educational Requirements (OFA).
Students with Additional Educational Requirements (OFA) will be duly informed by the instructors of the relevant disciplines regarding the deficiencies in their preparation and the obligation to attend the training activities provided to facilitate recovery within the first year of study. The methods for fulfilling OFA will be indicated by the instructor, who may conduct individual recovery lessons, guided deepening sessions, exercises, etc., or utilize the support of tutor students for recovery, established by the Orientation Office for the 2024 academic year.
OFA will be considered fulfilled upon passing the exams in the disciplinary areas subject to OFA. In case of failure to pass, pursuant to Article 49, paragraph 3, point b of the University Academic Regulations, which states: "Students who do not fulfill the Additional Educational Requirements under Article 28 of this Regulation by the date set by the University bodies and, in any case, within the first year of study, cannot enroll in the second-year courses." Therefore, enrollment in the second year must be permitted, provided that it is not possible to take second-year exams before fulfilling the individually assigned OFA.

COURSE: [L604] OBSTETRICS
SECTION: Syllabus, texts and objectives
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/615

Syllabus, texts and objectives Communication skills
The Obstetrics graduate must develop the following communication skills:
• Use appropriate communication skills with users and their families within the birth process and/or with other healthcare professionals in appropriate verbal, non-verbal and written form;
• Apply principles of teaching and learning for informative interventions or specific educational projects aimed at promoting and maintaining health for the woman and/or the community
• Establish professional relationships and collaborate with other healthcare professionals, being aware of the specificities of different professional roles and their integration with obstetric care
• Support and encourage users regarding health choices, reinforcing coping skills and enhancing available resources
• Conduct birth preparation courses aimed at informing and supporting the woman/couple during pregnancy, birth, postpartum period and breastfeeding.
• Assume leadership roles for support staff and/or students, including delegation and supervision of care activities provided by others, ensuring compliance with quality and safety standards for planning and management of care.
• Use appropriate strategies to promote self-esteem, integrity and comfort for the patient
• Communicate effectively with verbal, non-verbal and written methods the health assessments and decisions within the interdisciplinary healthcare team
• Facilitate coordination of care to achieve agreed health outcomes
• Collaborate with the care team to implement and develop protocols and guidelines.
The assessment method includes oral interviews and/or written assignments.
The activities carried out are recorded in a dedicated logbook and subsequently evaluated by the Committee, which includes the internship coordinator and teachers.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITY OF CHIETI/PESCARA GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO STUDIES
COURSE: [L604] MIDWIFERY
SECTION: Judgment
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/615

Judgment (making judgments)
The graduate in Midwifery must demonstrate judgment through the following skills:
• adapt obstetric care by recognizing similarities and differences in the user base, considering values, ethnicities, and socio-cultural practices of the people being assisted
• analyze guidelines and operational practices of health services and identify appropriate obstetric practices that reflect legal, political, geographical, economic, ethical, and social influences
• use critical thinking skills to safely provide personalized obstetric care
• integrate knowledge of cultural diversity, legal aspects, and ethical principles in providing and/or managing obstetric care in various contexts and health and social services
• assume responsibility and account for one's professional practice in accordance with the professional profile and Code of Ethics
• recognize differences in roles and responsibilities between midwives, support staff, and other healthcare professionals
• practice obstetric care in accordance with the professional Code of Ethics
• act responsibly in obstetric practice and ensure adherence to ethical and legal standards.
Teaching methods and activities, didactic tools to develop expected outcomes:
- lectures;
- guided reading and application;
- videos, image demonstrations, diagrams, materials, and charts;
- case discussions in small groups with presentations in plenary sessions;
- internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various contexts and with progressive assumption of autonomy and responsibility;
- debriefing sessions to reflect on and reprocess professional practice experiences.
Assessment methods include oral interviews and/or written assignments.
The internship activity completed is recorded in a dedicated logbook and subsequently evaluated by the Commission, which includes the internship coordinator and instructors.

STUDENT OPINIONS The data presented in this section refers to the results of questionnaires conducted in accordance with ANVUR guidelines and administered electronically.
For the evaluation of the current academic year 2022/2023 (data up to July 2023), after processing 1,090 questionnaires across a total of 61 teaching activities (with 100% coverage), a score of 3.49 was obtained. This value is the average of: a) overall student satisfaction of the program, 3.43, which is higher than the university average of 3.35 and the Health Area average of 3.33; b) logistical and organizational aspects, which achieved a score of 3.51, higher than the university average of 3.48 and the Health Area average of 3.43; c) teaching effectiveness, which achieved a score of 3.52, higher than the university average of 3.47 and the Health Area average of 3.42.
Compared to previous years, there is a notable upward trend in the number of courses considered and the scores of the courses, maintaining a B level.
All reported scores remain higher than those of the university and Health Area, particularly "Clarity in exam methods" and "Instructor availability to provide clarifications on covered topics" continue to reach the highest score levels as in previous academic years. It is noted that the score for "The study load required by the course is proportional to the assigned credits" is significantly higher than the university and Health Area averages.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding (applying knowledge and understanding)
The Obstetrics graduate must demonstrate knowledge relevant to the practice of the obstetric profession, must demonstrate having acquired knowledge and understanding applied to data collection for statistical purposes and the elaboration of a systematic study of the same, also for applied research with progressive judgment autonomy. Must also acquire the ability to learn tools and operational methods specific to operational scientific research in the obstetric field.
Must be able to apply computer knowledge to use major search engines and the English language to interpret scientific literature in the fields of obstetric-gynecological and neonatal competence.
Teaching tools aimed at achieving the ability to apply knowledge in characteristic activities include, besides the entire teaching activity directed at the student (frontal lessons, self-learning, etc.), a pre-clinical activity and clinical or simulated patient internship. Other fundamental tools will be the use of computer means, construction and updating of databases, bibliographic research, all aimed at preparing the thesis for the final exam. The evaluation of these skills will occur through exams, periodic practical assessments within internship activities, as well as through internship performance exams, aimed at verifying the acquisition of manual and technical skills in various clinical activities specific to the professional profile, and through the final exam itself. Obstetrics graduates must be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to demonstrate a professional approach to their work, and must possess adequate skills to support arguments and solve problems in their field of study.
Learning Skills
The Obstetrics graduate must develop the following self-learning abilities:
• demonstrate skills in self-assessment of their competencies and outline their own development and learning needs regarding the profession
• demonstrate the ability to independently study using effective and relevant evidence-based research methods
• plan, organize, and develop their own actions in response to continuous changes in knowledge and health and social needs
• collaborate and share knowledge within work teams
• demonstrate the ability to seek necessary information to resolve problems or uncertainties in professional practice, critically selecting secondary sources (guidelines, systematic reviews) and primary sources (research studies).
Teaching methodologies and activities, educational tools to develop expected outcomes:
- problem-based learning (PBL)
- use of cognitive maps
- use of contracts and self-learning plans to empower the student in planning their internship path and self-assessment
- laboratories of bibliographic research methodology online and paper-based
- guided reading for critical evaluation of scientific and professional literature in both Italian and English.
Evaluation tools to verify achievement of expected outcomes
- project work,
- tutorial supervision on the internship path
- active participation in work sessions and debriefing
- punctuality and quality in the presentation of reports
Knowledge and Understanding (knowledge and understanding)
Obstetrics graduates must acquire knowledge in the fields of basic biomedical disciplines and clinical disciplines, manual skills, and operational techniques, relevant to the practice of the obstetric profession. In particular, the Obstetrics graduate must possess fundamental knowledge of biological sciences for understanding the human body, especially the female genital apparatus, must know the principles of genetics and the methods used for prenatal diagnosis, must know risk factors and prevention strategies to support the health of the pregnant woman, her conceived product, and the couple.
The Obstetrics graduate must learn the necessary knowledge to monitor maternal-fetal well-being during physiological pregnancy, using cardiovascular imaging techniques, and to identify potentially pathological situations during emergencies through the use of available means and competence.
Must also know basic psychopedagogical notions for birth preparation. Must know psychological pathologies related to the pregnancy-postpartum state and have counseling skills to manage a good relationship with the woman and couple during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, including for foreign-origin clientele. Additionally, must know computer disciplines to use major search engines and the English language to interpret scientific literature in the fields of obstetric-gynecological and neonatal competence.
To acquire knowledge and learn to use the specific language of a healthcare profession, Obstetrics graduates must use appropriate textbooks. Must achieve knowledge and understanding in a post-secondary field of study that allows them to know some cutting-edge topics in their field of study. Such knowledge is acquired through basic and characteristic activities. The teaching method includes frontal lessons, laboratories, exercises, and clinical internships. Verification methods are oral interviews or written reports, requiring the application of logical rigor, and, for disciplines that require it, practical tests on simulators and patients.

The CdS, to ensure the appropriate relationship between the teaching provided and the research conducted in the disciplines activated within the CdS, will promote, in the spirit of continuous improvement, a constant updating process of the programs related to different courses and a careful monitoring of laboratory and internship training activities. Simplified description of related and integrative activities
The related or integrative training activities of the Obstetrics CdS include MED/08 - Pathological Anatomy and MED/46 - Laboratory Medicine Technical Sciences.
MED/08 was chosen as it fully aligns with the specific educational objectives of the course. Indeed, this course is indispensable in the training path to learn the necessary knowledge to identify potentially pathological situations through the use of available means. This will allow the obstetric professional to implement, where necessary, the relevant emergency measures.
It was decided to also include MED/46 - Laboratory Medicine Technical Sciences among the related and integrative disciplines. Examining the professional profiles identified for the Obstetrics CdS and its educational objectives, during the consultation meeting with the representative organizations of the CdS, it was deemed appropriate to include the MED/46 SSD in the curriculum to deepen techniques useful for the diagnosis of tumor markers for breast, ovarian, and uterine cancer, useful for the genetic prevention of such pathologies and the cytological diagnosis of tumors of the cervix and uterine body. This integration takes into account the importance of providing knowledge of advanced diagnostic techniques capable of acquiring skills to work in oncological screening centers, outpatient clinics, and territorial settings. These advanced diagnostic techniques promote knowledge of biochemical and biophysical changes typical of gender specificity.
Brief course description
The Study Course is aimed at training aspiring obstetricians through theoretical-practical preparation of obstetric-gynecological pathophysiology, principles of general medicine, medical-legal, clinical informatics, oncology, pharmacology, and pediatrics. Integrated courses also include other study subjects aimed at the cultural and behavioral preparation of obstetricians. The practical internship is aimed at developing autonomous management of childbirth and obstetric-gynecological care.
The obstetrician participates in planning diagnostic-therapeutic pathways in the obstetric-gynecological and neonatal area and implements related prevention, care, and rehabilitation programs.
External effectiveness
Data regarding the employment status in 2021 for 2020 graduates one year after graduation is not displayed on the Interuniversity Consortium AlmaLaurea website because the group has fewer than 5 graduates due to the Covid-19 pandemic.
Specific course educational objectives and description of the training path
The planning of the specific training path aimed at producing the Obstetrics graduate is carried out by the teaching structures through the appropriate selection of disciplinary areas of the characteristic training activities, with particular attention to professionalizing scientific-disciplinary sectors. The Obstetrics graduate, depending on the training path, must achieve the following specified professional competencies.
This process is realized through theoretical and practical training encompassing behavioral competencies, achieved through specific paths aimed at acquiring complete mastery and operational usability of every necessary competency. An integral and fundamental support of this training path is represented by practical activities and internships, guided by specific professional tutors, and coordinated by a teacher with the highest educational level for each profile and in compliance with any community regulations.
The internship teaching activity aims to achieve knowledge, skills, and professional behaviors directed at identifying, planning, delivering, and evaluating the profession of the Obstetrician. Practical activities and internships, defined by the Educational Ordinance, must be carried out both qualitatively and quantitatively in accordance with the relevant European Union regulations, particularly the educational standard must comply with the European Union Directive 80/154/EEC.
General educational objectives
1. Analyze women's health issues throughout their biological-sexual cycle and the responses of health and social services to the main needs of women, newborns, couples, and the community;
2. Acquire the necessary knowledge to understand biological phenomena, the main mechanisms of organ and system functioning, and specifically the physiology of human reproduction and embryonic development;
3. Understand the fundamentals of pathophysiology applied to various clinical situations, for conditions in pregnancy and for pregnancy, also in relation to diagnostic parameters.
4. Identify the needs for obstetric-gynecological care of the woman/couple and the community and formulate specific objectives according to the principle of priority.
5. Acquire the necessary knowledge to identify potentially pathological situations through the use of available means and competence, and implement, where necessary, the relevant emergency measures.
6. Achieve mastery of methods and content specific to the obstetric profession through theoretical, practical, and clinical internship training, under the guidance of appropriately assigned tutors at accredited SSN structures and through elective internships in Italian or foreign clinical departments according to the European standard (Directive 80/154/EEC).
7. Achieve a level of knowledge and competence in speaking at least one European Union language, besides Italian, within the specific field of obstetrics or for general information exchange.
Specific educational objectives
1. Identify physical, psychological, and social needs and diagnose the assistance needs of the woman, couple, and community in various socio-health contexts, integrating theoretical and practical knowledge to respond with technical-scientific competence;
2. Identify the needs for obstetric-gynecological care requiring preventive, curative, rehabilitative, and palliative competencies in specific areas of gynecology and obstetrics, such as breast pathology, pelvic static alterations, infertility, metabolic diseases, and infectious diseases, etc.;
3. Provide good information and advice regarding family planning according to the principle of responsible motherhood and fatherhood;
4. Provide the woman/couple with good information and advice regarding the birth process (having actively participated in preparing at least 25 women/couples in the birth process according to scientifically validated methodologies);
5. Implement health education interventions for the woman/couple and community, specifically regarding sexually transmitted diseases (STDs);
6. Implement health education interventions for the prevention of genital tract neoplasms and associated glands, through information processes and methodologies of which they are competent (e.g., breast self-examination, Pap test, etc.);
7. Identify socio-health needs of pregnant women, providing every informational-educational support aimed at removing conflicting situations in the presence of drug addiction, poverty, disability, etc.;
8. Evaluate clinical manifestations related to the biological-sexual cycle of women;
9. Evaluate clinical manifestations specifically related to pregnancy (having attended at least 100 prenatal examinations);
10. Plan, provide, and evaluate gynecological and obstetric-neonatal care for healthy and sick individuals within a complex and integrated socio-assistive system, promoting positive health lifestyles and adopting assistance systems oriented toward self-management and self-care;
11. Monitor maternal-fetal well-being during physiological pregnancy, during spontaneous labor, and (in collaboration with the specialist) in pathological situations (monitoring and care of at least 40 parturients);
12. Perform normal delivery when vertex presentation occurs (having actively participated in at least 40 deliveries or at least 30 deliveries with participation in an additional 20 deliveries);
13. Perform delivery in case of footling presentation in emergency situations (having actively participated in at least 2 footling deliveries, or in the absence of cases, having completed appropriate simulated exercises);
14. Perform normal delivery when vertex presentation occurs, including episiotomy if necessary (having actively participated in at least 5 deliveries with episiotomy and suturing, or in the absence of cases, having completed appropriate simulated exercises);
15. Prevent, identify, monitor, and manage potentially pathological situations requiring medical intervention and implement, where necessary, the relevant emergency measures through the use of available means and competence (having actively participated in monitoring at least 40 pregnant women, parturients, or postpartum women in pathological pregnancies or difficult deliveries);
16. Evaluate clinical manifestations related to gynecological, obstetric, and neonatal pathologies, reactions to disease stages, interventions in inpatient, day-hospital, and day-surgery settings, as well as home care (having actively participated during the internship in the care and treatment of gynecological-obstetric patients and neonates, also initiating cases in medicine, surgery, and TIN departments);
17. Evaluate clinical manifestations related to immediate, intermediate, and late physiological postpartum in inpatient settings, as well as home care, including evaluation of neonates without significant pathologies (having actively examined at least 100 postpartum women and neonates without significant pathologies);
18. Evaluate clinical manifestations related to immediate, intermediate, and late physiological and pathological postpartum in inpatient settings, including evaluation of clinical manifestations of preterm and post-term neonates with low birth weight or various pathologies (having actively participated during the internship in the care and treatment of postpartum women and neonates, including preterm and post-term neonates with low birth weight or various pathologies);
19. Implement planned care interventions according to verified and verifiable evidence-based guidelines (EBM/EBC);
20. Examine and care for the newborn, take any necessary initiative, and, if required, perform immediate resuscitation (having actively participated during the internship in the monitoring and care of at least 25 neonates in Neonatal Intensive Care – TIN);
21. Ensure the correct application of diagnostic-therapeutic services, respecting scientific principles and adapting them to the person being assisted, in relation to various priority health issues of women and couples;
22. Contribute to identifying, defining, and organizing gynecological and obstetric care in routine and emergency/urgent settings according to priority criteria, ensuring continuity of care through optimal use of human and material resources;
23. Define, implement, and evaluate research projects aimed at applying results in the gynecological-obstetric-neonatal care process and improving the efficiency and effectiveness of care;
24. Implement evaluation interventions for preventive, curative, palliative, and rehabilitative gynecological and neonatal services according to specific process and outcome indicators;
25. Demonstrate professional and decision-making ability in planning and implementing health and sexual education interventions for women, couples, and the community;
26. Demonstrate the ability to plan, implement, and evaluate training interventions for support staff, as well as directly contribute to the training and updating of their own professional profile, also in relation to guided clinical internships for university students in the specific field;
27. Demonstrate knowledge, skills, and abilities in performing innovative and traditional surgical procedures in collaboration with specialist doctors and other healthcare personnel (having actively collaborated in at least 30 cesarean sections, 30 traditional gynecological procedures, and 20 minimally invasive procedures such as laparoscopy and hysteroscopy);
28. Demonstrate knowledge of ethical-deontological and medical-legal principles and be able to implement and evaluate their application in the obstetric-gynecological-neonatal field;
29. Demonstrate recognition and respect for their own role and competencies and those of other members of the care team, in accordance with current regulations on responsibility and scope of practice for obstetricians, independently and in collaboration with other healthcare professionals;
30. Demonstrate knowledge of and ability to propose appropriate birth technologies respecting different ethnicities and according to the principles of personalization and appropriateness of care;
31. Demonstrate knowledge of and ability to use at least one European Union language, besides Italian, within the specific field of competence and for general information exchange.
The Course also aims to provide students with the most suitable tools for developing self-assessment and self-formation abilities to complete and enhance their professional skills.
The entire Training Project aims to structure the Curriculum through teaching/learning methods that allow the development of a comprehensive vision and critical synthesis according to the most modern principles of the holistic approach to patient care, also through the attempt to harmoniously integrate theoretical-scientific and technical-practical teachings.
The intent is to form a professional obstetrician characterized by the ability to operate while considering:
- the centrality of the person being assisted;
- the ability to implement interventions relevant to needs;
- openness to change;
- ability to update;
- scientific evidence of clinical/assistance choices made;
- research spirit.

During the 2022/2023 academic year, the CdS President Maria Cristina Curia met with the members of the Steering Committee both in collective meetings and individually.

Another point discussed was sensitizing these students to undertake a research path starting from thesis selection to participation in calls for doctoral programs in the health area.
On September 29, 2022, at the Gynecology and Obstetrics Department of the "SS. Annunziata" Hospital in Chieti, the Steering Committee meeting was held, attended by CdS President Maria Cristina Curia, President of the Chieti Province Obstetricians College Cinzia Di Matteo, and representatives of the College Antonella Di Matteo, Maura Di Giovanni, Alessandra D'Angelo.
During the meeting, the need to sensitize the CdS toward gender medicine was reiterated.
This is a very important topic for the obstetrician as the professional cares for a woman's life from childhood through puberty to more mature age such as menopause. Today, women live a certainly longer life than before, but not without pathologies related to the hormonal cycle as well as women's health. Women face cardiovascular, osteoarticular diseases, thyroid diseases, headaches, migraines, cataracts, arthritis, Alzheimer's, diabetes, obesity, urinary infections, hormone-dependent tumors. To this are added depressive disorders in which women are more affected. Additionally, women are more prone to household accidents, and drugs used for men are not always effective in women.
Medicine therefore needs a broader vision in which the obstetrician plays an increasingly important role and must be prepared to accompany women with chronic diseases.
Lastly, during the meeting, the need to move professionals to the territory and thus to consultoriums was reiterated. For this aspect as well, obstetricians must be prepared during training because the approach in the territory where the obstetrician enters the woman's home is different from the woman who voluntarily goes to the hospital.
During the meeting, it was also discussed to implement, even through the establishment of Master's degrees, topics such as: breastfeeding, vulvar atrophy, Assisted Reproductive Technology (PMA), urogynecology.

Final exam characteristics
Pursuant to Article 7 of the Interministerial Decree of February 19, 2009, the final exam, having the value of a state-licensing exam under Article 6, paragraph 3, of Legislative Decree No. 502/1992, consists of:
a) practical test during which the student must demonstrate having acquired the theoretical-practical and technical-professional knowledge and skills specific to the professional profile.
b) preparation of a thesis and its defense.
The exam is organized, by decree of the Ministry of Education, University, and Research in concert with the Minister of Labor, Health, and Social Policies, in two national-level sessions.
Final exam execution mode
The student has 7 CFU dedicated to preparing the final exam and thesis. Exam sessions are scheduled in October/November and March/April, according to a calendar determined at the beginning of the academic year.
The structure of the final exam and thesis includes:
1. a practical test (applied value) consisting of a structured practical simulation related to the prevention and/or care and assistance of a clinical case, to demonstrate knowledge, skills, abilities, and operational competencies specific to the professional profile, or resolution of an online clinical case in case of health emergency, as in the case of the Covid-19 pandemic in 2021.
2. the preparation and discussion of a theoretical-applied (compilative) or entirely experiential report.
The student must have passed the practical test scheduled in the same session to discuss the thesis.
The student, after contacting the Supervisor Teacher to carry out the graduation internship, presents to the Curriculum Commission, chaired by the President and responsible for approval, the thesis title and topic and the name of the Supervisor Teacher.
The approved request is submitted to the student office within 12 months for the experimental thesis and 6 months for the compilative thesis.
The certification of acquired credits is issued by the Course Director and the Supervisor Teacher.
The role of a Co-Supervisor Teacher may be provided.
The Degree Examination Commission consists of at least 7 and no more than 11 members, appointed by the Rector on the proposal of the Study Course Council (CCS) and includes at least two members designated by the Professional College.
To be admitted to take the Degree Exam, the student must:
a. have passed all exams specified in the study plan;
b. have accumulated a total of 180 CFU distributed over the three years of study;
c. have completed and passed the annual clinical internship exams;
d. have submitted the graduation request to the student office addressed to the Magnificent Rector by August 31 for the autumn session and by December 15 for the extraordinary session;
e. have submitted a copy of the thesis on digital support.
The final degree grade, expressed in hundredths, is determined by the following parameters, summed:
a. the average in hundredths of the grades of the curricular exams;
b. points assigned by the Commission to the practical test:
from 18/30 to 20/30 = 1 point
from 21/30 to 23/30 = 2 points
from 24/30 to 26/30 = 3 points
from 27/30 to 29/30 = 4 points
30 and 30/30 with honors = 5 points
c. one point for participation in the Erasmus Project, with a stay of at least two months;
d. 0.1 point for honors in passing exams;
e. one point for students in progress;
f. honors may be awarded with unanimous Commission opinion to candidates who have achieved a final score of 111 or higher.
The Commission has a maximum score of 4 points available for evaluating the method, presentation, and discussion.
The degree is conferred upon successful completion of a final exam.
The methods and guarantees for conducting the exam are regulated by the University's Teaching Regulations.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITÀ DEGLI STUDI GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO – CHIETI/PESCARA

TYPE: COURSE

Admission Procedures Candidates may be admitted to the Bachelor's Degree Program in Orthoptics and Ophthalmic Assistance if they hold a High School Diploma or an equivalent foreign qualification. The number of admitted students is determined by the actual availability of teaching staff, suitable facilities and equipment, and services operating within the local structures of the National Health Service or in Regional structures contracted with the University. Access to the program is quota-based in accordance with Law 264/99 and requires an admission exam whose procedures will be specified annually in the University admission notice. Admission is conditional upon passing a multiple-choice test covering topics in Logic, General Culture, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, and Mathematics. The enrollment and registration deadlines are set by the academic calendar. Students admitted with a score below 30% of the total score in the following subjects are assigned Additional Educational Requirements (OFA) that must be completed within the first year of the program:
BIOLOGY (score equal to or not less than 18)
CHEMISTRY (score equal to or not less than 12)
PHYSICS AND MATHEMATICS (score equal to or not less than 8)
Completion of the OFA is achieved by passing the following Integrated Courses:
- BIOCHEMISTRY, APPLIED BIOLOGY AND BIOENGINEERING
- PHYSICS, INFORMATICS AND STATISTICS In case of non-completion, students may enroll in the second year but cannot take second-year exams until the assigned OFA are fulfilled.

Graduates must have the ability to integrate acquired knowledge, manage its more complex aspects, and formulate judgments. The following learning objectives must be achieved: Critical Thinking and Scientific Research

1) Be able to identify the main elements of the profession, including moral and ethical principles and legal responsibilities that form the basis of the profession.

The Erasmus Charter for Higher Education was awarded to the University by EACEA (Education, Audiovisual and Culture Executive Agency), headquartered in Brussels.
The new European Erasmus+ Programme, supporting education, training, youth and sport, has replaced the Lifelong Learning Programme and will be valid for seven years. It will further encourage international mobility of students, teachers and staff.
The objective of the new Programme is to promote mobility for over four million people who will benefit from European funding for study and training periods abroad between 2014 and 2020, nearly doubling the number of those who have already taken advantage of this opportunity.
The Erasmus Charter was awarded to the University of 'G. d'Annunzio' Chieti-Pescara based on the Erasmus Policy Statement, which was one of the necessary documents for obtaining the Erasmus University Charter (EUC). The EUC is a certificate issued by the European Commission granting universities the right to participate in the Erasmus programme, containing the fundamental principles of all activities related to the programme.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding (applying knowledge and understanding)
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding (applying knowledge and understanding):
Graduates must be able to apply acquired knowledge. They must have comprehension skills and the ability to solve problems on new and unfamiliar topics within an ophthalmological context. The following learning objectives must be achieved:

Clinical Skills
1) Correctly perform an accurate medical history
2) Be able to perform diagnostic procedures within their competence, analyze and interpret results, and implement appropriate therapeutic procedures within the scope of their profession.
3) Be able to exercise correct clinical judgment.

The methodologies and teaching tools used to develop the expected outcomes related to the ability to apply knowledge and understanding are:
- professional laboratories
- seminars
- optional teaching activities
- clinical case simulations
- practical exercises on patients within the designated contracted facilities for the professional internship

Assessment tools to verify the achievement of the expected outcomes:
- written and oral assessments
- practical assessments on clinical cases

Learning Skills (learning skills)
Graduates must have developed learning abilities to allow independent study. Additionally:
1) Know the methods for continuous updating in their professional field.
2) Acquire a study method and the ability to work towards goals both in groups and independently.
3) Apply developed learning methods to update and deepen studied content in professional contexts, in subsequent study paths within research.

Final exams and the final project constitute the tools for assessing learning abilities.

Knowledge and Understanding (knowledge and understanding)
Graduates must have demonstrated possession of knowledge and understanding of the subject to operate independently and in collaboration with the ophthalmologist.
The student must acquire the following learning objectives:
1) Know the normal structure and functionality of the organism as a complex of biological systems.
2) Know the basics of molecular, cellular, biochemical, and physiological mechanisms of the organism.
3) Know the main risk factors for health and disease.
4) Know the etiology and natural history of acute and chronic diseases of interest to ophthalmology.
5) Know the basics of drug action principles, their uses, and the efficacy of various pharmacological treatments, with particular reference to ophthalmological diseases.
6) Know the basics of labor law and legal medicine.
7) Have basic knowledge of the main surgical techniques of interest to ophthalmology.
8) Know the main aspects of general psychology and pedagogy.

Methodologies and training activities, teaching tools to develop expected outcomes:
- mandatory attendance frontal lectures
- seminars
- guided and independent personal study
- videos, image demonstrations, diagrams, and materials
- clinical case simulations within the orthotics laboratory under the tutor's guidance

Assessment tools to verify the achievement of expected outcomes:
- written and oral assessments.
- orthotics laboratory simulations with clinical case discussions.

The Orthotics and Ophthalmological Assistance Study Program has defined a general planning of main activities based on internal needs and deadlines set by current regulations. Generally, the Parity Commission and AQ Management Group meet in view of deadlines set by regulations.

The planning, annual or multi-year depending on the subject, follows the following scheme:

* Periodic evaluation of the Study Program's activities in various areas: infrastructure (classrooms and laboratories) and their improvement, student opinions on teaching activities, analysis of knowledge and skill results, occurs before each Course Council meeting and in AQ Group meetings held at least quarterly.

Brief course description. The Degree Program in Orthotics and Ophthalmological Assistance is structured over 3 years.
The orthotist-ophthalmological assistant, pursuant to Law 10 August 2000, No. 251, is the healthcare professional who individually or in a multidisciplinary team treats motor and sensory vision disorders; performs instrumental ophthalmological diagnostic techniques; carries out assistance activities in ophthalmological operating rooms, and is responsible for the rehabilitation of low vision. They are responsible for the organization, planning, and quality of professional acts carried out within their scope.
Graduates in Orthotics and Ophthalmological Assistance perform their professional activities in National and Regional Health Service structures; in private accredited and contracted structures with the SSN; in clinics-structures-centers for rehabilitation and low vision, in Nursing Homes; at patients' homes; in medical and/or multi-specialty clinics; in individual or associated professional offices; at associations and societies with assistance purposes; in public or private prevention services; in IRCCS.
Graduates in Orthotics and Ophthalmological Assistance are equipped with adequate preparation in basic disciplines (preparatory sciences, biomedical sciences, first aid), enabling them to best understand the most relevant elements underlying human anatomy, physiology, and pathology, as well as the main elements of psychology and pedagogy.
The Study Program determines the specific educational path for orthotists and ophthalmological assistants through the appropriate selection of disciplinary areas of characteristic training activities.
In particular, the identified areas are: Orthotics and Ophthalmological Assistance Sciences, Human Sciences and Psychopedagogy, Medical and Surgical Sciences, Preventive Health Services Sciences, Interdisciplinary and Clinical Sciences, Health Management, Interdisciplinary Sciences.
Professional competence is achieved through theoretical and practical training that also includes the acquisition of behavioral skills, completed within the specific work context of the profile, ensuring full mastery of all necessary competencies and their immediate applicability in the workplace. Particular importance, as an integral and qualifying part of professional training, is given to practical training and clinical internship activities, conducted under the supervision and guidance of assigned professional tutors, coordinated by a faculty member belonging to the highest educational level specified by the professional profile and corresponding to European standards where applicable.

External effectiveness. Regarding employment effectiveness, the employment rate of graduates in the calendar year 2022 is 100%, increasing from the previous year.
18.2% of graduates are currently enrolled in a Master's Degree.
Of employed graduates, 80% states they extensively use the skills acquired with the degree and are highly satisfied with the work performed, rated 9 out of 10.
The net salary is 1,126 euros monthly.
These results will be discussed in the next CDS Council.

Specific course learning objectives and description of the educational path. At the end of the Orthotics and Ophthalmological Assistance Degree Program, the following specific learning objectives must be achieved:
learn the fundamental elements of general anatomy and in particular the visual apparatus, learn the principles of general physiology and in particular visual function, know the pathophysiological optics and correction of refractive errors including contact lens principles; classification, diagnosis, and therapy of concomitant and paralytic strabismus, strabismus surgical techniques; classification, diagnosis, and therapy of amblyopia.
Graduates in orthotics and ophthalmological assistance must know all ocular diseases related to the anterior segment, lens, ocular hydrodynamics, and retina, and know how to perform all instrumental ophthalmological diagnostic techniques related to them (perimetry, corneal topography, fluorangiography, electrophysiology, OCT, etc.). Additionally, knowledge of legislation regarding low vision and instrumental rehabilitation techniques used in visual disability rehabilitation is required.
Graduates must be able to assist the ophthalmologist in the operating room during cornea, lens, glaucoma, and retina surgery.
Orthotists and ophthalmological assistants must also acquire knowledge in physics, medical informatics and statistics, ocular pharmacology, hygiene, genetics, endocrinology, internal medicine, general surgery, neurology, legal medicine, and labor law.
At the end of the educational path, graduates in Orthotics and Ophthalmological Assistance will have acquired a wide range of knowledge in basic, characteristic, and related sciences.

A) Within the scope of basic sciences:
1) preparatory: knowledge of the fundamental principles of physics, informatics, statistics, and pedagogy;
2) biomedical: understanding of biological phenomena of the human body; knowledge of molecular, cellular, and biochemical mechanisms of the organism, knowledge of human anatomy and histology with particular reference to the visual apparatus, physiological phenomena of the human body and the eye; elements of general psychology and basic genetics with particular attention to main genetic eye diseases;
3) first aid: knowledge of main internal medical conditions of interest to ophthalmology (diabetes, hypertension, coagulopathies), knowledge of indications and surgical techniques.

B) Within the scope of characteristic sciences:
1) Orthotics and Ophthalmological Assistance Sciences: knowledge of pathophysiological optics and correction of refractive errors including contact lens principles; classification, diagnosis, and therapy of concomitant and paralytic strabismus, strabismus surgical techniques; classification, diagnosis, and therapy of amblyopia; ocular diseases related to the anterior segment, lens, ocular hydrodynamics, and retina; knowledge of instrumental ophthalmological diagnostic techniques related to ocular diseases (perimetry, corneal topography, fluorangiography, electrophysiology, OCT, etc.); knowledge of legislation regarding low vision and instrumental rehabilitation techniques used in visual disability rehabilitation; guidelines for assisting ophthalmological surgery in the surgery of the cornea, lens, glaucoma, retina, and strabismus.
2) Human Sciences and Psychopedagogy: knowledge of psychological elements;
3) Medical and Surgical Sciences: knowledge of pharmacology elements and in particular drug action, their uses, and efficacy of various pharmacological treatments, with particular reference to ophthalmological diseases;
4) Preventive Health Services Sciences: knowledge of health issues of individuals and/or communities and responses of health and social services to citizens' main needs; knowledge of general radioprotection principles, knowledge of legal medicine principles;
5) Interdisciplinary and Clinical Sciences: knowledge of main endocrine disorders associated with ocular diseases; knowledge of neurological and neuromuscular diseases with particular focus on neurological disorders of visual pathways;
6) Health Management: knowledge of labor law elements;
7) Interdisciplinary Sciences: knowledge of electronic and computer bioengineering elements with in-depth understanding of the functioning mechanisms of biomedical devices.

C) Within the scope of related sciences:
1) Related or integrated training activities: medical genetics deepening.

Consultation with representative organizations - at national and international levels - of goods and service production, and professions (Course establishment)
Summary of consultation with local representative organizations of production, services, and professions. The Guidance Committee was established in November 2017 and consists of the regional AIORAO representative Dr. Angela Telesca, Professor Antonio Mocellin as a member of the Italian Ophthalmology Society's Executive Council, and the CDS President Professor L. Mastropasqua, the CDS reference faculty Professors P. Carpineto, L. Toto, M. Nubile, to evaluate the study program's progress.
On 12/11/2018, the Guidance Committee reconvened to propose changes to the curriculum for the 2019/2020 academic year to improve graduate training and their integration into the workforce. The CDS Council discussed the committee's proposals and proceeded with the curriculum modification. Consequently, within the disciplinary area of Orthotics and Ophthalmological Assistance Sciences, the SSD MED/30 specific to ophthalmology was activated, and the SSD MED/48 specific to nursing sciences was removed. Within the disciplinary area, the SSD MED/50 specific to Orthotics graduates remained active.
The activation of the specific ophthalmology SSD MED/30 became necessary as graduates in orthotics and ophthalmological assistance increasingly play an important role in performing instrumental ophthalmological diagnostics, and the ophthalmologist represents the most competent professional for student training. Therefore, within the SSD MED/30, the number of CFU assigned to modules regarding all aspects of low vision, which is a growing social emergency, was increased, considering that orthotics and ophthalmological assistance graduates can also find employment in low vision rehabilitation centers. Additionally, the Ophthalmology Clinic, a regional excellence center directed by Professor Mastropasqua, recognized under Regional Law No. 4 of February 4, 2013, as a Regional High Specialization Center for Preventing Blindness and Visual Rehabilitation.
Additionally, within the Human Sciences and Psychopedagogy disciplinary area, the SSD MPSI/08 CLINICAL PSYCHOLOGY and SSD MPSI/03 PSYCHOMETRY were removed, and within the Preventive Health Services Sciences disciplinary area, the SSD MED/44 OCCUPATIONAL MEDICINE was removed as both were considered overly specific and not useful for graduate preparation. For the same reason, within Preparatory Sciences, the SPS/08 SOCIOLOGY OF CULTURAL AND COMMUNICATION PROCESSES was removed, and within Health Management, SECS-P/10 BUSINESS ORGANIZATION was removed.
Finally, within the Interdisciplinary and Clinical Sciences disciplinary area, the SSD MED/39 CHILD PSYCHIATRY was removed both because it was too specific and because the university does not have faculty in that field.
The curriculum modification was approved by the CDS Council on 21/11/2018 and will be presented to the Medicine and Aging Sciences Department Council on 28/11/2018.
