"Aree di apprendimento del CdS: SCIENZE PROPEDEUTICHE DI BASE, BIOMEDICHE E PSICOLOGICHE: per la comprensione dei fenomeni di comunicazione verbale e non verbale, nonché dei meccanisci biologici e di funzionamento degli organi ed apparati, dello sviluppo cognitivo e psicomotorio, dei fenomeni fisiologici anche in correlazione con le dimensioni psicologiche, sociali ed ambientali della malattia." → "Learning areas of the Course: PREPARATORY, BASIC, BIOMEDICAL, AND PSYCHOLOGICAL SCIENCES: for understanding verbal and non-verbal communication phenomena, as well as biological mechanisms and functioning of organs and systems, cognitive and psychomotor development, physiological phenomena also in correlation with the psychological, social, and environmental dimensions of disease."

"SCIENZE DELLA LOGOPEDIA: necessarie ad individuare i bisogni preventivi e riabilitativi del soggetto tramite la valutazione dei dati clinici in campo cognitivo e funzionale per entità e significatività dei sintomi; comprendere i costituenti che sono alla base dei processi patologici sui quali si focalizza l'intervento riabilitativo terapeutico in età evolutiva, adulta e geriatrica. Progettare e verificare l'intervento logopedico utilizzando modalità valutative oggettive, come i test e terapeutiche efficaci e tutti gli strumenti opportuni per la risoluzione del caso." → "LOGOPEDICS SCIENCES: necessary to identify preventive and rehabilitative needs of the subject through the evaluation of clinical data in cognitive and functional fields for the extent and significance of symptoms; understand the components underlying pathological processes focused on by therapeutic rehabilitation interventions in developmental, adult, and geriatric age. Design and verify the logopedic intervention using objective evaluation methods, such as effective tests and therapies, and all appropriate tools for case resolution."

"SCIENZE INTERDISCIPLINARI E MEDICO CHIRURGICHE: per la comprensione degli elementi fisio-patologici applicabili alle diverse situazioni cliniche, anche in relazione a parametri dignostici." → "INTERDISCIPLINARY AND MEDICAL-SURGICAL SCIENCES: for understanding the physiological-pathological elements applicable to various clinical situations, also in relation to diagnostic parameters."

"SCIENZE STATISTICHE: dei metodi quantitativi e dell'aggiornamento scientifico per lo sviluppo della conoscenza degli strumenti statistici utili alla pianificazione del processo di ricerca, di alcuni metodi analitici da scegliere ed utilizzare nell'esercizio della professione, utilizzando le migliori evidenze scientifiche in campo logopedico." → "STATISTICAL SCIENCES: of quantitative methods and scientific updates for developing knowledge of statistical tools useful for planning the research process, some analytical methods to choose and use in professional practice, using the best scientific evidence in the field of logopedics."

"MANAGEMENT: comprende tutti gli strumenti gestionali (risorse, informazioni, aspetti economici) indispensabili per la corretta attuazione dell'agire quotidiano del Logopedista attraverso le seguenti azioni: identificare la natura del problema, analizzare, scegliere, interpretare e individuare la risoluzione del problema ricorrendo ad eventuali collaborazioni. Nella gestione del proprio lavoro saper riconoscere e rispettare ruoli e competenze, interagire e collaborare con equipe multiprofessionali, utilizzare Linee Generali e protocolli per uniformare le modalità operative. In managing one's work, know how to recognize and respect roles and competencies, interact and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, use General Guidelines and protocols to standardize operational methods. In managing clinical risk, identify and report difficulties. Know how to use information and computer systems to analyze data."

"Nella formulazione del Progetto la priorità è rappresentata dallo studio teorico/pratico delle Scienze Logopediche, che si attua sia tramite lezioni frontali, esercitazioni che tirocinio professionalizzante nei settori qualificanti la Logopedia, come la riabilitazione nell'ambito odontoiatrico e della posizione linguale nella sindrome delle apnee ostruttive del sonno. La competenza e la capacità relazionale necessarie ad interagire con il paziente, i caregivers e il sistema professionale viene sviluppata tramite gli insegnamenti delle scienze umane e psicopedagogiche finalizzate all'acquisizione di quei comportamenti e atteggiamenti necessari e fondamentali per relazionarsi con il paziente/cliente." → "In the formulation of the Project, priority is given to the theoretical/practical study of Logopedics Sciences, which is implemented through frontal lessons, exercises, and professional internship in sectors qualifying Logopedics, such as rehabilitation in the dental area and linguistic positioning in obstructive sleep apnea syndrome. The competence and relational ability necessary to interact with the patient, caregivers, and the professional system is developed through the teachings of human sciences and psychopedagogy aimed at acquiring those behaviors and attitudes necessary and fundamental for relating to the patient/client."

"Gli insegnamenti sono articolati in moduli e sono svolti con lezioni frontali, esercitazioni in aula. I risultati di apprendimento sono valutati con eventuali prove in itinere, con valore anche di autovalutazione per lo studente, e con una prova conclusiva orale o scritta, occasione per la verifica del raggiungimento degli obiettivi preposti, unica e contestuale per ogni insegnamento, necessaria per l'acquisizione di crediti formativi. I risultati di apprendimento degli insegnamenti di laboratorio, di inglese e del tirocinio del 1° anno, danno luogo ad una idoneità." → "Teaching is structured into modules and is carried out with frontal lessons and classroom exercises. Learning outcomes are assessed through possible in-course tests, also serving as self-assessment for the student, and with a final oral or written exam, an opportunity to verify the achievement of the set objectives, unique and simultaneous for each course, necessary for acquiring credit points. Learning outcomes of laboratory, English, and first-year internship courses result in a pass."

"Per quanto concerne le attività professionalizzanti e di tirocinio il riferimento è il Manuale del tirocinio v.2009 e succ. mod e integr. disponibile presso il Corso di Laurea. Lo studente ha disponibilità di 5 crediti per la preparazione della prova finale del Corso presso strutture deputate alla formazione; tale attività viene definita 'internato di laurea' e può essere svolta anche in strutture non universitarie, quali quelle ospedaliere o private di ricerca, previa autorizzazione del Comitato per la Didattica e relativa stipula di convenzione per stage." → "Regarding professionalizing activities and internship, the reference is the Internship Manual v.2009 and subsequent modifications and integrations available at the Bachelor's Degree Course. The student has 5 credits available for preparing the final exam at training facilities; this activity is defined as 'graduation internship' and can be carried out in non-university structures, such as hospital or private research facilities, with prior authorization from the Teaching Committee and the signing of a stage convention."

"I laureati nella classe, ai sensi dell'articolo 6, comma 3, del decreto legislativo 30 dicembre 1992, n. 502 e successive modificazioni ed integrazioni, ai sensi della legge 26 febbraio 1999, n. 42, e ai sensi della legge 10 agosto 2000, n. 251, sono professionisti sanitari il cui campo proprio di attività e responsabilità è determinato dai contenuti dei decreti ministeriali istitutivi dei profili professionali e degli ordinamenti didattici dei rispettivi corsi universitari e di formazione post-base nonché degli specifici codici deontologici. Department DEPARTMENT OF MODERN LANGUAGES, LITERATURES AND CULTURES Website https://www.lingue.unich.it/didattica  Admission requirements Required knowledge for admission Students with a five-year secondary school diploma or other equivalent foreign qualification recognized according to current regulations are admitted to the L11 Course. Admission to the Study Course is regulated by an assessment of knowledge and skills through a verification test. The methods for verifying such knowledge and skills will be determined in the Study Course's Didactic Regulations. In case of negative verification results, additional educational obligations must be fulfilled during the first year of the course through specific recovery activities established in the Didactic Regulations. Admission methods All students holding a five-year secondary school diploma or an equivalent recognized qualification are admitted to the Course. At enrollment, students must indicate the chosen study languages as LANGUAGE A and LANGUAGE B (one of which must be European) from those listed in the Educational Offer. The three-year language (both Language A and B) can only be changed at the time of enrollment for the second year. The Ministry of Education, University and Research (Article 6 of D.M. 270/2004) requires all universities to verify the initial preparation of new students, to enable freshmen to assess their personal preparation against the basic knowledge required for university study, and to identify, with the assistance of Tutor teachers, individual paths to address any initial gaps, thereby facilitating the student's successful integration into the chosen study program. The ministerial provision also clarifies that any additional educational obligations must be fulfilled in the first year of the course. For the L11 Course, the verification test of required knowledge for admission is mandatory for first-year students. Students transferring from other universities and students enrolling for a second degree are exempt from the test. The verification test is held according to a schedule indicated on the Department of Modern Languages, Literature and Cultures website. Two sessions are scheduled: September and February. The Commission responsible for the test is appointed by the Department Director. This Commission consists of a minimum of three to a maximum of five permanent teachers. The 60-minute verification test consists of 30 multiple-choice questions designed to assess an adequate level of text comprehension, knowledge of morphosyntactic structures and vocabulary in Italian. Each correct answer is awarded a score of 1 (one), while each unanswered or incorrect answer receives a score of 0 (zero). The test is passed if the student achieves a score of at least 20/30. For students who take and pass the test, the Additional Educational Obligations are considered fulfilled. A negative test result instead results in the assignment of an Additional Educational Obligation (OFA) to be fulfilled during the first year by attending a mandatory 24-hour Italian language course offered by the Department. At the end of the recovery procedures, the student must retake the test to verify the required competence levels. The debt must be fulfilled within the first year of the course. If the debt is not fulfilled, the verification test must be retaken in the following academic year. As per the University's Didactic Regulations, students who have not fulfilled the OFA by October 31 of the year following enrollment cannot enroll in second-year courses, unless they have acquired at least eighteen CFU in the first-year basic and characteristic courses. In addition to the verification test of required knowledge for admission, a Placement Test is also administered to assess the level of linguistic competence in one of the following languages: French, English, Spanish or German. This second test is used to optimize the organization of courses and does not entail Additional Educational Obligations.

Syllabus, texts and objectives Note regarding credits for other activities The level of linguistic competence of students is verified through in-course assessments and curriculum examinations; students who have not acquired these skills are not admitted to the final examination.
Communication skills
Graduates of the Study Program L11 must be able to argue and communicate ideas, problems and solutions effectively in the foreign languages studied, as well as in Italian.
In particular, they must possess:
- the ability to present orally and in writing, considering textual types and literary and specialist genres, content, information and ideas related to their field of study, using appropriate communication forms depending on the interlocutors;
- the ability to interact in multilingual and multicultural contexts by selecting specific communication registers;
- the ability to process and present data using basic computer and multimedia tools.
In addition to the specific linguistic training and support activities provided by native speaker lecturers and CEL (University Language Center) staff at the University Language Center, the acquisition of the above communication skills is provided in different forms within various training activities, through direct engagement with multilingual and multicultural contexts thanks to the extensive international exchange program offerings.
These skills are verified through examinations that include comprehension of texts, preparation of written reports and documents, and oral presentation of the same.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITY OF CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [0658] LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES
TYPE: COURSE
CURRICULUM: CURRICULUM
SECTION: Judgment Autonomy
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/2

Judgment Autonomy
Graduates of the L11 Study Course must develop autonomous judgment capabilities regarding the specific themes of their field of study. In particular, they must have acquired:
- Ability to describe and interpret, based on the four linguistic skills, literary, journalistic and specialist texts;
- Ability to deepen the socio-cultural actuality of the historical-geographical and cultural contexts related to the studied languages, also from the perspective of interculturalism;
- Ability to identify and analytically rephrase the issues related to the socio-cultural contexts investigated and to propose autonomous solutions;
- Ability to address different work areas and themes, as well as to locate and evaluate information sources and data in the linguistic, philological-literary and artistic-historical-cultural fields.
To achieve this autonomy, in addition to frontal lessons and seminars, teaching tools include debate and exercises, support from laboratories and multimedia tools, attendance at professionalizing seminars, and experience through internships and traineeships.
The assessment of acquired judgment autonomy will be carried out through oral and/or written checks, during the course and at the end of each disciplinary course, as well as through the preparation of the final exam.

Orientation in Entry The activities of the Orientation in Entry for the Course of Study are organically integrated into the broader framework of those organized by the University (https://orientamento.unich.it/futuri-studenti) and by the Department of Modern Languages, Literatures and Cultures (https://www.lingue.unich.it/orientamento).
Coordinated by the Head of the Department and the Chairs of the four Courses of Study within it, these activities take place throughout the Academic Year and consist of various information and promotion initiatives regarding the educational offer, both at the Department's premises and, upon request, at secondary schools.
These activities are organized by the Department's Orientation Delegate (Prof. Enzo Fimiani) and the Department's Teaching Tutor (Dr. Lorena Savini), who rely on the collaboration of the Chairs of the four Courses of Study and various Department teachers.
The Teaching Tutor also benefits from the support of student-tutors (selected students from the Department, winners of the selection call for tutoring) and doctoral candidates, following specific training.
In July, September and October, meetings are held to provide practical information on logistics, functioning, organization of the Department, presentation of the educational offer and other training activities, to facilitate enrollment and student integration into the university environment.
Throughout the year, secondary schools from Abruzzo and/or neighboring regions, particularly Molise and Puglia, are also welcomed upon request, as well as meetings to present the educational offer to local schools.
During school meetings held at the Department, among the Orientation in Entry activities, there is the possibility to attend lectures and other training activities.
On April 4, 2024, an orientation day (Open Day) was held at the Pescara teaching campus. In addition to the overall presentation of the educational offer, short lectures were offered for each language within the Course of Study to illustrate the specific features of each language and the different teaching methods.
The dates of the meetings are published on the Department's website.
The Department's orientation activities complement those organized by the University's Orientation, Tutoring, Placement, Student Rights and Disability Office, which are listed on the website https://www.unich.it/orientamento.

SECTION: Mandatory training periods
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/2

Mandatory training periods Courses, internships or traineeships are mandatory and scheduled in the third year of the Study Program.
For internship or traineeship, it refers to a period of training and work orientation at an institution or company that has established a convention with the Department of Languages, Literatures and Modern Cultures, activated with the aim of connecting school and work.
Students may also identify companies or other organizations known to them or of interest, willing to host them, provided a convention is established with the Department or the Study Program.
This service allows students to gain their first contact with the world of work and to carry out activities at public and/or private entities, which may eventually serve as the topic for the final thesis.
The duration of an internship is calculated based on the CFU to be acquired as specified in the student's study plan. These CFU are automatically inserted into the student's academic record.
The organization and coordination of internships and traineeships are entrusted to the Department Teaching Tutor, Dr. Lorena Savini, who also manages the evaluation of interns and trainees by host entities.
The list of public and private entities with which conventions for conducting internships and traineeships are in place is available at the external link indicated in this section.
For students with disabilities, the Teaching Tutor is responsible for organizing internships at external entities and organizations (preparing the entity for welcoming the student, planning essential support to ensure autonomy during the internship or traineeship activity, etc.).
All students have the opportunity to experience an internationally paid work experience. The Erasmus for Traineeships Call provides an economic contribution to carry out an internship abroad for a duration ranging from 2 to 12 months.
The Traineeship can be curricular or extracurricular and can also occur post-graduation.
All information is available at the following link:
https://www.unich.it/didattica/international/mobilita/traineeship/bando-traineeship-2324
For further information:

Professional seminars The Study Course provides a series of professional seminars organized within the broader offer of the Department, aimed at acquiring skills and competencies that facilitate graduates' entry into the job market. Attendance is open to students of all years. Attendance is recorded by signing at the end of each session.
Professional seminars can be attended from the first year of the course, and the CFU acquired at each session, if insufficient to meet the requirement of the student's curriculum, may be supplemented by other qualifications held by the student (other courses, language certifications, ECDL). Students may request CFU recognition no earlier than after enrolling in the third year of the course, and the CFU will be automatically added to the student's academic record.
2. E-learning In case of necessity, and in accordance with the Ministry and University regulations, the Study Course is able to deliver courses, examinations, and graduation sessions remotely through a dedicated digital platform.

Student Opinions The L-11 Study Course provides an online pre-exam questionnaire to collect student opinions, managed by the University offices. The questionnaire covers the overall organization of the Study Course, individual courses, didactic activities and study, interest and satisfaction.
Each individual instructor has access, through a restricted area, to the evaluation results of students regarding their own courses, while the Course Director has access to all evaluations. Some aspects of the evaluations are periodically discussed in the Course Council to highlight positive aspects, critical elements, and potential improvement actions.
Data Analysis Regarding the evaluation of didactic activities by students, collected through pre-exam questionnaires, the average score of the L11 Course for the 2022-23 academic year is in line with the University average but slightly below the Humanities Area average.
More analytically, the scores for the 3 macro-areas are as follows:
Didactic effectiveness: Course 3.52; Area 3.60; University average 3.48;
Logistical and organizational aspects: Course 3.51; Area 3.58; University average 3.35;
Overall satisfaction: Course 3.37; Area 3.42; University average 3.35.
In the latest survey, the main critical factor remains the inadequacy of preliminary knowledge for understanding the topics covered in the courses (Course average 3.31, the worst score in the entire table).
As strengths, the consistency between information provided on the Department website and the actual delivery of didactic activities (D13, Course 3.57), respect for office hours and class schedules (D14, Course 3.61), and instructor availability to provide clarifications during lessons or during office hours (D22, Course 3.66) are noted.
Among improvement actions, the Department of Languages and the four affiliated Courses are preparing a call for student tutors, aiming to promote, through the introduction of these figures already successfully used in the previous academic year, the acquisition of information, knowledge of departmental structures, and interaction with the teaching organization.
Finally, it is noted that the PQA has established a centralized complaint management system at the University level, accessible at:
https://www.unich.it/parla-con-noi The data regarding student opinions were discussed in a dedicated point of the Course on October 12, 2023.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITY OF GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO CHIETI/PESCARA

Graduate Opinions The information regarding 2022 graduates of the L11 Degree Course in Foreign Languages and Literatures is based on the annual AlmaLaurea report (see attached PDF).
In the calendar year 2022, the number of graduates increased (113) compared to 2021 (88). Strengths and weaknesses already noted in previous comments remain: the percentage of graduates enrolled in a master's degree program remains significantly higher than the national average (81 percent); overall satisfaction with the degree course is also positive (38.5% of graduates report being highly satisfied, while 52.3% rate it positively overall); 55% of respondents would enroll in the same CDS again, while 22% would choose the same course but at a different university.
The employment rate one year after graduation rises to 41.7%, the average net monthly salary is 976 euros, and satisfaction with the work performed is rated at 6.8.
Overall, a mixed picture emerges, marked by growth factors (employment rates, salaries) alongside signals of dissatisfaction, already recorded in previous surveys, primarily related to teaching equipment and computer workstations.
To facilitate career progression, having tested its effectiveness during the pandemic emergency period, the Department of Languages and the four affiliated CDSs plan to permanently include an additional graduation session beyond those already scheduled.
Graduate opinions are discussed in the first autumn CDS meeting (see October 12, 2023), which includes a specific point on the agenda.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding
Graduates in Foreign Languages and Literatures are able to consciously apply theoretical and metalinguistic knowledge of at least two foreign languages, relating them to their socio-cultural contexts and identifying strategies and solutions for different communication situations. They are able to communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in a foreign language (as well as in Italian) in written and oral form to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, interfacing and interacting in multilingual and multicultural contexts. They are also able to apply their knowledge to both literary-cultural and philological-linguistic analysis of documents, also from a glottodidactic perspective. Additionally, they can apply their literary, philological, and linguistic competencies to conduct bibliographic research, compile indexes, draft reports on specific topics, and collaborate in project development.
These abilities to apply knowledge and understanding are developed through theoretical-descriptive lectures, seminar activities, debate and exercise tools, supported by laboratories and multimedia tools, through exchanges with native speakers of the studied languages, conducted both in collaboration with the Language Center's CEL/Readers and through international agreements (Erasmus, university agreements, etc.), as well as through internship and traineeship experiences.

Learning Skills
Graduates of the L11 CDS acquire appropriate learning skills and methodologies to pursue further studies on a solid foundation.
In particular, they must:
- Have acquired study methods, analytical and synthetic skills, and goal-oriented work abilities through individual and group study;
- Have acquired and developed linguistic skills suitable for continuing studies in specific disciplinary fields.
Learning skills are achieved through lectures, debates, and in-class exercises, as well as through ongoing tutoring activities.
Learning skills are assessed through written and/or oral verification methods provided by the training activities and during the preparation of the final thesis.

Knowledge and Understanding
Graduates in Foreign Languages and Literatures must demonstrate specific linguistic-communicative knowledge, aimed at deepening the study of foreign languages, along with solid written and oral knowledge of at least two foreign languages, one of which is European, in addition to Italian. They must also demonstrate in-depth knowledge of the cultural contexts (literary, historical, geographical, artistic, audiovisual-multimedia) of the studied foreign languages, enabling them to identify connections and interactions with those of their own country. They must also know and be able to use the main methodologies for analyzing and interpreting literary texts, even through philological tools.
Knowledge and understanding are verified not only through standard assessments at the end of each disciplinary course but also through in-course assessments. Acquired knowledge and understanding are applied during the preparation of the final thesis, which aims to develop research, collection, organization, and synthesis autonomy.

Organizational Structure and Responsibilities at the University Level The organization and management of the quality of the Degree Course in Foreign Languages and Literatures is handled at the university level by the Academic Senate, the Rector, the University Quality Assurance Office (PQA), the Rector's Delegate for University Quality, the Parity Commission of Teachers-Students, and the Director of the Department of Languages, Literatures, and Modern Cultures, each contributing according to their respective competencies and responsibilities as detailed on the web page below.
Organizational Structure and Responsibilities for Quality Assurance at the CDS Level The bodies involved in the Quality Assurance process of the Degree Course (AQ) are as follows:
- The President of the CDS, Prof. Paola Partenza, who performs the following tasks: coordination of the CDS AQ system, maintaining direct relations with the University Quality Assurance Office, the Evaluation Committee, and the Parity Commission of Teachers-Students, monitoring compliance with requirements set by specific regulations;
- The Vice President of the CDS assists the President and acts on their behalf when necessary;
- The Parity Commission of the School of Humanities, represented in the CDS by Prof. Barbara Delli Castelli, which monitors the training offer, teaching quality, and services provided to students by teachers and structures;
- The Departmental AQ Representative (ReAQD), Prof. Michele Sisto;
- The CDS Erasmus Delegate: Prof. Miriam Sette;
- The CDS Council, which discusses and approves the Review Report and collaborates in the smooth operation of the CDS AQ;
- The Responsible for the Quality Assurance Group (GAQ) of the CDS, composed of Prof. Paola Partenza (Responsible) and teachers: Proff. Anita Trivelli (PO), Federica D'Ascenzo (PA), Giovanna Moracci (PA), Michele Sisto (PA), Francesca Guazzelli (PA), Leonardo Coppola (RTDB).
The AQ Group evaluates the quality of the CDS in various areas: available infrastructure (classrooms, laboratories) and their improvement, student opinions on teaching delivery, analysis of results from knowledge and skills assessments. The Group prepares the Review Report and monitors the CDS AQ progress, highlighting strengths and improvement opportunities; conducting monitoring of indicators for continuous process control and improvement; promoting a quality culture within the CDS; planning and controlling the efficiency of contextual services. The AQ Group also conducts monitoring and self-assessment activities of the educational path to identify strengths and weaknesses for reporting within the CDS. These activities are directed at designing corrective and preventive actions for identified weaknesses and implementing improvement plans to be proposed to the CDS Council.

Work Planning and Implementation Deadlines To ensure the management of the organization aimed at improving alignment with its objectives over time, the Degree Course in Foreign Languages and Literatures has defined a general planning of the main activities based on internal needs and deadlines set by current regulations.
This includes periodic meetings of the Parity Commission, the AQ Commission, and the CDS Council. In particular, the Parity Commission and the AQ Commission meet before the deadlines set by current regulations and present their reports to the management bodies before the deadlines. Additionally, the CDS Quality Manager coordinates with the Department's teaching staff to monitor the smooth operation of CDS activities, ensuring that work is conducted as planned.

The annual or multi-year planning responds to the following scheme.
1. Annually, the CDS reviews or revises the educational objectives, proposing updates in time for inclusion in the SUA-CdS (February-March).
2. Similarly, the CDS reconsiders the validity of the educational path annually, respecting the necessary timing for inclusion of any updates in the SUA-CdS (January-February).
3. The CDS proposes to the Department Council the teaching coverage for the following year, indicating any shortages or issues in the delivery of standard teaching (January-February).
4. Analysis of data from student, graduate, and alumni opinion surveys is conducted during the summer (July-September).
5. The investigation into training demand, through meetings with social partners, entities, and companies involved in producing goods and services, occurs at least twice a year (February-March and September-October).
6. Periodic evaluation of the CDS activities in various areas (infrastructure and improvement, student opinions on teaching, analysis of knowledge and skills results) occurs before each CDS Council meeting, during meetings with other CDS Presidents of the Department of Languages, and during AQ meetings, which are held at least quarterly.
7. Annual evaluation of the results of corrective and improvement interventions occurs between November and December.
8. Redefinition of educational objectives (in relation to consultations with social partners) is typically carried out every three years, and in any case in time for inclusion in the SUA-CdS.

Annual Review The 2015 Review Report (RAR) stems from a detailed analysis of the topics covered in the report, conducted by the Review Group.
The 2015 RAR, presented, discussed, and approved at the CDS Council meeting on January 20, 2016, highlighted the key characteristics of the L11 CDS both in terms of the training offer and the outcomes achieved.
In particular, the positive response to the increase in enrollments in the L11 CDS was noted, confirming its strategic importance within the Chieti-Pescara University for the three-year courses affiliated with the Department of Languages, Literatures, and Modern Cultures.
Corrective actions were also identified to strengthen strengths and address existing weaknesses. These actions, suggested through a fruitful dialogue with students and their representatives, aim to improve space utilization, technological equipment, and the logistical organization of teaching activities, in view of better professionalizing students to meet the demands of the job market.

Synthetic Description of Related and Integrative Activities The L11 CDS allocates 18 CFU to Related or Integrative Training Activities, distributed within the Study Plan in the second and third years.
The following list of courses provides a synthetic description of the activities included in the Related or Integrative category, indicating how these activities contribute to the specific educational objectives of the Course.

PHILOSOPHY OF LANGUAGE (M-FIL/05): This course aims to acquire competencies on content and research methods in the scientific and didactic area linking philosophical studies to language, communication, mind, and the social environment. This discipline seeks to stimulate the application of these competencies in the study of languages and in the methodologies of interpretation and translation.

GEOGRAPHY (M-GGR/01): The course aims to provide interpretative foundations for analyzing major phenomena of human activity on territory. In particular, it highlights systemic correlations of environmental, economic, political, cultural, and social factors that frame the construction of linguistic and cultural identities.

GLOTTOLINGUISTICS (L-LIN/01): This course provides students with tools and methods of historical linguistics to address, through interlinguistic comparison, the reconstruction of the Proto-Indo-European language. Students will learn concepts of linguistic family and linguistic type, and the principles underlying the genealogical, typological, and areal classification of languages.

MODERN AND CONTEMPORARY ITALIAN LITERATURE (L-FIL-LET/11): In line with the educational objectives of the Degree Course, this course aims to provide students with adequate knowledge of methodologies for analyzing literary discourse, as well as the connections and relationships between European and extra-European critical-literary traditions. The course also deepens the history of literary aesthetics and ideas in modernity, with particular reference to methods and concepts of historical-literary criticism combined with the competencies and perspectives of militant criticism.

ITALIAN THEATRE LITERATURE (FIL-LET/10): This course aims to provide students with a deeper understanding of movements and issues in Italian theatrical literature, based on the ability to analyze texts in relation to dialogue and stage directions. The discipline seeks to deepen the relationship between the dramatic text and its staging, with particular attention to extratextual elements, potential didactic implications, and pedagogical uses.

INTERNATIONAL CINEMA MOVEMENTS AND AUTHORS (L-ART/06): This course contributes to achieving the educational objectives of the Degree Course by introducing students to key concepts of audiovisual language through the exploration of significant practices in international film production. The course aims to enable students to understand the general lines of International New Cinema, common elements among the examined film movements, and specific features of the proposed films, in light of the most advanced critical and theoretical reflections on cinema and audiovisual media. The acquired competencies can be productively applied in students' participation in the Venice and Pesaro International Film Festivals, valuable opportunities to meet scholars, experts, directors, and actors.

HISTORY OF COMMUNICATION (M-STO/04): This course is proposed in line with the interdisciplinary educational goals of the Degree Course, ensuring knowledge of the broader historical context for studying foreign languages and literatures, with particular attention to one of the main aspects of contemporary history, where communication processes and circuits at all levels represent an indispensable characteristic.

Brief Course Description The Degree Course in Foreign Languages and Literatures has a traditionally humanistic character: both languages and literatures represent central and defining aspects of culture understood broadly, expressing the history, territory, and artistic and social manifestations of a specific nation.
The Degree Course aims to train graduates with solid foundational training in linguistics and Italian language and literature; mastery of at least two foreign languages in written and oral form, as well as the literary and cultural heritage of the civilization they represent; ability to use the main communication tools in their specific areas of competence.
To provide this training, the Degree Course includes not only linguistic, literary, philological, glottodidactic, historical, and artistic courses, but also linguistic-training activities aimed at acquiring the fundamental knowledge necessary for written and oral interlinguistic mediation in the languages studied alongside their respective cultures and literatures.
The foreign languages and literatures offered in the Degree Course are Arabic, Chinese, French, English and Anglo-American, Portuguese and Brazilian, Russian, Serbian and Croatian, Spanish, German.
The Degree Course prepares students for editorial and cultural professions in general, as well as for teaching.

External Effectiveness The Chieti-Pescara University documents on the Quality Assurance Office website the entry statistics of graduates into the job market one year after graduation and their employment status. Information regarding 2021 graduates of the L11 Degree Course in Foreign Languages and Literatures, based on the AlmaLaurea survey, is accessible from the University Quality Assurance Office website.
As this is a first-level degree, it is important to note that one year after graduation, the percentage of graduates enrolled in a master's degree program remains consistently above 80%.
One year after graduation, 41.7% of graduates have found their first employment. The average net monthly salary is 976 euros. Both figures are significantly higher than the previous year's estimates. Satisfaction with the work performed, however, has decreased (6.8/10).
For comparison, the following data from the previous survey regarding 2019 graduates one year after graduation are provided. The sample consists of 61 respondents out of 96 graduates. Employment rate 13%; Graduates currently enrolled in a master's program 78.7%; Graduates using acquired skills extensively in their work 16.7%; Average net monthly salary 855 euros; Satisfaction with work performed 6.7/10.
In the latest AlmaLaurea report, indicators for class L11 across all Italian universities are distributed as follows: Graduates currently enrolled in a master's program 68.6%; Employment rate one year after graduation 59.6%; Average net salary 1,053 euros; 59.5% would enroll in the same course at the same university.
A positive balance is evident regarding career progression (percentage of enrollments in a second-level course); employment rates and salary levels remain negative (but improving).

Improvement Actions In light of the data presented, it is necessary to multiply opportunities for students to gain information and knowledge about the job market. To this end, the CDS, in agreement with other CDSs affiliated with the Department of Languages, Literatures, and Modern Cultures, plans a series of meetings with stakeholders and, where possible, joint orientation initiatives.
Data is generally presented and discussed in the first useful autumn CDS meeting (September-October).

Specific Educational Objectives and Description of the Educational Path The pre-educational focus of the L11 CDS centers on the study of Italian language and foreign languages from both theoretical and practical perspectives, within a curriculum that emphasizes the acquisition of knowledge and skills oriented toward literary, cultural, historical-artistic, and media-communication contexts.
The training of three-year graduates includes three interconnected areas:
1) Linguistic-Didactic Area. This area includes training activities in the two foreign languages (one of which is European) chosen by the student from those listed in the Didactic Regulations. Language teaching spans the entire three-year period and is organized to foster the development and progressive consolidation of linguistic-communicative skills, written and oral, suitable for the context of use and the specific cultural reality of the studied languages. This area includes linguistic, glottodidactic, multimedia, and logical-communicative training activities aimed at developing knowledge and metalinguistic reflection skills.
2) Philological-Literary Area. This area includes training activities aimed at developing awareness of the philological context and knowledge of the literary traditions of the studied languages, as well as Italian, from a diachronic, synchronic, and comparative perspective. During the three years, the path includes philological and historical-literary training activities designed to develop skills in analyzing and interpreting literary texts within a European and extra-European context, using appropriate theoretical, hermeneutic, philological, and sociological tools.
3) Historical-Artistic-Cultural Area. This area includes training activities in historical-geographical, artistic, and audiovisual-multimedia fields, forming the basis of interdisciplinary training to develop skills in analyzing contemporary socio-cultural phenomena in heterogeneous, multicultural, and transmedia contexts. The path also includes free-choice activities for students to enrich and complete their interdisciplinary horizon, as well as the mandatory acquisition of IT and telecommunication skills.
Professionalizing courses and seminars are also organized to provide knowledge useful for entering the job market (e.g., European community planning), as well as internships and traineeships at companies, entities, and public and private institutions.
The L11 CDS thus trains three-year graduates with theoretical and practical competencies related to language and its teaching/learning, literature, history, geography, and the artistic-cultural context of European and extra-European countries.
Knowledge, skills, and understanding related to the three learning areas are acquired through participation in lectures and seminars, individual study, training internships, courses at companies, institutions, or entities at local, national, and international levels. Professionalizing seminars and other training and cultural experiences complete the training, facilitating entry into the job market. Competencies acquired during the three years are applicable in various sectors, from tourism to communication, in national and international entities, and form a useful basis for continuing studies in a master's degree.

Learning of the chosen foreign languages is developed and monitored through exercises that include specific language laboratory activities and verified through written and oral exams, including in-course assessments.

Opinions of Entities and Companies with Internship/Traineeship Agreements The L11 CDS, like other Degree Courses of the Department of Languages, Literatures, and Modern Cultures, has conducted a survey of opinions from entities, companies, and institutions that have signed curricular or extracurricular internship/traineeship agreements. The survey was conducted with the assistance of the Department's Tutoring Office.
The numerous current agreements (list available at the provided link) include companies, entities, and institutions where L11 CDS students can complete internships and traineeships. The majority of involved actors, including companies, entities, and institutions that have previously hosted L11 CDS interns and trainees, have confirmed the renewal of their collaboration.
An annual survey of social partners' opinions is conducted, not only in the Abruzzo region.
In the perspective of enhancing the training offer of the four CDSs, the key points emerging from the discussion and widely supported by participants are:
- Stakeholder satisfaction with this annual working session and active involvement in making university paths more aligned with job market needs;
- Need to complement linguistic skills with sector-specific knowledge (economic, legal, tourism techniques, company functioning, etc.), as well as the acquisition of cross-cutting skills;
- Opportunity to enhance techniques for using foreign languages in professional contexts: from customer psychology to public communication techniques;
- Need to enhance practical use and spontaneous use of foreign languages at all levels;
- Need to enhance IT and digital skills (Excel, PowerPoint, cloud usage, etc.) and digital competencies (company websites, as well as digital teaching modules).

Synthesis of the Regional Coordination Committee's Opinion The L-11 Degree Course, already modified in accordance with the didactic reforms under Ministerial Decree No. 270 of October 22, 2004, and following a positive consultation with representative organizations of goods and service production as required by Article 11, Paragraph 4 of the said decree, qualifies graduates to work in teaching, cultural services, journalism, publishing, cultural institutions, companies, commercial activities, diplomatic and consular representations, and tourism.

Consultation with Representative Organizations of Goods and Service Production, and Professions (Course Establishment)
On February 16, 2017, a consultation was held at the Department of Languages, Literatures, and Modern Cultures with representatives of regional entities, institutions, and companies (stakeholders), including ARCI, Provincial Committee of Pescara; FAI - Italian Environment Fund, Pescara Delegation; CGIL - Pescara; ANCI Abruzzo, L'Aquila Office; Central Office of Abruzzo Chambers of Commerce; ASL Pescara; Chamber of Commerce I.A.A. of Pescara; as well as cultural and artistic associations, travel agencies, social cooperatives, and schools.
The President of the L11 CDS presented the distinctive features of the Degree Course: content, educational objectives, aims, and professional profiles the Course aims to train. After the presentation, the President distributed evaluation questionnaires for the L11 CDS, illustrating the 2017-18 training offer and inviting representatives to comment, ask questions, or provide suggestions. This led to an active and fruitful exchange of opinions with participants from various professional backgrounds (education, regional or state entities, private entities and institutions, cultural, assistance, and environmental associations), enriching the discussion significantly.
Representatives generally expressed appreciation for the name, structure, and knowledge/skills offered by the CDS. Additionally, entities and companies that had hosted L11 CDS students as interns and trainees expressed satisfaction with the activities performed and their commitment. Some participants highlighted aspects of the training offer that could be modified or integrated. Among the suggestions, there was an invitation to enhance spoken language skills and communicative interaction, as well as cultural knowledge; the need to include in the educational path activities more closely connected to the job market (e.g., elements of European community planning), also through internships and traineeships at entities and companies; the importance of implementing knowledge of regulatory frameworks for employment opportunities in Italian cultural institutions abroad.
A second consultation with stakeholders was held on October 4, 2017. Participants included representatives from the Chamber of Commerce of Chieti; CARITAS Pescara Foundation; National Center for Dannunzian Studies; Comune di Silvi, Community Policies Office; Central Office of Abruzzo Chambers of Commerce; Francesca Di Tonno Marketing and Internationalization Agency; Chieti Chamber of Commerce Development Agency; Spazio MATTA - Artists for the Matta of Pescara; DelloIacono Comunica Agency; Abruzzo Region, Energy Department, DPC025; I.I.S. E. Alessandrini of Montesilvano; Liceo "Gonzaga" of Chieti; Liceo Linguistico "Marconi" of Pescara; Liceo Scientifico "Galilei" of Pescara; Istituto Comprensivo of Loreto Aprutino; Istituto Onnicomprensivo "Spaventa" of Città S. Angelo; Liceo Scientifico "Leonardo" of Pescara.
The President distributed an evaluation questionnaire for the L11 CDS, containing in the first part a synthetic description of the current CDS, its aims, and professional profiles it aims to train, along with a scheme of the 2017-18 training offer. The second part consists of questions regarding possible modifications to the didactic structure, suggested within the framework of ministerial regulations to enhance the CDS. The President reminded that some participants had already attended the February 16, 2017 meeting, from which useful suggestions emerged, such as the possibility of enhancing cultural knowledge and giving greater emphasis to professionalizing activities and internship/traineeship experiences. The President then proceeded to illustrate the current features of the L11 CDS and some possible modifications to the structure, soliciting comments and suggestions from stakeholders. An intense and detailed discussion followed, during which stakeholders expressed general and strong appreciation for the modifications illustrated by the President, emphasizing their favorable opinion regarding the increase in professionalizing activities and cultural discipline. At the end of the consultation, thirteen representatives returned the duly completed and signed questionnaires. From the interventions of the social partners present and the analysis of the completed questionnaires, the following suggestions emerged: include subjects such as geography, art, and philosophy in the offer, along with deeper exploration of cultural aspects related to teaching foreign languages and literatures, in line with the L11 CDS's cultural vocation; include in professionalizing seminars topics related to planning, programs, and policies of the European Union, various forms of publishing and journalism, marketing and advertising, cultural institutions; give greater emphasis to multimedia languages, new technologies applied to language teaching, theory and techniques of communication, websites, social media, and IT skills for work; provide the possibility of completing internships/traineeships in the context of Italian L2 teaching (in accommodation centers, ASL, schools, etc.).

Consultation with Representative Organizations of Goods and Service Production, and Professions (Subsequent Consultations)
The President of the CDS, in agreement with the Teaching Tutor, the Director's Delegate for Orientation, and the Presidents of CDSs L12, LM 37, and LM 38, organizes a meeting with social partners at the beginning of each semester. Below is a summary of the meeting.

On March 25, 2024, a consultation was held with representative organizations of goods and service production and professions. The meeting was promoted by the Presidents of CDSs L11, L12, LM37, and LM38 of the Department of Languages, Literatures, and Modern Cultures (University of G. d'Annunzio), and organized by the Teaching Tutor, Dr. Lorena Savini. The meeting took place in Room 2 of the Viale Pindaro Teaching Complex in Pescara.
The meeting aimed to consolidate the established collaboration between the CDS and representative organizations of goods and service production and professions. This activity also serves as a consultation to monitor the job market's evolution in the territorial context and to represent the needs of economic and cultural operators two years after the pandemic event.

In the perspective of enhancing the training offer of the four CDSs, the key points emerging from the discussion and widely supported by participants are:
- Stakeholder satisfaction with this annual working session and active involvement in making university paths more aligned with job market needs;
- Need to complement linguistic skills with sector-specific knowledge (economic, legal, tourism techniques, company functioning, etc.), as well as the acquisition of cross-cutting skills;
- Opportunity to enhance techniques for using foreign languages in professional contexts: from customer psychology to public communication techniques;
- Need to enhance practical use and spontaneous use of foreign languages at all levels;
- Need to enhance IT and digital skills (Excel, PowerPoint, cloud usage, etc.) and digital competencies (company websites, as well as digital teaching modules).

Study Plan Attached: https://www.unich.it/sites/default/files/ugov_suafiles/149068.pdf

Characteristics of the Final Exam The final exam consists of preparing a written thesis on a topic related to one of the courses in the Degree Course curriculum, chosen by the student to verify the competencies and skills acquired during their educational path.

Final Exam Execution Method The final exam corresponds to 6 CFU. It consists of preparing a written thesis and discussing a topic related to one of the courses in the Degree Course, chosen by the student during their educational path.
Students are admitted to the final exam after acquiring all credits specified in the Didactic Regulations and after demonstrating at least B2 CEFR level linguistic competence in both study languages. This competence is verified concurrently with the third-year Language exam, whose content is structured to achieve the B2 level linguistic skills.
The final exam consists of preparing a written thesis (minimum 20 and maximum 40 pages, each containing 2,000-2,500 characters) on a topic related to one of the disciplinary areas in the Degree Course curriculum and belonging to one of the following types:
- Specialist article;
- Short linguistic analysis essay;
- Translation of a short text;
- Review article of recent publications on a specific topic or disciplinary field;
- Reasoned bibliography on a scientific issue or topic.
Students wishing to prepare the final thesis in a foreign language may request authorization from the CDS Council. In any case, a suitable summary in Italian must accompany the thesis written in a foreign language.
The topic choice, consistent with the Degree Course's educational objectives, must be agreed upon with a teacher who teaches a discipline for which the candidate has passed at least one exam and who will serve as the thesis supervisor.
It is possible to write the thesis in a Taf D course (taught at another Department) with prior authorization from the CDS Council, which will assess the congruence of the course with the student's educational path.
Examination committees, composed of at least five members, evaluate the candidate considering the entire educational path.
In assigning scores, the Committee starts from the weighted average of the scores obtained by the student in the profit exams, to which an additional score for the thesis evaluation is added. This additional score, ranging from 0 to 5, takes into account the breadth of the thesis, precision of writing and analysis, effectiveness of argumentation and/or translation. An additional score is also assigned to students who, at the time of the graduation exam, are not out of course, have participated in international mobility, and have obtained at least three honors (1 for each case).

Synthesis of the Technical Report of the Evaluation Committee The Course covers a central area in the humanities sector, scientifically and professionally relevant, consistently positioned at optimal levels in terms of enrollments, students, and graduates, relative to its class. The Department has adequate, appropriate, and effective facilities, and following an advanced restructuring program of the Pescara Campus, new teaching and scientific spaces will be acquired in the short term, fully aligned with the new programming and prospects for full implementation. The Department can rely on a specific teaching staff for basic and characteristic disciplines, largely adequate to the new programming and prospects for full implementation. The proposed structure, significantly improved in terms of compactness, transparency, and effectiveness, can contribute to the goals of rationalization and qualification of the University's training offer.

Department DEPARTMENT OF LETTERS, ARTS AND SOCIAL SCIENCES Website https://www.dilass.unich.it/didattica  Access Requirements Required knowledge for access Eligible to enroll in the Course of Study are graduates of Italian and foreign secondary schools of the second degree (subject to verification of the equivalence of the degree and proficiency in the Italian language). The methods for verifying the required access knowledge will be specifically defined in the teaching regulations, as well as the Additional Educational Obligations (OFA) assigned in case basic training deficiencies are identified.

SECTION: Admission Procedures
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/62

Admission Procedures Provided that admission to the course is not contingent upon passing any examination, in the initial phase of teaching activities (typically after enrollment is complete, no later than February), basic knowledge verification tests (in the linguistic-literary and historical-geographical fields) are scheduled in the form of multiple-choice questionnaires for students who scored below 80/100 in their secondary school diploma. Students transferring from other universities or other study programs at 'G. d'Annunzio' University, as well as those already holding a degree, are exempt from these tests. The test, conducted online, consists of two sections: the first covering the linguistic-literary field with questions on Italian grammar, linguistics, and text comprehension and contextualization; the second covering the historical-geographical field. For illustrative purposes, a sample test is attached. In case of a negative result, students will be assigned additional educational obligations (OFA) to be fulfilled in the first year of study; individual recovery paths will be defined with faculty members in the disciplinary areas where insufficient preparation was identified (these students may also utilize faculty tutoring, which will also function as a teaching office). A verification test for the recovery of initial deficiencies will be held before the summer exam session (passing which will extinguish the OFA). For preparation for the initial test, studying current secondary school textbooks is sufficient; specific guidelines are published on the course website. Regarding classical languages (Greek and Latin), relevant faculty may conduct initial preparation verification tests. However, failing these tests does not result in an OFA, as students may opt for a path that does not include classical disciplines. In any case, the study program offers 0-credit courses in 'Basic Latin Language' (beginner and advanced levels) and 'Basic Greek Language' (beginner and advanced levels) for all students. The fulfillment of OFA may also be achieved by passing a minimum of 18 CFU in foundational and characteristic courses specified in the first-year study plan (or in the first and second year for part-time students). Failure to fulfill OFA by the deadline means students remain obligated to satisfy this requirement and cannot take second-year exams until it is completed (Article 28, paragraph 5 of the University Academic Regulations).

URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/62

Communication Skills (communication skills)
Graduates in Letters must possess solid linguistic and argumentative skills enabling them to communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions to specialist and non-specialist audiences.
They also acquire communication and presentation skills (in written and oral form) applicable through the use of information and multimedia communication tools, both in Italian and in at least one European language (at B1 level).
The acquisition and verification of written and oral communication skills occur through training activities, including laboratory-based ones specifically dedicated to linguistic-communicative competence, as provided in the course's teaching plan, through seminars and through the production and presentation of papers, and especially through the final exam.

UNIVERSITY: GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO UNIVERSITY – CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [L270] LETTERS
SECTION: AUTONOMY OF JUDGMENT
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/62

Autonomy of Judgment (making judgments)
Graduates in Letters must be able to independently set up and carry out, even using new technologies, bibliographic and/or field research necessary to establish the required databases for their studies, and then be able to process and interpret such data with a critical spirit attentive to scientific, social, and ethical implications. In particular, they must know, be able to evaluate, and use methods for linguistic, philological, literary, rhetorical, aesthetic, and historical analysis of written documents in order to derive judgments that are both consistent and original.

The student's autonomy of judgment is developed primarily through exercises aimed at personal and conscious analysis of documents, sources, critical literature, etc., to be conducted within individual courses, laboratory experiences, seminars, and internships. It is verified during oral and/or written exams; it also serves as a verification point regarding the student's autonomous judgment abilities developed through the preparation of the final thesis.

Orientation in Entry The 'Gabriele d'Annunzio' University, through its Orientation, Tutoring, Placement, Student Rights, and Disability Office, offers a series of interventions on orientation and placement, structured into Orientation in Entry (targeted at students in the final years of Secondary School), Orientation in Progress, Tutoring, Student Rights, for university students, and Exit Orientation and Placement for students, graduates, and doctoral candidates, as well as the Disability and Specific Learning Disorders (DSA) Service for university students.
However, particularly regarding Orientation in Entry, the Course of Study in Letters, in synergy with the Department of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences, annually carries out a series of initiatives aimed at enabling students to make a fruitful choice in university selection. These activities are coordinated by the designated orientation officer, Professor Maria Luigia Di Marzio, who collaborates with a specific committee composed of Professors Fabio Andreazza, Luciana Pasquini, Silvia Scorrano, and a student representative. During the 2023/24 academic year, coordination was transferred to Professor Mario Cimini.
The main orientation actions are:
- Orientation meetings at Secondary Schools, particularly in the region, from January to May;
- Participation in orientation fairs and orientation days inside and outside the region for Secondary School students;
- Open Day programming: welcome days organized from January to May each year, allowing students to meet university faculty members of individual courses, senior students, for general information on services and enrollment procedures, or to attend orientation-specific lectures;
- Targeted teaching projects for high school students in collaboration with local schools;
- Specific projects involving current students (such as theatrical activities with mobile performances aimed at engaging local schools);
- Disability and DSA service: welcome and support for students with disabilities and/or learning disorders through targeted interventions to ensure the right to education and facilitate integration into the university community; this support is particularly carried out in synergy with the University's Psychological Listening and Orientation Counseling Service (SAPCO) (see https://www.unich.it/campus/servizi/servizi-di-contesto-agli-studenti);
- Tutoring and assistance service provided by specially trained senior students.
In addition to in-person activities, the Course of Study - in coordination with DiLASS - uses a specific online platform (see https://www.dilass.unich.it/orientamento-0), where the following are uploaded:
- Illustrative materials for the course in video and/or text format;
- Webinars on specific aspects of the Course of Study's educational project (or short lecture-type sessions);
- Calendar of 'remote' meetings with faculty and tutors available to provide information;
- Links to the University's orientation initiatives.
The assessment of admission requirements for the Course of Study also provides an opportunity to initiate tutorial activities that allow for a better understanding of the student, who can then be guided in choosing the study plan most suitable to their aptitudes. All faculty members of the Course of Study dedicate several weekly hours in September and October to meeting with incoming students to guide them, through personalized interviews, both in gaining a mature awareness of their choice and in building their study path. The Course of Study also organizes, at the beginning of the academic year, collective meetings with interested students, with the presence of the Course President and orientation delegates, to provide general information on the annual teaching organization, training opportunities (including partnerships with foreign universities), and the employment prospects offered by the course (see also https://www.dilass.unich.it/orientamento-0).
In the 2023-24 academic year, in addition to re-proposing tested initiatives from previous years (at the Night of Researchers and the University's Open Day), new events were held in the territory, many of which involved direct intervention in Abruzzo schools, also funded through participation in PCTO/PNRR projects. The following activities are highlighted:
- 23 September 2023. Ndr 2023, Chieti Campus "One World, one Health, one thousand Cultures".
- 13 and 14 December 2023. Student Fair. Dromedian Live Campus, via Piaggio 35, Chieti Scalo.
- 14 December 2023 (15:00-18:00): presentation of the Italian university system and the University D'Annunzio's university reality at Aula Giuntella for students from various schools in the province (Marialuigia Di Marzio).
- 1 February 2024. Lanciano, Benito Lanci Theater Fenaroli Fair. M. Di Marzio: "Towards and Metaverse: Professional Horizons", within the event "Choose Your Path. University and Workforce Orientation Days", 13th edition.
- 'Orienta UDA' program, with course presentations once a week.
- 'A Day as a New Student' initiative (guest students from 2 high schools attending DiLASS lectures).
For further details on all implemented initiatives, see the attached PDF.

Ongoing orientation and tutoring All teachers of the Study Course carry out ongoing tutoring activities; each tutor, assigned at the time of admission to the Study Course, follows the student constantly throughout the entire three-year study path, remaining available with a weekly reception schedule easily accessible for information, clarifications, and advice. Additionally, in various courses, dedicated time is allocated for assisted study, which includes targeted training activities to improve the learning of content presented within the course itself.
A specific internal commission within the Study Course, composed of Prof. Fabio Andreazza, Luciana Pasquini, Maria Luigia Di Marzio (chair), Pierluigi Ortolano, coordinates orientation and tutoring initiatives. During the 2023/24 academic year, coordination was transferred to Prof. Mario Cimini.
The Study Course, as easily evident from the Annual Monitoring Sheet of the Course and the Cyclical Review Report, implements periodic checks on the overall progress of student cohorts in acquiring training credits, and identifies strategies to improve study effectiveness, also aiming to reduce student dropout and abandonment. In particular, it activates to rationalize study plans and teaching calendars, evaluates the homogenization of CFU/exam programs and the consistency of programs with the Study Course's educational objectives, and monitors student careers through a specific application (INGRID). Results are verified through the increase of certain key indicators (acquisition of a sufficient number of CFU by students, percentage of students graduating on time, dropout percentage, student satisfaction index). In particular, in the INGRID system, the number of students with a percentage of acquired CFU below 30% compared to the annual course workload remains consistently below 15% (12.5% in 2021, 14.7% in 2022, 13% in 2023).
Tutors and course representatives, taking into account the career monitoring that statistically predominantly leads (or continues) to paths leading to teaching in secondary schools, constantly assist students in calibrating their study plans towards this professional goal, guiding them in meeting the requirements set by current legislation.
To enable students to make informed professional choices, the Study Course promotes a series of internship activities at appropriately selected and contracted institutions and productive structures. Delegates managing this service periodically monitor the effectiveness of internships and propose improvement strategies or enhancements to the service itself.
Ongoing orientation activities are also implemented by the University's Orientation, Tutoring, Placement, Right to Study, and Disability Office, in collaboration with the Study Course and the Department. In particular, this service:
- provides information and administrative support to disabled students and/or their families regarding opportunities reserved by the University;
- in collaboration with Schools and Departments, offers support to students interested in reorganizing or revising their study path;
- makes available assistance services reserved for disabled students or students with Specific Learning Disorders; in this regard, the Study Course, through its President and the delegate for support activities, Prof. Ilaria Filograsso;
- provides support and assistance to students regarding the Right to Study;
- coordinates tutoring calls reserved for students;
- coordinates calls for part-time collaboration activities reserved for students;
- makes available online a series of information reserved for students interested in undertaking internships not for credit.

Internship periods The Course has for years maintained an internal structure that activates and manages internship agreements with cultural institutions, companies, organizations from the world of work and social assistance, newsrooms, libraries, etc. The coordinator of this structure is Prof. Antonella Di Nallo, who also benefits from the support of an administrative unit, Dr. Maria Cristina Ricciardi. Additional opportunities for implementing study-work alternation within training processes, and to facilitate students' professional choices through direct knowledge of the world of work, are offered and managed directly by the University through the Orientation, Tutoring, Placement, Student Rights and Disability Sector.

International Mobility International student mobility primarily occurs within the Erasmus+ Programme (for both study and internship purposes), with minor activity under extra-European conventions. In this context, the Course's activities are integrated into those of the Department of origin (DILASS) and the University as a whole. The International Relations Office of the University is therefore primarily responsible for coordinating and managing student mobility (see www.unich.it/didattica/studiare-allestero). However, many faculty members affiliated with the Course hold specific conventions with foreign universities, established based on common scientific and research interests, which include Erasmus grants for student mobility. These faculty members also provide information on the modalities and characteristics of study and training periods at the partner universities. Overall, the Course places particular emphasis on internationalizing the education of its students.

Currently, 35 conventions are active (for details, see attached PDF or link, as technical issues prevent listing all conventions in the following screen). For internal coordination of Erasmus mobility, the Course relies on Professors Maria Grazia Del Fuoco and Antonella Di Nallo; the International Relations Delegate is Professor Francesco Caccamo. During the Erasmus mobility call period (February-March), the Course organizes meetings with students, in coordination with the University's International Mobility Delegate (Professor Enrichetta Soccio), to encourage participation and provide all possible information. Faculty members responsible for individual conventions provide information and support upon student request, maintaining contact with foreign university counterparts. To further promote and support international mobility, since 2019 the Course has decided to supplement the Erasmus grant with funds from its own resources (for the 2019/2020 academic year, this contribution equaled the grant amount; for the 2021/2022 academic year, it will be based on the Department's financial availability). The results of students' activities abroad (which inherently involve the internationalization of their education) are discussed in the Annual Monitoring Sheet of the Course and the Cyclical Review Report. Students take exams at partner universities for at least 12 CFU; these exams are recognized in their study plan, and the experience is also valued during graduation with a specific score.

In the 2023/24 academic year, 4 students enrolled in the Letters Course benefited from an Erasmus grant.

The Course, in coordination with the Department, has committed to improving the data on incoming Erasmus students, which was zero in 2019/20, reached 8 in 2022/23, and 12 in 2023/24.

Career Guidance The Program in Letters, for the purpose of facilitating the employment of its graduates, relies on the 'Orientation and Placement' service managed directly by the University through the 'Start' program. The University, therefore, promotes the employment of its graduates and alumni through the activation of a network of relationships between the University, Enterprises, and Research Systems aimed at developing and consolidating a virtuous cycle of relationships and services, facilitating the 'communication' between the needs of enterprises, the processes of labor market integration, and the implications for educational plans, while providing substance and continuity to the transition phase into the workforce. In this context, graduates in Letters can perform tasks and activities related to consulting and cultural promotion in production sectors that require specific disciplinary competencies combined with critical thinking: publishing, management of social services, libraries and museums, training and counseling activities, human resource management, and advertising. The Delegate of the Program for the management of the career guidance service is Prof. Pierluigi Ortolano, who works in coordination with the Departmental Delegate for Placement, Prof. Francesco Berardi.

The Program, together with the Department and the Master's program in Philology, Linguistics, and Literary Traditions, also promotes initiatives that offer graduates a concrete connection with the world of work. Additionally, considering that a significant portion of them pursue teaching careers by continuing their studies in a Master's program, the Program promotes seminar and conference activities featuring experts in the literary, historical, philological, and linguistic fields; these activities aim to deepen methodological and didactic aspects, also in preparation for teaching careers (the activity calendar is available on the website: https://www.dilass.unich.it/dipartimento/tutti-gli-eventi).

The Program evaluates the results of the activities promoted in the area of Placement through the analysis and discussion of data provided by AlmaLaurea and the student office for the corresponding Master's programs LM-14 and LM-15 during one of the meetings held during the year by the Steering Committee, which includes the Placement Delegate.
