Descrizione del corso in breve Il Corso di Laurea Triennale in Economia e Informatica per l'Impresa (CLEII) nasce dalle esigenze delle imprese di avere delle figure professionali che, oltre ad aver acquisito le conoscenze multidisciplinari previste dagli obiettivi formativi della Classe di Laurea in Scienze economiche, siano in grado di comprendere e utilizzare le emergenti tecnologie informatiche, al fine di
- gestire in modo efficiente i flussi informativi aziendali e le interazioni dell'impresa con il tessuto economico in cui è inserita;
- estrarre ed elaborare conoscenze di supporto alle decisioni;
- promuovere e gestire l'innovazione produttiva e organizzativa;
- garantire un'efficace presenza dell'impresa in Internet;
- sviluppare sistemi informatici e di intelligenza artificiale per la gestione dell'azienda.
Il Corso di Studio è stato più volte rivisto e migliorato:
- aggiornando nel tempo i contenuti informatici per rispondere ai rapidi cambiamenti della disciplina ed alle esigenze del territorio,
- aumentando l'integrazione fra gli insegnamenti in ambito economico, aziendale, giuridico ed informatico,
- inserendo insegnamenti di tipo quantitativo, ad esempio la statistica e l'econometria, ed insegnamenti innovativi, come il data mining, il machine learning e l'intelligenza artificiale.
Il laureato CLEII è in grado di sviluppare sistemi informatici e di intelligenza artificiale, di sfruttare le potenzialità di Internet e di applicare queste competenze rispondendo in modo adeguato e innovativo alle esigenze dell'impresa.
Dopo la laurea si può entrare subito nel mercato del lavoro, oppure proseguire gli studi con un corso di laurea magistrale, in ambito economico o aziendale come anche in ambito informatico o di intelligenza artificiale.
Efficacia esterna Dai dati Almalaurea relativi al Profilo dei laureati CLEII 2022 (allegato C2.1) risulta che il 100% dei laureati CLEII intende proseguire gli studi (il 75% iscrivendosi ad una laurea biennale magistrale, il 25% iscrivendosi ad un corso di master o di perfezionamento).
Gli aspetti ritenuti rilevanti nella ricerca del lavoro sono:
- Possibilità di guadagno 100%
- Acquisizione di professionalità 75%
- Possibilità di carriera 75%
- Rapporti con i colleghi sul luogo di lavoro 75%
- Luogo di lavoro (ubicazione, caratteristiche fisiche dell'ambiente di lavoro) 75%
- Stabilità/sicurezza del posto di lavoro 50%
- Coerenza con gli studi 50%
- Possibilità di utilizzare al meglio le competenze acquisite 50%
I dati sulla Condizione occupazionale dei laureati CLEII ad un anno dalla laurea mostrano quanto segue:
- un tasso di occupazione pari al 55,6%,
- un tasso di disoccupazione pari all'11,8%,
- una percentuale di laureati attualmente iscritti ad un corso di laurea magistrale pari al 59,3%, (con il 14,8% che contemporaneamente lavora);
- una retribuzione media mensile netta dei laureati pari a 1.092 euro;
- un valore medio di soddisfazione per il lavoro svolto dichiarato dai laureati, in una scala da 1 a 10, pari a 7,7.
Al quadro C2 si allegano i seguenti documenti sulla efficacia esterna del CLEII:
- Allegato C2.1 - Profilo dei Laureati;
- Allegato C2.2 - Condizione occupazionale dei Laureati ad un anno dalla laurea.
- Allegato C2.3 - Soddisfazione per il corso di studio concluso e condizione occupazionale dei laureati Motivi dell'istituzione di più corsi nella classe Il Corso di Laurea in Economia e Informatica per l'Impresa si differenzia nettamente dagli altri Corsi di Laurea attivati nella stessa classe principalmente per i suoi contenuti specifici di informatica e matematica. Infatti, pur condividendo con il Corso di Laurea in Economia e Commercio e con il Corso di Laurea in Economia, Mercati e Sviluppo un'ampia parte di contenuti generali nelle discipline caratterizzanti la classe di laurea, si differenzia nettamente da entrambi: infatti mentre il Corso di Laurea in Economia e Commercio è focalizzato sulle discipline economiche, finanziarie e giuridiche, ed il Corso di Laurea in Economia, Mercati e Sviluppo sui modelli di sviluppo, mercati e servizi finanziari, il Corso di Laurea in Economia e Informatica per l'Impresa, integra le discipline economiche con conoscenze di matematica e informatica, per formare un laureato in grado di rispondere ai mutamenti della società in ambito economico con competenze, oltre che economiche, anche scientifiche e tecnologiche. La diversificazione è particolarmente evidente nelle attività formative affini o integrative, che comprendono numerose discipline non rinvenibili negli altri corsi attivati nella stessa classe.
Il Rettore dell'Ateneo si impegna formalmente a garantire che in fase di articolazione del Regolamento Didattico dei predetti Corsi di Studio il vincolo di differenziazione previsto dalla normativa venga pienamente rispettato.
Obiettivi formativi specifici del corso e descrizione del percorso formativo Il Corso di Laurea si propone di formare un laureato che, avendo acquisito le conoscenze multidisciplinari previste dagli obiettivi formativi qualificanti della Classe di Laurea, sia in grado di comprendere e utilizzare l'Information and Communication Technology in ambito economico. Il corso di studio nasce direttamente dall'esigenza delle imprese di avere laureati che conoscano le emergenti tecnologie informatiche e siano in grado di applicarle nei contesti economico-aziendali e, al tempo stesso, possano interagire senza barriere culturali all'interno dell'impresa.
Il percorso formativo si articola in due fasi: una fase iniziale, corrispondente al primo anno e larga parte del secondo, nella quale verranno soprattutto acquisiti i contenuti generali tipici della Classe, integrati da cognizioni di informatica e di matematica; una seconda fase in cui verranno studiati quegli aspetti della realtà economica ed economicoaziendale in cui l'uso dell'Information and Communication Technology ha un ruolo significativo. Lo studente potrà approfondire:
- il funzionamento dei mercati, in particolare telematici, utilizzando gli strumenti di analisi tipici del s.s.d. SECS-P/01;
- la struttura dei flussi informativi all'interno dell'impresa e con il tessuto economico in cui e' inserita, nonché le dinamiche dell'innovazione d'impresa, attraverso insegnamenti nell'ambito dei s.s.d. SECS-P/07 e SECS-P/10;
- le tecniche per l'estrazione e l'elaborazione di conoscenze a supporto delle decisioni, attraverso insegnamenti nell'ambito statistico-matematico e informatico. Il Corso di Laurea fornirà inoltre un'adeguata conoscenza delle nuove tecnologie informatiche e delle loro applicazioni in ambito economico.
Il laureato avrà solide basi di economia ed informatica, e sarà in grado di
- riconoscere e risolvere i problemi informatici;
- proporre nuove soluzioni per migliorare l'utilizzo delle tecnologie informatiche a vantaggio delle imprese.
Il laureato potrà sia inserirsi professionalmente come dipendente o consulente in aziende private o pubbliche della produzione e dei servizi, sia proseguire la propria formazione in generale nell'ambito delle scienze economiche ed economico-aziendali, in particolare sulle tematiche dell'innovazione e dell'economia della conoscenza.
Opinioni enti e imprese con accordi di stage / tirocinio curriculare o extra-curriculare Fino alla corte 2015/2016 il Regolamento del CdS non prevedeva stage né tirocini.
A partire dall'anno 2016 il Consiglio di Corso di Studio ha deliberato che gli studenti possono sostenere come attività formative di libera scelta (lettera D):
- attività di stage e tirocini presso imprese, enti pubblici o privati, ordini professionali fino ad un massimo di 9 CFU;
- tirocini formativi e di orientamento fino ad un massimo di 6 CFU.
Il numero di studenti che hanno svolto attività di tirocinio presso imprese private o enti pubblici è pari ad otto nell'anno 2017, tredici nell'anno 2018, otto negli anni 2019 e 2020, cinque nell'anno 2021, undici nell'anno 2022.
Al fine di verificare l'efficacia delle attività di cui sopra, l'Ufficio Stage della Presidenza della Scuola delle Scienze Economiche, Aziendali, Giuridiche e Sociologiche ha messo a punto un questionario di valutazione che viene compilato dalle aziende e enti ospitanti alla fine dell'attività formativa.
L'elaborazione dei questionari, effettuata dal Corso di Studio, ha evidenziato una valutazione molto positiva sotto tutti gli aspetti.
Per quanto riguarda gli aspetti formativi, professionali e relazionali, si evidenziano in particolare i seguenti risultati, calcolati sugli stage conclusi nell'ultimo anno (2022)
- motivazione e impegno: media 4,7 su 5;
- raggiungimento degli obiettivi formativi: media 4,5 su 5;
- capacità di lavorare in gruppo e senso di collaborazione: media 4,7 su 5.
Per quanto riguarda le prospettive future, il 9% delle aziende ha offerto un posto di lavoro al termine dell'attività. Infine, il 73% delle strutture ospitanti si è dichiarato favorevole a nuove collaborazioni.
Tali valori sono sostanzialmente simili a quelli del 2021, di seguito riportati:
- motivazione e impegno: media 4,8 su 5;
- raggiungimento degli obiettivi formativi: media 4,8 su 5;
- capacità di lavorare in gruppo e senso di collaborazione: media 4,8 su 5;
- aziende che hanno offerto un posto di lavoro al termine dell'attività: 40%;
- strutture ospitanti favorevoli a nuove collaborazioni: 80%.
La differenza più evidente in termini percentuali è relativa al numero di aziende che hanno offerto un posto di lavoro al termine dell'attività. Tuttavia, in termini assoluti la differenza è pari ad una sola unità (due aziende nel 2021, una azienda nel 2022).

Il Corso nasce dalla collaborazione tra la Facoltà di Economia e la Facoltà di Scienze MM.FF.NN.. Attraverso questa collaborazione, il Corso si propone di formare un laureato che sia in grado di comprendere e utilizzare proficuamente l'Information and Communication Technology in attività di elaborazione e analisi di dati economici, di gestione e amministrazione, di approvvigionamento, di distribuzione di prodotti e servizi. Il laureato potrà quindi inserirsi tanto nel settore privato (in imprese sia di produzione che di servizi) quanto nella pubblica amministrazione, in ruoli operativi e di collaborazione, anche in posizioni di responsabilità. Potrà inoltre svolgere attività di consulenza.
A seguito di ampio esame, la consultazione risulta positiva.
Consultazione con le organizzazioni rappresentative - a livello nazionale e internazionale - della produzione di beni e servizi, delle professioni (Consultazioni successive)
Il Corso di Studio ha istituito un Comitato di indirizzo che attualmente è composto da 5 docenti del CdS, da 5 componenti esterni esponenti del mondo del lavoro e della ricerca scientifica, incluse le organizzazioni e le istituzioni interessate al profilo culturale e professionale dei laureati CLEII e dai rappresentanti degli studenti del Corso di Studio. Il Comitato si è riunito la prima volta il giorno 21 ottobre 2019 alle ore 17:00, presso lo studio della prof.ssa Francesca Scozzari.
Ai fini della consultazione di aziende ed enti per la proposta formativa del Corso di Studio in Economia e Informatica per l'Impresa (CLEII), sono stati effettuati:
1) un incontro di consultazione con le parti sociali il giorno 26 novembre 2015 alle ore 12:30, presso la Sala EX Presidio del Rettorato dell'Università degli Studi 'G. D'Annunzio' di Chieti-Pescara;
2) diversi incontri con alcune aziende del territorio dal 2016 ad oggi in particolare:
- Digimetrica
- Aptar Italia
- Konvergence
- Do It Yourself per lo svolgimento di stage e tesi di laurea su temi di interesse comune;
3) una survey online nel corso dell'a.a. 2017/2018 alla quale hanno risposto in modo completo 7 organizzazioni;
4) un incontro con il Comitato di Indirizzo del CdS il giorno 21 ottobre 2019 alle ore 17:00, presso lo studio della Presidente in carica del Cds, prof.ssa Francesca Scozzari.
5) un incontro con le aziende digitali del Polo pescarese il giorno 4 marzo 2020, presso la sede della DigitalSoft azienda digitale multinazionale, con quartiere generale a Pescara. All'incontro hanno partecipato la Presidente in carica del Cds, prof.ssa Francesca Scozzari e la prof.ssa di Informatica del CdS, Maria Chiara Meo, in carica come Direttore del Dipartimento di Economia. All'incontro ha partecipato anche il sindaco di Pescara che ha esposto le esigenze digitali della città di Pescara.
6) un incontro presso la Sala Consiliare del Rettorato dell'Università degli Studi 'G. D'Annunzio' il giorno 25 marzo 2021. All'incontro hanno partecipato le aziende DigitalSoft e AESYS della Digital Valley, il Rettore, il Delegato alle attività della Terza Missione in Ateneo, il Delegato per le attività di Placement di Ateneo, la Delegata ai Sistemi Informatici per la Didattica a Distanza di Ateneo, prof.ssa Francesca Scozzari, e la Presidente di Corso di Studio, prof.ssa Maria Chiara Meo.
7) un incontro con il Comitato di Indirizzo del CdS il giorno mercoledì 2 febbraio 2022 ore 15:00 via Microsoft Teams.
8) un incontro con il Comitato di Indirizzo del CdS il giorno 27 marzo 2023 ore 15:00 in modalità mista.
9) un incontro con il Comitato di Indirizzo del CdS il giorno 25 marzo 2024 ore 15:00 in modalità mista.
All'incontro con le parti sociali tenutosi il 26 novembre 2015 sono emerse le seguenti esigenze:
- integrare le consultazioni attraverso la somministrazione di un questionario da inviare agli stakeholders;
- possibilità di proseguire in Ateneo la propria formazione in un corso di laurea magistrale;
- forte necessità di rinnovare il corso di studi attraverso l'introduzione di insegnamenti che siano molto più aggiornati, nelle tecnologie affermate da pochi anni e non da decenni, rispetto alle richieste e alle necessità del mercato;
- possibilità di stipulare una convenzione tra Università e Comune di Chieti con la quale quest'ultimo si impegna a trovare gli enti ospitanti per permettere allo studente di poter praticare un periodo di tirocinio o stage.
La survey online effettuata nel corso dell'a.a. 2017/2018 ha visto la partecipazione di 16 aziende. Di queste, 7 si sono mostrate disponibili a fornire una loro completa valutazione. Le organizzazioni che hanno risposto al questionario, nella percentuale del 43,8%, sono state le seguenti: Città di San Benedetto del Tronto, Digimetrica, Digital Ascetic s.l., Maglificio Gran Sasso S.p.A., Wonder International Inc., Marsh LTD, Centri Locali per la Formazione Professionale della Provincia di Ascoli Piceno.
Tra le 7 aziende che hanno partecipato in maniera completa ed attiva al questionario, 2 di esse avevano già accolto nella loro struttura studenti/laureati per attività di stage/tirocinio, mostrandosi pienamente soddisfatti dei risultati conseguiti; la quasi totalità di esse – in misura pari all'80% – si era dimostrata invece interessata a ricevere i nostri studenti per un tirocinio/stage futuro.
Il Corso di Studio in Economia e Informatica per l'Impresa è stato istituito, nel 2000, per riempire una lacuna ben precisa: la mancanza di figure professionali che fungano da ponte tra un universo tecnologico in continua evoluzione ed il mondo delle decisioni e delle strategie economiche e d'impresa, tra il linguaggio dell'economista e del dirigente d'impresa ed il linguaggio dell'informatico. Dall'analisi dei risultati delle risposte date al questionario, è emerso che il CdS CLEII è capace di comunicare in modo chiaro tali finalità riportate nell'articolo 2 del regolamento (percentuale rispondenti: 71% più sì che no, 29% decisamente sì). Gli obiettivi formativi sono ritenuti adeguati alle esigenze del mercato del lavoro (86% più sì che no, 14% decisamente sì) e tali da comprendere le necessità di un settore strategico nonché fornire gli strumenti (informatici) necessari per lo sviluppo ed il consolidamento dell'attività aziendale. Le abilità/competenze fornite dal CdS sono ritenute prevalentemente adeguate e coerenti con le richieste di mercato (86% più sì che no, 14% più no che sì) seppur proposte di miglioramento del percorso formativo sono state riferite all'area informatica e sono volte ad includere tematiche quali l'Intelligenza Artificiale, il Blockchain, la Digital Transformation, Python, Web App, Digital Marketing, Data science e ancora ERP, CRM, la Gestione del Cambiamento, l'Organizzazione Aziendale e la Gestione della Conoscenza. Il CdS è impegnato nella formazione di figure professionali capaci di rispondere alle esigenze delle strutture intervistate (71% più sì che no, 29% più no che sì) e rappresentanti per le stesse soggetti desiderabili da parte del mercato del lavoro nei prossimi 3 anni (86% più sì che no, 14% decisamente sì).
Dall'analisi dei risultati è emerso anche il timore da parte di alcune aziende relativo alle dimensioni del mercato locale, che avrebbe potuto assistere ad un aumento della ricerca di figure, come quelle formate dal Corso di Laurea, ma con ritmi inferiori rispetto ad altri territori. Questo timore si è poi rilevato infondato, nelle consultazioni successive che si sono tenute con le organizzazioni rappresentative della produzione.
In particolare, già nell'incontro del 4 marzo 2020, ma ancora di più in quello del 25 marzo 2021, le aziende hanno invece manifestato la forte necessità di figure professionali del mondo digitale da parte del mercato e l'esigenza di un ecosistema locale per la crescita della realtà produttiva digitale, locale e nazionale. Hanno inoltre richiesto all'Università, e in modo particolare al CdS in Economia e Informatica per l'Impresa, di collaborare per realizzazione integrata di competenze informatiche e digitali. A tale scopo si è stabilito di creare un tavolo di lavoro permanente e si è fissato un successivo incontro che si è tenuto il 16 aprile 2021.
Nell'incontro del 2 febbraio 2022 è stato evidenziato dal parte della Presidente del Corso di Laurea che molti suggerimenti dati dai rappresentanti dell'industria nella precedente riunione del Comitato di indirizzo sono stati implementati. I rappresentanti delle aziende hanno evidenziato nuovamente uno scollamento fra la formazione universitaria e il mondo lavorativo nel territorio, in quanto ci sono molteplici opportunità di lavoro in ambito informatico in Abruzzo, anche nell'ambito della Pubblica Amministrazione, che però non hanno una corrispondente offerta di laureati. I rappresentanti delle aziende hanno ribadito che il CLEII fornisce una formazione valida anche per via della sua l'interdisciplinarietà, che è molto utile nel mondo lavorativo.
Nell'incontro del 27 marzo 2023 è stata evidenziata, da parte degli studenti e dei rappresentanti delle aziende, la necessità di declinare ulteriormente i programmi degli insegnamenti orientandoli verso la natura multidisciplinare del CLEII, dell'informatica e dell'economia digitale; ad esempio inserendo all'interno degli insegnamenti economici, l'approfondimento dei fenomeni micro e macroeconomici caratteristici dell'economia digitale.
E' stata inoltre sottolineata l'importanza formativa del tirocinio che andrebbe ulteriormente incentivato e personalizzato sulla base delle esigenze dell'azienda ospitante.
Nell'incontro del 25 marzo 2024 si sono ribadite le esigenze già manifestate l'anno precedente, pur evidenziando il fatto che molti suggerimenti forniti dai componenti esterni nella precedente riunione del Comitato di indirizzo sono stati implementati.
Infine, la consultazione continua con le rappresentanze del sistema produttivo e dei settori professionali, presenti a livello locale, ma anche a livello nazionale ed internazionale, è garantita dalla promozione costante e ripetuta di iniziative seminariali in cui i relatori provengono da diversi contesti aziendali e professionali, anche internazionali. I feedback raccolti in occasione di detti incontri vengono attentamente analizzati e permettono al CdS di avere regolarmente una conoscenza precisa della realtà produttiva a cui il Corso si rivolge.
Dati di ingresso, di percorso e di uscita Con la diffusione delle tecnologie informatiche nelle imprese e nelle amministrazioni pubbliche e lo sviluppo dei mercati telematici, è emersa la necessità di figure professionali che posseggano non solo adeguate competenze informatiche, ma anche una cultura in ambito economico, aziendale e giuridico per poter comprendere le esigenze specifiche delle aziende e delle amministrazioni in cui si trovano ad operare. Il Corso di Studio in Economia e Informatica per l'Impresa si propone di formare giovani con un profilo culturale e professionale che dia una risposta a questa esigenza.
Data la peculiarità del corso, che prevede l'acquisizione sia di competenze economiche che di competenze scientifiche e tecnologiche in ambito informatico, riteniamo molto soddisfacente la numerosità degli iscritti, che risulta in linea con la numerosità di altri corsi di studio con paragonabili contenuti scientifici.
Il documento allegato presenta i dati di ingresso, percorso e uscita fino alla coorte 2022/2023 elaborati dall'ateneo. Da segnalare in particolare il numero degli immatricolati che nell'anno accademico 2022/2023 è di 126 unità, dato che conferma il crescente interesse in competenze scientifiche all'interno di studi economici, aziendalistici e giuridici.
I dati sono discussi periodicamente in Consiglio di CdS e verranno ridiscussi nel Consiglio di CdS di settembre per confrontarli con i dati (parziali) sulle immatricolazioni dell'AA 2023/2024.
Caratteristiche della prova finale La prova finale consiste nella redazione di un elaborato scritto su un tema avanzato o su un progetto realizzato appositamente, da redigere in lingua italiana o in lingua inglese, che evidenzi la preparazione del laureando su uno specifico argomento attinente alla sua formazione curriculare. Il candidato deve dimostrare padronanza degli argomenti, capacità di operare in modo autonomo e un buon livello di comunicazione.
Il voto di laurea assegnato è espresso in centodecimi, con eventuale lode. Per la determinazione del voto di laurea la Commissione valuta tutte le attività formative previste durante il Corso di Studio. Ferme restando le prerogative spettanti per legge alla Commissione giudicatrice, il Consiglio del Corso di Studio stabilisce i criteri di massima di valutazione della carriera dello studente, al fine di garantire la necessaria uniformità e trasparenza di giudizio.
Modalità di svolgimento della prova finale La prova finale, alla quale sono assegnati 3 CFU, consiste nella redazione di un elaborato scritto in italiano o in inglese, preparato dallo studente, su un argomento di carattere teorico o pratico nell'ambito delle attività formative del corso di laurea. L'argomento viene concordato con un docente che assume il ruolo di relatore.
Nella prova finale lo studente deve mostrare di avere adeguata conoscenza e comprensione dell'argomento oggetto di analisi e autonoma capacità di sintesi e rielaborazione. L'elaborato, una volta approvato dal relatore, sarà valutato da una Commissione giudicatrice composta da non meno di cinque docenti. Della Commissione fanno parte il relatore ed almeno altri quattro docenti appartenenti prioritariamente allo stesso raggruppamento scientifico-disciplinare del relatore, ovvero a settori scientifico-disciplinari affini. Il Presidente della Scuola che gestisce il corso di laurea procede alla nomina della Commissione, sentito il Dipartimento a cui il corso stesso afferisce.
La Commissione valuta l'elaborato del candidato e procede all'assegnazione di un punteggio che in ogni caso non può essere superiore a sei punti. La Commissione procede, altresì, alla valutazione dell'intero percorso di studi del candidato, cui può attribuire un ulteriore punteggio di merito che non può comunque superare quattro punti per i candidati in corso e due punti per quelli fuori corso. La partecipazione al progetto Erasmus verrà considerata quale significativa per qualificare il percorso di studi e comporterà in sede di esame di laurea l'assegnazione allo studente di due punti a valere sul monte di punti attribuibili per il percorso di studi.
Il voto di laurea del candidato attribuito dalla Commissione è dato dalla somma algebrica fra il totale dei punti assegnati all'elaborato e al curriculum del candidato, e la media (espressa su base di centodieci e ponderata per i crediti formativi di ciascun insegnamento) delle votazioni degli esami di profitto superati dal candidato, approssimata all'intero superiore. Qualora il voto finale sia uguale o superiore a centodieci, la Commissione, accertata l'eccellenza dei risultati raggiunti dal candidato, può conferire, all'unanimità, la lode. La proclamazione è pubblica e si svolge al termine di ciascuna sessione di laurea.

Adeguate le motivazione all'istituzione di più corsi nella stessa classe. UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITÀ DEGLI STUDI GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO – CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [L601] DIETETICS
SECTION: Admission Procedures
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/606

Admission Procedures: Candidates admitted to the Dietetics program must possess a five-year secondary school diploma or an equivalent foreign qualification.
Access to the first year, the modalities of which are indicated annually in the University's admission notice, will be subject to passing an admission test consisting of multiple-choice questions on topics of Logic and general culture, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, and Mathematics.
Students admitted to the Course who score below 25% of the maximum score in Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, and Physics on the entrance test will be assigned additional educational requirements (OFA).
The Course Council establishes preparatory teaching activities to be carried out during the first semester of the first year of the course and which must be compulsorily followed by students in debt. The verification of results achieved in the preparatory teaching activities will take place within the evaluation of integrated courses that include the SSDs in which the OFA were assigned. Furthermore, in accordance with Article 49, paragraph 3, point b of the University's Academic Regulations, it is specified that students who do not fulfill the additional educational requirements as stated in Article 28 of the University's Academic Regulations cannot enroll in the second-year courses. Therefore, although enrollment in the second year is permitted, it will not be possible to take second-year exams before fulfilling the assigned OFA.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITÀ DEGLI STUDI GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO – CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [L601] DIETETICS
SECTION: Program, texts and objectives
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/606

Program, texts and objectives Communication skills
The ability in communication in terms of acquiring appropriate competencies and tools for communication techniques referring to: communication in Italian and English, written and oral; computer skills, data processing and presentation; ability to work in a group; transmission and dissemination of information on food and nutritional sector topics (information to patients and families by the dietitian regarding the effectiveness of dietary protocols, administration of food diaries, nutritional counseling, interaction between multiple drugs and foods, local tolerance and toxicity from contaminants: pesticides, additives).
The communication ability is acquired through teaching activities that include both frontal lessons, theoretical-practical exercises, laboratory activities and professional internship.
Verification methods are oral interview, written report, simulation of clinical cases in human and clinical nutrition, project work and report.

-----

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITY OF STUDIES GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO – CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [L601] DIETETICS
SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/606

Autonomy of Judgment
Autonomy of judgment in terms of conscious acquisition regarding: evaluation and interpretation of laboratory experimental data and their use in the food, nutritional, and technological fields; critical evaluation of the quality of processes for the production and transformation of food products; selection of nutritional protocols both in physiological and clinical settings; evaluation of risk and safety in the food and nutritional fields; principles of professional ethics and scientific approach to bioethical issues.
Autonomy of judgment is acquired through teaching activities that include both frontal lectures, theoretical-practical exercises, laboratory activities, and professional training internships.
The assessment methods are oral interviews, written reports, simulation of clinical cases in human and clinical nutrition, project work, and reports.

SECTION: Entry Orientation

Entry Orientation Within the framework of entry orientation activities, this University organizes periodic meetings to illustrate the educational offerings, introduce the teaching centers in Chieti and Pescara, and guide students toward a conscious choice of study program. To this end, the University officially organizes orientation days, inviting schools from the territory and neighboring regions. During the pandemic years, online events were held. In this context, the faculty members delegated to orientation will present the educational paths included in the following disciplinary areas (Humanities Area, Social Area, Health Area, Scientific Area). Students will be informed about the teaching contents of each course belonging to the disciplinary area of interest for which registration was made, and will gain a general overview of the study paths related to the same area. Each year at the start of activities, the Dean of the Degree Program and the Director of Professional Teaching meet with new students to explain in detail the objectives and structure of the Degree Program. Information is provided on the location of classrooms where lessons will be held and the sites of internships. The names of the tutors (listed in the dedicated section of this sheet) are also provided, to whom students may turn for explanations or other requests throughout their educational journey.

UNIVERSITY: UNIVERSITY OF CHIETI-PESCARA GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO
COURSE: [L601] DIETETICS
SECTION: Ongoing orientation and tutoring
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/606

Ongoing orientation and tutoring Ongoing orientation is expressed through various delivery methods: the ongoing tutoring activity is carried out by all teachers of the Course of Study, typically during office hours, and is aimed at assisting students in resolving their issues (e.g., suggesting a correct study method). Support tutoring and assisted study consist of training activities aimed at improving learning for certain courses, generally those of the first year of the academic path. Additionally, reference teachers are appointed to whom students can turn in case of need to request personalized tutoring services and agree on the corresponding delivery methods.
During the Course of Study, the University provides on request a service of individual meetings with qualified orientation operators. The service is intended for all students of the Dietetics Course of Study, especially those who need a moment of reflection for potential difficulties in planning and structuring their academic path, or for changes in their pedagogical expectations. Furthermore, for all issues related to the study plan, transfers, students will be supported by both the Teaching and Curriculum Committee of the Course of Study and the Unified Student Secretariat managers. The names of the Course of Study President, the Professional Teaching Director, and the Tutors (teachers and student representatives) available to students during office hours to assist them in resolving any problems encountered during their academic path are listed on the Course of Study website. The ongoing orientation and tutoring service is also provided by the teaching secretariat through the continuous updating of the reference Course of Study website, which contains all information regarding the organization of lecture schedules, exam session calendars, internship calendars, and updates on teaching activities.
Additionally, the University offers the Psychological Listening and Orientation Counseling Service (SAPCO), jointly with the Specific Learning Disorders Service (SDSA) and the Disability Orientation and Welcome Service (SOASD), which form an integral part of the University 'G. d'Annunzio' 'Context Services'. In accordance with regulations on orientation and disability, and in compliance with the current Guidelines of the Conference of Rectors of Italian Universities (CRUI) and the National Conference of University Delegates for Disability (CNUDD), the University responds to specific needs of its users, implementing targeted actions to ensure equal opportunities for study and integration into university life for each student, aiming at maximum participation of the student population in academic activities, while promoting, as much as possible, alongside the regular completion of the academic paths undertaken, student well-being and quality of life.

Career Guidance The Dietetics study program promotes, supports, harmonizes, and enhances the exit orientation services of the program. It provides students who request it and graduates with information and training paths aimed at building a professional identity and thus planning their future. Additionally, efforts will be made to establish connections with all National and International Services and Centers that can be integrated into an information network to guide graduates in the job market.
With exit orientation, understood as specifically oriented training and professional guidance aimed at integrating graduates into the job market, the 'd'Annunzio' University has established a genuine placement structure aimed at increasing the employment and employability of its students through the implementation of assisted career guidance pathways. Therefore, students in the Dietetics program can also benefit from this service.
The service promotes the S.T.A.R.T. project (Internships, Traineeships, Advanced Training, Research, Territory and Placement), which aims to systematize the university, businesses, and research systems to develop and consolidate a virtuous connection of relationships and services. This is intended to facilitate communication between business needs, employment processes, and educational planning, while also providing substance and continuity to the transition phase into the workforce for knowledge resources, thereby enabling our economic/production system to meet the continuous challenges of the market.
Therefore, to increase the employment and employability of its students, the 'd'Annunzio' University has established a genuine placement service.
As is known, pursuant to Law 30/03, commonly known as the Biagi Law, Italian universities can now carry out labor intermediation activities, complementing public employment centers and private operators in providing new employment services.
In compliance with this legal provision, the 'd'Annunzio' University has promptly activated a centralized Placement Service available for its graduates and for local businesses. The University is therefore able to offer those seeking young talent to be integrated into their structure—whether through employment contracts or through training and orientation internships—not only a direct connection with the sought-after professional profile, but also support services aimed at facilitating the identification of professionals matching the specific needs presented.

Student opinions In the new Student Opinion Surveys (ROS) system, it is possible to collect student opinions on 60 Teaching Activities (AF) (5 more than last year) that received at least 6 valid questionnaires as of the update date, with 1,088 questionnaires processed. Analysis of the data shows that 26.6% of courses fall under Level A (score from 3.5 to 4), 63.3% under Level B (score from 3 to 3.5), and only 10% (6 courses) under Level C (score from 2.5 to 3). The 6 Level C courses that do not exceed a score of 3 are consistent with last year. Analysis of these courses that do not reach a score above 3 mostly reveals deficiencies in teaching effectiveness: uninteresting topics, insufficient prerequisite knowledge for understanding the topics covered, lack of teaching materials, and lack of stimulation from the instructor. The overall average score for the courses in the study program (CdS) is 3.3 out of 4, slightly lower than last year. However, this value places the Dietetics CdS in last position among the 16 CdS in the Health Area analyzed.
-In general, most students (80%) are satisfied with the 60 AF offered, despite the number of students nearly tripling from the 2020-2021 academic year, demonstrating the teaching effectiveness of the CdS and the ability of instructors to continue following each student almost personally. However, further analysis elements will be collected for courses that received an evaluation below the average (fortunately only 10%), to understand the reasons and suggest, in collaboration with students of the CdS, particularly those present in the CPDS, targeted measures to improve critical aspects of course delivery from the students' perspective. In particular, it is proposed to revise the various teaching programs to tailor them to the training needs of the CdS under analysis; it is also proposed to focus the delivery of seminars, ADO, etc., according to the training needs of the CdS under analysis. The proposed improvement activities will be reported in the Cyclical Review Reports of the CdS.
These data, which were released in the first week of August 2023, will be discussed in the next CdS council meeting. The CdS has not established an internal Customer Satisfaction system. However, the PQA has established a centralized complaint management system at the university level, accessible at: https://www.unich.it/parla-con-noi.

GRADUATE OPINIONS According to data available on the AlmaLaurea website (updated to June 2023, added as PDF files) (graduate satisfaction regarding the Course of Study), 15 students graduated in 2022, 14 completed the questionnaire (93.3%), of whom 86.7% were women and 13.3% men. The average age at graduation for 46.7% of respondents is between 23 and 24 years (significantly lower than the previous year), for 26.7% it is 27 years or older, and for 20% it is under 20 years. The overall average age is 25.9 years.
- Regarding social origin, 92.9% have no parent with a degree, while only 7.1% have at least one parent with a degree. 57.1% have parents with a secondary school diploma, and 35.7% have parents with a professional qualification.
- Regarding secondary education, more than half of graduates come from a high school education (66.7%), mostly from a scientific high school (46.7%), while the remaining 20% come from technical education and 13.3% from professional education. These data align with the previous year. The average high school diploma grade is 91/100, slightly higher than the previous year. The secondary diploma was obtained in 20% of cases in the same province as the university, a decrease compared to the previous year; 26.7% in a neighboring province, and 26.7% in a non-neighboring province within the same geographical region, slightly increased compared to the previous year, indicating that difficulties in relocation due to the recent pandemic have been largely overcome.
- Regarding academic success, 50% had no prior university experience, while the other 50% had prior university experience, of which only 14.3% was completed. The regular enrollment age or with a 1-year delay is 66.7%, while with 2 or more years of delay it is 33.4%, in line with the previous year. The average exam score is 28.5 (out of 30), with an average graduation grade of 111.5 (out of 110), in line with the previous year. 66.7% of graduates are on track, 20% are one year off track, and 6.7% are four or five years off track, a slightly worse result compared to the previous year when all graduates were on track. Graduates have an average study duration of 4.5 years with a graduation delay of 1.5 years, worsening the previous year's values. This may reflect the lingering difficulties students faced during the pandemic years, which forced them to attend classes, exams, and internships remotely without direct interaction with peers and professors. This assessment will be further analyzed when evaluating students from future years who have not experienced remote learning (at least in university) due to the pandemic.
- Regarding study conditions, 100% regularly attended more than 75% of the required courses (attendance is mandatory), in line with the previous year. Over 50% of the study duration was spent living within an hour's travel from the university (57.9%), and 42.9% for less than 50% of the study duration. Only 21.4% received a scholarship, about half as many as the previous year. Unfortunately, none completed studies abroad (Erasmus), while 92.9% completed internships organized by the Course of Study (in line with the previous year), of which 78.6% were completed outside the university and 14.3% at the university. The time spent on the thesis is 4.5 months.
- Regarding work during studies, 42.9% had work experience during university, of which 35.7% had occasional work and 7.1% had part-time work, while none had work related to their studies (a decrease compared to previous years), and the remaining 50% had no work experience.
- Regarding satisfaction with the university experience, 64.3% feel satisfied (42.9% more yes than no, 21.4% definitely yes), in line with the previous year, while 28.6% and 7.1% responded more yes than no and definitely no, respectively. 85.7% feel satisfied with the relationship with professors (57.1% more yes than no, 28.6% definitely yes), slightly increased from the previous year. 85.8% feel satisfied with the relationship with students. 100% used classrooms considered adequate by 92.8%. 64.3% used computer workstations, a significant increase from the previous year, though 55.6% of respondents rated the number of workstations as inadequate. 92.9% used library services, rated as fairly positive by 61.5% and decidedly positive by 30.8%. 57.1% used equipment for other teaching activities, of which 87.5% considered it adequate. 78.6% used individual study spaces, and 64.3% used post-graduation study orientation services, which were rated as inadequate by 77.7% of respondents. 64.3% used career orientation training initiatives, rating them as inadequate (77.8%). 64.3% used job search support services, rating them as unsatisfactory (66.6%). 64.3% also used the "job placement" office, rating it as moderately unsatisfactory (55.5%) compared to 44.4% who rated it satisfactory. The evaluation of exam organization is positive for 86.7%, and the study load is positive for 85.7%, in line with the previous year. 35.7% stated they would enroll again in the same course at the university (a decrease from the previous year), while 50% would enroll in the same course at another university.
- Regarding language and IT skills, 50% report knowledge of foreign languages, mostly English and written, at B2 level. 85.7% report knowledge of internet navigation and online communication, 57% report knowledge of Word, 71.4% of spreadsheets and presentation tools, and 71.4% of operational tools.
- Regarding further study prospects, 100% intend to continue studies (a significant increase from the previous year); 42.9% as a two-year master's degree, while 35.7% would pursue a university master's, and 7.1% would pursue post-graduation specialization, other master's, or professional qualifications. The main reason for enrolling in a two-year master's is to complete training (66.7%) or as a required choice (33.3%). The university they intend to enroll in is 50% another university in the center, while only 33.4% would choose the same university as their first-degree.
- Regarding work prospects, key factors for job search include acquiring professional skills (85.7%), earning potential and career opportunities (78.6%), alignment with studies and prestige (64.3%), involvement in decision-making processes and flexible working hours (50%), free time (57.1%), and the ability to effectively use acquired skills (78.6%). They would work in both private and public sectors equally, with a preference for full-time (78.6%), while 50% prefer part-time and 57.1% would also opt for telework. 100% prefer a contract with increasing protections, 28.6% fixed-term, and 57.1% self-employed. Graduates are mostly inclined to work in their province of residence or the province and region of their studies, but also in other parts of Italy; graduates are also willing to travel for work, though only 14.3% are not willing to travel.
Overall, the evaluation of the current Course of Study appears positive and satisfactory regarding academic success, study conditions, work during studies, and general satisfaction with the university experience, in line with pre-pandemic years, confirming the Course of Study's ability to meet student and future worker needs and to overcome pandemic-related challenges, regaining graduate trust.
However, a negative aspect requiring further analysis relates to work prospects. Graduates report low satisfaction with post-graduation study orientation services, career orientation training initiatives, job search support services, and the "job placement" office, indicating the university's limited ability to engage with the territory and the job market for Dietetics graduates. Another negative aspect relates to further study prospects, where only 33.3% of graduates would enroll in a two-year master's at the same university as their first degree, despite 100% intending to continue studies. This also indicates the university's inability to attract first-degree graduates for a master's. Finally, the low percentage of students who know a foreign language and effectively use IT services reduces their job prospects abroad.
AlmaLaurea data have not yet been discussed in the council but will be addressed in the next council meeting, where we can evaluate potential improvements to the Course of Study, particularly the possibility for students to complete part of their studies abroad in countries offering similar courses, and discuss the information barrier graduates face with post-graduation orientation offices.
Learning Skills
Ability to learn in terms of adequate acquisition for further development and deepening of additional competencies, referring to: Consultation of bibliographic material, Consultation of databases and other online information, Basic knowledge tools for continuous updating of knowledge in human nutrition and clinical, bromatological chemistry, and food technologies and biotechnologies, and ability to learn to plan and carry out specific research projects in public or private sectors in the food and nutrition field.
Learning ability is acquired through training activities, integrating knowledge gained through specific activities with those acquired through personal study, evaluating the critical contribution demonstrated during seminar and clinical internship activities.
Verification methods include oral interviews, written reports, clinical case simulations in human nutrition and clinical, project work, and reports.

Brief Course Description
Within the healthcare profession of Dietitian, graduates of the Dietetics Course of Study are healthcare professionals with responsibilities as defined by the Ministry of Health Decree 14 September 1994, No. 744 and subsequent amendments: they are competent for all activities aimed at the correct application of diet and nutrition, including educational aspects and collaboration in implementing food policies, in compliance with current regulations.
The Dietitian is "the professional who applies the science of diet and nutrition to promote health, prevent and treat diseases, optimizing the health of individuals, groups, communities, and populations" (ICDA, International Confederation of Dietetics Associations).
Graduates organize and coordinate activities related to general nutrition and dietetics; collaborate with bodies responsible for the hygienic-sanitary aspects of food services; develop, formulate, and implement diets prescribed by doctors and monitor patient acceptability.
Dietitians collaborate with other professionals in the multidisciplinary treatment of eating disorders; study and develop food rations to meet population nutritional needs and plan the organization of food services for healthy and sick communities.
Dietitians conduct educational and informative activities to disseminate principles of correct nutrition, enabling the recovery and maintenance of good health for individuals, collectives, and population groups. Dietitians perform their professional activities in healthcare facilities, public or private, in dependent or self-employed status.
Beyond healthcare, the Dietitian contributes to optimizing the nutritional environment for all citizens by acting with governments, industry, academia, and research (EFAD, The European Federation of the Associations of Dietitians).

Specific Course Learning Objectives and Description of the Study Path
Graduates in this class are, in accordance with Law 10 August 2000, No. 251, Article 3, Paragraph 1, operators in the technical-healthcare professions who perform technical methodologies for clinical-medical procedures in accordance with regulations concerning the roles of defined professional profiles established by a decree of the Ministry of Health.
The Course of Study aims to achieve the following learning objectives:
Dietitian graduates must have adequate preparation in basic disciplines to best understand the most relevant elements underlying pathological processes in pediatric, adult, and geriatric age groups, which are the focus of their diagnostic intervention. They must also be able to use at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian, within their specific field for general information exchange.
Based on adequate mastery of general scientific methods and content, the Dietitian, as a healthcare professional with responsibilities as defined by the Ministry of Health Decree 14.09.1994, No. 744 and subsequent amendments, must be able to perform all activities aimed at the correct application of diet and nutrition, including educational aspects and collaboration in implementing food policies, in compliance with current regulations. Graduates organize and coordinate activities related to general nutrition and dietetics; collaborate with bodies responsible for the hygienic-sanitary aspects of food services; develop, formulate, and implement diets prescribed by doctors and monitor patient acceptability; collaborate with other professionals in the multidisciplinary treatment of eating disorders; study and develop food rations to meet population nutritional needs and plan the organization of food services for healthy and sick communities; conduct educational and informative activities to disseminate principles of correct nutrition, enabling the recovery and maintenance of good health for individuals, collectives, and population groups.
Students must be able to apply, through internships, knowledge related to their professional practice and participate in identifying health needs and planning, delivering, and evaluating dietetic care for individuals and communities, ensuring correct application of diagnostic-therapeutic prescriptions; they must also know general bioethical, deontological, legal, and medical-legal principles of the Dietitian's professional profile. Finally, they must be able to orient themselves for further specialist in-depth studies. They perform their professional activities in accordance with agreements between universities and regions in hospital settings, university polyclinics, IRCCS, and other structures of the national health service, as well as at accredited private institutions. Training facilities must meet minimum requirements established by law.
The course duration is three years:
Year 1 is focused on providing knowledge in basic disciplines and the foundations of the professional discipline, aimed at applying the principles of general nutrition and dietetics through a structured educational path starting from knowledge of foods, to collective catering, to dietotherapy. Regarding the Year 1 internship, the program is developed within collective catering as the Dietitian's specific professional focus is to combine organizational and hygienic-sanitary aspects with nutritional aspects.
Year 2 is focused on nutritional knowledge to address health issues in medical and surgical areas, specialized, maternal-child, oncological, and within the context of eating behavior disorders. Multiple clinical internships are planned in contexts where students can apply learned knowledge and techniques. It is important that the Dietitian involved in nutritional treatment centers the patient and their needs, applying guidelines from national and international standards.
Year 3 is focused on specialized in-depth study but also on acquiring knowledge and methodologies related to professional practice, the ability to work in teams, and in complex organizational contexts. The relevance of internships increases, allowing students to gradually assume autonomy and responsibility under expert supervision. Training activities are planned to develop methodological skills for understanding scientific research and supporting the thesis.
The average number of credits to acquire per year is 60, for a total of 180 credits. The University Credit is the unit of measurement for the learning effort required by the student for the completion of prescribed training activities. One University Credit (CFU) corresponds to 25 hours of learning effort, including lecture hours, theoretical-practical lectures, exercises, laboratory, seminars, and other training activities, including individual study hours.
Each CFU, depending on the type of training activity, may be worth: 10 hours of frontal lectures + 15 hours of student self-study; 15 hours of laboratory internship + 10 hours of student self-study.
Internship refers to internship activities carried out in the training structures of Local Health Authorities or at collective catering structures, public or private.

Entry, Path, and Exit Data
Entry, path, and exit data, available at the link: https://pqa.unich.it/dati-statistici (and added as PDF files), show that 31 students enrolled in the 2022/23 cohort of the Dietetics Course of Study, in line with the previous year, for a total of 77 students in the entire course, 13 more than the previous year. Of the 31 enrolled, 22 are pure enrollments, 73 are on track, and 4 are off track (two more than the previous year), with a total of 67 regular students.
Regarding geographical origin, 7 enrolled and 5 pure enrolled students come from the same municipality; 17 enrolled and 12 pure enrolled from another municipality in the province; 7 enrolled and 1 pure enrolled from another province in the region; and 6 enrolled and 4 pure enrolled from other regions. Compared to the previous year, there is an increase in students from the same municipality, while those from another municipality in the province or other regions have decreased.
Regarding the type of diploma obtained, 14 enrolled and 8 pure enrolled come from high schools; 7 enrolled and 5 pure enrolled from technical institutes; 6 enrolled and 6 pure enrolled from professional institutes; 4 enrolled and 3 pure enrolled from magistrali. Compared to the previous year, there is a slight decrease in students from high schools and technical institutes, while there is a slight increase from professional institutes.
Regarding the high school diploma grade, 2 enrolled and 2 pure enrolled have 100 with honors, 3 enrolled and 1 pure enrolled have 100, 16 enrolled and 13 pure enrolled have between 80 and 99, and 10 enrolled and 6 pure enrolled have up to 80. Compared to the previous year, results are similar.
Regarding exit data, 15 students graduated in 2022: 12 students have a graduation grade of 100 with honors, of whom 8 are on track, 2 with one year beyond the course duration, 1 with two years beyond, and 1 with less than one year beyond; 2 students have a grade between 105 and 110, of whom 1 with one year beyond and 1 with two years beyond; 1 student on track has a grade of 105. Compared to the previous year's graduates, the total is slightly increased (15 vs 13), and the number of students graduating with 100 with honors has slightly increased, although all graduates the previous year were on track.
Regarding cohort trends, the number of enrolled students remains stable between 2022 (14), 2021 (15), and 2020 (15) after the trend of reduced enrollment reported in 2021 (13), compared to 2020 (14) and 2019 (16). The data (still partial as the 2022-23 academic year is not yet completed) show an average of 4 exams passed per student, decreasing from 2021 (7.4) and 2020 (8.6); with CFU acquired relative to required CFU at 29, a significant decrease from 2021 (75.2) and 2020 (72.2).
Regarding first-year enrollment and progression to the second year, data show that 33 students enrolled in the cohort, compared to 15 the previous year, with 75.76% progressing to the second year of the same course, compared to 100% the previous year; 72.73% progressing to the second year of the same course with more than 40 CFU (compared to 80% the previous year); 9% of the cohort enrolled as inactive (with CFU ≤ 20% of required CFU), compared to 0% the previous year; and 3% of the cohort enrolled who did not earn any CFU, compared to 0% the previous year. Overall, the percentage of CFU acquired relative to required CFU is 69.95%, compared to 79.44% the previous year.
Overall, these data indicate an increase in students from the same municipality, while those from other municipalities in the province or other regions have decreased. While graduation grades remain mostly consistent, fewer students progress to the second year with 40 CFU, and there is an increase in inactive students and those who did not earn any CFU.
The data have not yet been discussed in the council but will be analyzed in the next Course of Study Council.
Final Exam Characteristics
To be admitted to take the Study exam, the Student must:
a) Have successfully completed all front-facing teaching activities of the Course of Study, including all Integrated Courses, and passed all exams;
b) Have earned a total of 180 CFU over the three years of the Course of Study;
c) Have completed all mandatory professional training activities and passed the mandatory professional training internship with a minimum grade of 18/30, evaluated and certified at the end of the third year through a formal document;
d) Have taken and passed the final exam of the third year at least 30 days before the graduation session. Prior to this, third-year teachers must establish exam dates at least 30 days before the graduation session date to allow the Student Secretariat to prepare documentation in time;
e) Submit to the Unified Student Secretariat:
► At least 90 (ninety) days before the graduation session:
• The graduation application addressed to the Rector;
► At least 20 (twenty) working days before the graduation session:
• The university transcript showing regular attendance and passed exams throughout the Course of Study;
• The internship transcript, properly completed and signed, showing regular attendance and passed internship exams throughout the Course of Study;
• The thesis front page;
• The Alma Laurea;
• The final exam report;
► At least 7 (seven) working days before the graduation session:
• One (1) copy of the Study thesis on CD.
The final exam consists of:
• A practical exam where the student must demonstrate acquisition of theoretical-practical and technical-professional knowledge specific to the professional profile;
• A thesis paper written by the student on a specific topic, aimed at demonstrating the ability to address professional topics in an original and independent manner.
The practical exam grade must be considered by the Commission for the final grade assignment. The points assigned by the Commission are:
18/30 to 21/30 = 1 point;
22/30 to 24/30 = 2 points;
25/30 to 27/30 = 3 points;
28/30 to 30/30 = 4 points.
In case of a negative practical exam result, the student cannot be admitted to the thesis paper discussion. In this case, the Commission President will announce the result via notice in the venue where the practical exam was held and before the thesis discussion, indicating the procedures to access the documents.
The Commission deliberates by majority of its members. In case of a tie, the President's vote prevails.
The Commission prepares a formal report on the practical exam and its outcome. The Commission President ensures the results are posted at the venue where the practical exam was held and at the Course's teaching venue.
The Commission uses the Study Transcript, which lists the exams taken during the Course of Study and the average grade achieved during the training path.
Points assigned by the Commission for the thesis discussion (from 0 to a maximum of 6 points for experimental theses and 0 to 3 points for compilation theses).
The Study Commission evaluates the candidate as a whole, considering the study curriculum in the Study Transcript, the practical exam performance, the thesis paper, and the thesis discussion.
The exam is considered passed with a minimum grade of 66/110.
In case of a maximum grade (110/110), the Commission may award honors upon proposal by the President and unanimous decision of the Commission.
The Commission may recognize scientific value in the thesis paper and propose its publication, even electronically.
Final Exam Execution Method
The final exam, to be conducted over two days as per ministerial guidelines, in the presence of a Commission and representatives of the profession and/or the Ministry of Health, consists of:
1) A practical exam where the student must demonstrate acquisition of theoretical-practical and technical-professional knowledge specific to the professional profile. The practical exam consists of a written report, randomly selected (blindly by one of the present students) from 3 clinical cases proposed. The practical exam score will be expressed in 30/30, converted to 1, 2, 3, or 4 points (see below), to be added to the final grade after the oral exam to express the final grade in 110/110;
2) A thesis paper written by the student on a specific topic under the supervision of a tutor, aimed at demonstrating the ability to address professional topics in an original and independent manner. The thesis discussion will use slides for explanation.
In case of a negative practical exam result, the student cannot be admitted to the thesis paper discussion. In this case, the Commission President will announce the result via notice in the venue where the practical exam was held and before the thesis discussion, indicating the procedures to access the documents.
The Commission then evaluates the candidate as a whole, considering the study curriculum in the Study Transcript, the practical exam performance, the thesis paper, and the thesis discussion.
The points assigned by the Commission for the practical exam are:
18/30 to 21/30 = 1 point;
22/30 to 24/30 = 2 points;
25/30 to 27/30 = 3 points;
28/30 to 30/30 = 4 points.
Points assigned for the thesis discussion range from 0 to 6 for experimental theses and 0 to 3 for compilation theses.
The exam is considered passed with a minimum grade of 66/110.
In case of a maximum grade (110/110), the Commission may award honors upon proposal by the Commission President and unanimous decision of the Commission members.
The Commission may recognize scientific value in the thesis paper and propose its publication, even electronically.

CURRICULUM: HEALTH ASSISTANCE
SECTION: Admission procedures
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/608

Admission procedures Admission to the Study Course is granted upon passing a specific test based on ministerial decrees regarding the procedures and content of entrance tests for university courses with national quota-based access.
Additional Training Obligations Additional training obligations (OFA) are required for candidates below a specified evaluation threshold. In addition to serving a selective function for entry into the first year of the course, the entrance test also fulfills the obligation (pursuant to DM 270/04) to verify the basic preparation of all students enrolling for the first time in the Health Assistance Study Course at 'G. d'Annunzio' University of Chieti-Pescara. This verification aims to identify any educational gaps among new enrollees and organize necessary recovery activities (in addition to the regular teaching activities of the Study Course), thereby providing academic support to students assigned Additional Training Obligations (OFA) based on gaps identified through the entrance test/initial knowledge assessment.
For the purpose of verifying initial knowledge, only answers to questions in the entrance test related to the following subjects are considered:
- Biology
- Chemistry
- Physics and Mathematics Questions related to general culture and logical reasoning are not considered.
How Additional Training Obligations are Determined For the disciplinary areas listed above where recovery activities are provided, students who provide correct answers below 25% of the questions in individual subjects will be assigned OFA to be completed obligatorily within the first year through methods established by the Course Director and the instructors of the relevant disciplines after enrollment.
Completing OFA within the first year of the course is mandatory to be eligible to take the corresponding official exams as specified in the Study Plan.
Recovery procedures If necessary, the Study Course will activate recovery courses - in addition to regular course lectures - for each disciplinary area where students have educational deficits. In this regard, instructors of the disciplines subject to OFA will establish 1 or 2 weekly hours dedicated to recovery. Attendance at the recovery course is mandatory. Students attending recovery courses are not exempt from the obligation to attend regular courses. The educational deficit is considered fulfilled upon passing a verification test, which can be taken on dates published on the Study Course website: http://www.med.unich.it/corsi-di-laurea/assistenza-sanitaria If the deficit is not fulfilled within the first year of the course, enrollment in the second year will be permitted, but the corresponding exams specified in the Study Plan cannot be taken before completing the assigned OFA.

Program, texts and objectives Communication skills
The graduate in Health Assistance must have acquired the ability to:
- communicate with users and colleagues using appropriate language;
- structure the reception of individuals, families and groups in services;
- transmit information and communications of a health, psychological and social nature appropriate to the target audience;
- establish correct and effective relationships aimed at obtaining useful elements for the collection of anamnesis and the implementation of epidemiological and health-social research;
- report and document;
- identify appropriate communication methods for each specific operational situation;
- structure effective relationships with educational, supportive or promotional purposes for the individual in different life stages, for the family and for the community;
- establish correct communication within the institutional context for hierarchical and functional aspects;
- structure an interview setting for analyzing needs and evaluating health needs regarding both manifest and latent aspects;
- speak publicly using effective bidirectional engagement methods;
- develop effective communication within monoprofessional and interdisciplinary work groups, facilitating information circulation and task/project work;
- promote network work by demonstrating ability to build community networks;
- motivate citizens to engage in prevention and health promotion practices within the community;
- apply individual interview and group device communication skills for the promotion of sexual, reproductive, socio-affective health and family planning;
- apply specific relational skills for participation in family therapy programs;
- express relational skills within problematic settings related to family difficulties, relational issues, infectious or genetic risks, work risks, etc.
- express relational skills for structuring effective pedagogical and promotional settings specific to childhood, adulthood, problematic population groups, immigrants, etc.
- express relational skills for managing and conducting preventive interventions including health emergency conditions;
- express relational skills in the use of tools for verifying processes regarding the quality of health service performance;
- use communication and marketing techniques related to prevention, promotion and health education;
- be competent in listening for the protection of citizens' rights.
Communication skills will be acquired through theoretical teachings in psychology, pedagogy, sociology, and professional methodology, as well as through professional workshops and internship.
The acquisition of behavioral competencies will be verified by tutors through teaching activities, during the internship and in workshops, and through the final assessment.

UNIVERSITY: GABRIELE D'ANNUNZIO UNIVERSITY OF CHIETI/PESCARA
COURSE: [L648] HEALTH ASSISTANCE
SECTION: JUDGMENT AUTONOMY
URL: https://unich.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/608

Judgment Autonomy
The graduate in Health Assistance must have the ability to collect and interpret data for the areas of health promotion, prevention and health education, and to reflect on key social, scientific and ethical issues related to them in order to formulate autonomous judgments that account for the complexity and variability of contexts. In particular, the graduate must demonstrate judgment autonomy in identifying health needs, identifying biological and social risk factors, planning, implementing and evaluating educational projects, and identifying priorities for preventive, educational and recovery interventions.
The graduate must possess analytical, critical and responsible skills in performing the functions outlined in the professional profile.
They must demonstrate the ability to apply ethical principles in professional practice.
They must be able to recognize their own limitations in professional practice, activate network resources, and participate in multidisciplinary team work to achieve prevention strategies.
Judgment autonomy will be verified through evaluations by assigned supervisors, examinations, internship assessments, and through verification related to the final exam.

c) difficulties in activating internationalization pathways.

Learning Skills
The graduate must have developed learning skills that enable them to continue studying independently in their specific fields of interest.
Since prevention and health promotion interventions, which constitute one of the main areas of interest for the Healthcare Assistant, require not only acquired knowledge but also the ability to analyze individual problems and construct an applicable intervention model in specific situations, the Healthcare Assistant graduate must be able to:
- Seek necessary information to solve problems or uncertainties regarding professional practice, critically selecting sources;
- Structure circular learning environments;
- Study independently;
- Learn within the workgroup;
- Update theoretical knowledge through consultation and analysis of scientific publications, also using databases and retrieving information available on the internet, while critically examining them;
- Achieve sufficient knowledge and methodological skills to continue their study and cultural growth independently (Master's Degree, University Specialization Courses, University Master's Programs).
Learning skills are assessed through continuous verification during training activities, integrating knowledge acquired during specific activities with those gained through personal study, evaluating the critical contribution demonstrated during seminar and internship activities, as well as the ability to self-learn developed during the final project activity.
